temas.descripcion: Standard precautions, bloodborne pathogens, PPE, sharps, exposure incidents, HIPAA, CLIA and scope of practice.

preguntas.pregunta: May a physician decline to take on a patient or to provide a treatment that has been requested?
opciones: Yes, as when the treatment is not indicated by the history given
Yes, but only where another provider has already agreed to take over
No, once the person has been registered as a patient of the practice
No, unless an emergency elsewhere makes the schedule impossible
preguntas.explicacion: The right runs in both directions. A physician may in many circumstances decline to enter into the relationship or to offer a treatment, for instance when accepting a referral for a specific treatment seems unwarranted or the treatment is not indicated by the history provided. The privilege is old, dating to the Hippocratic era, but no law protects it as broadly as the profession states, and the laws that do protect it usually rest on freedom of religion.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal (by Both Patient and Physician)
preguntas.subtema: The provider's refusal · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1

preguntas.pregunta: In which setting may an employer decide that gloves are not routinely required for every phlebotomy?
opciones: A volunteer blood donation center, under conditions such as gloves for trainees
A clinical laboratory, if it applies Universal Precautions to all specimens
An outpatient draw station, if the phlebotomist has no cuts on the hands
Any facility, if the employee documents that gloves reduce manual dexterity
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix) requires gloves for vascular access procedures with one carve-out, (d)(3)(ix)(D): a volunteer blood donation center whose employer judges routine gloving unnecessary. Even there the employer must periodically reevaluate the policy, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, never discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination is likely such as with an uncooperative donor, and during phlebotomy training. No other setting gets the exception.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix) and (d)(3)(ix)(D), Gloves
preguntas.subtema: Glove exception for blood donation · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4

preguntas.pregunta: After a draw with an evacuated tube system, how does the WHO say the needle and holder should be disposed of?
opciones: Discard barrel and needle together as a single unit whenever possible
Unscrew the needle by hand and drop it into the sharps container, keeping the barrel
Recap the needle with both hands, then remove it from the barrel for reuse
Leave the needle on the barrel and place both in the regulated-waste bag
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says to discard the barrel and needle as a single entity where possible; if the barrel must be reused, the needle is removed with a one-hand scoop technique or with a sharps container that has a needle removal hold, always one-handed. Annex E adds that an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and OSHA prohibits two-handed recapping and removal except where no alternative is feasible.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1 and Annex E; and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot raise sputum on his own and sputum induction is started. When is the procedure stopped?
opciones: When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 15 minutes of nebulization, or if chest tightness begins
When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 60 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient coughs hard
When 10 to 20 mL has been obtained, after 15 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient coughs hard
When 1 to 2 mL has been obtained, after 5 minutes of nebulization, or if the patient starts to gag
preguntas.explicacion: Induction has the patient breathe a nebulized 3 percent hypertonic saline mist for about five minutes to thin the secretions, then take deep breaths and cough. It is halted once 1 to 2 mL of sputum is in the container, at 15 minutes of nebulization, or if chest tightness, breathlessness or wheezing appear, because a pleural bulla can rupture and cause a pneumothorax. Saliva goes into an emesis bowl, not the container.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Sputum Induction
preguntas.subtema: Sputum induction limits · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4)

preguntas.pregunta: Which products fall outside the scope of the FDA guidance on sharps injury prevention features?
opciones: Sharps containers and needle recapping devices
Winged sets and retractable safety lancet devices
Insulin syringes and their orange needle covers
Blood collection needles fitted with a shield
preguntas.explicacion: That guidance covers medical devices carrying an active or passive component that protects the user from a sharps injury. It says plainly that it does not deal with sharps containers or with needle recapping devices, which are handled by separate guidance of their own.
preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Section 4, Scope
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's driver takes blood samples to the hospital laboratory every afternoon. Besides a rack or padded holder for the tubes, what must the vehicle carry according to WHO?
opciones: A blood spillage kit, so that a broken sample can be cleaned up safely on the way
A portable centrifuge, so that serum can be separated if the trip is delayed
A carbon dioxide incubator, so that culture specimens keep their organisms viable
A second set of empty tubes, so that a broken sample can be recollected on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: For transporting blood samples outside a hospital, WHO asks that the vehicle be equipped with a blood spillage kit, because a sample can break during transport just as it can in the phlebotomy area; the spill is then handled with gloves and, for large spills, a gown or apron, paper towels that go into infectious waste, and a freshly prepared bleach solution. Multiple tubes travel in a rack or padded holder precisely to avoid that breakage.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 10 and 11
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5D k89 · PBT III.D · CCMA 3E14 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A cream is applied to a child's antecubital skin before a venipuncture. What is EMLA and when does it peak?
opciones: 2.5% lidocaine with 2.5% prilocaine; peak plasma levels come about 2 to 6 hours after application under occlusion
5% lidocaine alone; peak plasma levels come about 15 to 30 minutes after application, as with infiltration
2.5% lidocaine with 2.5% bupivacaine; peak plasma levels come within 1.5 to 2 hours, its half-life
2% chloroprocaine gel; peak plasma levels come immediately, which is why it is preferred in neonates
preguntas.explicacion: EMLA is a eutectic mixture of 2.5% lidocaine and 2.5% prilocaine used for topical analgesia before venipuncture, IV catheter placement and lumbar puncture; after application under occlusion the reported Tmax is roughly 2 to 6 hours, and the elimination half-life of both drugs is about 1.5 to 2 hours. The 15 to 30 minute peak belongs to infiltrated lidocaine, and chloroprocaine is an injectable ester.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Local Anesthetics in Children", sections Indications and Pharmacokinetics
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.B age-specific needs, II.D preparation

preguntas.pregunta: Which measures were proposed to reduce the blood lost to serial phlebotomy in intensive care?
opciones: Fewer and batched tests, smaller tubes, and blood conservation devices
Fewer and batched tests, larger tubes, and more frequent line flushing
Capillary sampling for every test, so that no venous tubes are needed
Drawing all of the day's tests through the vascular access line at once
preguntas.explicacion: A substantial portion of daily phlebotomy in the unit is blood discarded as waste during vascular access. The measures discussed are cutting the number and frequency of tests, batching samples and offering add-on orders, reducing the volume held in collection tubes, and blood conservation devices that remove access waste. Smaller tubes are described as an adjunct, not a replacement for testing less.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, Patient harm associated with serial phlebotomy and blood waste in the ICU, PLoS One 2021 (PMC7806151), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: Serial phlebotomy harm · CPT D4 4E k83 volume requirements

preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for the first step of two-step gestational screening asks what she should do about food beforehand. What do you tell her?
opciones: No fast and no diet change: the screening step needs neither one
No food or drink, apart from sips of water, for 8 to 14 hours before
Eat an unrestricted diet with 150 g of carbohydrate a day for 3 days
Eat a light breakfast exactly one hour before the appointment time
preguntas.explicacion: For the screening step the patient does not have to prepare or change her diet in any way: she drinks the glucose liquid and blood is drawn one hour later. The 8-to-14-hour fast belongs to the 3-hour follow-up test and to the one-step 75 g test; the three-day carbohydrate load is a condition of the nonpregnant diagnostic OGTT. Eating normally in the days before is the only instruction given.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test is Performed and How to Prepare for the Test
preguntas.subtema: Gestational screening preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-month-old infant weighing 5 kg needs a capillary specimen. Which site does WHO Table 7.1 indicate, and where on it is the lancet placed?
opciones: The heel, on the medial or lateral plantar surface
The heel, on the posterior curve where skin is thickest
The middle or ring finger, on the side of the ball
The thumb or index finger, on the side of the ball
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 assigns the heel-prick to infants from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, with the lancet on the medial or lateral plantar surface; the finger-prick is for children over 6 months and over 10 kg. Chapter 7 says the posterior heel should be avoided because the bone lies only 2.33 mm beneath the skin, and the table itself warns against the thumb and index finger.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1; and Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: Site by age · CPT D3 k55 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5

preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture, what form of consent does WHO step 2 describe obtaining?
opciones: Verbal consent, after discussing the test with the patient
Written consent, signed by the patient and witnessed by staff
Implied consent, shown by the patient's presence in the clinic
Consent given by the ordering physician on the laboratory form
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO step reads: discuss the test to be performed and obtain verbal consent, adding that the patient can refuse at any point before the sampling. StatPearls describes written documentation for informed consent in general, but the WHO phlebotomy step relies on a spoken yes after an explanation. Nothing in either source lets the requester's signature stand in for the patient.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E types of consent · CCMA 3E1 · CMA E.3.b (both outlines) · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: How are the vessels sampled in a capillary blood collection best described?
opciones: The smallest vessels, 5–10 μm wide, connecting arterioles and venules
The smallest arteries, about 30 μm wide, connecting arteries to capillaries
Thin-walled vessels, 8–100 μm wide, that carry blood on toward the veins
Superficial veins that run in the roof of the cubital fossa of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Capillaries are the body's smallest vessels, 5 to 10 micrometers across, linking arterioles and venules; a capillary sample is usually taken by heel or finger prick, and the narrowest capillaries just fit one erythrocyte. Arterioles average 30 micrometers or less and venules 8 to 100 micrometers, and the superficial veins of the cubital fossa are venipuncture sites, not capillaries.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Glossary: Capillary blood collection; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Capillaries
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 k7 (applied D3 k71) · PBT I.B.1 I.A.4 · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse asks why a glucose flagged as a critical value is handled differently from a test ordered STAT. What distinguishes the two?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far the result deviates from the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT test is defined by how far the result deviates from the normal range
A critical value applies only to results from laboratory analyzers; a STAT designation applies only to point-of-care devices
A critical value must be repeated on a new specimen; a STAT test is reported from the first run without any repetition
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are defined solely by the degree to which a result deviates from the established normal range, regardless of the patient's condition, whereas STAT or urgent tests are designated by the ordering clinician and usually presuppose knowledge of the patient's status. Point-of-care results that reach a critical value are addressed promptly and often change management, so both the result and the actions taken are documented.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13 k111

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse is about to insert an IV cannula and asks whether the blood tests can be drawn at the same time. What does the WHO say?
opciones: It is acceptable but not ideal, when the cannula is first inserted and before the fluids are connected
It is the preferred method, because it spares the patient a second puncture and gives identical results
It is never acceptable; specimens from any in-dwelling device carry a risk of contamination
It is acceptable only for blood cultures, which must be drawn before any fluid is connected
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 states that it is acceptable, but not ideal, to draw blood when first introducing an in-dwelling venous device, before the cannula is connected to the intravenous fluids. The same passage forbids drawing from an access that is already in use because of false results, and notes that central line specimens taken by nurses or physicians under protocol carry a contamination risk.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and IV access · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the superficial arm veins is typically the larger of the two?
opciones: The basilic vein, although the cephalic is sometimes larger
The cephalic vein, although the basilic is sometimes larger
The median cubital vein, which is larger than either of them
Both are the same calibre, since they drain equal territories
preguntas.explicacion: Size varies a great deal between patients, but the basilic is usually the larger superficial vein of the arm and sometimes the cephalic takes that place. Calibre alone does not decide the puncture: an artery and a nerve travel with the basilic, which makes it the riskier of the two.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8

preguntas.pregunta: A draw with a needle and syringe has finished. How are the two treated at the moment of disposal?
opciones: As a single unit, dropped straight into a robust sharps container
As two items, the needle in the sharps bin and the syringe in waste
As a single unit, but only after the needle has been re-sheathed
As two items, the syringe rinsed first and the needle discarded
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction treats a needle and syringe as one unit and asks for the used device to go immediately into a robust sharps container. The prohibition on the other side of the table is equally plain: an unprotected needle is never left lying outside that container.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A lavender tube arrives in the emergency laboratory with no label at all, together with a requisition for a CBC. According to the rejection criteria used by emergency laboratories, what happens to it?
opciones: It is rejected as a misidentified specimen and a new sample is requested
It is accepted if the requisition in the bag identifies the patient
It is held at 4 °C for up to 24 hours until the ward sends a label to attach to it
It is tested and the result is reported with a comment about the label
preguntas.explicacion: Unlabeled, mislabeled and mismatched samples fall under misidentification, one of the standing rejection criteria of the emergency laboratory, alongside missing barcodes, improper containers, insufficient volume, hemolysis, lipemia and clots. The requisition in the bag does not identify the tube, storing it while waiting for a label amounts to relabeling, and reporting a result from an unidentified tube is the error the criteria exist to prevent.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: What does the blood culture bottle in the WHO order-of-draw table contain, and what is it used for?
opciones: A broth mixture that keeps microorganisms viable; aerobes, anaerobes and fungi
Sodium citrate that removes calcium; coagulation tests such as prothrombin time
Acid-citrate-dextrose that inactivates complement; HLA typing and DNA studies
A clot activator that yields serum; chemistries, serology and cross-match
preguntas.explicacion: Row 1 of Table 2.3 describes the yellow-black striped blood culture bottle: its additive is a broth mixture, its mode of action is to preserve the viability of microorganisms, and its uses are microbiology for aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. The other three descriptions are the rows for the light blue citrate tube, the pale yellow ACD tube and the red clot activator tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: An accessioning clerk scans a specimen barcode and the screen fills with far more than the patient's name. What kind of data does such a barcode key typically pull up?
opciones: Tube and specimen type, print and collection times, the ward, and who drew it
Only the patient's names and hospital number, kept short to avoid misreads
The analyser assigned to the tube and the position it holds in the rack
The insurance carrier, the diagnosis code and the billing account number
preguntas.explicacion: In the hospital that published its rejection audit, a nine-digit internal barcode identified name, surname, gender, age, tube type, specimen type, the time the label was printed, the collection date and time, the service where the specimen was taken, the tests requested, the ordering physician and the phlebotomist. Access to those databases is restricted to clinical and laboratory staff.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k89 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k112 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: Which employers must keep a sharps injury log, and how must the log treat the injured worker?
opciones: Those that must keep injury records under 29 CFR part 1904, protecting the worker's confidentiality
Every employer with a single exposed worker, listing the worker's name for follow-up
Only hospitals accredited by CMS-approved organizations, identifying each worker by badge number
Only employers who have had an exposure incident, keeping the log for 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(ii) applies the sharps injury log requirement to any employer already required to keep a log of occupational injuries and illnesses under 29 CFR part 1904, and (h)(5)(iii) keeps it for the period required by 1904.33. The information is recorded so as to protect the confidentiality of the injured employee, which is the opposite of listing names. Accreditation is not the test, and the 30-year period belongs to the employee medical record in (h)(1)(iv).
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), (ii) and (iii), Sharps injury log
preguntas.subtema: Who keeps the sharps log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11

preguntas.pregunta: According to the standard, where may staff food and drink NOT be kept?
opciones: In refrigerators, cabinets or on benchtops where blood or OPIM is present
In any refrigerator inside the laboratory building, labeled or not
In a break-room refrigerator that lacks a fluorescent orange biohazard label
In any refrigerator that is not inspected and decontaminated on a set schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(x) forbids keeping food and drink in refrigerators, freezers, shelves, cabinets or on countertops and benchtops where blood or other potentially infectious materials are present. The test is the presence of blood or OPIM in that storage space, not the building or the label. Labels under (g)(1)(i)(A) go on refrigerators that contain blood, which is the reverse of the situation; a break-room refrigerator with no specimens needs no label and may hold lunches.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Food storage near specimens · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: The dressing on a bleeding wound soaks through. What does first-aid guidance say to do?
opciones: Do not remove it; place another cloth on top and keep pressing
Remove it, rinse the wound with water, and apply a clean one
Remove it to inspect the wound, then apply a tighter bandage
Loosen the pressure so the clot is not disturbed, then re-dress
preguntas.explicacion: When blood seeps through the material held on a wound, the dressing is not removed; another cloth is placed over the first and pressure continues, and medical attention is sought right away. The guidance is equally clear on what not to do: do not peek to see whether bleeding has stopped, do not remove a dressing that has become soaked, do not probe the wound, and do not try to clean a large wound or one whose bleeding has just been brought under control. The less the wound is disturbed, the better the chance of controlling the bleeding.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, First Aid and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: Soaked dressings · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10

preguntas.pregunta: For an adult fingerstick glucose, which puncture site does the procedure recommend, and which fingers are avoided?
opciones: The side of the fingertip of the 2nd, 3rd or 4th finger; the thumb, index and little finger are avoided
The center of the fingertip pad of the index finger, because it has the thickest tissue over the bone
The side of the fingertip of the little finger, because it is the least sensitive and heals the fastest
The center of the thumb pad, because its larger surface yields the biggest drop with the least squeezing
preguntas.explicacion: The lateral aspect of the distal fingertip of the second, third or fourth finger gives enough tissue depth to protect the bone. The fifth finger is avoided because its tissue may be too shallow, and the thumb and index finger because they are more sensitive. Lancet depth is set to no more than 2.0 mm, and alternate sites such as forearm or palm are used only if the device's instructions approve them.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Fingerstick site · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19

preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen for culture will not be processed for another hour. Where should it be kept?
opciones: At room temperature or in a carbon dioxide incubator, never in the refrigerator
In the refrigerator at 4 degrees, the same as a urine specimen that is held for culture
On ice at the bedside, so the cell count is not altered before it is read
In a freezer at −70 degrees, the way a viral culture specimen is transported
preguntas.explicacion: Cold kills the very organisms the culture is looking for: Neisseria meningitidis and Haemophilus influenzae lose viability at low temperature, so cerebrospinal fluid for microbiology is held at room temperature or in a carbon dioxide incubator until it is examined. Refrigeration is the rule for urine, and freezing at −70 degrees Celsius is how viral culture specimens travel.

preguntas.pregunta: Which question in the WHO Annex C script asks for the patient's consent?
opciones: 'Are you willing to be tested?'
'Have you ever had blood taken before?'
'How are you feeling at the moment?'
'Did you understand what I explained?'
preguntas.explicacion: After describing the needle, the tests and where results go, the script asks three things in a row: whether the patient has questions, whether they understood, and whether they are willing to be tested. The last is the consent question. The questions about earlier draws and current feelings belong to the second part of the script, the pre-draw interview.

preguntas.pregunta: What harm from unnecessary or excessive testing is named as falling directly on the patient's arm?
opciones: Repeated phlebotomies that cause phlebitis, pain or bruising
Repeated phlebotomies that cause haemolysis in every tube
Repeated phlebotomies that void the earlier results on file
Repeated phlebotomies that trigger a specimen rejection notice
preguntas.explicacion: Testing without clear clinical justification carries risk: unnecessary or excessive testing may lead to repeated phlebotomies that cause phlebitis, pain or bruising, and may delay essential diagnostic procedures. It also wastes patient and laboratory time, raises costs, and breeds confusion or anxiety through false-positive results.

preguntas.pregunta: When is the Lemmens-Bernstein-Brodsky equation preferred over the Nadler equation?
opciones: At higher body weights and body mass indices, in patients who are not critically ill
At lower body weights and body mass indices, in patients who are critically ill
In children under 12, whose height cannot be entered into the other formula
In pregnancy, when blood volume rises by roughly half above the baseline
preguntas.explicacion: The Lemmens-Bernstein-Brodsky equation is more accurate for higher ranges of body weight and body mass index in patients without critical illness; it takes weight and BMI rather than height. Pregnancy is a separate matter: a woman's blood volume climbs by roughly 50% during it, and women carry a lower volume than men to begin with.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Blood Volume", section Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a stool sample for culture asks whether it matters if urine or toilet water gets into it. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: urine, toilet water and toilet tissue must all be kept out of the sample
Only urine matters; toilet water is acceptable because the sample is cultured anyway
Only toilet tissue matters, because paper fibers block the culture medium
It matters only for occult blood cards, not for a culture or a parasite exam
preguntas.explicacion: Stool for culture or for parasites must not be mixed with urine, water or toilet tissue. The patient can catch it on plastic wrap laid loosely over the bowl and held by the seat, in a container that fits on the toilet, or with the special tissue in a kit, then transfer it to the clean container provided and return it as soon as possible. The occult blood card has the same rule about urine.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a newborn's bilirubin specimen collected in an amber tube and kept covered?
opciones: Bilirubin isomerizes and oxidizes in visible light, so measured values fall the longer serum is lit
Bilirubin is unstable at room temperature, and amber glass keeps the specimen cooler
Bilirubin binds to clear plastic, and amber tubes are coated to prevent that loss
Bilirubin oxidizes with dissolved oxygen, and amber tubes are filled under nitrogen
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin absorbs visible light and undergoes isomerization and oxidation in serum exposed to it, lowering measured values, and that protection from light is a recognized need in neonatal bilirubin assessment, where amber rather than clear tubes are commonly used. Purging with nitrogen did not change the photolysis rate, and specimens in the dark at room temperature kept their total bilirubin.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is deciding who may draw blood on its premises. Which staff are named as able to perform phlebotomy?
opciones: A physician, a nurse, a laboratory technician or a certified phlebotomist
A certified phlebotomist only, in every health-care setting without exception
A physician or a nurse only, since the others may not handle sharps at all
A laboratory technician or a physician only, and never a nurse on a ward
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure may be carried out by a physician, a nurse, a laboratory technician or a certified phlebotomist. For complex cases where venous access is difficult, the advice is to bring in a certified phlebotomist, and supervision plus structured training is expected of everyone who draws blood.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Personnel and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes

preguntas.pregunta: A parent will hold a 3-year-old on their lap for a finger-prick. How should the parent hold the child?
opciones: Legs crossed around the child's legs, one arm across the chest tucking the free arm, the other hand grasping the elbow and wrist palm down
Child facing the parent chest to chest, arms wrapped around the child's back, with the puncture hand held out by the phlebotomist alone
Child lying face up across the parent's knees, the parent holding both wrists above the head so neither hand can move
Child seated beside the parent, the parent holding only the puncture hand while the phlebotomist steadies the shoulders
preguntas.explicacion: A child is immobilized for a finger-prick by asking the parent to sit in the phlebotomy chair with the child on their lap, cross their legs around the child's legs, extend an arm across the child's chest and tuck the free arm under their own, grasp the elbow of the puncture arm, and use the other arm to hold the wrist palm down. A helper is essential for safety and success.

preguntas.pregunta: Which urine dipstick finding appears in the list of qualitative results that must be reported to the treating physician immediately?
opciones: A strongly positive reaction for both glucose and ketones (acetone)
A trace of protein in a concentrated first morning urine specimen
A pH of 8 in a specimen that stood at room temperature for several hours
A positive nitrite together with a positive leukocyte esterase reaction
preguntas.explicacion: Among qualitative laboratory results listed for immediate notification is a strongly positive test-strip reaction for glucose and acetone in urine; red cell casts, more than 50 % dysmorphic erythrocytes and severe hemoglobinuria without erythrocytes on microscopy are listed as well. Trace protein, an alkaline pH in a stale specimen, and the nitrite plus leukocyte esterase pattern of a urinary infection are abnormal findings but are not on the critical list.

preguntas.pregunta: A Spanish-speaking patient arrives; the phlebotomist took two years of high-school Spanish. What is the correct course?
opciones: Use a qualified interpreter; do not get by with basic or intermediate language skills
Proceed in Spanish, because the instructions for a blood draw are simple enough
Ask the patient's adult son, waiting outside, to interpret the pre-draw questions
Use a bilingual coworker who has never been assessed as a healthcare interpreter
preguntas.explicacion: Unacceptable language access services are: staff who are not sufficiently proficient in both languages, staff not trained or certified as healthcare interpreters, and the patient's family and friends unless they are qualified interpreters. Acceptable options are confirmed bilingual clinicians and qualified interpreters on site, by telephone or by video.

preguntas.pregunta: The HIPAA Security Rule requires which three categories of safeguards for electronic PHI?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Clinical, financial and operational
Encryption, passwords and firewalls
Privacy, transactions and enforcement rules
preguntas.explicacion: While the Privacy Rule covers all PHI, the Security Rule is specific to electronic PHI and organizes protection into administrative safeguards, such as written procedures, a designated official, access authorization, training, backups and audits; physical safeguards, such as controlling access to hardware, keeping monitors out of public view and training contractors; and technical safeguards, such as access controls, protection of transmissions over open networks and integrity checks. Encryption, passwords and firewalls are tools within those categories, and privacy, transactions and enforcement are separate HIPAA rules.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Security Rule
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38

preguntas.pregunta: What does a CLIA certificate of registration allow a laboratory to do?
opciones: Moderate or high complexity testing until a CMS survey confirms compliance
Waived testing only, until the laboratory applies for accreditation
PPM procedures by a dentist, with no other testing permitted
Testing in a State exempt from CLIA, after the State licenses the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate of registration, or registration certificate, enables an entity to conduct moderate or high complexity testing, or both, until CMS or its agent determines through a survey that it complies, or until it is accredited by an approved organization. Waived testing needs only a certificate of waiver, PPM procedures have their own certificate, and a CLIA-exempt laboratory is one licensed by a State whose requirements CMS has found equal to or stricter than CLIA, which removes it from the federal certificate system altogether.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (4) Certificate of registration; CLIA-exempt laboratory

preguntas.pregunta: After discovering a breach of unsecured protected health information, how quickly must a covered entity notify the affected individuals?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted
By the end of the calendar year, regardless of the number of individuals
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.404 requires notice to each individual whose unsecured PHI was, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed, acquired, used or disclosed, without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after the breach is discovered; a breach counts as discovered on the first day it is known, or should have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member other than the person who caused it. Written notice goes by first-class mail or, if agreed, e-mail; when contact details are missing for 10 or more people, a substitute web posting or media notice runs for 90 days.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(a), (b) and (d), Notification to individuals

preguntas.pregunta: A capillary collection on an infant is finished. What is done at the puncture site?
opciones: Apply firm pressure until the bleeding stops, and watch the site afterwards
Apply an adhesive strip at once, since infants bleed longer than adults
Leave it uncovered and unpressed so that a clot forms without disturbance
Massage the site gently to disperse any haematoma that has started to form
preguntas.explicacion: When the collection is complete, firm pressure is applied to the site to stop the bleeding. One listed complication is skin breakdown from repeated use of adhesive strips, particularly in very young or very elderly patients, and this can be avoided if sufficient pressure is applied and the puncture site is observed after the procedure. Massaging is discouraged because it causes haemolysis.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: A neonatal unit's hemolysis rate is near 40 %. Which combination of measures cut the rate to under 30 % in the quality project cited?
opciones: Heel warmers for consistent warming before the draw, education in correct collection technique, and monitoring with feedback to collectors
Switching every newborn draw from heel stick to venipuncture, and sending all tubes by hand rather than through the pneumatic tube
Adding an automated hemolysis index to the analyzer, and reporting all results regardless of the index with a cautionary comment
Replacing microtubes with full-size evacuated tubes, so that the fill volume meets the required blood-to-anticoagulant ratio
preguntas.explicacion: At one academic medical center the neonatal unit's hemolysis rate was near or above 40 % in 2012 and fell to 28.6 % within a few months after changes that included heel warmers, to get more consistent warming before drawing, and increased education in correct blood withdrawal technique; the authors stress that monitoring and feedback to the collecting personnel keep the improvement. In the newborn series most hemolysis was in vitro, produced by the difficult collection itself.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A pathologist proposes to start managing demand by tackling repeat requests before touching anything else. What supports beginning there?
opciones: As many as half of all requests may be inappropriate, and duplicates are the easiest to cut
Duplicate requests are the single largest source of hemolysed and clotted specimens
Repeat requests are the only preanalytical problem the laboratory can measure directly
Accreditation requires the repeat interval for each test to be fixed by the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: Requests repeated inside a defined interval represent wasted testing, and they often arise simply from poor access to earlier results or from a lack of standardisation between laboratories. With the suggestion that up to half of requests may be inappropriate, managing duplicates is described as a useful first step that does not challenge the clinician's autonomy in deciding.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the 'mature minor' doctrine is correct?
opciones: Recognized in very few states, usually for minors 12 or older who show adequate capacity
Recognized in every state for minors 16 or older who still live with their parents
It applies automatically to any minor who is married or serving in the military
It applies to any unaccompanied minor screened in an emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: The doctrine is recognized by very few states and applies usually to minors 12 years or older who demonstrate the maturity to grasp risks, benefits, alternatives and likely outcomes, and often restricted by age, parental availability and the clinical situation. Marriage and military service are grounds for emancipation, and emergency screening falls under EMTALA.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the WHO device table state that auto-disable (AD) syringes are NOT recommended for drawing blood?
opciones: Their mechanism can trigger during probing, forcing a new puncture, and they do not prevent needle-sticks
Their sleeve cannot cover the needle while the syringe is full of blood or during transfer
The air in their tubing means the first tube has to be drawn without additive or discarded
Their needle-locking mechanism requires additional training and has a high cost
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists auto-disable syringes under passive devices with the note that they are designed to prevent reuse, not needle-sticks: during probing the safety mechanism can activate and require a new venepuncture, blood transfer is still needed, air in the syringe can affect results, and they offer no needle-stick protection. The sleeve limitation belongs to self re-sheathing devices, and the air in the tubing to winged needles.

preguntas.pregunta: A service cannot afford to throw away tube holders and must reuse them. How is the used needle taken off?
opciones: With a one-hand scoop, or a sharps container that has a removal hold
With both hands, holding the holder still while the needle unscrews
By pressing the holder against the bench until the needle drops free
By recapping the needle two-handed and then unscrewing the holder
preguntas.explicacion: Where possible the barrel and the needle are discarded together as one item. If the barrel really has to be reused, the sharp end is covered with a one-hand scoop before it is removed, or a sharps container with a needle removal hold is used, again with one hand only.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the rubber septum of a blood culture bottle be prepared before it is inoculated?
opciones: Disinfect it with 70% isopropyl alcohol and do not touch it afterwards
Scrub it with 2% chlorhexidine gluconate, as for a donor's arm
Paint it with povidone-iodine and let it dry for two minutes
Remove only the flip cap, because the septum beneath it is supplied sterile
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's model procedure disinfects the rubber septum of each bottle, or of the evacuated tubes used for the culture, with 70% isopropyl alcohol, and disinfecting bottle tops before inoculation is described as standard blood culture practice. The chlorhexidine-alcohol scrub is what donor arms receive, and povidone-iodine is one of the agents listed for central-line hubs; neither is the step for the bottle.

preguntas.pregunta: Which target levels correspond to gentamicin?
opciones: Peak 5 to 10 mcg/mL and trough 0.5 to 2 mcg/mL
Peak 20 to 25 mcg/mL and trough 5 to 10 mcg/mL
Peak 10 to 20 mcg/mL and trough 4 to 12 mcg/mL
Peak 0.8 to 2.0 ng/mL and trough 0.2 to 1.0 ng/mL
preguntas.explicacion: Gentamicin is monitored with a peak of 5 to 10 mcg/mL and a trough of 0.5 to 2 mcg/mL. Tobramycin shares the same peak range with a trough of 0 to 2, while amikacin runs much higher, 20 to 25 at peak and 5 to 10 at trough. preguntas.pregunta: What is the minimum hemoglobin or hematocrit for a female allogeneic blood donor?
opciones: 12.5 g/dL of hemoglobin, or a hematocrit of 38 percent
13.0 g/dL of hemoglobin, or a hematocrit of 39 percent
11.0 g/dL of hemoglobin, or a hematocrit of 33 percent
12.0 g/dL of hemoglobin, or a hematocrit of 36 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Female allogeneic donors must reach 12.5 g/dL or a hematocrit of 38 percent. preguntas.pregunta: How does the capillary order of draw relate to the venipuncture order of draw?
opciones: It is the reverse of the venipuncture order
It is identical to the venipuncture order
It matches the venous order for two tubes only
It has no fixed order, as microtubes lack additives
preguntas.explicacion: The order used for skin punctures, haematology first and then chemistry and blood bank, is the reverse of the one used for venepuncture. The reason is platelet clumping. The sequence is defined by specimen type, not by the container. When more than two specimens are needed, venepuncture may provide more accurate results.

The light blue sodium citrate tube

preguntas.pregunta: For which part of a visit does the ADA guidance say an interpreter will generally be needed?
opciones: Taking the medical history of a patient who uses sign language
Pointing out where the waiting-room chairs and the toilets are

preguntas.pregunta: Before a fasting lipid panel the patient drank two bottles of lemon-flavored sparkling water. Does that keep the fast?
opciones: Not acceptable; only plain water is allowed, and flavored water may contain sweeteners
Acceptable; any water, still or sparkling, keeps the fast intact regardless of flavoring
Acceptable if the label shows zero calories, since only calories can break a fast
Acceptable, but only up to one bottle, since larger volumes dilute the sample
preguntas.explicacion: Plain water is allowed during a fast, with a specific warning against lemon-flavored or flavored carbonated water, which may contain sugars or artificial sweeteners. preguntas.pregunta: When is hand hygiene performed in relation to a single venous draw?
opciones: Before the gloves go on, and again once the procedure is over
Before the gloves go on, and not again until the next patient
Only after the gloves come off, since the gloves cover the hands
Only when the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath

preguntas.pregunta: What alcohol concentration does the CDC recommend for hand sanitizer used in healthcare settings?
opciones: At least 60 percent, and under the Life Safety Code no more than 95 percent
At least 70 percent, the concentration used to disinfect the skin before venipuncture
At least 50 percent, matching the 1:10 dilution used for blood spills
At least 95 percent, since lower concentrations do not kill spores
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based hand sanitizer for healthcare should contain at least 60 percent alcohol, and the Life Safety Code provisions it cites cap the content at 95 percent by volume for fire safety, with limits on dispenser size and distance from ignition sources. Seventy percent alcohol is WHO's skin preparation before drawing blood, a different use. The 1:10 dilution is WHO's bleach mixture for spills, and no alcohol concentration kills spores, which is why C. difficile care calls for soap and water.

preguntas.pregunta: What should every patient who undergoes phlebotomy receive, according to the WHO's marker of quality of care called patient cooperation?
opciones: Clear information about the procedure, either written or verbal
A signed written consent form filed in the medical record
A copy of the laboratory results within 24 hours of the draw
A printed list of the tube colours and additives used
preguntas.explicacion: Patient involvement and cooperation are treated as an essential marker of quality in phlebotomy, and clear information, written or verbal, is to be available to each patient, with a sample explanation text provided in the annexes. Consent for a routine draw is verbal, results go back to the ordering clinician, and tube details belong to the laboratory, not to patient information.

preguntas.pregunta: The first blood culture set has just been drawn from the left antecubital fossa. Where should the second set come from?
opciones: A separate venipuncture, preferably the right antecubital fossa
The same venipuncture, by attaching a second pair of bottles
The patient's existing peripheral IV catheter, to avoid a second stick
A central line, since catheter draws are less often contaminated
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's 2025 procedure repeats the whole sequence for the second set and specifies a separate venipuncture site, with the upper extremity preferred and the right and left antecubital fossae used when possible. Peripheral venipuncture has consistently shown lower contamination than draws through existing central venous catheters, so catheter draws are reserved for suspected catheter-associated infection, when both a peripheral and a catheter set are taken.

Light blue citrate, light grey fluoride, purple EDTA

preguntas.pregunta: Which structures does the bicipital aponeurosis partly cover in the roof of the cubital fossa?
opciones: The median nerve, the brachial artery and the ulnar artery
The median cubital vein, the cephalic vein and the radial nerve
The basilic vein, the ulnar nerve and the biceps tendon itself
The brachial artery only, the veins running above the sheet of tendon
preguntas.explicacion: The roof of the fossa is skin and fascia reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, a tendon-like sheet off the biceps that forms a partial covering over the median nerve, the brachial artery and the ulnar artery. preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders blood gases. Which type of sample is used, and in what units is the PO2 reported?
opciones: Blood from an arterial stick; the PO2 is recorded in mm Hg
A venous sample from the median cubital vein; the PO2 in percent
A capillary sample from the heel; the oxygen recorded in mm Hg
A pulse oximeter reading from the fingertip; saturation in mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: An arterial stick is used to analyze blood gases, and oxygen measured directly as free oxygen in plasma after an arterial stick is expressed as the partial pressure of oxygen, PO2, in millimeters of mercury. The pulse oximeter is a different measure: it reports percent saturation of hemoglobin, normally 95 to 100 percent, from light passed through a fingertip.

preguntas.pregunta: A respiratory specimen in viral transport medium will not ship to the public health laboratory for five days. How should it be stored?
opciones: Frozen at −70 degrees Celsius, because the delay runs past 3 to 4 days
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius, the same as for a same-day shipment
Frozen at −20 degrees Celsius, because the delay runs past 3 to 4 days
At room temperature, the way cerebrospinal fluid for culture is held
preguntas.explicacion: Specimens go into viral transport medium and straight onto refrigerant gel packs or into a refrigerator at 4 degrees Celsius, and they are kept at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius until shipment. Once the delay will exceed 3 to 4 days the specimen is frozen at −70 degrees Celsius instead. Room temperature is the rule for cerebrospinal fluid and other body fluids going for culture.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Storing and Shipping

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist attaches a 10 mL syringe to a butterfly for a 2-year-old. What is the rule on syringe size in children?
opciones: Use a 1 to 5 mL syringe; the vacuum from drawing with a larger syringe often collapses the vein
Use a 10 to 20 mL syringe; a small syringe cannot generate enough vacuum to fill through a butterfly
Use any size, since the syringe barrel does not affect the vein; only needle gauge matters
Use a 1 to 5 mL auto-disable syringe, which the WHO recommends for all paediatric draws
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe should have a barrel volume of 1 to 5 mL depending on collection needs, because the vacuum produced by drawing with a larger syringe will often collapse the vein. If an evacuated tube is used instead, it should be a small-volume tube, 1 mL or 5 mL, with low vacuum. Auto-disable syringes are for injection and are not appropriate for phlebotomy.

preguntas.pregunta: Rejections keep repeating in one ward, and the laboratory director asks what CLIA expects beyond simply counting them. What does the preanalytic quality assessment standard require?
opciones: Reviewing whether corrective actions worked, revising procedures and telling staff
Reporting the recurring problem to the accrediting organisation each quarter
Suspending testing for that ward until its collection practice is re-approved
Repeating the proficiency testing challenge for every affected specialty
preguntas.explicacion: The standard asks for written policies and an ongoing mechanism to monitor, assess and, where needed, correct problems in the test request and specimen handling systems. That assessment has to include a review of how effective the corrective actions were, revision of the policies so the problem does not come back, and discussion of the reviews with the relevant staff, all documented.

preguntas.pregunta: Which comfort measures during the newborn heel stick reduce the baby's distress?
opciones: Skin-to-skin holding or breastfeeding, swaddling, or a pacifier dipped in sugar water
Dimming the lights and playing recorded heartbeat sounds through headphones
A topical anesthetic cream applied to the heel 2 to 6 hours before the puncture, under occlusion
Warming the whole body under a radiant heater until the baby falls asleep
preguntas.explicacion: Babies whose mothers hold them skin to skin or breastfeed them during the heel prick show less distress, and that wrapping the baby tightly in a blanket or offering a pacifier dipped in sugar water may also ease pain and calm the baby. preguntas.pregunta: In the classic stat-laboratory series of preanalytical errors, which problem dominated the hematology samples?
opciones: Clotted samples
Hemolysed samples
Lost samples
Wrong tube samples
preguntas.explicacion: The most commonly reported preanalytical error types in that stat laboratory were hemolysed samples (46.4 % in biochemistry), clotted samples (43.2 % in hematology), lost samples (6.4 %), inadequate sample-to-anticoagulant ratio (2.9 %), patient misidentification (0.7 %), wrong collection tube (0.3 %) and missing test requests (0.1 %). preguntas.pregunta: Which infections does the CDC give as examples requiring Airborne Precautions?
opciones: Tuberculosis, measles, chickenpox and disseminated herpes zoster
Influenza, pertussis and mumps, which travel in respiratory droplets
Clostridioides difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, the bloodborne pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: Tuberculosis, measles, chickenpox and disseminated herpes zoster are the infections spread by the airborne route, and smallpox joins them among those for which susceptible staff should be kept out of the room. StatPearls places influenza, pertussis and mumps under Droplet Precautions and C. difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms under Contact Precautions. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV are bloodborne and are covered by Standard Precautions and the OSHA standard rather than by isolation categories.

preguntas.pregunta: Which requirement applies to exit routes under OSHA's Subpart E?
opciones: Exit doors must be unlocked and routes kept free and unobstructed at all times
Exit doors may be locked during night shifts if a key is kept at the desk
Exit routes may be used for temporary storage if a path 3 feet wide remains
Exit routes must be marked but need not be lighted when the building is closed
preguntas.explicacion: The exit route rules of 29 CFR 1910.34 through 1910.37 require an adequate number of routes of sufficient capacity, discharging directly outside or to a safe open space large enough for the occupants, adequately lighted and marked, with an operable employee alarm system, exit doors unlocked, and routes free and unobstructed at all times. Compliance with the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code or the International Fire Code exit provisions is deemed to satisfy those sections. Locking, storage and unlit exits all violate the rules.

preguntas.pregunta: Which health information falls outside the requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
opciones: De-identified information, with no code that would allow re-identification disclosed
Health information about a patient who died more than 6 years before the request
Health information kept only on paper charts and never transmitted electronically anywhere
Health information spoken aloud rather than written or stored
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(d) says information that meets the de-identification standard of 164.514 is not individually identifiable and the Privacy Rule does not apply to it, with two provisos: disclosing a code or other means of re-identification is itself a disclosure of PHI, and re-identified information is PHI again. Paper and spoken information remain protected, which is why elevator conversations and unattended charts are violations, and a deceased person's information stays protected for 50 years after death.

preguntas.pregunta: Which change to the intake forms is recommended so a practice welcomes patients from the LGBTQ community?
opciones: Add the term partner beside spouse, and include transgender as an option
Add a field for the sex assigned at birth and leave the rest unchanged
Add a note asking staff to record the patient's appearance and manner
Add a required field naming the patient's next of kin and their gender
preguntas.explicacion: Among the steps for a welcoming practice: train staff to refer to patients by their name and chosen descriptive pronouns, and on intake forms include the term partner in addition to spouse, and include transgender as an option. Forgetting gender-neutral terms such as partner is listed as a challenge, as is making assumptions about behaviour from appearance.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is scheduled for a catheterized urine culture and says he has no urge to urinate. What preparation applies?
opciones: He should not have urinated for at least 1 hour, and may be told to drink a glass of water 15 to 20 minutes before
He should not have urinated for at least 2 to 3 hours, and may be told to drink a glass of water 1 hour before
He should empty his bladder completely just before the procedure so the catheter drains only fresh urine
He should fast for 6 hours and avoid caffeine and smoking, as required before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: The only preparation for a catheterized specimen is not to urinate for at least an hour beforehand; a patient without the urge to void may be asked to drink a glass of water 15 to 20 minutes before the procedure. The 2-to-3-hour bladder dwell is the ideal for a voided clean-catch, emptying the bladder first would leave nothing to collect, and fasting with no caffeine or smoking belongs to breath and metanephrine testing.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, when must a mask with eye protection or a face shield be worn?
opciones: When blood may splash or spray and contamination of the eyes, nose or mouth can be anticipated
Whenever gloves are worn, since hand contact with blood implies facial exposure
Whenever gross contamination is anticipated, as with autopsies or orthopaedic surgery
Whenever the patient is on Droplet Precautions, but not for routine venipuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(x) ties facial protection to the task: masks combined with goggles, glasses with solid side shields, or chin-length face shields are worn whenever splashes, spray, spatter or droplets of blood or OPIM may be generated and contamination of the eyes, nose or mouth can reasonably be anticipated. Gloves have their own trigger in (d)(3)(ix). Gross contamination, as in autopsies, is the trigger for caps, hoods and shoe covers in (d)(3)(xii). Droplet Precautions are a CDC isolation category, not the test this OSHA paragraph applies.

preguntas.pregunta: A nursery nurse asks why the laboratory keeps a separate list of critical limits for newborns. What is the reason?
opciones: Neonatal limits differ from adult ones for several analytes; a published list gives a lower glucose threshold and higher haemoglobin thresholds for newborns
Neonatal limits are the adult limits halved, since newborn blood volume is smaller and the same absolute change carries more weight
Neonatal specimens are capillary, and capillary blood has no critical limits because its values are not comparable with venous ones
Neonatal limits are the same as adult limits; the separate list exists only because newborn results are reported to the mother's chart
preguntas.explicacion: Published critical-limit tables carry a separate neonatal section: in the 2003 list, glucose becomes critical below 30 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L) in a newborn against 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) in adults, haemoglobin below 8.5 or above 23 g/dL against 6.6 and 19.9 g/dL, and entries such as cord blood IgM above 20 mg/dL exist only for neonates. Those figures come from one author's list, so the working numbers are the ones each laboratory agrees with its clinicians.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), Table 1 and Table 3

preguntas.pregunta: What is syncope?
opciones: A transient loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery, from reduced cerebral perfusion
A brief seizure with loss of sphincter control and confusion on waking, from an acute neurologic event
A feeling that one is about to pass out without actually losing consciousness, caused by cerebral hypoperfusion
A prolonged loss of consciousness lasting several minutes, from a fall in blood glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is a transient loss of consciousness and postural tone followed by spontaneous recovery, resulting from decreased cerebral perfusion. The feeling of being about to pass out without doing so is what the chapter calls near syncope or presyncope, and an episode lasting more than a few minutes is not syncope but more likely a seizure. Hypoglycemia is listed among conditions that mimic fainting.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", sections Continuing Education Activity and Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of donors was fainting most often reported in?
opciones: Female donors giving for the first time
Male donors over fifty giving again
Male donors under thirty giving again
Female donors over sixty giving again
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting was reported in 5.3 per cent of cases and usually happened in first-time female blood donors, while vasovagal attacks occurred occasionally and ranged from mild to severe. It is a reminder to ask about earlier faints and to have the chair ready for a reaction.

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of natural rubber latex is linked to the type IV hypersensitivity reaction?
opciones: The chemical antioxidants added during processing
The natural rubber proteins bound by IgE antibodies
The cornstarch powder that carries particles in the air
The fruit proteins that cross-react with banana and kiwi
preguntas.explicacion: The natural proteins in rubber are associated with asymptomatic sensitisation and with type I IgE-mediated hypersensitivity. What can produce type IV reactions is the chemical antioxidants added while the latex is processed. Cornstarch in gloves and tyre dust are the usual sources of inhaled particles, and cross-reacting foods are a separate risk marker.

preguntas.pregunta: Which circumstances raise the chance that a needlestick from an HIV-positive patient transmits the virus?
opciones: A visibly bloody device, a needle that was in a vein or artery, and a deep injury
A solid needle, a superficial scratch, and contact limited to intact skin
A small-bore needle, a source on treatment, and a splash onto the forearm
A used lancet, a gloved hand, and a source patient with a low viral load
preguntas.explicacion: The average risk after a percutaneous injury with HIV-infected blood is about 0.3 percent, but it is not the same for every injury. A case-control study found the risk higher when the worker met a larger quantity of blood, which showed up as a visibly bloody device, a procedure that put the needle in a vein or an artery, or a deep injury. Large-bore hollow needles and a source with a high viral load point the same way; intact skin carries no meaningful risk at all.

preguntas.pregunta: After installing a longer, faster pneumatic tube route, a laboratory sees more hemolysed samples. Which change in how tubes are sent is supported by the literature as reducing transport hemolysis?
opciones: Using padded inserts inside the carriers, gel tubes and properly filled tubes
Sending tubes uncapped so that pressure changes do not build up inside them
Sending each tube in its own carrier at the highest speed to shorten travel time
Chilling the carriers before use so that the red cells are less fragile in transit
preguntas.explicacion: Variables shown to increase hemolysis during transport are rapid accelerations and decelerations, greater length of travel and high speeds; variables shown to reduce it are gel tubes, properly filled tubes and padded inserts within the canisters. Higher speed works in the wrong direction, and neither uncapping nor chilling appears in the evidence the study cites.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's right to refuse care is founded on which ethical principle?
opciones: Autonomy, the right to make informed decisions about one's own care
Beneficence, which asks that actions be taken for the patient's benefit
Non-maleficence, which requires steps be taken so no one is harmed
Justice, which spreads benefits and risks evenly and without bias
preguntas.explicacion: Refusal of care rests on autonomy: every person may make informed decisions about their health care, and staff should not impose their own beliefs or decisions on the patient. Beneficence, non-maleficence and justice sit alongside autonomy and guide the same difficult situations, but the refusal itself is not founded on them.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations is a covered entity REQUIRED, rather than merely permitted, to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual who requests access or an accounting, and to HHS investigating compliance
To law enforcement on request, and to the patient's employer for workers' compensation
To any treating provider, and to the health plan paying the claim, on request
To public health authorities, and to a coroner or medical examiner determining cause of death
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(a)(2) names only two required disclosures: to the individual when requested under the right of access or the right to an accounting of disclosures, and to the Secretary of HHS when required to investigate or determine the entity's compliance. preguntas.pregunta: Which statement must appear prominently at the top of a notice of privacy practices?
opciones: A header stating how medical information may be used and disclosed and how to access it
The names of every business associate that may receive the patient's information during care
The civil penalty amounts for HIPAA violations, from $100 up to $50,000 per violation
A list of the 18 identifiers that turn health information into protected information
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be written in plain language and open with a prominently displayed header telling the reader that it describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking them to review it carefully. It then describes uses for treatment, payment and operations with examples, the other permitted purposes, the uses that require authorization, the individual's rights, the entity's duties, how to complain without retaliation, a contact person and the effective date. preguntas.pregunta: To open the pre-draw interview, which question follows the principle of open-ended questioning first?

'Have you ever fainted during a blood draw?'
'You're not scared of needles, are you?'
'Did you fast for twelve hours like the doctor said?'

preguntas.pregunta: A donor turns pale and sweaty and her blood pressure and pulse fall during collection. What is happening, and what helps?
opciones: Syncope: stop the donation, support her, and keep her reclined a few minutes
Syncope: finish the unit quickly, then sit her upright and offer fluids
A hematoma: release the needle, apply ice, and watch the site closely
Citrate toxicity: slow the return line and give oral calcium at once
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is the second most common adverse effect of donation, often vasovagal or related to low volume, and shows as a fall in systolic pressure and pulse with weakness, sweating, dizziness or pallor. The donation is paused or stopped and supportive measures begin; keeping the donor reclined a few minutes and moving her upright gradually lowers the risk. Hematoma is the most common effect, and citrate toxicity belongs to apheresis.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Donation", section Complications

preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is put in the specimen refrigerator to await pick-up. Why is that the wrong choice?
opciones: Whole blood for these assays is held at room temperature, not chilled
Whole blood for these assays is held frozen, and chilling is not enough
Refrigeration bursts the red cells and haemolyses the whole specimen
Refrigeration hardens the gel barrier and traps the plasma underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood drawn for clotting tests is kept at room temperature, roughly eighteen to twenty-four degrees, and refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII. Chilling whole blood also lowers factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, which can imitate a bleeding disorder.

Disclosure: the risks of the procedure were never fully listed
Capacity: the patient's understanding was never assessed
Documentation: the consent form was never signed
preguntas.explicacion: Valid consent requires a patient competent to make a voluntary decision, and clinicians must avoid creating any sense of coercion toward their recommendation; the research-consent list names the voluntary nature of the decision as one of three elements. preguntas.pregunta: Why is EMLA cream a special concern in a 6-week-old infant?
opciones: Prilocaine can cause methemoglobinemia, especially in neonates and infants under 3 months
Lidocaine cannot cross the thick neonatal stratum corneum, so the cream has no effect
The occlusive dressing causes hypothermia in infants under 3 months
Neonatal skin absorbs the cream so fast that it peaks within 15 to 30 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Prilocaine, alone or as EMLA cream, can cause methemoglobinemia, especially in neonates and infants younger than 3 months, and that the risk rises with drugs such as acetaminophen, dapsone, phenytoin and phenobarbital. Section 6, which also covers containment and cleanup after a spill
Section 9, which also gives the flash point and the boiling range
Section 7, which also covers safe storage and incompatible products
preguntas.explicacion: Section 5 is written for the fire: which extinguishing equipment is suitable and which is not appropriate for a given situation, the specific hazards the chemical develops while burning, such as hazardous combustion products, and any special protection or precautions for the people fighting it. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck at the end of her shift and says she will go to occupational health tomorrow. What is the recommendation?

Be seen within seven days, the deadline that applies to hepatitis B treatment
Be seen at the end of the shift, once the incident report has been written
Be seen within ninety days, while the baseline sample is being preserved
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up with occupational health should be immediate rather than delayed by twelve to seventy-two hours, because the decisions that depend on it are time-sensitive: baseline testing, hepatitis B immune globulin within about a day, and antiretroviral prophylaxis started preferably within hours. preguntas.pregunta: A patient faints in a crowded corridor where there is no room to lie down. What is the alternative position?

Seated upright, with the chin lifted and eyes closed
Standing, leaning back against the corridor wall
Seated backwards, with both legs stretched out flat

preguntas.pregunta: Which test is called the gold standard for diagnosing a type I hypersensitivity to latex?
opciones: The skin prick test, though it is not available in the United States
The serum assay for bound IgE, which rarely gives a false positive
A trial of exposure to latex, run as the first step by an allergist
The blood test for latex antibodies, which is the in-vivo assay
preguntas.explicacion: Skin prick testing, an in-vivo assay that applies a non-ammoniated latex extract and watches for a wheal, is considered the gold standard for type I hypersensitivity to latex, yet it is not available in the United States for want of an approved reagent. preguntas.pregunta: A differential on a patient with a bacterial infection shows 80 percent of one leukocyte type. Which type is normally the most common and rises with bacterial infection?
opciones: Neutrophils, normally 50 to 70 percent of leukocytes
Lymphocytes, normally 20 to 30 percent of leukocytes
Monocytes, normally 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
Eosinophils, normally 2 to 4 percent of leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Neutrophils are the most common leukocyte at 50 to 70 percent of the count; they respond fast to infection, prefer bacteria, and high counts point to bacterial infection or inflammation, as well as burns and stress. Lymphocytes are second at 20 to 30 percent and rise with viral infections; monocytes are 2 to 8 percent and eosinophils 2 to 4 percent, rising with allergies and parasitic worms.

Repeat testing is capped at three panels for any single admitted patient
Repeat panels are drawn only when the earlier tubes were rejected as unfit
Repeat panels cost little, since testing is under 5% of health spending
preguntas.explicacion: A test should be relevant to the diagnostic hypothesis; timing and necessity ask whether a change in the patient's condition justifies performing or repeating it, with repeats reserved for situations likely to yield new or useful information. Weekly, since the logger records continuously and alarms on excursions
Only when the alarm sounds or a control result falls out of range
Monthly, when the QC records are reviewed for shifts and trends
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigerator, freezer and storage-room temperatures are checked and recorded daily, and the testing room's temperature before the room is used, regardless of whether the unit has an alarm, a chart recorder, a data logger or a continuous monitoring system. preguntas.pregunta: Twenty minutes after drinking the glucose solution, a pregnant patient says she feels nauseated, sweaty and lightheaded. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Reassure her: those reactions are known, and serious effects are very uncommon
Stop the test and report it to the provider as a failed glucose screen
Offer her a light snack to settle her stomach before the next blood draw
Have her drink the glucose solution again, since some may not have stayed down
preguntas.explicacion: Most patients have no side effects from the glucose tolerance test, but some feel nauseated, sweaty or lightheaded after the solution, and serious side effects are very uncommon. The patient stays seated through the test. Eating is not allowed while the test runs, and there is no second drink; only vomiting that prevents the load from staying down is a reason to talk to the provider.

preguntas.pregunta: What may the healthcare professional's written opinion after an exposure incident contain?

The source individual's test results and the diagnosis, so that the employer can plan work restrictions
All findings and diagnoses from the evaluation, so the employer can complete the sharps injury log
The dates of hepatitis B vaccination and the employee's serologic status for the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5)(ii) limits the post-exposure opinion to two statements: that the employee has been informed of the evaluation results, and that the employee has been told about any conditions from the exposure that need further evaluation or treatment. Paragraph (f)(5)(iii) adds that every other finding or diagnosis stays confidential and is left out of the report. preguntas.pregunta: A patient on daily low-dose aspirin keeps bleeding at the puncture site longer than expected. What does aspirin do to hemostasis?
opciones: It is an antiplatelet; it inhibits the aggregation of platelets
It is a thrombolytic; it converts plasminogen into plasmin
It inactivates factor X, in the same way antithrombin does
It blocks vitamin K, so the liver makes fewer clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Aspirin is an antiplatelet drug that is very effective at inhibiting platelet aggregation, which is why it is given during heart attacks and strokes and sometimes daily at low dose to people at cardiovascular risk. preguntas.pregunta: For a blood cortisol test, when are the samples usually drawn?
opciones: Once in the morning and again around 4 p.m. on the same day
Once at midnight, when cortisol is normally at its peak
Once in the morning only, after a strict 12-hour overnight fast
Every hour for 2 to 3 hours after a sugary glucose drink
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples are usually taken twice in one day: in the morning, when cortisol is normally highest, and again around 4 p.m., when it is normally much lower, which is why the patient needs two appointments. Use the cot number as the second identifier next to the form

preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old needs a finger-prick. Which puncture depth is recommended for that age?
opciones: 1.5 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
2.4 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
0.85 mm, the depth for any child who has not reached school age
2.2 mm, the longest lancet, because the finger has no bone risk
preguntas.explicacion: There are two finger-prick depths for children: 1.5 mm for a child over 6 months and below 8 years, and 2.4 mm for a child over 8 years. Change the lancet and wipe the platform with a dry gauze pad
Rinse the platform under running water at the end of the round
Keep it in a clean bag between patients, which avoids contact
