preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, requires the log to contain at least the type and brand of device involved, the department or work area where the exposure incident occurred, and an explanation of how it occurred, all recorded in a way that protects the injured employee's confidentiality. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the median cubital vein the most common choice for a blood draw?
opciones: Its thick walls tolerate the negative pressure of the draw
It is the only vein in the fossa that lacks an accompanying nerve
It is the preferred location for establishing an intravenous site
It is the most prominent vein without any tourniquet applied

preguntas.pregunta: The glucometer's liquid control reads outside the range printed on the bottle. Three patients are waiting. What should the operator do?

Test the patients now and note on each result that the control was out of range that morning
Repeat the control once; if it is still out, average the two readings and proceed if within range
Switch to a new bottle of control solution and report the patients if the second control passes
preguntas.explicacion: An unexpected control result, internal or external, stops patient reporting until the problem is found and fixed. preguntas.pregunta: The morning temperature log for the specimen refrigerator reads 10 °C (50 °F). Why does this reading call for action?
opciones: A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F), so 10 °C is above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 15 and 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), so 10 °C is below range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), so 10 °C is far above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 0 and 4 °C (32 to 39 °F), so 10 °C is above range
preguntas.explicacion: A refrigerator used to store patient samples is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F); the 15 to 30 °C band is room temperature for testing and storage, and −25 to −15 °C is the usual sample freezer. The acceptable range for any unit is fixed by the manufacturer's instructions for the reagents, kits, controls and samples inside it, and the temperature is checked and recorded daily even when the unit has an alarm or a data logger.

preguntas.pregunta: In what order does the CDC-recommended sequence put on personal protective equipment?
opciones: Gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection, then gloves
Gloves, then gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection
Mask or respirator, then gloves, then gown, then eye protection
Eye protection, then mask or respirator, then gown, then gloves
preguntas.explicacion: The donning order is gown first, covering neck to knees and wrapping the back; then the mask or respirator, with the nose band fitted and a fit check for respirators; then goggles or a face shield; and gloves last, pulled over the cuffs of the gown. Donning takes place outside the patient room. Gloves go on last so that they are the cleanest item when patient contact begins and so that they cover the gown cuffs.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the three legal approaches to adequate informed consent do many states apply?
opciones: The reasonable patient standard, built on what a typical patient needs to know
The reasonable clinician standard, built on what a typical clinician would say
The subjective standard, built on what this one patient needs to understand
The documentation standard, built on what the consent form has room to hold
preguntas.explicacion: The state decides the standard, and three approaches are recognised: subjective, reasonable patient and reasonable clinician. preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognised at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.

opciones: Agglutinogens
Agglutinins
Isoantibodies
Immunoglobulins
preguntas.explicacion: With red cells the antigens may be called isoantigens or agglutinogens, and the antibodies isoantibodies or agglutinins, though the plainer words antigen and antibody are more common. Immunoglobulin is another name for antibody. The agglutinogen is the marker on the cell; the agglutinin is the Y-shaped antibody that clumps cells carrying it.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for every interaction that may involve the patient or the patient's environment, donned on room entry and discarded before exit to contain the pathogen. A mask on entry is the Droplet Precautions rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne Precautions. Standard Precautions still apply underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough by themselves; the gown is added because the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient and surroundings.

preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?

preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: Tort cases are decided by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, or greater than 50 percent; the criminal standard of beyond a reasonable doubt does not apply, and depending on the state a verdict against a tortfeasor may not require the whole jury to agree. One is liable for a tort, not guilty of it. Damages themselves must be proved to a certainty rather than estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that requirement concerns the amount awarded, not the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.pregunta: How far into a fast are the liver's glycogen stores described as running out?
opciones: After about 24 hours
After about 8 hours
After about 12 hours
After about 72 hours

After roughly 24 hours the stores are depleted and the body turns to fat and protein. Eight and twelve hours are fasting windows asked of patients, not the glycogen limit.

preguntas.pregunta: Which protective device belongs on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles in a hospital, according to OSHA's recognized controls?
opciones: A ground-fault circuit interrupter, which shuts off power on a ground fault
A surge protector, which absorbs voltage spikes from the power line
A three-prong adapter, which grounds equipment lacking a ground prong
A step-down transformer, which lowers the voltage below 1,000 volts
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's Hospitals eTool recommends ground-fault circuit interrupters on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles. A GFCI is a fast-acting circuit breaker that cuts power the moment a ground fault occurs, so that current from a damaged cord or an energized metal enclosure does not flow through a worker's body and cause burns or electrocution. The standard also requires electrical service near water sources to be properly grounded under 29 CFR 1910.304(g)(6); adapters that bypass a missing ground prong are the kind of damaged connection the eTool warns against.

preguntas.pregunta: A molecular laboratory sees sporadic false-positive results in negative specimens. Which workflow controls does the review recommend against sample and amplicon contamination?
opciones: Separate pre- and post-amplification areas with one-way workflow, frequent glove changes and aerosol-barrier pipette tips
A single shared bench for extraction and amplification, so that every step is handled by the same pair of gloves
Reusing pipette tips within one patient's series of tubes, so that no foreign template can enter the reaction
Leaving opened sample tubes uncapped in the post-amplification area to let aerosols settle before analysis
preguntas.explicacion: Because amplification makes millions of copies from a few templates, a positive sample or its amplicons can contaminate a negative one at collection, processing or analysis. Guidelines therefore ask for separate pre- and post-amplification areas, ideally physically apart, a one-way workflow from pre to post, separate clean protective equipment for each area with frequent glove changes, dedicated equipment, aerosol-barrier tips and pipetting technique that limits aerosols, plus routine cleaning with 10 to 15 % bleach and wipe-tests of the environment.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.4 Specimen contamination
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b

preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33

preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count is ordered. Which tube is used, and what does the CBC measure?
opciones: A lavender EDTA tube; red cells, white cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV
A light blue citrate tube; the seconds the sample takes to clot and the INR
A grey fluoride tube; plasma glucose and the average glucose of recent months
A gold serum separator tube; electrolytes, kidney waste products and the liver enzymes
preguntas.explicacion: Hematologic assays go in the lavender EDTA tube, and a CBC counts the blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and the mean corpuscular volume. Clotting seconds and the INR belong to the PT/INR in citrate, glucose to the grey tube, and electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and liver enzymes to the metabolic panels run on serum.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC), What is a complete blood count?; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", Lavender

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital introduces safety-engineered needles but its needlestick rate does not fall. Which contributing factors were most often reported in a study that found this pattern?
opciones: Difficulty operating the safety mechanism and continued improper needle disposal
Reuse of needle holders and the mixing of components from different manufacturers
Prolonged tourniquet time and failure to activate the feature with one hand
Overfilled sharps containers and the absence of double gloving
preguntas.explicacion: A 2018 study from the Netherlands recorded 1.9 needlestick injuries per 100 healthcare workers before safety-engineered devices and 2.2 afterwards; the factors most commonly reported were difficulty operating the safety mechanism and continued improper needle disposal. That is why ongoing training on the devices, surveillance and a strong safety culture are described as necessary companions to the technology.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern, Impact of Safety Devices on Needle Stick Injuries

preguntas.pregunta: An accreditation programme asks a laboratory to show how it addresses its four patient safety goals. Which of these is one of them?
opciones: Coordinating the laboratory's patient safety role across the organisation
Verifying the calibration of every analyser at each change of reagent lot
Reviewing the appropriateness of the tests that clinicians order each month
Confirming the competency of each testing employee twice in the first year
preguntas.explicacion: The four goals all sit outside the analysis itself: improving patient and sample identification at collection, analysis and reporting; improving verification and communication of life-threatening or life-altering information; improving the timely identification, communication and correction of errors; and improving coordination of the laboratory's patient safety role within the organisation.

preguntas.pregunta: After heavy, chronic use, which substance has the longest urine detection window?
opciones: Cannabinoids, at about three months
Cocaine metabolites, at about three weeks
Heroin metabolites, at about eleven days
Amphetamines, at about ten days
preguntas.explicacion: After heavy chronic use the reported windows are ten days for amphetamines, eleven days for heroin metabolites, three weeks for cocaine metabolites and three months for cannabinoids, so cannabis is far and away the longest. These figures are for chronic use: after a single small dose most drugs are gone from urine in one to three days.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Clinical Drug Testing", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with capacity refuses a treatment that the whole team believes would help him. What is the legal position?
opciones: He may refuse, whatever others judge the benefit to be
He may refuse once a second clinician has confirmed it
He may refuse only treatments that are not life-sustaining
He may refuse only after signing a form releasing the team
preguntas.explicacion: Any patient who has capacity also has the right to refuse any treatment, regardless of whether other people consider giving it an act of beneficence, and a Supreme Court decision extended that right even to measures that decide life or death. The right comes from autonomy and travels with informed consent: capacity is the condition, and the assessment of capacity is part of the consent discussion itself.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)

preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. A clinician's view that the test is good for the patient is the paternalism the consent literature warns against; language barriers call for an interpreter; and a psychiatric diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to consent.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Exceptions to Informed Consent

preguntas.pregunta: Two patients on the same dose of the same drug show different levels. Which factors are named for that?
opciones: Ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection change how a drug is processed
The colour of the tube stopper and the order in which the tubes filled
The arm chosen for the draw and how long the tourniquet stayed on
The time of day alone, since every drug level follows a diurnal rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: As soon as a medicine is taken the body begins to process and remove it, so the level in the blood varies over time, and ageing, pregnancy, illness and infection all affect how quickly that happens. Levels also differ between individuals on the same dose because of absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion, and of diet and other drugs taken alongside.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is therapeutic drug monitoring?; and StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes come back faulty from the same phlebotomist: one is haemolysed and one holds small clots. What separates the two errors?
opciones: Too much mixing haemolyses the sample; too little leaves small clots
Too little mixing haemolyses the sample; too much leaves small clots
Too much mixing leaves clots; a short draw is what haemolyses a sample
Both faults come from mixing too little, at different points in the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant are inverted in a figure-of-8 until the blood and additive are properly combined. Push it too far and haemolysis appears; stop too soon and small clots form. Both faults make the specimen unusable, and both are decided at the bedside, not in the laboratory.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: The requisition says 'Robert', but the patient introduces herself as Roberta and uses she/her. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Use the name and pronouns she gives, and note them in the record for next time
Use the legal name on the requisition until the record has been formally amended
Ask the partner who accompanies her which pronouns you should use
Avoid using any name or pronoun for the rest of the visit, to be safe
preguntas.explicacion: Staff should refer to patients by their name and chosen descriptive pronouns, to follow the patient's lead and ask when in doubt, and to make a note in the record so the same pattern is followed at future visits, modifying the electronic record if needed. Identification for the specimen is a separate step that uses the identifiers on file.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", sections Patient Versus Provider Use of Slang Terms, and How to Create a Practice That Welcomes Members of the LGBTQ Community

preguntas.pregunta: A smear shows platelets sticking to the white cells rather than to each other. What is that finding called?
opciones: Platelet satellitism
Platelet clumping
Rouleaux formation
Pseudo-polycythaemia
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets adhering to polymorphonuclear cells is known as platelet satellitism, and careful microscopic review of the smear is what picks it up. Clumping of platelets with one another in EDTA is the neighbouring artefact, and rouleaux are stacks of red cells, not platelets.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: Which anticoagulant and container are recommended for a blood alcohol specimen?
opciones: Heparin or EDTA, in a pre-evacuated sterile tube of the smallest capacity
Sodium fluoride only, in a pre-evacuated sterile tube of the largest capacity
Heparin or EDTA, in a sterile syringe emptied into an open-topped tube
Sodium citrate only, in a pre-evacuated sterile tube filled to the mark
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendations are to choose either heparin or EDTA, to use only pre-evacuated sterile collection tubes of the smallest capacity, about 2.5 mL, to fill and mix them completely, and to avoid air suction, tube venting and hemolysis. Vented or opened tubes are a hazard, especially if the specimen has to be re-analyzed, and probing a difficult vein should give way to changing the site.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, Blood alcohol concentration in the clinical laboratory: a narrative review, Biochemia Medica 2024 (PMC10564119), Table 1 seven pillars

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)-(4), Core elements and requirements
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: How often must a certified biological safety cabinet be recertified in a laboratory working with concentrated HIV or HBV?
opciones: When it is installed, whenever it is moved, and at least once a year
Every three years, the period for which training records are kept
Once at installation, and again only after a spill occurs inside it
Every six months, and after each change of the exhaust air filter
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(iii) requires certified biological safety cabinets, or equivalent containment such as special clothing, respirators, centrifuge safety cups and sealed rotors, for any activity that could throw droplets, splashes, spills or aerosols of infectious material. Subparagraph (B) sets the schedule for certification: at installation, at every move, and at least annually. The annual cycle is shared by the biosafety manual review in (e)(2)(ii)(M); three years is the retention period for training records.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(2)(iii)(A) and (B), Containment equipment

preguntas.pregunta: A single-dose vial of lidocaine contains far more than one patient needs. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Do not keep the remainder for later or another patient; buy the smallest vial that meets the need
Label it with the date and use it for up to 28 days, as with a multi-dose vial
Pool the leftover contents with other single-dose vials in a clean preparation area
Save the remainder for the same patient's next visit, since it is dedicated to one person
preguntas.explicacion: A single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection, typically lacks a preservative, and must never be used for more than one patient. If it holds more than needed, the remainder is not retained for future use even on the same patient, leftover contents are not pooled or stored, and the practical advice is to purchase the smallest vial necessary. The 28-day dating rule applies to opened multi-dose vials, which contain a preservative.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for single-dose vials

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fasted asks when she can eat again. What is the answer?
opciones: As soon as the test is over; bringing a snack helps, since light-headedness is common
One hour after the draw, once the laboratory has confirmed the sample is usable
Only after the provider has reviewed the results and cleared her to eat
After a second sample is collected two hours later, as in a tolerance test
preguntas.explicacion: The patient can eat as soon as the test is over; feeling light-headed after a fasting blood test is common, and bringing a snack to eat right away is a good idea. The two-hour second sample describes the oral glucose tolerance test, a different situation in which the patient must keep fasting until the final sample.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the lactose tolerance blood test measure, and how is the specimen obtained?
opciones: Glucose, in several venipuncture samples before and after a lactose drink
Hydrogen, in several venipuncture samples before and after a lactose drink
Lactose, in a single venipuncture sample two hours after a lactose drink
Glucose, in a single capillary sample taken two hours after a lactose drink
preguntas.explicacion: The blood version looks for glucose, which the body produces when lactose is broken down, and several samples are drawn from a vein before and after the patient swallows the lactose liquid. Hydrogen belongs to the breath test, not to blood, and one sample is not enough because the result is a rise measured against the fasting value.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), How the Test is Performed

preguntas.pregunta: Before a routine venipuncture, what does the WHO's Step 4 require for hand hygiene and gloves?
opciones: Soap and water, or 3 ml of alcohol rub if hands are not visibly soiled, then well-fitting non-sterile gloves
Use 3 ml of alcohol rub in every case, even on visibly soiled hands, then put on sterile gloves
Wash with soap and water, dry with a reusable towel, then put on sterile gloves for every patient
Put on well-fitting non-sterile gloves first, then clean the gloved hands with alcohol rub
preguntas.explicacion: Step 4 gives two options: wash the hands with soap and water and dry them with single-use towels, or, if they are not visibly contaminated, rub 3 ml of alcohol rub over palms, fingertips and backs of the hands until dry; only then are well-fitting non-sterile gloves put on. Sterile gloves are reserved for blood cultures. Gloves are never a substitute for hand hygiene.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 4: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60%. What should be considered when collecting a citrate specimen from this patient?
opciones: The high hematocrit raises the citrate effect, so the anticoagulant volume may need adjusting
The high hematocrit lowers the citrate effect, so the tube should be filled only halfway
The tube is collected as usual, since hematocrit affects the EDTA tube and not the citrate tube
A larger 16 to 18 G needle is used so the viscous blood reaches the 9:1 ratio faster
preguntas.explicacion: Inadequate filling or a hematocrit above 55% increases the citrate level in the sample and interferes with the recalcification performed during analysis, and with a high hematocrit the anticoagulant volume may need to be adjusted. Half filling would make the citrate excess worse. The 16 to 18 gauge belongs to blood donation in the WHO needle table, not to coagulation draws, for which 19 to 22 G is suggested.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample looks pink after centrifugation. Which result on the chemistry panel should the processor expect the laboratory to question first?
opciones: Potassium
Magnesium
Chloride
Glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Among frequent chemistry tests, the analytes most sensitive to hemolysis are lactate dehydrogenase, creatine kinase and its MB isoenzyme, potassium, conjugated bilirubin, ALT, AST and iron; potassium is the one whose distortion most often changes patient management, which is why one hospital measures the hemolysis index on every potassium sample. Albumin, glucose and other analytes showed biases that stayed within CLIA limits in the study on graded hemolysis, as did magnesium and chloride.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must a bloodborne pathogens training record include?
opciones: Dates, a summary of the content, the trainer's name and qualifications, and attendees' names and titles
Dates, the trainer's name, and each attendee's hepatitis B vaccination status and serology
Dates, the content, and the type and brand of any device that caused an injury during the year
Dates, the attendees' names, and a copy of each attendee's signed declination or consent
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(i) lists four items for the training record: the dates of the sessions, the contents or a summary, the names and qualifications of whoever conducted the training, and the names and job titles of everyone who attended. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for one-step gestational testing. What should she be told to expect?
opciones: An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 100 g drink, and about 3 hours in the office
No fast at all, a 50 g drink, and about 1 hour in the office
A 3-day carbohydrate diet, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
preguntas.explicacion: One-step testing means nothing to eat or drink except sips of water for 8 to 14 hours, a liquid holding 75 g of glucose, and draws before the drink and every 60 minutes for two hours, so at least two hours should be allowed. The 100 g / 3-hour version is the second step of the other pathway, and the 50 g nonfasting drink is its first step. Nothing may be eaten during the test.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the FDA's design recommendations for sharps injury prevention features, what must be true once the feature has been activated?

It can be reset once so the device can be used on the same patient
It stays protective until the device reaches the sharps container
It may be released by a second single-handed action if needed
preguntas.explicacion: Table 1 of the FDA guidance lists, for all feature types, that the user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and should remain protective through disposal. preguntas.pregunta: A man scheduled for a semen analysis asks how long he should abstain from ejaculation beforehand. What is the usual instruction?
opciones: From 2 to 3 days, and in no case longer than 5 days before the test
From 2 to 3 hours, and in no case longer than 5 hours before the test
At least 7 days, and preferably 10 days or more before the test
No abstinence at all, since recent activity does not change the count
preguntas.explicacion: To get an adequate sperm count the patient avoids any sexual activity that ends in ejaculation for 2 to 3 days, and the interval should not stretch past 5 days because quality falls off after that. The StatPearls account of the same test sets the window differently, at a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 7 days, so the figure a candidate quotes depends on which reference the laboratory follows.

preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, may a facility apply Standard Precautions instead of Universal Precautions?
opciones: Yes, as an alternative, if the facility follows all other provisions of the standard
No; Universal Precautions is the only approach the standard's definitions recognize
Yes, but only in hospitals accredited by a CMS-approved accreditation organization
Yes, and doing so exempts the facility from the exposure determination requirement
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool explains that Body Substance Isolation and Standard Precautions define all body fluids and substances as infectious, and that OSHA permits them as alternatives to Universal Precautions provided the facility adheres to every other provision of the bloodborne pathogens standard. preguntas.pregunta: What pulse findings does a blood donor have to meet?
opciones: A regular pulse between 50 and 100 beats per minute
A regular pulse between 60 and 100 beats per minute
Any pulse between 50 and 120 beats per minute
A regular pulse between 40 and 90 beats per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The donor's pulse must be regular and between 50 and 100 beats per minute. Rhythm counts as much as rate: an irregular pulse inside the range still needs the responsible physician to determine and document that donating would not adversely affect the donor's health, and so does a rate outside the limits.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is far below normal. What is the term for this, and what is the main risk?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia; excessive bleeding even from minor wounds
Thrombocytosis; the formation of unwanted clots or thrombosis
Leukopenia; an inability to ward off infection and disease
Thrombophilia; an inherited or acquired tendency to form thrombi
preguntas.explicacion: An insufficient number of platelets is thrombocytopenia; blood may then fail to clot properly, so excessive bleeding can follow even minor wounds. The opposite, too many platelets, is thrombocytosis and carries a risk of unwanted clots. Leukopenia is too few white cells, and thrombophilia (hypercoagulation) is a tendency to thrombosis that can be genetic or acquired.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the correct way to take off a gown after caring for a patient?
opciones: Release the ties, touch only the inside, and turn it inside out
Release the ties, roll it from the sleeves toward the neckline
Pull it over the head without untying, keeping the front outward
Fold it front to front and hang it for the rest of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: The gown is third in the doffing sequence. Its ties or straps are released, and it is removed touching only the inside, pulled away from the neck and shoulders, turned inside out so the contaminated face ends up enclosed, and placed in the proper container. The bloodborne pathogens standard adds the companion rule: a garment penetrated by blood comes off immediately, in a way that avoids contact with its outer surface, and a gown is never hung up for reuse.

preguntas.pregunta: A work surface in the draw room is splashed with blood during a procedure. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Decontaminate it with an appropriate disinfectant immediately or as soon as feasible
Decontaminate it at the end of the work shift, the time the standard sets for possibly contaminated surfaces
Remove and replace the protective covering at the end of the shift, as with plastic wrap over equipment
Flush it with water immediately, as the standard requires for skin and mucous membranes
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(A) names three moments for decontaminating a work surface with a suitable disinfectant: when a procedure is finished; right away, or as soon as feasible, when the surface is visibly contaminated or blood or OPIM has been spilled on it; and at the end of the shift if it may have been contaminated since the last cleaning. A visible spill falls under the second case and does not wait for the shift to end. Protective coverings, in (d)(4)(ii)(B), are likewise replaced as soon as feasible once overtly contaminated. Flushing with water is the rule for eyes and mucous membranes in (d)(2)(vi), not for surfaces.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to check each new hire's antibody level first and offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to those who are not immune. What does the standard say?

Screening is required before the first dose, and has to be repeated a year later
Screening replaces the vaccine when the employee signs the declination form
Screening is allowed only within ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Two sentences have to be read together. preguntas.pregunta: A patient has fainted in the chair and been eased to the floor. How high should the feet be raised?
opciones: About 12 inches (30 cm) above the level of the heart
About 4 inches (10 cm) above the level of the heart
About 3 feet (90 cm), by resting the legs on the chair seat
Level with the heart, with the head turned to the side
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps after a faint are: check airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing around the neck, raise the feet above heart level by about 12 inches or 30 centimeters, turn the person on the side if they have vomited, and keep them lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes. The side position is for vomiting; it does not replace elevating the legs.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient recovers from a faint during a draw. Which finding afterwards is a red flag pointing away from a simple vasovagal episode?
opciones: A bitten tongue, which suggests a seizure
Pallor and sweating during the event itself
A slow pulse and low blood pressure during the event
Generalized weakness for a few minutes after waking
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is usually bradycardic, hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic during the event and should have an entirely normal examination afterwards; findings such as tongue biting, which suggests a seizure, or ongoing pallor, which suggests symptomatic anemia, call for a more thorough evaluation. preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factors require vitamin K for their production?
opciones: II, VII, IX and X
I, V, XI and XIII
III, IV, VIII and XII
VIII, IX, XI and XII
preguntas.explicacion: Four factors need vitamin K for their synthesis: prothrombin (II), proconvertin (VII), antihemolytic factor B (IX) and the Stuart-Prower factor (X), all made in the liver. preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a blood cortisol test asks how many visits it will take that day. What is the answer?
opciones: Two appointments at different times on the same day
One appointment, with two tubes drawn back to back
Three appointments, spread across the same morning
One appointment, followed by a 24-hour urine jar
preguntas.explicacion: For a blood cortisol test the patient needs two appointments at different times on the same day. Samples are usually taken twice: once in the morning, when levels are normally at their highest, and again around 4 p.m., when they are normally much lower. The 24-hour urine collection is a different form of the test, not an add-on to the blood one.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep her worklist on a personal flash drive and check it over the clinic's open wireless network. What is the guidance?
opciones: Avoid storing it on portable media, and use only encrypted networks
Store it on the drive but keep the drive locked in the staff room
Use the open network, since the worklist holds no test results
Store it on the drive after deleting the names, keeping the numbers
preguntas.explicacion: Portable media are a documented source of breaches: laptops and flash drives get stolen, so workers are told not to keep patient data on them, and to encrypt it if it must be kept, or better, to view the data without storing it. Where several computers reach records over a wireless network, the network's encryption has to be switched on, and staff must stop using an unencrypted one because of the risk of interception.

preguntas.pregunta: Minutes after the gloves touched her arm a patient has trouble breathing and cold, clammy skin. What does this suggest?
opciones: A severe allergic reaction, an emergency needing treatment at once
Irritant contact dermatitis, treated by washing and a steroid cream
Latex-fruit syndrome, which shows as an itchy mouth after eating
A delayed type IV reaction, the one behind allergic dermatitis
preguntas.explicacion: Signs of a severe reaction usually involve more than one part of the body: difficulty breathing or swallowing, dizziness or fainting, confusion, vomiting, diarrhoea or cramps, pale or red skin, and shock with shallow breathing and cold, clammy skin. A system of storage that keeps every tube upright at four degrees
A system of billing that records which tests each patient received

preguntas.pregunta: When an evacuated tube is used for a paediatric venipuncture, which tube is chosen?
opciones: A small-volume tube, 1 mL or 5 mL, with a low vacuum, to avoid collapsing the vein
A standard 10 mL tube, since a partial fill still keeps the correct blood-to-additive ratio
A 1 mL or 5 mL tube with a high vacuum, so that the small needle fills it quickly
A non-additive tube only, because additive tubes cannot be filled through a butterfly
preguntas.explicacion: When an evacuated tube is used in a child, choose one that collects a small volume, 1 mL or 5 mL, and has a low vacuum; this helps avoid collapse of the vein and may decrease haemolysis. preguntas.pregunta: While washing hands at a sink for routine hand hygiene, which technique detail is correct?
opciones: Keep the hands below the elbows and turn off the faucet with a towel
Keep the hands above the elbows, as in the surgical scrub, and rinse toward the fingertips
Turn off the faucet with clean hands so the towel stays dry for drying
Dry the hands on a shared cloth towel and apply lotion before gloving
preguntas.explicacion: Routine handwashing is done with the hands kept below the elbows so water runs from less to more contaminated areas, 3 to 5 mL of soap, at least 15 to 20 seconds of friction over palms, backs, wrists, finger webs, fingertips, thumbs and nails using WHO's six-step pattern, a thorough rinse, drying with a clean or disposable towel, and using a towel to turn off the water so the clean hands are not recontaminated. Hands above the elbows is the surgical scrub position, where the hands are the cleanest area.

The full sixteen-section data sheet printed and taped to the bottle
The date it was filled and the initials of the employee who filled it
Only the biohazard symbol, since the area also handles specimens

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant finds an adult unresponsive, not breathing, and with no pulse. In what order are the steps of CPR performed?
opciones: Chest compressions first, then the airway, then rescue breathing
The airway first, then rescue breathing, then chest compressions
Rescue breathing first, then the airway, then chest compressions
The airway and two breaths, then a pulse check, then compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Circulation is handled first: compressions are started before the airway is opened and before any breath is delivered. The older airway-first order was set aside in 2010 after research showed that beginning compressions early gave better results than managing the airway first. A lone rescuer compresses and leaves ventilation for a second responder.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample for bilirubin sits uncovered on the bench under laboratory lights. What happens to the measured value over 9 hours?
opciones: Total bilirubin fell by about 59% in normal specimens and 41% in hyperbilirubinemic ones; specimens kept dark did not change
Total bilirubin rose by about 59% in normal specimens as conjugated forms broke down into unconjugated pigment
Total bilirubin fell by about 10% whether the tube was lit or wrapped in foil, so light made no difference
Total bilirubin was unchanged, but direct bilirubin fell by half only in the specimens kept in the dark
preguntas.explicacion: Serum exposed to fluorescent laboratory lighting for 9 hours lost on average 59% of its total bilirubin in normobilirubinemic specimens and 41% in moderately hyperbilirubinemic ones, while controls kept in the dark showed no change in total bilirubin. Light exposure should be limited to under 2 hours to keep losses below 10%, and amber tubes are used for neonatal bilirubin collection.

preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial is carried into a patient's room for an injection. What does the CDC say about that vial afterwards?
opciones: Dedicate it to that single patient; it may not go back into use for others
Return it to the clean medication room and keep using it for up to 28 days
Discard it immediately, since any vial entering a patient area is contaminated
Wipe the septum with alcohol and continue using it for other patients
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC asks that multi-dose vials be assigned to a single patient whenever possible and, when used for several patients, kept and accessed only in a clean medication preparation area away from immediate patient treatment areas. If a multi-dose vial enters an immediate patient treatment area, such as a procedure room, a cart or a patient room or bay, it is dedicated to single-patient use only. It does not have to be thrown away at once, but it can no longer serve other patients, and the 28-day limit still applies to it.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood donor asks how long the red cells she just gave would have lived. What is the lifespan of an erythrocyte, and what removes it?
opciones: About 120 days; macrophages in spleen, liver and marrow remove them
About 10 days, after which macrophages phagocytize them in the spleen
About 4 to 6 weeks, the time the body needs to replace donated cells
A few hours to a few days, like most of the granular leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Erythrocytes live up to 120 days in the circulation and are then removed by macrophages located mainly in the bone marrow, liver and spleen. The 10-day figure is the platelet lifespan, the 4 to 6 weeks is how long it takes the body to replace the cells lost in a blood donation, and hours to days is the lifespan of most white cells.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hematocrit result comes back as 42. What does that number mean?
opciones: That 42% of the blood volume is made up of red blood cells
That 42% of the blood volume is plasma, the liquid portion
That the red blood cell count is 4.2 million per microliter
That 42% of the formed elements are white cells and platelets
preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is reported as the percentage of the blood that consists of red cells; the rest of the sample is white cells, platelets and plasma. The usual figure is about 45 percent, with women at 37 to 47 (mean 41) and men at 42 to 52 (mean 47). White cells and platelets together form under 1 percent of a sample, so they are not counted in the hematocrit, and 4.2 million per microliter would be a cell count, not a percentage.

preguntas.pregunta: When should anti-HBs be tested to document a healthcare worker's response to the hepatitis B vaccine series?
opciones: 1 to 2 months after the final dose
6 months after the final dose
Within 10 working days of the final dose
Every year, at the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Postvaccination serologic testing for anti-HBs is done 1 to 2 months after the third dose, so that the worker's response status is on record for any future exposure; a level of 10 mIU/mL or more after a documented series is the correlate of protection. For workers who also received HBIG, testing may have to wait until the HBIG antibody has cleared, about 6 months after it was given. Ten working days is the OSHA deadline for offering the vaccine, and annual testing is not recommended for immunocompetent responders.

preguntas.pregunta: After a capillary draw on a 5-year-old, what follow-up care is suggested for the child beyond the requisition?
opciones: A gesture that leaves the child on a positive note, such as praise, a handshake or a fun sticker
A dose of oral sucrose, 0.012 to 0.12 g, which the WHO recommends as analgesia at any age
An explanation of every result the laboratory will report, so the child feels informed
A brief period lying flat, since children faint more often than adults after skin punctures
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up has two parts, completing the requisition and providing comfort and reassurance; a simple gesture, verbal praise, a handshake, a fun sticker or a pat on the back, is all it takes to leave the child on a positive note. The sucrose dose of 0.012 to 0.12 g is for newborns undergoing venepuncture or heel-pricks, not for older children.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration
It should be repeated immediately with a second cassette from the same kit, since a single negative can never be reported
It confirms that the patient is not pregnant, because urine tests are 97 to 99 % accurate at any point after a missed period
preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. First morning urine is the most concentrated. Because hCG rises daily in early pregnancy, a negative test is repeated about a week later, and a still-suspected pregnancy is referred to the provider. The 97 to 99 % accuracy figure applies to tests done a week or two after a missed period.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vein of the antecubital fossa does the WHO describe as usually the easiest to puncture, and why is the basilic vein riskier?
opciones: The median cubital vein, which lies between muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein
The basilic vein, between the muscles; an artery and a nerve run under the median cubital vein
The cephalic vein, since it is visible with no tourniquet; the basilic is where veins are diverting
Whichever vein already has a peripheral venous access in place; the basilic is too deep to reach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 of the guideline singles out the median cubital vein: it sits between muscles and is usually the easiest to puncture. The basilic vein has an artery and a nerve running beneath it, so a puncture there risks damaging one of them and tends to hurt more; swapping the two veins reverses the guideline. The same step warns against putting the needle in where veins branch, because that raises the chance of a haematoma, but it does not say that of the basilic vein, and it does not single out the cephalic vein at all. And in hospitalized patients it says NOT to draw from an existing peripheral venous access, because the result may be false.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement best describes the analytical phase of laboratory medicine compared with the rest of health care?

It is the extra-analytical phases that carry four to five times more errors, and the 46 to 68 % share belongs to the pre-pre-analytical phase.

Every day that patient specimens are assayed, before the first control material is run
Whenever a newly trained operator begins to run patient testing on the instrument

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks how a filled additive tube should be moved to mix it. Which pattern is described?
opciones: Inverting the tube in a figure-of-8 pattern
Rolling the tube between both palms briskly
Shaking the tube eight to ten times in a row
Inverting it once and standing it in the rack
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant need enough mixing, and the movement described is inversion following a figure-of-8. Overmixing can produce haemolysis and inefficient mixing leaves small clots, so neither brisk shaking nor a single inversion serves. Eight to ten mixes is the figure given for culture bottles.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: How long is a CLIA Certificate of Waiver effective, and what must the site do to keep it?
opciones: Two years; pay the waiver fee and renew every two years
One year; pay the waiver fee and renew every year
Five years; renew after a routine survey by the state agency
Indefinitely, as long as ownership does not change
preguntas.explicacion: All CLIA certificate types are generally effective for two years. A site with a Certificate of Waiver or a PPM certificate pays only a waiver or PPM fee on that two-year cycle, with no registration or compliance survey fees. Renewal does not depend on an inspection, because waived sites are not subject to routine surveys, but the certificate must be kept current.

preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the blood filling the tube is dark red rather than bright red. What does that color indicate?
opciones: Venous blood carrying deoxyhemoglobin, which is a darker red
Arterial blood carrying oxyhemoglobin, which is bright red
Hemolyzed blood in which hemoglobin has left the red cells
Blood with a high hematocrit from living at high altitude
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin is a pigment whose color depends on oxygen: freshly oxygenated blood is bright red, and blood that has given up oxygen in the tissues is a duskier, darker red. Oxyhemoglobin is the bright red form and deoxyhemoglobin the darker form. Dark red is therefore the expected color of venous blood, not a sign of hemolysis or of a high hematocrit.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood

preguntas.pregunta: A retractable safety needle is activated after the draw. What has to be true of the sharp afterwards?

It is fully covered by a cap held on with adhesive tape
It is bent back on itself so it cannot be straightened
It is left partly visible so the worker can confirm it fired
preguntas.explicacion: For a retractable design the recommendation is that the sharp ends up fully retracted inside the housing. That sits alongside two rules for every design: the user should be able to tell easily that the feature has fired, and once fired it cannot be undone and stays protective through disposal.

preguntas.pregunta: Ideally, how long should urine have been held in the bladder before a clean-catch sample for culture is collected?
opciones: About 2 to 3 hours
At least 1 hour
At least 8 hours
About 15 to 20 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Both the clean-catch instructions and the urine culture instructions ask, when possible, for urine that has been in the bladder for 2 to 3 hours. One hour is the minimum wait before a catheterized specimen or a urethral swab, and 15 to 20 minutes is how long before a catheterization a patient may be told to drink a glass of water if there is no urge to void. An eight-hour hold is a fasting interval for blood work, not a urine rule.

The mechanism cannot be reset, and the needle is too short for adult veins
The mechanism can trip while probing, and the barrel cannot hold two tubes
The mechanism jams when cold, and air in the syringe dilutes the additive

preguntas.pregunta: Parents ask whether they can decline the newborn blood spot screen. What is its legal status?
opciones: It is mandated by state law, so the baby is screened unless the parents refuse
It is voluntary everywhere and is performed only with signed consent
It is required by federal law and cannot be refused in any state
It is optional in hospitals but mandatory for out-of-hospital births
preguntas.explicacion: Because screening can be the only way to detect certain conditions, it is mandated by state law in the United States, meaning the baby will have newborn screening unless the parents refuse, and each state has its own legally required list of conditions. Participation is automatic and, in most states, mandatory. Babies born outside hospitals still need it, often via a midwife.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the chain of custody document for a forensic specimen?
opciones: Its continuity of possession from collection through to the courtroom
The analytical methods each laboratory used to examine the specimen
The consent the patient gave before the specimen was ever collected
The storage temperature the specimen was held at while in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The chain of custody is the continuity of possession of a piece of evidence and of its movement and location, from the point of discovery and recovery, through transport to the laboratory, until it is admitted in court. It exists to assure the court that what is examined is the same material that was seized and that it was never unaccounted for. Storage conditions are recorded within it, not instead of it.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Definition/Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO procedure, at what point is the tourniquet applied in relation to finding the vein?
opciones: After a vein is located that is visible without it; it is then applied and the vein re-examined
Before looking for any vein, so that all the veins stay engorged during the whole of the inspection
Only if no vein is visible after the site has been disinfected and allowed to dry
Immediately after the needle enters, to keep the vein distended while the tubes fill
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says the vein should be visible without applying the tourniquet, that locating it helps decide the needle size, and that the tourniquet is then applied four to five finger widths above the site and the vein examined again. Disinfection is Step 5 and comes after the site is chosen; and the tourniquet is in place before the needle enters, not applied afterwards.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal or administrative proceeding. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review when a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and remain accessible.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)-(4), Standard: Access to protected health information

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as an exception to a patient's confidentiality rights?
opciones: Sharing what is needed to head off imminent danger to someone
Sharing a diagnosis with a coworker who asks out of concern
Sharing a chart with a relative who is not involved in the care
Sharing a record with a magazine once the name is left out
preguntas.explicacion: The exceptions are named and narrow: sharing within the organization or with its business partners for medical, revenue, quality or risk management purposes; to head off imminent physical danger to the patient or to others; to assist a criminal investigation when a law official demands it; to preserve public health, which is why certain infections are reportable; and to communicate with a surrogate when the patient lacks the legal capacity to decide. Concern for a colleague's patient is not on the list.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is 155,000 per microliter. Is that typical, and where is about a third of the body's platelets kept?
opciones: Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
Yes, typical is 150,000 to 160,000 per µL; about a third is held in the liver
No, typical is 5,000 to 10,000 per µL; about a third is held in the spleen
No, typical is 2,000 to 3,000 per µL; about a third is held in the red marrow
preguntas.explicacion: A typical platelet count is 150,000 to 160,000 per microliter, so 155,000 fits. After entering the circulation, about one third of the platelets migrate to the spleen, where they are stored and released when a vessel ruptures. The 5,000 to 10,000 figure is the leukocyte count, and 2000 to 3000 is the number of platelets one megakaryocyte releases in its lifetime.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets

preguntas.pregunta: In an acute hemorrhage with no time to cross match, type O negative blood is transfused. Why is O negative called the universal donor?
opciones: Its cells lack A, B and Rh D antigens, so recipient antibodies do not react
Its plasma lacks anti-A and anti-B, so it cannot agglutinate any cells
Its cells carry both A antigen and B antigen, matching every recipient
It is the most common type, so it is the one always kept in stock
preguntas.explicacion: Type O erythrocytes display neither A nor B antigen, so the anti-A or anti-B antibodies in the recipient's plasma find nothing on the donated cells to attack, and Rh negative cells also lack the D antigen. One caution: type O plasma does carry anti-A and anti-B, but the transfused volume is small compared with the recipient's own blood, so the effect is usually limited.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, ABO Transfusion Protocols

preguntas.pregunta: What must the employer's written cleaning and decontamination schedule take into account?
opciones: The location, the kind of surface, the soil present, and the tasks done there
The brand of disinfectant and the date its container was first opened
The number of employees on each shift and the dates of their training
The volume of regulated waste the area produced during the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(i) makes the employer keep the worksite clean and sanitary, and then requires a written schedule for cleaning and a method of decontamination decided from four things: where in the facility the area is, what kind of surface has to be cleaned, what kind of soil is on it, and which tasks or procedures are performed there. preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO describe the order of draw for skin-puncture (capillary) specimens compared with venipuncture?
opciones: It is the reverse: haematology first, then chemistry and blood bank
It is the same: culture first, then coagulation, then the additive tubes
It is the reverse: chemistry and blood bank first, then haematology
It has no fixed order, because microtubes hold too little for carry-over
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.3 says that with skin punctures the haematology specimen is taken first, followed by chemistry and blood bank, and that this is the reverse of the venipuncture order. The reason given is to limit the effect of platelet clumping. The same section adds that when more than two specimens are needed, venipuncture may give more accurate results.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reuses the same elastic tourniquet all morning without cleaning it. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Tourniquets have been found carrying hospital-acquired bacteria
Tourniquets lose their elasticity after several patients in a row
Tourniquets absorb the alcohol used to prepare the puncture site
Tourniquets have to be discarded after each patient is finished
preguntas.explicacion: Best practice for the tourniquet is a clean elastic band that is reprocessed between patients, and the reason given is direct: contamination with nosocomial bacteria has been documented on tourniquets, so one that travels from arm to arm carries them along. The related warning is that a latex glove must not be used as a tourniquet on a patient with a history of latex allergy.

preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee reviews a one-year audit of an emergency laboratory that received 453,171 specimens. Which test group carried the highest rejection ratio?
opciones: Coagulation testing, rejected at about 13 % of what arrived
Blood gas analyses, rejected at about 10 % of everything arriving
Urine analyses, rejected at about 9 % of what arrived
Biochemistry testing, rejected at about 3 % of what arrived
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation led that audit at 13.3 %, with therapeutic drug monitoring close behind at 12.8 % and hormone testing around 12 %. Blood gases reached 9.8 % and urine 9.2 %, while biochemistry at 2.5 % and the complete blood count at 3.2 % were the least affected. Coagulation suffers most because red cell clots and a wrong blood-to-anticoagulant ratio are exactly what ruin a citrate tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory audits its identification errors and finds that most of them share one feature. Based on a seven-year study of preanalytical errors, which feature is that?
opciones: The sample carried fewer than two patient identifiers
The barcode had been printed for a different test panel
The sample had been labeled after arriving in the laboratory
The requisition and the tube listed different collection times
preguntas.explicacion: In the laboratory that measured its preanalytical quality indicators, identification problems were the second most frequent error, and most of them consisted of a label with fewer than two identifiers; in newborns the rate was ten times higher because the small tubes leave little room to write two. Wrong panels, late labeling and time mismatches are other errors, not the one that dominated.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the light grey top tube (sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate) the usual choice for a glucose specimen?
opciones: Its antiglycolytic additive keeps the glucose level stable for days
Its gel separator keeps the plasma away from the cells after spinning
Its clot activator produces serum faster than a plain red top tube
Its broth mixture keeps microorganisms alive until they can be cultured
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table describes the additive of the grey tube as an antiglycolytic agent, that is, one that blocks the breakdown of glucose, and says it keeps the glucose value stable for up to five days. Glucose is the use the table gives for it, with a note that it needs a full draw because a short draw may cause haemolysis. Gel separators belong to the serum separator and PST tubes, the clot activator to the red top, and the broth to the blood culture bottle.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a culture where health decisions are made collectively hesitates to sign a consent form. What is the culturally aware reading of that?
opciones: Written consent may be seen as a sign of mistrust; the process should allow for the family's role
Hesitation to sign means the patient lacks capacity and a surrogate must be sought
The patient is refusing care and the refusal should be documented at once
The form must be signed regardless, since the signature is the legal proof of consent
preguntas.explicacion: In certain cultures decisions are made collectively rather than by an individual signature, written consent may be perceived as a sign of mistrust, and the process may involve consulting a family patriarch or a designated male representative; undocumented immigrants may also fear signing. Cultural sensitivity is part of the consent process, and the emphasis on the signature as proof of understanding is itself being questioned.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences

preguntas.pregunta: About how far above the intended puncture site is the tourniquet applied, measured in inches?
opciones: About 3 inches above the site
About 1 inch above the site
About 6 inches above the puncture site
About 2 cm above the site
preguntas.explicacion: A preferably disposable tourniquet goes almost 3 inches above the targeted venipuncture site, tight enough to stop venous flow while arterial flow continues. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the purple EDTA tube before the serum separator tube that will be used for a chemistry panel. What problem does this kind of error create?
opciones: Anticoagulant on the needle can be carried into the following tube and contaminate it
The serum tube will fail to clot within the 10 to 15 minutes expected before it is spun
The vacuum of the second tube is lost, so it fills only partially or not at all
The EDTA tube will show platelet clumping and a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: Under Issues of Concern, the tube review describes contamination in which anticoagulant from one tube sticks to the vacutainer needle and passes into the next tube; that is why the sequence matters. preguntas.pregunta: Two blood culture sets are collected from an adult, each with one aerobic and one anaerobic bottle filled to the CDC target. What total volume of blood has been drawn?
opciones: 40 mL
20 mL
30 mL
80 mL
preguntas.explicacion: At 10 mL per bottle, one set of two bottles holds 20 mL and two sets hold 40 mL. That is the figure the CDC uses when it describes the two-set collection. An adult set is expected to contain 20 to 30 mL per venipuncture, and at least two sets, 40 to 60 mL in all, are needed to optimize the detection of pathogens; 20 mL is only one set, and 80 mL would be four sets.

preguntas.pregunta: How does an under-filled citrate tube distort coagulation results?
opciones: PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out longer and fibrinogen comes out lower
PT, aPTT and thrombin time come out shorter and fibrinogen comes out higher
PT and aPTT are unchanged, but the platelet count comes out falsely low
PT comes out longer while aPTT and fibrinogen are unaffected by the fill level
preguntas.explicacion: When too little blood meets a fixed volume of citrate the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong, and the clotting times PT, aPTT and thrombin time become significantly longer while fibrinogen levels come out significantly lower. The direction matters for the exam: the error mimics a bleeding tendency, not a hypercoagulable one, and it touches the citrate tube, not the platelet count from the EDTA tube.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient who has fainted kept lying flat rather than allowed to sit up right away?
opciones: Standing up too soon can bring the episode back before the postural hypotension has resolved
Sitting up compresses the abdomen and forces blood down into the legs, raising the heart rate
The horizontal position lets the tourniquet be reapplied safely for the remaining tubes
Sitting up too soon converts the faint into a seizure with tonic-clonic activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly with the legs raised to recover from reflex postural hypotension, and they should be kept horizontal after the event while being prevented from standing up too soon. The chapter does not describe abdominal compression, does not say a faint turns into a seizure, and nothing in it involves resuming the draw.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management

preguntas.pregunta: In which of these situations should 911 be called for a person who has fainted?
opciones: The person does not become alert within a couple of minutes
The person is pale and weak for a few minutes after waking
The person fainted while seated and woke up within a minute
The person reports having fainted once before during a blood draw
preguntas.explicacion: Call 911 or the local emergency number if the person who fainted fell from a height, especially if injured or bleeding, does not become alert quickly (within a couple of minutes), or is pregnant. Pallor and weakness for a few minutes after waking are the normal aftermath of a faint, and a past faint is a reason to draw the patient lying down, not an emergency.

preguntas.pregunta: Which use of protected health information always requires a HIPAA authorization, even when it relates to treatment, payment or operations?
opciones: Sale of protected health information
Referral of the patient to a specialist
Consultation between two treating providers
Submission of a claim to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Three uses need an authorization notwithstanding the rest of the rule: most uses and disclosures of psychotherapy notes, marketing beyond face-to-face communications or gifts of nominal value, and any disclosure that is a sale of PHI, where the authorization must state that the covered entity will be paid. preguntas.pregunta: A safety data sheet says the exact percentage of one ingredient has been withheld as a trade secret. Where does that statement belong?
opciones: In section 3, with the chemical names and the identification numbers
In section 15, with the other regulatory information on the product
In section 10, with the stability and the incompatible materials
In section 16, with the revision date and any other information
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3 lists what is in the product: chemical name, common names, the Chemical Abstracts Service number and other identifiers, and the impurities and stabilizing additives that count toward the classification. Exact percentages are required, with ranges allowed only for a trade secret claim, batch-to-batch variation, or a group of very similar mixtures. When an identity or a percentage is withheld as a trade secret, the sheet must say so, and it says so in this section.

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the cephalic and basilic veins of the arm begin, and which side of the limb does each drain?

From the palmar venous arches of the hand; cephalic on the medial side, basilic on the radial side
From the brachial vein, which splits at the elbow into a lateral cephalic and a medial basilic branch
From the median antebrachial vein of the forearm, which divides into both of them below the elbow
preguntas.explicacion: The superficial veins of the hand arise from the dorsal venous arch on the back of the hand, which drains into the cephalic and basilic veins; the cephalic drains mainly the radial side of the limb and the basilic the medial side, and the two are joined near the elbow by the median cubital vein. Ask the patient to bend the arm
Withdraw the needle and apply gauze
Invert the collected tubes 8 to 10 times

preguntas.pregunta: Which test opens the two-step approach to gestational diabetes screening recommended by ACOG?

A 2-hour 75 g glucose tolerance test after an overnight fast
A 3-hour 100 g glucose tolerance test after an overnight fast
A 1-hour 75 g glucose challenge given at the first prenatal visit

preguntas.pregunta: Only a tiny drop of blood appears after the needle enters and the flow stops. What is the likely cause and the adjustment?
opciones: The bevel may still be partly outside the vein; flatten the angle and advance 1 to 2 mm
The vein has been passed through completely; withdraw the needle fully and re-puncture above
The tube has lost its vacuum; pull the needle back out of the skin and change the tube
The tourniquet is too tight; remove it entirely and wait for the flow to return
preguntas.explicacion: If only a small drop of blood is seen, the needle bevel may remain partially outside the vein, and the device should be flattened slightly and advanced in 1 to 2 mm increments until flow is adequate. preguntas.pregunta: A plasma sample will be tested for viral load now and possibly retested several times over the coming months. Why is it aliquoted before freezing?
opciones: So each retest thaws a fresh portion, avoiding the loss seen after repeated freeze-thaw cycles
So the erythrocytes settle in one portion and the plasma stays free of heme when it thaws
So the laboratory can send one portion to a reference laboratory without a referral record
So the heparin concentration falls below the level that inhibits amplification in each portion
preguntas.explicacion: Serum and plasma tolerate freezing, but the number of freeze-thaw cycles a target survives varies: one study saw a 16 % fall in HCV RNA titres after five cycles and recommended aliquoting the sample to limit the loss, while others found no loss after eight or ten. Splitting the sample lets each retest use a portion thawed only once. Erythrocytes are removed before freezing, not by aliquoting, and heparin is a reason to reject the tube, not to split it.

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker asks you to look up a neighbor's laboratory results, saying she only wants to know whether the neighbor is all right. What should you do?
opciones: Refuse, because access is limited to the information each role needs for its own job duties
Look it up but read out only the abnormal values, which keeps the disclosure to a minimum
Look it up, since a coworker inside the same covered entity is part of the same workforce
Look it up after the neighbor's next visit, once a treatment relationship has been created
preguntas.explicacion: Internal access is governed by role. A covered entity's policies must name who needs which categories of information to do their duties, and access outside that is a violation whether or not anything is repeated afterwards. preguntas.pregunta: How do anti-Rh antibodies differ from the anti-A and anti-B antibodies of the ABO system?
opciones: They form only in Rh− people after exposure to Rh+ cells (sensitization)
They are preformed from early exposure to antigens in foods and microbes
They form in Rh+ people after a first transfusion of Rh− blood
They are present in all type O plasma along with anti-A and anti-B
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems differ: ABO antibodies are preformed because A and B antigens are met early in life in food and microbes, whereas antibodies to the Rh antigen are made only by Rh negative individuals after exposure to Rh positive cells, a process called sensitization, which follows an Rh-incompatible transfusion or, more often, the birth of an Rh positive baby to an Rh negative parent.
