preguntas.pregunta: Besides treatment and surgery, for which of these is informed consent listed as required?
opciones: Blood and medication infusions, and anaesthesia
Routine vital signs and a height measurement
Transport of specimens to a reference laboratory
Storage of leftover serum for one further week
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is required for treatment, for dissemination of patient information, for the discussion of the HIPAA rules, for specific procedures, for surgery, for blood and medication infusions, and for anaesthesia. It is a communication process between clinician and patient, not merely a signature on a document.

preguntas.pregunta: The GHS uses nine hazard pictograms. How many does OSHA enforce, and which one is optional?
opciones: Eight; only the environmental pictogram is optional
Nine; none is optional under the 2012 revision
Seven; the environmental and the health hazard ones are optional
Eight; the flame pictogram is optional for laboratory reagents
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA adopted the GHS pictograms but enforces the use of eight of the nine; the environmental pictogram is not mandatory because environmental hazards fall to other agencies, though label preparers may add it as supplementary information, so workers may still see it. Health hazard and flame pictograms are among the eight that are required whenever the classification calls for them. The names of the eight appear in a figure of the OSHA brief; the count and the exception are what the text states.

preguntas.pregunta: In the common pathway of coagulation, what is the job of thrombin?
opciones: Turns soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin
Turns inactive prothrombin into its active form
Cross-links and stabilizes the fibrin clot
Degrades the fibrin once the vessel has healed
preguntas.explicacion: The common pathway has three moves: once factor X is active, prothrombinase converts prothrombin (factor II) into thrombin; thrombin then converts fibrinogen (factor I) into insoluble fibrin strands; and factor XIII stabilizes the fibrin clot. Activating prothrombin is the job of prothrombinase, not of thrombin, and breaking fibrin down later is the work of plasmin.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Common Pathway

preguntas.pregunta: Why is newborn screening for phenylketonuria usually done a day or two after birth rather than in the first hours?
opciones: The baby needs protein from breast milk or formula before the sample
The heel is too small to puncture safely during the first day of life
The screening card cannot be processed until the birth is registered
Maternal blood in the newborn's circulation invalidates an early result
preguntas.explicacion: Accurate results need the baby to have taken some protein from breast milk or formula before the blood is collected, which is why the test is usually done a day or two after birth. If it was drawn sooner than 24 hours after birth, a normal result is not the end of it: the baby may need to be tested again at one to two weeks of age. No special preparation is required.

preguntas.pregunta: On the top of the foot, which venous network collects blood from the digital veins?
opciones: The dorsal venous arch
The plantar venous arch
The great saphenous vein
The small saphenous vein
preguntas.explicacion: The superior surface of the foot drains into the digital veins and then into the dorsal venous arch, which feeds the anterior and posterior tibial veins; the inferior surface drains into the plantar veins and the plantar venous arch. The great saphenous vein runs up the medial leg and thigh into the femoral vein, and the small saphenous runs along the lateral leg into the popliteal vein.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Lower Limbs and Table 20.16

preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a needle and syringe, from which end does the WHO say each package should be opened?
opciones: The needle from the hub end, kept capped; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle still protected
The needle from the tip end, with the cap removed; the syringe from the nozzle end, ready to attach
Both from the middle, so the two parts can be joined without touching either end
The needle from the hub end, cap removed; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.2.1 opens the hypodermic needle from the hub end, the back of the needle, keeping it capped, and the syringe from the plunger end, keeping the nozzle protected in its packaging; the nozzle is then pushed firmly into the exposed hub of the still-capped needle, and the assembly is left in place until needed. Uncapping early or exposing the nozzle defeats the purpose of the sequence.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.2.1, Needle and syringe

preguntas.pregunta: A fasting plasma glucose of 112 mg/dL on the baseline sample of an OGTT falls into which category?
opciones: Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
Normal fasting glucose (60 to 99 mg/dL)
Diabetes (126 mg/dL or higher on two tests)
Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: Impaired fasting glucose is a fasting plasma glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L); the WHO and some other bodies set the lower limit at 110. A normal fasting value runs 60 to 99 mg/dL, and 126 mg/dL or higher on two different tests diagnoses diabetes. Impaired glucose tolerance is defined by the 2-hour post-load value, not by the fasting sample.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic keeps a tidy temperature log that nobody has ever countersigned. Who is supposed to sign it, and how often?
opciones: The person who directs or supervises the testing, once the month is complete
The staff member who took the readings, at the end of every working week
The laboratory director of the reference laboratory, once a calendar quarter
The manufacturer's field representative, at each preventive maintenance visit
preguntas.explicacion: Each reading is dated and initialled or signed by whoever took it, and on top of that the person who directs or supervises the testing reviews and signs the log once it is complete for the month. That monthly review is what turns a column of numbers into a control: it is where a drift nobody acted on at the time gets caught.

preguntas.pregunta: Which staff group is named as using teach-back to check that patients know what to do before the next visit?
opciones: Staff making appointments, covering arrival time, medicines and fasting
Only the clinician, at the end of the consultation that ordered the test
The laboratory staff, at the moment the specimen reaches accessioning
The billing staff, when the patient settles the account on the way out
preguntas.explicacion: Every member of staff who deals with patients should use teach-back, and the example offered is staff making appointments checking that patients understand what will be required of them at the next visit: arrival time, insurance documentation, bringing medicines, fasting, and details of referrals to other clinicians.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, requires the hospital to inform each patient, or the patient's representative where state law allows, of the patient's rights in advance of furnishing or discontinuing care whenever possible. The same standard requires a grievance process with a clear procedure for written or verbal grievances, time frames for review and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the result. Visitation rights are explained at the same time as the other rights, not at discharge.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, protective equipment counts as appropriate only when it does what?
opciones: Keeps blood from reaching work clothes, skin, eyes or mouth for as long as it is worn
Carries the manufacturer's label with the biohazard symbol printed in orange-red
Is picked by the employee from the sizes the supplier keeps in stock at the site
Is worn over the uniform, which the standard also counts as protective clothing
preguntas.explicacion: The definition of appropriate in paragraph (d)(3)(i) is a performance test, not a brand or a label: under normal conditions of use, and for the whole time it will be worn, the item must not let blood or other potentially infectious materials through to the work clothes, street clothes, undergarments, skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes. Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) is what puts the right sizes within reach; and the definitions in (b) exclude ordinary uniforms, pants and shirts from being protective equipment at all.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the red-grey tiger top or gold serum separator tube separate the serum, according to the WHO table?
opciones: A gel at the bottom of the tube separates blood from serum when it is centrifuged
A clot activator on the tube wall makes the blood clot so the serum can be poured off
Lithium heparin keeps the blood liquid and a gel separates the plasma on spinning
Sodium citrate binds calcium and the serum rises above the cells within an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists no additive for the serum separator tube and describes its action as a gel at the bottom that separates blood from serum on centrifugation, for chemistries, immunology and serology. The clot activator belongs to the plain red tube; lithium heparin with a gel is the light green PST, which yields plasma; and sodium citrate is the coagulation tube, which never yields serum.

preguntas.pregunta: A worker who never reached a protective anti-HBs level after two complete vaccine series is exposed to an HBsAg-positive source. Per the CDC table, what is given?
opciones: Two doses of HBIG, the first right away and the second one month later
One dose of HBIG plus the start of a third complete vaccine series
A single vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months later
No further treatment, since two series show the worker is a documented responder
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's guidance for vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs below 10 mIU/mL after two complete series says that if the source is HBsAg-positive or unknown, the clinician receives two doses of HBIG, the first as soon as possible and the second 1 month later, and that further vaccine is not recommended because two series have already failed. If the source is HBsAg-negative, neither HBIG nor vaccine is needed. WHO's Table D.1 groups known non-responders with the unvaccinated for HBIG, but the CDC table is the more specific source here.

preguntas.pregunta: While transferring blood from a syringe, a phlebotomist pushes the plunger to speed up filling of a slow tube. What does the WHO say about this?
opciones: Do not press the plunger; the extra pressure raises the risk of haemolysis
Press the plunger only for tubes with additives, which need a full draw
Press the plunger gently once the stopper has been removed from the tube
Pressing is acceptable for the last tube, once the tourniquet has been released
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 instructs the phlebotomist to pierce the stopper from directly above with slow, steady pressure and not to press the syringe plunger, because additional pressure increases the risk of haemolysis; for tubes without a rubber stopper it asks for an extremely slow injection for the same reason. There is no exception for additive tubes, for the last tube, or after removing the stopper.

preguntas.pregunta: An unvaccinated phlebotomist is stuck by a needle used on an HBsAg-positive patient. According to the CDC, what is given and when?
opciones: HBIG and the first vaccine dose, as soon as possible and preferably within 24 hours, at separate sites
The vaccine series only, started within 7 days, since HBIG is reserved for known non-responders
HBIG only, repeated one month later, since starting the vaccine after exposure is too late
A 28-day antiviral course started within 72 hours, followed by the vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's table for unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated clinicians exposed to an HBsAg-positive or unknown source calls for one dose of HBIG plus the hepatitis B vaccine, given as soon as possible, at a different anatomical site such as a separate limb, with the series completed on schedule and anti-HBs tested 1 to 2 months after the last dose. The older brochure says HBV post-exposure treatment should start preferably within 24 hours and no later than 7 days. Two HBIG doses a month apart are for non-responders after two series; the 28-day antiviral course is HIV PEP.

preguntas.pregunta: You finish the fasting questions with a hard-of-hearing patient and now have to explain the finger stick. How should the change of subject be handled?
opciones: Pause a moment, lift the voice slightly or gesture toward what comes next, then explain
Move into the new topic in a higher pitch, since that register marks a change more clearly
Write the new topic on a notepad and hand it over without saying any of it out loud
Have the companion tell the patient that the subject is changing, then carry on speaking
preguntas.explicacion: A change of subject is announced to a patient with hearing loss: pause a moment, raise the volume a little, point toward what is going to be discussed, touch the patient gently or ask a question. The notepad is for writing down key terms, alongside the spoken explanation, not instead of it. A high pitch is hard to hear, and remarks are not directed only to the companion.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits and Families and caregivers as part of the health care team

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is called to draw blood in the fluoroscopy suite while imaging is under way. Which protection is meant for that setting?
opciones: A lead apron, leaded glasses and cap, and a thyroid collar
A fluid-resistant gown, a face shield and two pairs of gloves
An N95 respirator with eye protection, as for airborne cases
A chemical-resistant suit with a self-contained air supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where x-ray and gamma radiation are in use, especially in fluoroscopy and other image-guided procedures, the protective equipment is leaded: an apron or vest, leaded glasses, a leaded cap and a protective collar, all of which reduce the dose received. Dose monitoring with a personal dosimeter is required for workers who enter a high radiation or restricted area, or who receive more than a quarter of the occupational limit in a calendar quarter.

preguntas.pregunta: Which facility falls outside the CLIA definition of a laboratory?
opciones: A draw station that only collects and prepares specimens, with no testing
A physician office that performs only waived tests on its own patients
A hospital laboratory accredited by a CMS-approved organization
A mobile unit that performs hematology testing on human specimens
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA defines a laboratory as a facility that examines materials from the human body, by biological, microbiological, serological, chemical, hematological or similar methods, to provide information for diagnosis, prevention, treatment or health assessment, and it states that facilities that only collect or prepare specimens, or only serve as a mailing service, without performing testing are not laboratories. A waived-testing office and a mobile unit that runs hematology tests both perform examinations and therefore need a certificate; a pure collection site does not.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of the safety devices and sharps containers a draw station uses every day?
opciones: They are examined and maintained or replaced on a regular schedule so they keep working
They are examined only after an exposure incident has been reported and logged
They are replaced every three years, the period set for keeping training records
They are checked by the manufacturer at installation and then left in service
preguntas.explicacion: Engineering controls are the devices that take the hazard away from the worker: sharps disposal containers, self-sheathing needles, needleless systems. Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) says they have to be examined and either maintained or replaced on a regular schedule, so that they still do what they were bought to do. Waiting for an injury reverses that logic, and the three-year figure is the retention period for training records in (h)(2)(ii), not a replacement interval.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a hematoma, and which two technique errors cause it?
opciones: Blood pooled under the skin; a needle pushed beyond the vein lumen, or too little pressure during and after the draw
Pinpoint bleeding into the dermis; leaving the tourniquet on too long, or using a needle that is too small
Pooling of blood under the skin; shaking the tube after filling, or drawing the tubes out of sequence
Bleeding into the skin larger than 2 mm; drawing from the basilic vein, or using povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma is the pooling of blood under the skin, and two errors are linked to it: deep insertion of the needle beyond the lumen of the vein, and failure to apply adequate pressure during and after the draw. The WHO adds a third, letting the patient bend the arm. Pinpoint dermal bleeding is petechiae, and spots larger than 2 mm are purpura in the petechiae chapter.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Technique or Treatment and Complications

preguntas.pregunta: The flow into the tube is slow during a child's draw. Which measure does the WHO offer for the parent to do?
opciones: Rhythmically tighten and release the child's wrist to help the flow
Lower the child's arm below the level of the table for a minute
Press firmly above the elbow until the vein stands out clearly
Rub the puncture site briskly with dry gauze between the tubes

preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory notifies a phlebotomist that a specimen was rejected for a critically ill patient. Why must the recollection be arranged without delay?
opciones: Rejection forces a new sample request, prolongs turnaround and can delay diagnosis and treatment
Rejected specimens are discarded after 30 minutes, after which the original order is cancelled
The laboratory cannot issue any report for the patient until the replacement sample is received
A second rejection from the same unit automatically triggers an accreditation incident report
preguntas.explicacion: Sample rejection stops the analysis and generates a new request, which lengthens turnaround time and delays diagnosis and treatment of critical patients, with adverse outcomes described in the literature; that is the reason the task of contacting the patient or unit for recollection matters. Rejected tubes are actually kept 24 hours at 4 °C, other reports are not blocked, and accreditation bodies ask for monitoring, not automatic incidents.

preguntas.pregunta: Which four mechanisms are given as the primary causes of petechiae and purpura?
opciones: Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, loss of vascular integrity
Low platelets, high haematocrit, iron deficiency, loss of vascular integrity
High platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, raised blood pressure
Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, dehydration, prolonged tourniquet pressure
preguntas.explicacion: These rashes come from haemorrhage into the dermis, and the underlying mechanisms named are thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction, disorders of coagulation and loss of vascular integrity. preguntas.pregunta: Why does laying a patient flat bring them round after a faint?
opciones: Blood returns from the legs and the heart no longer pumps uphill
Blood leaves the legs and pools where the tourniquet had been
The vagus nerve is compressed and the heart rate rises at once
Cooling of the skin restores the vascular tone that had been lost
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient falls or is laid supine, circulating volume returns from the lower limbs and the heart no longer has to deliver blood against gravity, so consciousness comes back quickly. That is also why the person is asked to sit or lie down promptly as soon as the warning symptoms appear.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Pathophysiology

preguntas.pregunta: The Joint Commission gives a two-fold intent for NPSG.01.01.01. What are the two purposes?
opciones: Confirm the person is the one the service is meant for, and match the service to that person
Confirm the person is the one the service is meant for, and report critical results on time
Confirm the specimen label is complete, and match the container to the requisition form on file
Confirm the person's identity, and record the room number as a backup identifier
preguntas.explicacion: The rationale says wrong-patient errors happen at virtually every stage of diagnosis and treatment, so the goal aims first to reliably identify the individual as the intended recipient, and second to match the service or treatment to that individual. Timely reporting of critical results is Goal 2, a separate goal, and the room number is expressly excluded as an identifier.

preguntas.pregunta: The forearm a patient offers shows a hot, red area diagnosed as cellulitis. Why is that site excluded for venipuncture?
opciones: Cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria entering the blood directly
The inflamed skin blanches under pressure, which hides the vein from view
The swelling dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid, just as squeezing a finger does
Alcohol cannot be used on inflamed skin, so the site cannot be disinfected
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions such as cellulitis or an abscess can increase the risk of bacteria infiltrating the blood directly, so another site is chosen. Blanching is the feature that tells erythema from bleeding into the skin, tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's capillary warning about squeezing, and nothing in the material forbids alcohol on inflamed skin.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to start monitoring extra-analytical quality but can only afford two indicators. Which two areas do accreditation criteria and the literature put first?
opciones: Patient and sample identification, and the handling of critical results
Reagent inventory control, and calibration of the chemistry analyzers
Phlebotomist productivity, and the number of tubes drawn per patient
Duplicate test requests, and the utility of interpretative comments on reports
preguntas.explicacion: Review of accreditation requirements and patient safety concerns points to two priorities: patient and sample identification on the pre-analytical side and the handling of critical results on the post-analytical side, both already required by regulation or safety goals in many places. Duplicate requests and interpretative reporting are suggested as a later step into the pre-pre and post-post phases, and inventory or productivity are not extra-analytical quality indicators.

preguntas.pregunta: The son says, 'I'll sign the consent, she's forgetful.' No proxy or power-of-attorney paperwork exists. Who decides?
opciones: The patient remains responsible for her own choices; set clear boundaries with the family
The son may sign, because adult children are the default decision-makers for parents
A clinic staff member signs on the patient's behalf as a neutral third party
The draw is deferred until a court appoints a guardian for the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Adult children may want to step in for a parent with cognitive impairment, but that only a family member named as health care agent or proxy has legal authority in some circumstances; without it the patient makes her own choices, and the clinician sets boundaries. Court-appointed guardians are reserved for when the state hierarchy of surrogates fails.

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant takes a refrigerated control and a refrigerated patient sample straight from the fridge to the bench and starts the run. What step was skipped?
opciones: Letting the refrigerated material come up to room temperature first
Recording the refrigerator temperature at the moment of removal
Checking that the kit lot matches the lot of the control material
Writing the date of opening on the outside of the reagent vial
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation checklist for waived testing puts several steps before the run: inspect reagents or vials for damage, discoloration or contamination, prepare them as the current instructions say, write the opening date on a newly opened vial or kit, allow refrigerated reagents and samples to reach room temperature, and then perform quality control as the instructions recommend.

preguntas.pregunta: Under Contact Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for a blood pressure cuff and similar patient-care equipment?
opciones: Disposable or dedicated equipment; if sharing is unavoidable, clean and disinfect it before the next patient
Shared equipment may be used freely, since the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient, not with objects
Wrap shared equipment in a protective cover that is changed at the end of the shift
Autoclave the equipment after each use, since disinfection does not reach contact pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Contact Precautions recommendations name blood pressure cuffs as the example: use disposable or dedicated patient-care equipment, and when common use for several patients cannot be avoided, clean and disinfect it before use on another patient. The reason is that contact transmission includes the patient's environment and objects, not only skin. The same page asks that rooms of these patients be cleaned and disinfected frequently, at least daily or before another patient uses the space in outpatient settings, with attention to high-touch surfaces.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the puncture stroke itself be made in capillary sampling?
opciones: One quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to get good flow and avoid repeating the puncture
Two short strokes in the same track, so that the second opens the capillary bed fully
A slow, controlled stroke that stops as soon as the first drop of blood appears
A rocking stroke across the fingerprint lines, which widens the opening without going deeper
preguntas.explicacion: The skin is punctured with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke, to achieve a good flow of blood and to prevent the need to repeat the puncture. A second puncture would mean either reusing the lancet or the site, both of which are prohibited because of bacterial contamination and infection. Depth is controlled by lancet length, not by rocking.

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient asks for a sign language interpreter for a long pre-test discussion. May the laboratory tell him to bring a family member instead?
opciones: No, responsibility for effective communication rests on the covered entity itself
Yes, if that family member signs and agrees to interpret for him on the day
Yes, if hiring an interpreter would be an undue burden for the laboratory
No, unless the laboratory offers video remote interpreting as the alternative
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities cannot require a person to bring someone to interpret. An accompanying adult may interpret in only two narrow cases: an emergency with an imminent threat when no qualified interpreter is available, and a non-emergency where the individual asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate. Undue burden does not erase the duty either; it shifts it to another effective aid.

preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient calms down 20 minutes into a 4-hour restraint order. What should happen?
opciones: Remove the restraints immediately; he is no longer a danger to anyone
Keep the restraints on until the 4-hour order expires, as written
Keep the restraints on until the next scheduled face-to-face evaluation
Loosen one limb every 15 minutes until the order runs out
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient is no longer a danger to themselves or others, the restraints are removed at once; the time limit on the order is a maximum, not a prescribed duration. Restraint and seclusion are interventions of last resort, required to be the least restrictive measure, with no evidence that they are therapeutic or reduce aggression, and staff observe the patient regularly throughout.

preguntas.pregunta: How must the hepatitis B vaccination and any post-exposure follow-up be made available to an exposed employee?
opciones: Free, at a reasonable time and place, and under a licensed healthcare professional
Free, but only at the occupational health service the employer has contracted
At the employee's expense, reimbursed once the written opinion has arrived
Free, and only during the first ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) puts four conditions on every medical evaluation and procedure the standard requires, prophylaxis included: no cost to the employee, a reasonable time and place, performance by or under the supervision of a licensed physician or another licensed healthcare professional, and agreement with the Public Health Service recommendations current at that moment. preguntas.pregunta: Which change in practice is credited with markedly reducing needle-stick injuries?
opciones: Dropping recapping and putting the sharp straight into a safety container
Recapping every needle carefully with the cap held in the other hand
Storing used needles on the tray until the end of the drawing session
Rinsing the used needle before it goes into the puncture-resistant bin
preguntas.explicacion: Eliminating needle recapping and disposing of the sharp immediately into a puncture-resistant container is described as markedly reducing these injuries. Routine recapping is no longer recommended precisely because handling a used needle is what creates the chance of a puncture.

preguntas.pregunta: A karyotype has been ordered and a buccal specimen is requested. How is it collected?
opciones: A swab is put into the mouth and rubbed across the inside of the cheek to gather cells
A swab is put into the mouth and rubbed over the tongue and under it to gather saliva
The patient rinses with sterile saline and spits the rinse into a sterile screw-top tube
A blade scrapes the inner surface of the lower lip and the scraping goes onto a slide
preguntas.explicacion: A buccal swab is one of the specimens a karyotype can be run on: the swab goes into the mouth and is rubbed across the inside of the cheek to pick up cells. It needs no preparation and carries no risk. A normal report means 46 chromosomes with no unusual change in their structure.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides fear and pain, which everyday events are listed as bringing on a faint?
opciones: Coughing hard, straining at stool, standing still too long, passing urine
Eating a light meal, reading in poor light, walking upstairs, yawning
Drinking water, sitting down slowly, wearing loose clothing, resting
Breathing slowly, lying flat for an hour, raising the legs, whistling
preguntas.explicacion: Faints are described as happening during or just after coughing very hard, having a bowel movement with straining, standing in one place too long, or passing urine, especially at night. Emotional distress, fear and severe pain sit on the same list, and all of them can appear in a drawing room.

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn received a blood transfusion before the screening card was collected. Why does that matter for galactosemia?
opciones: The screen measures enzyme activity, so normal enzyme from the transfused cells can mask an affected baby
The screen measures galactose in plasma, and the transfused donor plasma dilutes it below the cut-off value
The transfusion adds lactose, which raises galactose and causes a false positive
The transfusion does not matter, because the screen uses DNA that is unaffected by donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Newborn screening for galactosemia evaluates enzyme activity, so it can detect the disease even before galactose enters the diet; but if a blood transfusion occurred before screening, the case may be misinterpreted as normal because of normal enzyme activity in the transfused blood. For that reason babies who had transfusions may be tested later or need further testing.

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory wants its accessioning staff to apply rejection criteria consistently. What training scheme did the published laboratory use for the secretaries who accept or reject samples?
opciones: One week of specialised training on the rejection criteria, with the programme updated by laboratory specialists every 6 months
One day of orientation on the rejection criteria, with an annual refresher delivered by the nursing education department
Three months of supervised practice on the rejection criteria, after which no further update of the programme was required
Self-study of the rejection criteria table, verified by a written test at the time of hiring and not repeated afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: In that laboratory two specialised secretaries by day and one at night receive the samples and decide to accept or reject them against the laboratory's written criteria; they were trained for one week to specialise in those criteria, and laboratory specialists updated the training programme every six months. For the clinical staff who collect, the laboratory added comprehensive education seminars every two months aimed at the emergency departments and intensive care units.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wearing gloves finishes a draw and removes them. Which CDC moment for hand hygiene applies?
opciones: Immediately after glove removal, before anything else
Only if the gloves were visibly soiled with blood
Before touching the next patient, which covers this case
At the end of the shift, because gloves replace hand hygiene
preguntas.explicacion: Immediately after glove removal is one of the CDC moments for hand hygiene, alongside immediately before touching a patient, before an aseptic task, before moving from a soiled to a clean body site, after touching a patient or the surroundings, and after contact with blood or contaminated surfaces. The same page states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Waiting for the next patient skips the glove-removal moment, and visible soiling changes only the method, soap and water instead of alcohol rub, not whether hygiene is done.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a service expected to keep enough laboratory tubes in stock at all times?
opciones: So blood is never decanted from one tube into another to reuse tubes
So the tubes on the tray can be replaced before their expiry each month
So a second tube of every colour is always drawn as a spare specimen
So the same manufacturer supplies the needles and holders in the tray
preguntas.explicacion: Management is asked to make enough sample tubes available precisely to keep dangerous shortcuts out of the room, and the example given is decanting blood so that tubes can be recycled. The single-manufacturer rule is a separate point about components fitting one another.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes cleaning a spill and her hands are visibly soiled. Which form of hand hygiene is required before the next draw?
opciones: Soap and water, dried with single-use towels
Alcohol rub, worked in until the hands are dry
Alcohol rub, followed by a second pair of gloves
Soap and water, dried with a shared cloth towel
preguntas.explicacion: Hand hygiene before a draw can be done two ways: washing with soap and water and drying on single-use towels, or rubbing with alcohol when the hands are not visibly contaminated. Visible soiling therefore rules the rub out. Well-fitting non-sterile gloves go on once the hands are dry.

preguntas.pregunta: The fasting instruction sheet exists only in English and the patient reads Haitian Creole. What is offered?
opciones: An interpreter trained in sight translation reads the sheet aloud to her
A member of staff with school Creole writes a summary on the sheet
The sheet is handed over as it is, since a copy has to be given anyway
The sheet is dropped, and fasting is left to the appointment reminder
preguntas.explicacion: It should not be assumed that people who use another language will understand notes written in English. Where materials cannot be obtained in the patient's language, interpreters trained in sight translation are enlisted, which means reading a written document aloud in a language other than the one it is written in. Getting by on basic or intermediate skills is ruled out.

preguntas.pregunta: A glucose specimen will not reach the laboratory for two days. What does the additive in the grey top tube provide?
opciones: It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to five days
It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to twelve hours
It activates clotting so the glucose stays with the separated serum
It inactivates thrombin so the glucose stays with the plasma fraction
preguntas.explicacion: The light grey tube holds sodium fluoride with potassium oxalate. The oxalate binds calcium and stops clotting, and the fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent credited with preserving glucose for as much as five days. Clot activation belongs to the red tube and thrombin inactivation to the heparin tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a 'trough level' represent in antiepileptic drug monitoring?
opciones: The lowest drug concentration, typically just before the next dose is due
The highest drug concentration, shortly after the dose has been taken
The unbound, pharmacologically active fraction of the drug in blood
The average concentration across the whole dosing interval
preguntas.explicacion: The trough is the concentration at its lowest point, typically just before the next dose, a measurement that matters most for drugs with short half-lives because it shows the minimum level maintained between doses. Free levels are the unbound active fraction, measured when protein binding may be altered. The peak and the interval average are different quantities.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Other Issues, Trough Versus Free Levels

preguntas.pregunta: Why do the veins of the limbs have valves, and roughly what share of the blood volume is in the veins at any moment?
opciones: To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; almost 70 percent
To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; about 10 percent
To produce the pulse felt at the radial artery; almost 70 percent
To regulate flow into the capillary beds; about 5 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are low-pressure vessels, so the larger ones, especially in the limbs, carry valves that keep blood moving toward the heart against the low pressure and the pull of gravity. Thinner, less rigid venous walls let veins hold more blood, almost 70 percent of the total volume, against about 10 percent in the systemic arteries and 5 percent in the systemic capillaries.

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's card has all its circles filled. What must happen before it is sent to the laboratory?

The card must be kept refrigerated
A second card must be collected first
The spots must be sealed under clear tape

preguntas.pregunta: A technician who moves to another hospital finds a different list of specimen rejection criteria in force there. Why does that happen?
opciones: There are no internationally accepted guidelines for unacceptable specimens
Rejection criteria are issued by the accrediting body, and accreditors differ
Rejection criteria follow the analyser, so they change with the manufacturer
Each laboratory adopts the criteria of the outside laboratory it refers work to
preguntas.explicacion: For some of the most contested steps of the preanalytical phase there are still no internationally accepted recommendations, nor agreed quality measures. preguntas.pregunta: For adult CPR, what compression-to-breath ratio and compression rate are used?
opciones: 30 compressions to 2 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
15 compressions to 2 breaths, at 60 to 80 compressions per minute
30 compressions to 5 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
5 compressions to 1 breath, at 120 to 140 compressions per minute
preguntas.explicacion: Adult CPR runs in cycles of 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, repeated until the person recovers or help arrives, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute with pauses for breaths kept under 10 seconds. The heel of one hand goes in the center of the chest between the nipples with the other hand on top, elbows locked and shoulders over the hands. With two or more rescuers, compressors switch every 2 minutes or about 5 cycles to avoid fatigue, and an AED is used as soon as one is available.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits to a history of panic attacks during blood draws. Which two simple measures are described to lower anxiety and prepare for a possible reaction?
opciones: Counting down before the puncture, and having the patient lie down when the history is severe
Drawing without warning so the patient has no time to react, and using a smaller needle
Applying the tourniquet early so the draw is quicker, and keeping the patient standing
Postponing the draw until a family member is present, and skipping the identification questions
preguntas.explicacion: Simple steps such as counting down can significantly reduce anxiety and improve the conditions for the venipuncture, and a patient with a severe history of panic attacks during the procedure may be asked to lie down; identifying patients afraid of blood tests or with a history of vasovagal attacks in advance lets the team prepare for a possible faint. Drawing without warning contradicts the emphasis on transparent communication and consent.

preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the phlebotomist notices a tear in one glove. What does the standard require?
opciones: Replace it as soon as feasible; a single-use glove is never washed for reuse
Finish the draw, then wash the glove with soap and water so it can be reused
Cover the tear with tape until the procedure ends, then discard the glove
Replace it only if blood reached the skin; otherwise finish the draw and discard it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(A) requires disposable gloves to be replaced as soon as practical when contaminated, or as soon as feasible when torn, punctured or otherwise unable to act as a barrier. Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(B) adds that single-use gloves are not washed or decontaminated for reuse; only utility gloves may be reused, and only while intact, under (d)(3)(ix)(C). The trigger is the loss of the barrier, not whether blood has already reached the skin.

preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time and a partial thromboplastin time are ordered together. What does that mean for the order of draw?

The prothrombin tube goes third and the thromboplastin tube tenth
Both are citrate tubes, but they follow the serum separator tube
The thromboplastin tube goes second, ahead of the prothrombin tube

preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient is refusing to sit for the draw. Which de-escalation techniques are described?
opciones: A moderate distance, calm body language, and awareness of the exits
Standing over the patient, speaking firmly, and blocking the doorway
Leaving without a word and returning with two more staff members
Sitting close and holding eye contact so he feels fully attended to

preguntas.pregunta: How many oxygen molecules can a single hemoglobin molecule carry, and what binds them?
opciones: Four, one on the iron ion of each of its four heme groups
Two, one on each alpha-beta pair of globin chains
Four, one bound directly to each of the four globin proteins
About 300 million, one for every hemoglobin in the cell
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin consists of four folded globin chains, two alpha and two beta, each holding a heme group with an iron ion. Oxygen binds to the iron, not to the globin protein, so each hemoglobin carries up to four oxygen molecules. A single red cell holds about 300 million hemoglobin molecules, which is why one cell can carry about 1.2 billion oxygen molecules.

Directly over the wound itself, on top of the soaked dressing
As close as possible to the armpit, no matter where the wound is
Below the wound, between the bleeding point and the fingertips

preguntas.pregunta: Which ethical principle is at work when a limited supply of a treatment is spread fairly across the patients who need it?
opciones: Distributing resources equitably across the patients
Preserving the patient's life and their autonomy
Avoiding acts known to expose a patient to harm
Placing a high value on the dignity of the person
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights grow out of a short list of principles: valuing the dignity of the person, acting with goodwill toward the patient and in particular preserving life and autonomy, avoiding acts or omissions known to expose the patient to harm, and distributing resources equitably across patients. Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril afterward, to rinse the suction catheter out
The catheter is passed to a shallower depth, stopping short of the turbinates on either side

Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect right after the evening meal

opciones: To keep germs from the penis or vagina out of the sample, so contaminants and formed particles are minimized
To obtain the most concentrated urine of the day, which shows the kidneys' ability to concentrate
To bypass the urethra entirely, which is the only way to get a sample free of periurethral flora
To capture the first portion of the stream, where epithelial cells and leukocytes are most numerous

preguntas.pregunta: Roughly how much blood circulates in an average adult, and how is it divided?

About 3 liters, roughly 60% plasma and 40% red cells with the other cells
About 8 liters, roughly 50% plasma and 50% red cells with the other cells

Ten working days is the vaccine deadline of (f)(2)(i), and three years is how long the training records are kept, not how often the training happens.

A large tube volume and as long a tourniquet time as the vein allows
A fasting patient and a puncture placed over the basilic vein instead
A second discard tube and a needle finer than twenty-three gauge
preguntas.explicacion: For coagulation work the puncture should be atraumatic and made without delay, and the tourniquet should stay on as briefly as possible, because both faults produce artifacts such as haemolysis. preguntas.pregunta: For roughly how long after the last drink can a blood alcohol test still detect alcohol, and what preparation does the patient need?

About 12 hours, and an 8-hour fast is needed beforehand
About 48 hours, and no special preparation is needed
About 3 hours, and the patient must avoid mouthwash first

With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?

Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the colour has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood

Repeat it word for word until it finally registers with him
Speak much louder, since hearing is usually the underlying problem
Ask the caregiver to answer so the visit stays on schedule
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient can hear but does not understand, the clinician should try rephrasing rather than repeating, and should not speak too quickly or too loudly. preguntas.pregunta: A 78-year-old has large purple patches on the backs of both hands and forearms. What is this and what causes it?
opciones: Actinic (senile) purpura: sun-damaged, atrophic dermis lets capillaries rupture with minor trauma; it fades in 1 to 3 weeks
Thrombocytopenic purpura: a low platelet count lets blood leak from intact vessels, and it needs an urgent platelet transfusion
Vasculitis: inflamed vessel walls leak blood into the dermis; the patches are tender and last for several months
Medication bruising: anticoagulants thin the blood so that every venipuncture leaves a spreading haematoma
preguntas.explicacion: Actinic purpura, also called senile or Bateman purpura, consists of purpuric macules and patches on sun-exposed skin, most often the dorsal hands and extensor forearms of older adults, caused by dermal atrophy and vascular fragility so that minor trauma ruptures capillaries. The lesions are painless, without inflammation, and resolve in 1 to 3 weeks; about 30% of people aged 75 or older are affected.

preguntas.pregunta: Which habit is recommended to workers so that a used needle never becomes a hazard in the room?
opciones: Plan how the needle will be handled and discarded before the procedure starts
Recap the needle with one hand until a container can be brought to the room
Set the used needle on the tray until the tubes have been labeled correctly
Carry the needle to the container at the end of the round of draws
preguntas.explicacion: The advice to workers is a short list: avoid needles where a safe alternative exists, help evaluate and then use the safety devices provided, avoid recapping, plan safe handling and disposal before beginning any procedure with needles, dispose of them promptly in the proper container, report every injury promptly, point out hazards, and take part in training and hepatitis B vaccination. Leaving a used sharp on a tray or carrying it around are exactly the delays this list is meant to remove.

preguntas.pregunta: A combined nasal and throat swab is being collected for influenza. Which area does the throat swab deliberately miss?

The tonsillar areas, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are both swabbed
The posterior pharynx, while the tonsillar areas and the tongue are swabbed
The soft palate, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are swabbed
preguntas.explicacion: For the throat half of a combined specimen, a second dry polyester swab goes into the mouth and collects from the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas, and the instruction is to avoid the tongue. preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes becomes shaky, sweaty and confused while waiting, but can swallow and follow directions. What is offered?
opciones: Juice, a sugary drink or glucose tablets, and then the provider is told
An injection of glucagon into the muscle of the outer part of the thigh
A glass of water and a rest in a cool room until the shaking settles
No food or drink, because the glucose must be measured in the lab first
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who is awake and able to swallow is given fast sugar: juice or another sugary drink, food, or glucose tablets. Glucagon, a medicine that raises blood sugar, is the route when the patient cannot take sugar by mouth. If the signs do not improve after a snack with sugar, the patient goes to the emergency room and does not drive.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient with hearing loss keeps asking you to repeat the fasting question. What should you do?
opciones: Face her at eye level and speak clearly in a normal tone, with less noise
Raise your voice and use a higher pitch so that the words carry across the room
Turn to the computer and type the questions for her in a large font
Ask her companion to answer the fasting questions on her behalf
preguntas.explicacion: For hearing deficits: check the hearing aid and background noise from equipment, talk clearly in a normal tone because shouting distorts sounds and can sound angry and a high pitch is hard to hear, and face the person directly at eye level so they can lip-read. Do not talk while typing and not to direct remarks only to the companion.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory uses the patient's electronic chart, rather than a separate form, as the test requisition. When is this acceptable under CLIA?

When the ordering physician signs a paper copy of the chart entry within 30 days of the order
When the chart is used only for waived tests performed at the point of care
When the laboratory also keeps a duplicate paper requisition for every order

preguntas.pregunta: Tuberculosis is suspected. How does the sputum collection differ from a routine sputum culture?
opciones: A series of 3 early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL is collected on separate days
A single early morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL is collected and sent the same day
A series of 3 specimens is collected 2 hours apart on the same morning and pooled
A series of 3 specimens is collected on separate days and pooled into one container
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each is collected on consecutive days, refrigerated and returned to the laboratory daily; each is examined separately, never pooled. Class II, and exempt from design controls once cleared once

First and last name and room number, confirmed against the card on the bed
First and last name, read aloud by the phlebotomist for the patient to confirm
The ID bracelet number on its own, cross-checked against the laboratory form

preguntas.pregunta: At what angle does the WHO guideline say the needle should enter the vein?
opciones: Swiftly, at 30 degrees or less, then along the vein at the easiest angle
At 30 degrees or more, steepening the angle as the needle advances along the vein
At 90 degrees, straight down, as when piercing a tube stopper directly from above
At 30 degrees or less, with the thumb anchoring the vein just ABOVE the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to enter the vein swiftly at an angle of 30 degrees or less and then keep advancing the needle along the vein at whatever angle gives the easiest entry: the angle does not steepen. The step pairs this with anchoring the vein first, holding the patient's arm with a thumb placed BELOW the puncture site, not above it, and asking the patient to make a fist so the veins stand out. Piercing straight down from above is how Step 7 fills a tube through its stopper, not how the needle enters a vein.

preguntas.pregunta: How often may a healthy donor give whole blood, and what changes after a double red cell collection?
opciones: Once in 8 weeks, extended to 16 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 8 weeks, extended to 24 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 4 weeks, extended to 8 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 16 weeks, shortened to 8 weeks after a double red cell collection
preguntas.explicacion: Donation frequency must be no more than once in 8 weeks, which blood centers count as 56 days, for a single unit of whole blood or red cells; after an apheresis collection yielding two units of red cells the donor waits 16 weeks. Even 56 days may not be enough to rebuild the iron lost, which is part of why repeat donors are deferred for low hemoglobin.

preguntas.pregunta: A 5-month-old infant who weighs 6 kg needs a capillary blood sample. Where is the lancet placed?
opciones: On the medial or lateral plantar surface of the heel
On the side of the middle or ring finger, across the print
On the posterior curve of the heel, where the tissue is deepest
On the great toe, which has more tissue over bone than the heel
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary site is chosen by age and weight: heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, finger-prick over 6 months and above 10 kg. On the heel the lancet goes on the medial or lateral plantar surface. In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance is 3.32 mm there, only 2.33 mm at the posterior heel, which is to be avoided, and 2.19 mm at the toe.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's veins are small and hard to see. Which measures can improve the chance of success before the puncture?
opciones: Tapping the skin over the vein and applying a warm compress or briefly soaking the limb in warm water
Applying an ice pack for up to 15 minutes each hour so the vein wall becomes firmer
Keeping the tourniquet in place for two to three minutes so the veins fill completely
Asking the patient to fast for 12 hours and avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Measures that help include ballotting or tapping the skin over the vein, followed by antiseptic preparation, and applying a warm compress or soaking the limb briefly in warm water, along with good positioning and lighting. Ice is first aid for a bruise, a two-to-three-minute tourniquet exceeds both the WHO and StatPearls limits, and the fasting rules concern the tests, not vein visibility.

preguntas.pregunta: In a study of blood donors, how often did bruising and haematoma appear at the puncture site?

In about fifty per cent of the donors studied
In under one per cent of the donors studied
In about thirty per cent of the donors studied

preguntas.pregunta: A patient brings in a 24-hour urine container that he kept on the kitchen counter for the whole collection day. What was wrong?
opciones: The container should have been kept refrigerated or in a cool place throughout the collection period
The container should have been kept frozen, since freezing preserves urine better than refrigeration
The urine should have been carried to the laboratory after each void instead of being pooled at home
The container should have been kept at body temperature and delivered within 30 minutes of the last void
preguntas.explicacion: During a 24-hour collection the capped container stays in the refrigerator or a cool place, and the sample is kept refrigerated throughout the period; a preservative may be added by the laboratory to stabilize it. preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is the ear lobe used as a capillary sampling site?
opciones: Rarely, in mass screening or research studies
Routinely, as the preferred adult capillary site
In neonates, as the alternative to the heel
In children who walk and have callused feet
preguntas.explicacion: Capillary sampling may be done from a finger, heel or, rarely, an ear lobe. The finger is the usual site in an adult, the sides of the heel are used only in paediatric and neonatal patients, and ear lobes are sometimes used in mass screening or research studies. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to take a breath alcohol test and has just finished a cigarette. What waiting rule applies?

Wait 15 minutes after smoking, and 1 minute after an alcoholic drink
Wait 15 minutes after smoking, and 15 minutes after an alcoholic drink
Wait 2 hours after smoking, as for a hydrogen breath test

preguntas.pregunta: A patient denies any latex allergy but says bananas and avocados make her mouth itch. How should that be handled?
opciones: Treat her as at risk for a latex reaction and ask further before using latex items
Fruit allergies are unrelated to latex; proceed with the standard latex gloves
Only a chestnut allergy is linked with latex, so no precaution is needed here
She must have a skin prick test for latex before any draw can take place
preguntas.explicacion: Some people with latex allergy also react to foods whose proteins resemble those in latex, the latex-fruit syndrome; bananas, avocado and chestnuts are the most strongly linked, with kiwi, peaches, nectarines, celery and melons less so, and the association runs in both directions. Skin prick testing for latex is not available in the United States for lack of an approved reagent.

No extra step; a waived analyzer needs controls only with each new lot or shipment, wherever it is used
Recalibrate it at the event using a patient sample of known value brought along from the clinic
Run it for 30 minutes without samples at the event so its internal temperature stabilizes

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR tube is filled only two thirds of the way. What effect does the short fill have on the reading?
opciones: Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out higher
Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out lower
The citrate is diluted and the red cells stop stacking altogether
The plasma layer disappears and no reading at all can be taken

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory validating its own storage limits asks how long nasopharyngeal swabs in viral transport medium have been shown to hold up at room temperature.

As long as three days for one coronavirus target, and no longer for any other
As long as three weeks for every respiratory virus target that was studied

preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits she ate a biscuit two hours ago before a fasting panel. What does the guidance say happens next?

She waits in the department for two more hours and is then drawn
She is drawn now, and the result is reported with a comment on diet

preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to say so if they ate or drank before the test, and that it may need to be rescheduled for a time when they can fast, so the results come out accurate. preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes himself as 'queer'. May staff use that word to describe him?
opciones: Follow the patient's lead, but staff should not use such terms to describe him
Use the same word in the chart, since the patient chose it himself
Correct the patient and suggest the clinical term 'homosexual' instead
Avoid noting any description of the patient's orientation in the record
preguntas.explicacion: Members of the LGBTQ community may use words like queer or gay for themselves, but the same words are considered derogatory when a provider uses them to describe a patient; staff listen, follow the patient's lead, and ask how the patient and partner should be described, then record the agreed terms. 'Homosexual' is listed as a term that has been replaced.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no insurance arrives at an emergency department in crisis. Which federal law applies?
opciones: The one requiring an attempt to stabilize, whatever the ability to pay
The one requiring a written estimate before any care is given
The one requiring transfer to a public hospital within the hour
The one requiring the plan to be billed before treatment begins
preguntas.explicacion: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act, enacted as part of a budget reconciliation law, requires organizations that provide at least a third of their services as emergency services to attempt to stabilize an emergency condition regardless of the patient's ability to pay. It came about because patients known or suspected to be unable to pay were being refused. The law leaves each organization to interpret what counts as an emergency and when a patient is stable enough to stop.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation specimen is about to leave the ward. Which details are required on the tube and on the request slip?
opciones: Name, medical record number or date of birth, collection date and specimen source
Name, insurance policy number, ordering clinic and the room where blood was drawn
Name and medical record number only, since the laboratory time-stamps arrival itself
Name, date of birth and the phlebotomist's initials, with no need for the collection date
preguntas.explicacion: Results depend on specimen quality, and the labelling asked for on both the tube and the slip is the patient's name, the medical record number or date of birth, the date of collection and, where it applies, the source of the specimen. Arrival time in the laboratory does not replace those fields.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a central venous catheter is suspected of having a catheter-associated bloodstream infection. How should the blood cultures be obtained?
opciones: One set by peripheral venipuncture and one set through the catheter
Only through the catheter, since that is where the infection is suspected
Only by peripheral venipuncture, because catheters are never used for cultures
Two sets through the catheter, one from each lumen
preguntas.explicacion: Peripherally drawn cultures are preferred over catheter-drawn ones because they are contaminated less often, with one exception: when a catheter-associated bloodstream infection is suspected, both a peripheral draw and a catheter draw are indicated. Drawing only from the catheter loses the comparison, and ruling catheters out altogether ignores the exception the CDC states.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting blood work asks the phlebotomist whether to skip the morning blood-pressure pill. What is the right guidance?
opciones: Take usual medicines unless the provider said to stop, and tell the provider of every medicine, vitamin and supplement
Skip all medicines on the morning of a fasting test, since swallowing any pill counts as breaking the fast
Take prescription medicines but stop vitamins and supplements, which are the only products that alter results
Take the pill only if it can be swallowed without water, because liquids are not allowed during the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to ask their provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines may be taken, and never to stop a medicine unless the provider says so; for some tests the provider will ask them to hold a drug, and the phlebotomist does not make that call. Vitamins and supplements are reported too, because some medicines raise or lower blood glucose and can change a result drawn too soon after a dose. Plain water is allowed throughout the fast.

preguntas.pregunta: For an infection to be classified as healthcare-associated (nosocomial), which condition must be met?
opciones: The patient was admitted for a reason other than that infection
The infection was acquired from a healthcare worker rather than from equipment
The infection appeared within 24 hours of admission to the facility
The infection is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: Healthcare-associated infections are infections acquired in health-care facilities, and the defining condition is that the patient was admitted for some reason other than the infection. They are often linked to surgery or invasive procedures that give pathogens a portal of entry, and to contaminated equipment such as catheters and ventilators; in 2011 more than 720,000 occurred in U.S. hospitals, with surgical sites and pneumonia each about 22 percent. The source may be equipment, staff or the environment, the organism need not be resistant, and there is no 24-hour cutoff in the definition.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Healthcare-Associated (Nosocomial) Infections

preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage of the evacuated tube system arises after the draw rather than during it?
opciones: Reusing the tube holder risks a needle-stick while it is taken apart
Reusing the tube holder risks a haemolysed specimen in the next tube
Filling several tubes risks losing the vacuum in the last of them
Filling several tubes risks carrying additive back into the syringe
preguntas.explicacion: Among the drawbacks listed for vacuum systems is that reuse of the needle holder creates a needle-stick risk during disassembly, which happens once the blood is already drawn. Skill in use, mixing components from different makers and higher cost are the other entries on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: Incompatibility between the barcode print area size or symbology on the wristband or label and the scanner settings
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding is recommended as an evidence-based best practice because it reduces identification errors in specimens and testing, yet the laboratory observed that scanners occasionally misread patient identification barcodes when the print area size or the symbology on the wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner settings. Its internal nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?
opciones: Leave the cap on a surface, guide the tip in with one hand, then secure it
Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered
Hold the cap with forceps and press the needle down onto a firm surface
preguntas.explicacion: The cap is left resting on a surface, or set against a firm upright surface with its opening facing the worker, and the used tip is guided into it with one hand only. The needle and syringe are then lifted vertically and the other hand fixes the cap once the tip is covered.

preguntas.pregunta: How much blood should one adult blood culture set contain per venipuncture, according to the CDC?
opciones: 20 to 30 mL, which may require more than two bottles
10 to 20 mL, which always fits in exactly two bottles
40 to 60 mL, which requires four bottles in all
5 to 10 mL, which fits in a single aerobic bottle
preguntas.explicacion: An adult set should hold 20 to 30 mL of blood collected by venipuncture, and depending on the culture system and the institution's policy that can take more than two bottles. The 40 to 60 mL range is the total the CDC wants from at least two sets drawn within 24 hours, not the content of one set. Ten millilitres is the target for a single bottle, not for a set.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on omeprazole and a recent course of antibiotics is booked for a urea breath test. What has to happen first?
opciones: Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 2 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 4 full weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 days and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 days
Only the antibiotic has to stop, for 4 weeks; acid suppressants do not interfere
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics and bismuth compounds are stopped at least 4 weeks ahead, and proton pump inhibitors and sucralfate at least 2 weeks ahead, because all of them suppress the urease activity the test measures and produce a false negative. Histamine-2 blockers are ideally held 24 to 48 hours beforehand. Plain antacids are allowed and do not interfere.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urea Breath Test", Procedures (Urea Breath Test)

preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist greets an 80-year-old as 'dear' and starts explaining quickly. Which recommendations for older patients does this ignore?
opciones: Use formal address such as Mr. or Ms. unless told otherwise, and do not hurry the patient
Use first names to build trust, and keep the explanation brief so the patient is not overloaded with detail
Address the accompanying relative first, since older patients usually defer to family members
Use medical terminology, since older patients expect a professional register from clinical staff
preguntas.explicacion: Speak to the patient as a fellow adult, defaulting to formal terms such as Mr. or Ms. and avoiding familiar words like 'dear', which can be perceived as disrespectful. Do not hurry: speak more slowly, do not interrupt, and use plain language rather than medical terminology. A companion's role is checked with the patient first, to protect privacy.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, key communication tips and Families and caregivers

preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: Pictograms on shipped containers consist of a red square frame set on a point with a black hazard symbol on a white background, wide enough to be clearly visible. An empty red frame with no symbol is not a pictogram and is not permitted on the label. The fluorescent orange label with the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are required by the Department of Transportation for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the fingerprint lines
On the centre of the fingertip pad, parallel to the fingerprint lines
On the side of the ball of the finger, parallel to the fingerprint lines
Over the tip of the finger next to the nail, perpendicular to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: The finger-prick goes on the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the lines of the fingerprint. Heel-pricks go to the medial or lateral plantar surface. The puncture should be made with one quick, continuous and deliberate stroke so that flow is good and the puncture does not have to be repeated.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasting since midnight reports a dull headache. Which mechanisms are proposed for it?
opciones: Low blood sugar, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal
Low blood sugar, high potassium and a raised cortisol
Dehydration, low iron stores and a raised cortisol
Caffeine withdrawal, high potassium and low iron stores
preguntas.explicacion: A tension-type headache is described as a notable effect at the beginning of a fast. Its precise cause has not been identified, and the mechanisms proposed for it are hypoglycaemia, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal. That is one more reason a fasting draw is scheduled early in the morning, so most of the fasting time passes during sleep.

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the thoracic cavity, medially between the lungs in the mediastinum, inside its own pericardial sac; the base is at the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex lies just left of the sternum between the fourth and fifth ribs, with about two thirds of the mass to the left of the midline. That position matters when placing a stethoscope on the chest.

preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which empties into the cephalic and the basilic veins, the two main superficial channels of the limb.
