opciones: The social security number or the patient's address
The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The colour of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place

preguntas.pregunta: When must a provider with a direct treatment relationship give a new patient its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: No later than the first service delivery, with a good-faith effort to obtain acknowledgment
Within 60 days of the first visit, by mail to the patient's home address
Only when the patient asks for it, since posting the notice in the office is sufficient by itself
At the first visit, and the patient must sign it before any care may be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.520(c)(2) requires a covered provider with a direct treatment relationship to give the notice no later than the date of first service delivery, electronic service included, or as soon as practicable after an emergency; to make a good-faith effort to obtain a written acknowledgment of receipt and, if it fails, to document the attempt and the reason; and to have the notice available on site and posted prominently. The acknowledgment is sought, not made a condition of care. Sixty days is the window for a health plan without a website to distribute a materially revised notice.

preguntas.pregunta: Surgical caps or hoods and shoe covers are required by the standard in which situation?
opciones: When gross contamination can reasonably be anticipated, as in autopsies
When performing any vascular access procedure on an uncooperative patient
When splashes to the eyes, nose or mouth can reasonably be anticipated
When entering the room of a patient placed on Contact Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(xii) reserves caps, hoods, shoe covers and boots for situations where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, and gives autopsies and orthopaedic surgery as the examples. An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why the tubes cannot simply be filled in whatever order is convenient. What reason does the WHO give in Step 8 for a fixed order of draw?
opciones: It prevents the additive in one tube from being carried over into the next tube
It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the correct order to avoid cross-contamination of additives from one tube to the next. The clotting time of 10 to 15 minutes is a processing detail for red tubes, not a reason for the order; and platelet clumping is the reason Chapter 7 gives for the reversed skin-puncture order, not for venipuncture.

preguntas.pregunta: The same hospital had earlier published rejection figures for its routine core laboratory rather than the emergency one. Which reason topped that list?
opciones: Clotted specimens, followed by inadequate volume
Hemolysed specimens, followed by clotted ones
Misidentified specimens, followed by lipemic ones
Improper containers, followed by delayed transport
preguntas.explicacion: In the core laboratory clotted specimens caused 55.8 % of all rejections and inadequate volume 29.3 %, a pattern the authors describe as similar to the emergency laboratory data. Most of those clotted tubes came from adult inpatient services, 54.3 %, and then from paediatric inpatient services, 26.8 %, which points the training effort at the wards rather than at the laboratory.

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency department reports that 15 % of its blood samples are hemolysed. How does that compare with published figures?
opciones: It sits inside the 6 to 30 % range reported for emergency departments, far above the 2 % ASCP benchmark
It is below the 20 % benchmark set by the ASCP for samples drawn during intravenous placement
It is unusually high, since emergency departments typically report hemolysis in fewer than 3 % of samples
It matches the 13 to 14 % rate expected for any sample sent through a pneumatic tube system
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency department blood samples carry a hemolysis rate of 6 to 30 %, much higher than the 2 % benchmark of the American Society for Clinical Pathology; in the pneumatic tube study the ED rate was about 13.5 % against roughly 3 % elsewhere in the hospital, a difference the authors tie to drawing blood during IV placement rather than by straight stick. The 13 to 14 % figure was that hospital's rate, not a rate caused by the tube system.

preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a lancing device for a fingerstick glucose test, what depth setting is advised?
opciones: No more than 2.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
No more than 3.0 mm, to minimize the risk of bone injury
At least 2.4 mm, to guarantee a drop large enough for the strip
The deepest setting on the first finger, then shallower on repeats
preguntas.explicacion: For a capillary glucose test the lancing device depth is set to no more than 2.0 mm to minimize the risk of bone injury; newer lancing devices cause less pain than older systems. Modern meters need only 0.3 to 1 microlitre of blood, so a deep puncture is not needed for the strip. The general limit for any finger-prick is 2.4 mm.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: A liquid Category B specimen is being packed for shipment. Where does the absorbent material go, and how much is needed?
opciones: Between the primary receptacle and the secondary packaging, enough to absorb all of it
Between the secondary packaging and the outer box, enough to absorb the whole contents
Between the primary receptacle and the secondary packaging, enough to absorb about half
Inside the primary receptacle alongside the specimen, enough to absorb the whole contents
preguntas.explicacion: For liquids, both the primary receptacle and the secondary packaging must be leakproof, and absorbent material goes between them in a quantity able to take up the entire contents of the primary receptacles without spoiling the cushioning or the outer packaging. Several fragile primary receptacles in one secondary must be wrapped or separated. Ice and dry ice go outside the secondary packaging or in an overpack.

preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer keep the medical record it maintains for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus 30 years
For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iv) requires the records of paragraph (h) to be kept at least for the length of employment plus 30 years, following 29 CFR 1910.1020. The record itself holds the employee's name, hepatitis B vaccination status and dates, results of examinations and follow-up, the employer's copy of the written opinion and the information sent to the healthcare professional. Three years is the retention of training records in (h)(2)(ii); six years is the HIPAA documentation period in 45 CFR 164.530(j), a different regulation.

preguntas.pregunta: Which non-verbal behaviours signal active listening during the patient interview?
opciones: Eye contact, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient
Standing at a right angle to the patient, near the exit
Sitting at a safe distance and avoiding eye contact
Typing notes while nodding so the patient keeps talking
preguntas.explicacion: The table pairs expression, stance and gestures: eye contact and facial expressions that show interest, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient. Its footnote reserves distance and caution with eye contact for patients with psychosis or paranoia, and standing at a right angle near an exit is a de-escalation technique for agitation. NIA separately warns against talking while typing.

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a grey tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing poorly from a heel-prick in a cold, fussy infant. Which measure improves flow?
opciones: Keep the child warm, swaddled, with only the puncture extremity exposed; warmth can raise flow up to sevenfold
Lower the heel below the level of the heart for two minutes so gravity fills the capillary bed
Squeeze the heel rhythmically at the puncture itself until a steady stream of blood appears
Switch to a 25-gauge butterfly on the dorsal hand, which the WHO prefers when a heel-prick fails
preguntas.explicacion: The child is kept warm by removing as few clothes as possible, swaddling an infant in a blanket and having a caregiver hold the infant with only the sampling extremity exposed; warmth may increase blood flow by as much as sevenfold, with warm cloths on the site. Squeezing causes haemolysis, and 25-gauge or thinner needles are to be avoided.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.2.2 and 7.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact concern: if contamination by tissue fluids or thromboplastins is possible, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. That keeps the sequence of the table intact, because the plain tube is position 2 and citrate is position 3. EDTA is far down the list at position 8, and citrate never moves to the end.

preguntas.pregunta: A sputum specimen for molecular bacterial testing is too thick to pipette and cannot be run today. Which pair of handling points applies?
opciones: Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to a week
Thin it with sterile saline; hold it at room temperature for up to a week
Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; freeze it at −20 °C the same day
Thin it with buffered glycerol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to three days
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is one of the viscous specimen types that jam automated pipetting, and the additives named for it are N-acetyl l-cysteine and dithiothreitol; homogenisation with inert beads in sterile buffer is the physical alternative. For storage the general guideline is 4 to 8 °C for up to seven days, with below −70 °C reserved for keeping it as long as twelve months.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 5

preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.2 Comparison of Arteries and Veins; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse

preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is advanced beyond the needle tip before the needle is withdrawn from the vein, so what comes out of the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Examples of Safety Device Designs

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?
opciones: Consent should be a two-way talk with time to ask questions and reflect
Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits
preguntas.explicacion: The improper methods singled out are discussing the procedure shortly before it happens, taking consent in the preoperative holding area, and taking it while the patient is medicated or on the point of falling asleep. What is called for instead is a structured two-way dialogue in a clinic or office, leaving the patient time to ask questions and reflect.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Time Pressures

preguntas.pregunta: Under ISO 15189, at what point does the preanalytical phase end?
opciones: When the analytical examination begins
When the laboratory receives the specimen
When the specimen has been centrifuged
When the request is entered into the LIS
preguntas.explicacion: The ISO 15189 definition runs the preanalytical phase in chronological order from the clinician's request through preparation and identification of the patient, collection of the primary sample and transport to and within the laboratory, and ends it when the analytical examination begins. Receipt, centrifugation and order entry all happen inside that span, not at its end.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?
opciones: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room
preguntas.explicacion: The five moments are before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic procedure, after exposure to body fluids or after removing gloves, after contact with the patient, and after contact with the patient's immediate surroundings. Preparing the skin for a puncture is the aseptic procedure itself, so the hand hygiene belongs before it, not only at the start of the encounter. The three moments that begin with after come later and are counted separately.

preguntas.pregunta: Which organization created the first patient bill of rights, in 1973?
opciones: The American Hospital Association (AHA)
The American Medical Association (AMA)
The American Cancer Society (ACS)
The Joint Commission (TJC)
preguntas.explicacion: The American Hospital Association produced the first patient bill of rights in 1973, a document about relationships between patients, professionals and organizations that carried little enforceability. The American Cancer Society also produced one in the same decade, and the AMA did not publish a list of patient rights until 2017. Such bills remain non-enforceable.

preguntas.pregunta: A technologist telephones a critical potassium result to a nurse. According to the Joint Commission International communication goal, what must the receiver do?
opciones: Write down the result, read it back, and confirm that what was written is accurate
Repeat the result aloud once and hang up so the physician can be notified as quickly as possible
Enter the result in the chart and ask the laboratory to send a written copy later
Ask a second nurse to listen in on the call as a witness to the reported value
preguntas.explicacion: The second international patient safety goal requires a procedure for verbal and telephone orders and for critical results: the receiver writes down or enters the complete result, reads it back, and both parties confirm that the written value and the read-back are accurate. A single repetition, a later written copy or a second listener do not complete the write-down / read-back / confirm sequence that surveyors look for.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
opciones: It may be compartment syndrome, which can threaten the limb and life
It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. It is described as life-threatening and needing emergency care, sometimes surgery.

preguntas.pregunta: Having measured an overall specimen rejection rate of 6 %, a laboratory sets itself a target below 2 %. Which two measures did it adopt to get there?
opciones: Monthly documentation of rejected samples and training where rejection is worst
Automatic acceptance of borderline samples and a monthly report to the medical director
A separate set of rejection criteria for the night shift and longer storage of rejects
Weekly rotation of the accessioning secretaries and a stricter barcode reading policy
preguntas.explicacion: The plan to bring 6 % down below 2 % rested on two things: enhanced documentation of every rejected sample, reviewed monthly, and periodic training organised for the departments with the highest rejection rates. Identifying and documenting the problem is described as the first step in improving quality; loosening the criteria would only move the error further down the line.

preguntas.pregunta: A lumbar puncture yields three numbered sterile tubes. Which tube is routinely designated for microbiological culture and sensitivity?
opciones: Tube 2, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 3, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 2 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to cytology and tube 3 to chemistry and serology
preguntas.explicacion: Cerebrospinal fluid collected under strict asepsis, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5, is distributed into three sterile tubes: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytological examination. Processing has to be immediate, because delay degrades the cells and shifts the biochemical values, glucose in particular, so a mis-sent tube costs time the specimen does not have.

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant records a rapid strep result in the log as '+'. What does the record-keeping guidance say?
opciones: Qualitative results are recorded in words or abbreviations, such as 'Positive' or 'Pos', not as symbols
A '+' is acceptable as long as the cover page of the log has a key that explains what each symbol means
Symbols are preferred for qualitative results because they save space and they cannot be misspelled
Only the final result is recorded; a first result that was invalid is omitted so that the log stays clean
preguntas.explicacion: Results are recorded accurately and kept as a permanent record with enough detail to be retrieved. Quantitative results carry the units of measurement given in the manufacturer's instructions, and qualitative results are written as words or abbreviations rather than symbols: 'Positive' or 'Pos', 'Negative' or 'Neg', 'Reactive' or 'R', 'Non-reactive' or 'NR'. Invalid or unacceptable results are recorded too; the test is repeated and only the final acceptable result is reported.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Recording Results
preguntas.subtema: Recording qualitative results · CPT D5 k94 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss does not catch the instructions before the draw. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Face her at eye level and speak clearly in a normal tone, without raising the voice
Raise the voice and lift the pitch so the words carry over the background noise
Repeat the same sentence faster, since a shorter run of speech is easier to follow
Ask the relative who came with her to interpret, rather than saying it again herself
preguntas.explicacion: Shouting distorts the sounds of speech and can read as anger, and a high-pitched voice is harder to hear, so the advice is a clear normal tone with the face visible at eye level for lip reading and visual cues. Background noise should be reduced, and a notepad kept handy for the words that matter, such as the test being drawn.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits

preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told in the 2 days before an endocervical culture?
opciones: No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and empty the bladder and bowel
No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and drink water to fill the bladder
No tub baths and no tampons, and take a dose of an antifungal cream the night before
No solid food after midnight, and empty the bladder and bowel just before the examination
preguntas.explicacion: For the 2 days ahead the patient avoids creams or medicines in the vagina, douching and intercourse, and she empties bladder and bowel before the examination. The provider then uses a speculum to see the cervix and swabs mucus and cells from the endocervix, the part at the opening of the uterus. Douching is discouraged in general because it can cause infection.

preguntas.pregunta: A state laboratory reports a newborn screening specimen as unacceptable. Who is responsible for repeating it?
opciones: The submitting hospital, which contacts the parents and repeats it
The state laboratory, which sends a mobile collector to the family's home
The parents, who must return to any clinic within 30 days of the report
The pediatrician of record, who is billed for the second card and collects it
preguntas.explicacion: Under the program rules, the laboratory contacts the submitting hospital to request a repeat screen, the submitting hospital is responsible for repeating unacceptable samples and for contacting the parents, and it submits a second screen before the infant is one week old. preguntas.pregunta: Which container is exempt from the biohazard labeling requirement of the standard?
opciones: A unit of blood labeled as to contents and released for transfusion
A refrigerator that stores specimens of blood awaiting testing
A sharps container that is only one-quarter full
A bag of regulated waste that is going to an off-site incinerator
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(F) exempts containers of blood, blood components or blood products that are labeled as to their contents and released for transfusion or other clinical use; (g)(1)(i)(G) also exempts individual containers placed inside a labeled container, and (g)(1)(i)(I) waste that has already been decontaminated. preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how soon a urine culture will tell which organism is growing. What is the usual answer?
opciones: In 24 to 48 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 2 to 4 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 48 to 72 hours, the incubation time the plates need before any organism can be identified
In about a week, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is plated with a calibrated loop on media such as blood agar and MacConkey agar, held at 35 to 37 degrees Celsius, and read after 24 to 48 hours; that is also how long the laboratory tells the patient the culture takes. Susceptibility testing follows from the isolated colonies. A few unusual organisms, such as Oligella urolytica, need longer than 48 hours, which is the exception rather than the routine.

preguntas.pregunta: When a safety feature has to be activated by the user rather than working on its own, how should that be done?
opciones: With one hand, and with the worker's hands staying behind the exposed tip
With both hands, so the shield is seated squarely over the used needle
After the needle is in the container, where the tip can hurt no one
By the coworker who receives the device, before the tube is removed
preguntas.explicacion: A passive feature, one that needs nothing from the user, is preferred. Where the user does have to activate it, the recommendation is a single-handed technique that keeps both hands behind the exposed sharp, and a feature the user can plainly see has engaged. Waiting until the device is inside the container defeats the purpose, since injuries also happen during disposal, and passing an unprotected device to another worker adds a second person to the risk.

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices placed for venous access rule out a site for a routine draw?
opciones: A venous port, a central catheter or an intravenous catheter
A venous port only, since catheters can be drawn through safely
An intravenous catheter only, when fluids are actually running
A central catheter only, when the line was placed within a week
preguntas.explicacion: The contraindication is written broadly: any device used for venous access, and the three examples given are a venous port, a central catheter and an intravenous catheter. preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the laboratory about a 5-hour oral glucose tolerance test to work up hypoglycemia that appears a few hours after meals. What is the standing view of that test?
opciones: It is generally not recommended, because false-positive results are common
It is the standard workup, and the only way to confirm the diagnosis
It is recommended only when the ordinary 2-hour test comes back normal
It is recommended only in pregnancy, once the 3-hour test is abnormal
preguntas.explicacion: Reactive, or postprandial, hypoglycemia is a fall in blood glucose 2 to 5 hours after a high-carbohydrate meal, early between 2 and 3 hours and late between 3 and 5. A 5-hour oral glucose tolerance test can be used to look into it, but in clinical practice it is generally not recommended for diagnosing reactive hypoglycemia because of the risk of false-positive results.

preguntas.pregunta: One hour after lunch, a patient's fingerstick meter reads 205 mg/dL while a venous sample drawn at the same time gives 186 mg/dL in the laboratory. What does this pattern reflect?
opciones: Capillary values run slightly higher than venous ones after meals; discrepant results are confirmed by the laboratory venous test
The meter is out of calibration and must be taken out of service until two levels of liquid control material have been run and passed
The venous sample was falsely low because it was drawn from an arm that was receiving an intravenous glucose infusion at the time
Capillary values run lower than venous ones after meals, so the laboratory value should be reported instead of the meter
preguntas.explicacion: A clinically relevant difference exists between capillary blood glucose and venous or arterial plasma values: capillary readings tend to be slightly higher in the postprandial state. Results from point-of-care capillary testing should not be casually combined with laboratory venous values, and discrepant capillary results are confirmed with laboratory venous testing, particularly in hospital. A postprandial gap of this kind does not by itself indicate a meter failure.

preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments, numbering 150,000 to 160,000 per µL
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Leukocytes are the only formed elements that are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and they are far fewer than red cells, typically 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is within range. Unlike erythrocytes, which stay inside the vessels, leukocytes routinely leave the bloodstream to work in the tissues. Anucleate discs are the red cells and fragments are the platelets.

preguntas.pregunta: Is sodium fluoride required as a preservative for a forensic blood alcohol specimen?
opciones: No, provided a sterile pre-evacuated tube is used and handled correctly
Yes, because without it the concentration climbs during storage
Yes, but only when the specimen will be stored for more than 24 hours
No, because the ordinary glucose tube already carries enough of it
preguntas.explicacion: With sterile pre-evacuated tubes filled, mixed and kept closed, no specific preservative is needed for a forensic result, and fluoride brings complications of its own. preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?
opciones: Albumin, about 54 percent of plasma protein
Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

The list is fixed by CLIA in 42 CFR 493.1291, which names the analytes and the limits that every certified laboratory must apply without local changes
The list is the one published by the analyzer manufacturer, since limits are method-dependent and cannot be changed by the laboratory or the clinicians
The list is set by the accreditation body at each inspection cycle and applies unchanged to every client the laboratory serves
preguntas.explicacion: For the laboratory to report a critical result immediately there has to be an agreement between the treating physician and the laboratory on what counts as critical, and the choice of parameters and limits hinges on which diseases the clinic or practice expects to see; ISO 15189 likewise wants the definition of critical results decided locally with the clinicians who use the laboratory. CLIA requires immediate alerting of life-threatening and panic values but sets no numbers.

preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old with paper-thin skin bruises after a routine draw. What age changes explain this?
opciones: Thinner, paler, less elastic outer skin and more fragile blood vessels, so older adults bruise more easily
The skin thickens with keratin and the veins sink deeper, so the needle tears more tissue on the way in and out
The skin loses its sweat and oil glands, so the alcohol cannot dry and irritates the puncture site
The platelet count falls sharply after 80, so every puncture bleeds under the skin
preguntas.explicacion: With aging the outer layer of the skin gets thinner, paler and less stretchy, and that because blood vessels get more fragile with age, older adults tend to bruise more easily and bruises take longer to heal. About 55 percent
About 45 percent
About 7 percent

Squeeze the wound to bleed it, then report the incident at end of shift
Cover the wound with a dressing, then wait for the source result to arrive
Apply an alcohol swab for thirty seconds, then finish the current draw

Heparin, infusion and light; at the point of care by a built-in spectrophotometric check on every strip

No: the amount of virus in the upper airway stays steady for about two weeks after onset

Use the precise medical terms so the patient learns them for next time
Hand over the printed sheet and skip the spoken explanation entirely

preguntas.pregunta: A trough level is ordered for a patient on an antiepileptic drug. When is the sample drawn?
opciones: At the lowest point of the dosing interval, just before the next dose
At the highest point of the dosing interval, just after the next dose
Halfway between two doses, when the concentration is most stable
At the same hour each morning, independently of the dose times
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration of the drug in blood at its lowest point, which falls just before the next dose is due; it matters most for drugs with short half-lives. The value shows the minimum concentration reached between doses, so it tells the prescriber whether the level stayed inside the therapeutic range all the way through the interval and, for seizure drugs, whether breakthrough seizures are likely.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides proof of identity, what must be obtained from a donor on the day of donation?

A postal address where the donor can be reached for 16 weeks afterwards
A photograph of the donor, kept with the unit's identification number
The name of a physician who can be contacted about abnormal results
preguntas.explicacion: Proof of identity and a postal address where the donor may be contacted for 8 weeks after donation are both required on the day of donation. The donor also acknowledges having reviewed the educational material, agrees not to donate if it would put recipients at risk, and is told that a sample will be tested and that deferral would be notified. preguntas.pregunta: Which foods are patients told to avoid before a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?
opciones: Red meat, cantaloupe, raw broccoli, turnip, radish and horseradish
Beets, blackberries, rhubarb, carrots and other strongly colored foods
Onions, garlic and asparagus, which change the odor of the specimen
Cranberry juice and a high-protein diet, which acidify the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Red meat carries heme with peroxidase activity, and raw produce such as turnip, broccoli, horseradish, radish and cantaloupe is rich in plant peroxidases; either can turn a guaiac card falsely positive, and about 3 days of avoidance is advised. The other lists are urine interferences: colored foods alter urine color, onions and asparagus its odor, and cranberry juice or a high-protein diet its pH. Immunochemical kits need no diet.

preguntas.pregunta: One antecubital fossa is inflamed with cellulitis and the other holds a fresh haematoma. Where does the search for a vein continue?

Through the intravenous line running in one of the two arms
In the antecubital fossa with the smaller of the two problems
In the femoral vein, which is inspected when both arms are ruled out
preguntas.explicacion: Site selection begins by extending the arm and inspecting the antecubital fossa or the forearm, so the forearm is the next place to look when both elbows are ruled out. The band comes off once pressure has been applied with gauze
The band comes off before the first tube is pushed on the needle

preguntas.pregunta: A set of blood cultures is added to an order that already includes a light blue, a lavender and a grey tube. Where do the culture bottles go in the draw?

After the light blue tube, before the lavender
Last, after the grey tube
Right after a non-additive discard tube

The CDC's procedure likewise has the culture set collected as the first draw of the venipuncture. Filling the bottles after additive tubes risks carrying additive into them, and a discard tube ahead of the bottles is not part of either sequence.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C daily and is about to do a guaiac stool test. What effect should be expected if she continues?
opciones: A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid blocks the guaiac color reaction
A false-positive result, because ascorbic acid has peroxidase activity
An unchanged result, because only vitamin C above 2,000 mg a day interferes
A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid stops intestinal bleeding for 3 days
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is a reducing agent that interferes with the oxidation the guaiac reaction depends on, so it hides blood that is really there. Patients are told to avoid more than 250 mg a day from supplements, juice or fruit, and high amounts for the 3 days before the test can cause a false negative; 1 to 2 grams daily has produced false negatives in studies. It does not stop bleeding and has no peroxidase activity.

The name of the person who decided to accept the flawed specimen
A recommendation that the ordering provider repeat the collection
The measured haemolysis index alongside every affected analyte

preguntas.pregunta: Why does a therapeutic drug level have to be drawn at the scheduled time rather than whenever the patient arrives?
opciones: The useful range is narrow: too high is harmful and too low does not work
The tube additive breaks down if the specimen is collected off schedule
The laboratory only runs drug levels in fixed batches during the day
A late sample would need a larger volume to reach the same sensitivity
preguntas.explicacion: For most medicines a certain level in the blood is needed for the proper effect: some are harmful if the level climbs too high and useless if it falls too low, so monitoring keeps the drug inside its therapeutic range. The published ranges assume a set moment in the dosing interval, such as 12 hours after the dose, which is why the clock, not the workload, sets the draw time.

preguntas.pregunta: How long does a patient usually need to fast before a blood test, and who sets the exact time?
opciones: Usually 8 to 12 hours; the provider sets it according to the test ordered
Usually 4 to 6 hours; the laboratory sets it according to the tube type
Usually 24 hours; the provider sets it according to the patient's body weight
Usually 12 to 16 hours; the phlebotomist sets it at check-in
preguntas.explicacion: The usual fast is 8 to 12 hours, and the provider states exactly how long, depending on the test, sometimes with extra instructions such as avoiding alcohol for longer. Needles, tube holders and vacuum tubes
Glucometers, lancets and test strips

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with limited English insists that her sister interpret for her. What is the correct course?
opciones: Respect the request, and also bring in a qualified interpreter to confirm accuracy
Refuse the sister and proceed only once a telephone interpreter is on the line
Accept the sister alone, because the patient has the right to choose her
Accept the sister, or her 12-year-old son if the sister has to step out

preguntas.pregunta: When taking a manual blood pressure, where is the stethoscope placed, and which artery is being heard?
opciones: In the antecubital fossa, listening over the brachial artery
At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery
In the antecubital fossa, listening over the median cubital vein
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff goes around the arm at heart level, and the stethoscope is placed on the antecubital region while the cuff deflates, to hear the Korotkoff sounds as blood returns through the brachial artery; the first sound marks the systolic pressure and the last the diastolic. The radial and carotid arteries are pulse sites, not where the cuff is read.

preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; and Fibrinolysis

Routine venous blood sampling in adults
Arterial blood gas sampling
Capillary sampling in infants

preguntas.pregunta: The only clearly visible vein in a patient's antecubital fossa forks into two branches right at the point that would be easiest to reach. What does the WHO's Step 3 say about that spot?

Insert the needle at the fork, because two branches give the best blood flow
Insert the needle just below the fork only if the tourniquet has been on for less than a minute

preguntas.pregunta: A male patient bleeds into his joints after exercise and lacks functional factor VIII. Which disorder is this, and how common is it among hemophilias?
opciones: Hemophilia A, roughly 80 percent of cases
Hemophilia B, roughly 20 percent of cases
Hemophilia C, the rare autosomal form
Thrombocytopenia, a shortage of platelets
preguntas.explicacion: Hemophilia is a group of inherited disorders in which one or more clotting factors are not produced in functional amounts. Hemophilia A, a deficiency of factor VIII, accounts for about 80 percent of cases; hemophilia B, a deficiency of factor IX, about 20 percent. Both are X-linked and typically passed from carrier mothers to sons. Hemophilia C is a rare autosomal defect of factor XI.

preguntas.pregunta: The rapid HIV test on the source patient will not be back for hours. What do the WHO and CDC guidance say about starting PEP?
opciones: Start it without waiting for results; stop it later if the source proves negative
Wait for the result, since PEP is only prescribed once the source is confirmed positive
Start it only if the worker's own baseline test is negative and the 72-hour window has closed
Skip it and rely on follow-up testing at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: Health workers should not wait for test results before taking or administering PEP, and prophylaxis can be stopped if the source turns out to be negative. The CDC says the same for the exposed person's own rapid test: if results are unavailable and PEP is indicated, give the first dose immediately and stop later if the person has HIV or the source is found not to. The 72-hour window is the deadline to start, not a period to wait out, and follow-up testing complements PEP rather than replacing it.

preguntas.pregunta: Why may a level be drawn while a patient on an antiepileptic is entirely seizure-free?
opciones: It sets a benchmark to compare against if control or symptoms change
It confirms the diagnosis of epilepsy without an electroencephalogram
It takes the place of the clinical assessment of how the drug is working
It is required before any brand may be exchanged for a generic
preguntas.explicacion: A single level can reasonably be taken while the patient is seizure-free, and it then serves as a benchmark for future reference should seizure control deteriorate or symptoms of toxicity appear. Assessment of efficacy should itself be clinical, with level monitoring used as a complementary tool; epilepsy is assessed clinically with electroencephalograms and imaging.

preguntas.pregunta: A man is having a urethral discharge culture collected. Which instruction protects the result?
opciones: Do not urinate for 1 hour before the test, and ideally wait 2 hours after voiding
Urinate right before the test, so the urethra is clear of any residual urine
Do not urinate for 8 hours before the test, and take no fluids at all during that time
Urinate a small amount into the toilet first, then hold the rest for the swab
preguntas.explicacion: Voiding washes away the very organisms the swab is meant to pick up, so the patient is asked not to urinate for an hour before the test and the swab is best taken at least 2 hours after the last void. The tip of the penis is cleaned with sterile cotton or gauze, and the swab goes about three-fourths of an inch, roughly 2 cm, into the urethra and is turned.

preguntas.pregunta: In a finger-prick on a small child, what can the parent be asked to do with the child's wrist to help blood flow?

Hold the wrist tightly throughout, as a tourniquet
Shake the hand downward between drops
Press the wrist flat, palm up, on the chair arm

preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms does the WHO describe in some vacuum-tube systems for dealing with the used needle?

One shears the needle from the hub with a small blade; another bends it so it cannot be used a second time
One recaps the needle automatically; another sterilizes it in place for reuse on the same patient

Shearing or breaking contaminated needles is prohibited by OSHA, and no source describes automatic recapping, dissolving or sealing a needle in a tube.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is a bluing agent placed in the toilet before a federal drug test collection?

To preserve the drug metabolites until the specimen reaches the laboratory
To disinfect the bowl between one donor and the next donor
To mark the temperature strip so the reading can be seen clearly

preguntas.pregunta: By what mechanism does the EDTA in a purple top tube keep the blood from clotting?
opciones: It binds the calcium in the sample so the coagulation cascade cannot proceed
It inhibits the formation of thrombin, as the heparin in a green tube does
It activates clotting on contact so the cells can be spun away from the serum
It blocks the breakdown of glucose, which also keeps the cells from clumping
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA works by chelating the calcium ions in the blood, and the WHO table describes the same action as forming calcium salts to remove calcium. Because the blood never clots, the liquid left after spinning is plasma. Thrombin inhibition is how heparin works, contact activation is the plain red tube, and blocking glycolysis is the sodium fluoride of the grey tube.

preguntas.pregunta: 'Don't worry, this won't hurt a bit and I never miss.' Which communication pitfall is this?

Unsolicited advice
Changing the subject abruptly
Responding defensively
preguntas.explicacion: The pitfalls table warns that false reassurance can cause a severe rupture in the relationship, especially when the promised outcome does not happen, which a missed vein would make obvious. preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker, the CDC puts the risk of HBV infection from a single needlestick with HBV-positive blood at which figure?
opciones: 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source's HBeAg status
0.3 percent, the same figure the CDC gives for HIV
About 1.8 percent, the same as for hepatitis C
Under 0.1 percent, since most workers are vaccinated
preguntas.explicacion: A susceptible person stuck or cut with HBV-infected blood faces a 6 to 30 percent chance of infection, and where in that range depends on the source's hepatitis B e antigen status: HBsAg-positive individuals who are also HBeAg-positive carry more virus and transmit more readily. Workers who were vaccinated and developed immunity are at virtually no risk, which is why the question specifies a susceptible worker. There is no known risk from intact skin. preguntas.pregunta: A lavender EDTA tube for a CBC arrives with a visible red-cell clot. Which handling error is the most likely cause according to the rejection study?
opciones: Poor mixing after collection and leaving the tube lying horizontally instead of upright
Centrifuging the tube too soon, before the anticoagulant had time to dissolve
Transporting the tube in a padded holder, which stops the additive from circulating
Filling the tube above its nominal volume so that the EDTA was diluted by excess blood
preguntas.explicacion: Visible clots in anticoagulated tubes, whether red-cell clots in whole blood or fibrin in plasma, are attributed mainly to poor mixing after the draw and to tubes left horizontal rather than vertical; manufacturers and CLSI ask for gentle inversion several times to bring blood and additive into contact. Anticoagulated tubes are not centrifuged for a CBC, and racks or padded holders are the recommended way to carry tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimetres. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimetres
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimetres
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimetres: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.

preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of a hazardous disinfectant arrives at a laboratory with a label but no safety data sheet. What must the employer do?
opciones: Obtain one from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible
Return the shipment unopened, since the sheet travels with the label
Write one from the label, which carries the same hazard information
Wait for the next shipment, which must include the updated sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers and importers have to provide a safety data sheet with the first shipment and with the first shipment after the sheet is updated, either with the containers or beforehand. When a shipment labeled as a hazardous chemical arrives without one, the duty falls on the distributor or employer to obtain it from the manufacturer or importer as soon as possible, and they must also supply one on request. A label alone is not a substitute: it carries a fraction of what the sheet holds.

Labeling may wait until the laboratory receives the tubes with the matching requisitions

preguntas.pregunta: How is therapeutic communication defined, following van Servellen (1997)?

A verbal exchange meant to obtain a complete and accurate medical history quickly
A written and verbal exchange meant to document that informed consent was given
A non-verbal exchange used mainly with patients who are unable to speak

Draws should be postponed until safety devices can be purchased
Needles may be reused between patients if they are sterilized first

Three degrees off vertical can lower the value by as much as thirty per cent
Thirty degrees off vertical can raise the value by as much as three per cent
Tilt has no measurable effect once the tube has been standing for an hour

preguntas.pregunta: In which layer of the cubital fossa does the median cubital vein actually lie?
opciones: In the roof, superficial to the tendon sheet that reinforces it
In the floor, deep to the brachialis and supinator muscles below
Beside the brachial artery, between the two heads of pronator teres
Under the biceps tendon, which shields it from the skin above it
preguntas.explicacion: The roof of the fossa is skin and fascia reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, and the median cubital vein runs within that roof, which is why it can be reached with a short needle. preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for PT and aPTT arrives filled to about two-thirds of its nominal volume. Applying the acceptance criteria of the emergency laboratory, what is done?
opciones: It is rejected: under-filled citrate tubes below 80 % of target volume fail acceptance because the blood-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong
It is accepted for both tests, because prothrombin time remains reliable at 67 % fill and aPTT is only slightly affected
It is accepted for the prothrombin time only, and the aPTT is cancelled with a note asking for a properly filled tube
It is topped up with blood from the lavender tube of the same patient to restore the nominal volume before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Insufficient volume gives an inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, and in citrate tubes that lengthens PT, aPTT and thrombin time and lowers fibrinogen; a clinically significant bias appears below 89 % of fill for aPTT and 78 % for fibrinogen, so the laboratory rejects any citrate tube under 80 % of target. Prothrombin time alone stays fairly reliable down to 67 %, but that does not rescue a tube ordered for both tests, and blood is never moved between tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting morning blood work says she had only black coffee and water since dinner 13 hours ago. Is the fasting acceptable?

No; the fast must be at least 24 hours, the same interval set for alcohol
Yes, provided she also avoided physical activity for the previous 24 hours

preguntas.pregunta: Both arteries and veins have three tunics. Which tunic is normally the thickest in an artery, and which in a vein?
opciones: Tunica media in arteries; tunica externa in veins
Tunica externa in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica intima in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica media in both, since both carry blood under pressure
preguntas.explicacion: The layers from inside out are tunica intima, tunica media and tunica externa. The media, rich in smooth muscle and elastic fibers, is normally the thickest layer in arteries, while in veins the media is thinner than the externa, which is the thickest layer there. Veins have less smooth muscle and connective tissue overall, which is why their walls are thinner than those of arteries.

A few minutes, the time the intrinsic pathway needs
About 3 hours, until bradykinin dilates the vessel again
preguntas.explicacion: When a vessel is injured the smooth muscle in its wall contracts sharply; the response is thought to be set off by endothelins released by the lining cells and by pain receptors, and it typically lasts up to 30 minutes but can go on for hours. Seconds and minutes are the completion times of the extrinsic and intrinsic pathways, and 3 hours is the window for thrombolytic drugs after a stroke.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory measures its stat turnaround time from the moment the specimen is received to the moment the result is reported. Which phases of the total testing process does that interval leave out?
opciones: The collection and transport steps before receipt, and the clinician's review after the report
The analytical phase, because instrument run time is not counted in any turnaround definition
The post-analytical phase, because reporting happens only after the measured interval has ended
None, since receipt-to-report is the complete turnaround time by the usual definition

preguntas.pregunta: A programme wants to document substance use over the past several months. Which matrix fits?

Oral fluid, which reflects roughly the last three months of exposure
Blood, which reflects roughly the last three weeks of exposure
Urine, which reflects roughly the last three weeks of exposure

preguntas.pregunta: The process by which leukocytes squeeze between the cells of a vessel wall to enter the tissues is called what?

Chemotaxis
Phagocytosis
Hemopoiesis

preguntas.pregunta: An alert patient with diabetes who feels shaky has a meter glucose of 48 mg/dL (2.7 mmol/L). Under the classification used for hypoglycemia, what level is this?
opciones: Level 2, below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L), the threshold where neuroglycopenic symptoms begin and immediate action is required
Level 1, between 54 and 70 mg/dL (3.0 to 3.9 mmol/L), the threshold for the adrenergic counter-regulatory response
Level 3, because any glucose below 50 mg/dL (2.8 mmol/L) is defined as a severe event regardless of the symptoms
Not hypoglycemia, since the meter's capillary sample reads about 10 % lower than a venous plasma sample would
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA scheme has three levels: level 1 is a glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) but at or above 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L); level 2 is below 54 mg/dL, the point at which neuroglycopenic symptoms begin and immediate action is required; level 3 is a severe event defined by altered mental or physical functioning that needs another person's help, whatever the glucose value. At 48 mg/dL an alert patient is at level 2.

No later than 60 days after receipt, the same limit as breach notification
No later than 15 days after receipt, the same limit as the OSHA written opinion after exposure
No later than 10 working days, with unlimited extensions if the record is large or on paper

The entity may require requests in writing if it says so. Sixty days is the breach notification limit and 15 days the OSHA written opinion; neither governs access.

preguntas.pregunta: How much of the percutaneous injury burden can safety-engineered devices avoid, and what undoes that gain?

Up to twenty-five per cent; disassembly, recapping, or not activating the feature
Up to seventy-five per cent; using them on paediatric rather than adult patients
Up to ninety-nine per cent; storing them in a tray rather than in the packaging
preguntas.explicacion: Replacing conventional devices with engineered ones can avoid as much as seventy-five per cent of percutaneous injuries. preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation test (prothrombin time) is ordered. Which tube does it require, and what is the additive?
opciones: A light blue top tube with sodium citrate, always filled completely
A purple top tube with EDTA, which also removes calcium, filled completely
A red top clot activator tube, spun so the serum can be tested
A light grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also requires a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table lists the light blue coagulation tube for tests such as protime and prothrombin time. Its additive is sodium citrate, which binds calcium as calcium salts and so keeps the blood from clotting, and the table marks it as one of the tubes that needs a full draw. EDTA works the same way on calcium, but the table assigns it to haematology and cross-match, not coagulation; the red top carries a clot activator and gives serum, which a clotting test cannot use; and the grey fluoride/oxalate tube, which also needs a full draw, is the glucose tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a routine urinalysis for a patient coming in tomorrow. Which specimen should the medical assistant ask the patient to bring, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because urine that collected overnight is more concentrated
A random specimen collected two hours after breakfast, because food raises the analyte levels
A 24-hour collection, because a single void cannot be dipped reliably for protein or glucose
A specimen collected after drinking a liter of water, because dilute urine is easier to read
preguntas.explicacion: First-void or morning urine is considered the best specimen for routine testing: the urine that accumulates in the bladder overnight is more concentrated, which reflects the kidneys' ability to concentrate and lets the strip detect trace substances that a dilute sample would miss. Random, postprandial and 24-hour collections exist, but each is ordered for a specific purpose, not for the routine dipstick.

Permitted, provided the patient requests it and the child agrees to help out
Permitted, because the pre-draw questions are short and simple
Permitted, as long as a staff member witnesses the exchange

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency patient is typed AB positive. Which blood types could he theoretically receive, and why?
opciones: Any type, since his plasma carries neither anti-A nor anti-B
Only AB+, since both antigens must match the donor exactly
Only O−, since that is the type of the universal donor
Any Rh− type, since Rh+ cells would sensitize the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The AB positive patient is the universal recipient: with both A and B antigens on his own cells he makes neither anti-A nor anti-B, and as an Rh positive person he can take Rh positive or Rh negative blood. Matched blood is still preferred, because the donor's plasma brings its own antibodies. An Rh positive recipient is not sensitized by Rh positive cells; that risk belongs to Rh negative people.

preguntas.pregunta: Which single fault explains both an unreliable clotting result and the loss of the specimen that produced it?
opciones: A clot in the tube, which uses up the very factors being measured
A tube filled to its line, which leaves the anticoagulant in excess
A tube inverted six times, which shears the fibrin strands apart
A tube kept at room temperature, which activates factor VII early
preguntas.explicacion: When a specimen clots, the clotting factors are consumed inside the tube and whatever the analyser then measures cannot be trusted. Wait until the patient asks what is going to be discussed next

preguntas.pregunta: A patient collected a clean-catch specimen at home at 7 a.m. and cannot bring it to the office until noon. What should she have been told to do with it?
opciones: Screw the lid on tightly, put the cup in a plastic bag and keep it in the refrigerator until she brings it in
Leave the cup capped on the kitchen counter at room temperature, since refrigeration would alter the cells
Keep the cup in an inside coat pocket so the specimen stays at body temperature during transport
Freeze the specimen at home and let the office thaw it later, since freezing preserves it better than cold
preguntas.explicacion: After collecting, the patient closes the lid tightly without touching the inside of the cup or lid; when the sample is collected at home it goes into a plastic bag in the refrigerator until it can be delivered. preguntas.pregunta: What sample does a fingerstick PT/INR meter use?
opciones: A drop of capillary whole blood placed directly on the test strip
Citrated plasma separated from a light-blue-top tube by centrifugation
Serum from a clotted red-top tube after the clot has been removed
Anticoagulated whole blood transferred from a lavender-top tube
preguntas.explicacion: With a fingertip method, in the office or at home, a small needle punctures the finger, a drop of blood is placed on a test strip or special instrument, and the strip goes into a small device that calculates the result. Laboratory coagulation tests, by contrast, are run on citrated plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are consumed when serum forms. Patients on long-term warfarin may be trained to self-test this way.

Switch to serum separator tubes with gel, which trap the fibrin below the barrier during centrifugation
Switch to citrate tubes filled completely, which keep the fibrinogen in solution until testing

An ordinary latex condom is acceptable as long as it is rinsed with sterile saline before it is used
Collection during intercourse is never acceptable, because the first fraction is always lost that way

preguntas.pregunta: A processor holds a separated serum tube up to the light and records it as clear. Below roughly what free haemoglobin concentration will hemolysis escape the naked eye?
opciones: About 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, below which separated serum still looks normal
About 0.5 to 0.6 g/L, the level taken as significant interference at the bench
About 1.0 to 1.5 g/L, the level at which potassium begins to climb
About 0.05 to 0.1 g/L, roughly the detection limit of the analyser
preguntas.explicacion: Once the serum has been separated, hemolysis becomes visible at a free haemoglobin of about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the concentration accepted as clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. It applies now only to patients who are already taking insulin

Once with the new shipment; a lot change and a new operator do not call for controls
Only when the manufacturer's insert makes external controls mandatory for that kit

It is high; men average about 4.8 million and women about 5.4 million
It is high; the reference count is 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter
It is normal only if reticulocytes are under 25 percent of the count

No, unless the patient pays out of pocket and in full, which removes the restriction

preguntas.pregunta: A potassium sample is flagged by the analyzer as mildly hemolysed (HK) rather than grossly hemolysed (GHEMO). How was this handled in the hospital that measured the hemolysis index on every potassium?

The result was corrected with a formula based on the index and reported without any comment
The sample was recentrifuged and the potassium was repeated before any result was released
preguntas.explicacion: In that laboratory the hemolysis index is measured on every plasma and serum sample sent for potassium; when hemolysis is detected the record shows either grossly hemolysed and rejected, or mildly hemolysed with a cautionary comment attached to the numerical result. preguntas.pregunta: After the tourniquet is released, a patient's forearm shows a scatter of red dots about 1 mm across that do not fade when pressed. What are they called?

Ecchymosis

preguntas.explicacion: In neonatal samples, where elevated bilirubin is common, the ability to detect hemolysis by visual inspection is further biased towards underestimating it; this is one more argument for automated, objective assessment of hemolysis, lipemia and icterus. To a depth equal to the distance from the nostril to the outer corner of the eyelid

preguntas.pregunta: Bleeding from a small puncture stops within minutes, before any fibrin has formed. Which step of hemostasis is doing the work, and which plasma glycoprotein stabilizes it?

The fibrin mesh, which factor XIII cross-links and stabilizes
The vascular spasm, which serotonin from platelets maintains
Fibrinolysis, which plasmin made from plasminogen carries out

So the draw can be logged as high risk and handed to a nurse
So the tourniquet time can be cut to under thirty seconds
So the patient can be given a sugary drink to break the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Specific attention is to be paid to identifying patients who are afraid of blood testing or who have a positive history of a vasovagal attack during earlier similar procedures, so that every means of acting on a vagal syncope is prepared beforehand. Simple steps such as counting down may greatly reduce anxiety, and a severe history of panic attacks may call for lying down.

preguntas.pregunta: The chemistry analyzer goes down and a stat troponin ordered from the emergency department will not be reported within the laboratory's established time frame. What does CLIA require?
opciones: The laboratory decides, based on the urgency of the test, whether to notify the appropriate person of the delay
The laboratory must notify the ordering person of every delayed result, regardless of the urgency of the test
The laboratory must refer the specimen to another CLIA-certified laboratory within 30 minutes of the failure
The laboratory may wait until the analyzer is repaired, since delays are addressed only by its accreditor
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(h) says that when the laboratory cannot report patient results within its established time frames it must determine, based on the urgency of the tests requested, whether the appropriate individuals need to be told of the delay; a stat cardiac marker is the kind of request where that decision goes toward notification. preguntas.pregunta: For printed fasting instructions handed to older patients, what is the recommended minimum type size?

At least 12-point
At least 10-point
At least 18-point

preguntas.pregunta: On palpation, a vein feels hard and cord-like from previous punctures. Which contraindication does this represent?

A vascular graft in the arm
Cellulitis or abscess
Ipsilateral radical mastectomy

A vascular graft, cellulitis or abscess and a history of radical mastectomy on the same side are separate entries in the same list, each with its own history or appearance rather than a fibrotic feel of the vein itself.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a specimen taken for a wound culture?
opciones: A special swab picks up cells or pus; for a deeper wound a syringe draws fluid or a biopsy is taken
A special swab picks up cells or pus; for a deeper wound the drainage is squeezed onto a glass slide
The wound is irrigated with sterile saline and the runoff is caught in a sterile container
A dry dressing is left on the wound overnight and then sent to the laboratory in a sealed bag
preguntas.explicacion: Wound cultures look for infection in open wounds or burns. A swab collects cells or pus from the surface, and when the wound is deeper a syringe is used to draw out fluid or a piece of tissue is biopsied. Most disease-causing bacteria are ready to read in one to two days, though some need five days or more. A skin or nail culture is collected with a swab or blade instead.

preguntas.pregunta: Which method is preferred for diagnosing lactose intolerance?
opciones: The hydrogen breath test
The lactose tolerance blood test
The stool acidity test
A small bowel biopsy
preguntas.explicacion: Measuring hydrogen in exhaled air is the method of choice: the patient breathes into a balloon-type container, swallows a flavored liquid holding lactose, and samples of breath are taken at set times to follow the hydrogen level. Very little of it is normally exhaled, so a rise points to lactose that was neither broken down nor absorbed. A biopsy is invasive and is kept for ruling out other causes such as celiac disease.

preguntas.pregunta: A 'true' latex allergy is which type of reaction?
opciones: Type I, IgE-mediated, with symptoms within minutes of exposure
Type IV, delayed, caused by the chemical antioxidants added in processing
Irritant contact dermatitis from friction or chemical contact
Type IV, delayed, caused by inhaling the cornstarch powder on gloves
preguntas.explicacion: A true latex allergy is a type I hypersensitivity mediated by IgE antibodies bound to the rubber proteins; within minutes the patient may develop hives, wheezing, a runny nose and conjunctivitis, and systemic reactions up to anaphylaxis are possible. The processing chemicals cause a delayed type IV reaction, and irritant dermatitis is a non-immune reaction, neither of them a true allergy.

preguntas.pregunta: For which antiepileptic drugs is the trough level said to matter most?
opciones: Those with short half-lives, since the trough marks the between-dose minimum
Those with long half-lives, since the level then reflects long-term usage
Those given intravenously, since the peak arrives with the infusion
Those newly substituted between a brand and a generic preparation
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration at its lowest point, typically just before the next dose falls due, and that is called crucial for antiepileptic drugs with short half-lives, since the trough marks the minimum reached between doses. Phenytoin's long half-life is why its level reflects long-term usage, and monitoring can guide dosing when a substitution is unavoidable.

The needle may go to general waste once its safety feature is activated; the gloves go to the sharps container instead
Every item from a blood draw, gloves included, goes to the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 discards the used needle and syringe or sampling device into a puncture-resistant sharps container, and places the other items in their waste category: items that would not release a drop of blood if squeezed, gloves being the example, may be discarded in the general waste unless local regulations say otherwise. preguntas.pregunta: How far should an isolation gown reach when it is put on correctly?

From the shoulders to the hips, left open behind for ventilation
From the neck to the ankles, with the ties left loose at the neck
From the chest to the knees, over the uniform but under the badge
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the gown goes on first, outside the patient room, and it has to cover the body from neck to knees and the arms to the wrists, and wrap around the back, with the neck and waist ties fastened if the gown has them. preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks to add a test to a serum sample collected the previous day and kept refrigerated. What decides whether the laboratory can honour the add-on?
opciones: Whether the analyte is documented as stable for that storage time and temperature in that tube type
Whether the request reaches the laboratory within 30 days of the original oral order for the panel
Whether the original requisition already listed the panel to which the new test belongs
Whether the sample can be recentrifuged, since a second spin restores the quality of the serum
preguntas.explicacion: Add-on acceptability rests on stability data: studies such as the one that measured common biochemical analytes in serum separator tubes with and without gel under various storage conditions exist precisely to define the time and temperature within which a stored sample can be retested. The 30-day rule concerns written authorisation of oral orders, the original panel does not fix what may be added, and recentrifugation does not restore an analyte that has already changed.

preguntas.pregunta: When placing a peripheral IV line, how far proximal to the intended site is the tourniquet applied, and how tight?
opciones: 5 to 10 cm proximal, tight enough to engorge the veins without obstructing arterial flow
2 cm proximal, tight enough to abolish the radial pulse for the duration of the draw
15 to 20 cm proximal, loose enough that the veins remain flat until the fist is made
5 to 10 cm distal, tight enough to engorge the veins without obstructing the arterial flow
preguntas.explicacion: For a peripheral line the tourniquet goes roughly 5 to 10 cm proximal to the intended site, tight enough to engorge the veins but not so tight that arterial flow is blocked, since engorgement is what makes the vein easy to identify and cannulate. preguntas.pregunta: A tube of blood shatters on the floor of the draw room. How must the broken glass be picked up?
opciones: With mechanical means such as a brush and dust pan, tongs or forceps, never by hand
With gloved hands, since gloves are the barrier the standard requires for contaminated items
With paper towels soaked in disinfectant, so the glass is decontaminated as it is lifted
With a reusable sharps container held open, so the pieces can be swept directly into it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(D) is explicit: broken glassware that may be contaminated is not picked up directly with the hands, gloved or not, but cleaned up by mechanical means such as a brush and dust pan, tongs or forceps. WHO's blood spillage annex describes the same sequence, tongs or pan and brush for the glass, which then goes into a sharps container, followed by absorbing the fluid, cleaning with detergent and applying 0.5 percent hypochlorite. preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC describe an HIV exposure as a medical emergency?
opciones: Infection often takes hold within 24 to 36 hours, so PEP works best when begun within hours
Antibodies appear within 24 to 36 hours, so a rapid test must be done before any PEP
PEP is only effective if started before the source patient's viral load is known
The exposed worker becomes infectious to others within 24 to 36 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Infection with HIV takes hold fast, usually 24 to 36 hours after exposure, which is why patients are evaluated rapidly and the first dose is given immediately when rapid test results are unavailable and PEP is indicated. The older CDC brochure makes the same point: treatment should start preferably within hours rather than days, since animal studies suggest less benefit after 24 to 36 hours. Antibody appearance and infectiousness take much longer, which is why follow-up testing runs for months.

preguntas.pregunta: What is done first for the patient in a traumatic amputation, before the severed part is dealt with?
opciones: Airway, breathing and circulation are checked and the bleeding is controlled
The stump is rinsed with sterile saline and wrapped in a bulky dressing
The patient is walked to a chair so the injured limb can be raised
The part is searched for, since reattachment depends on finding it early
preguntas.explicacion: The patient comes before the part: airway, breathing and circulation are checked, rescue breathing, CPR or bleeding control is started if needed, and help is called. Bleeding is controlled with direct pressure and elevation, and a tight bandage or tourniquet is easier than direct pressure when the bleeding threatens life.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who faints at every blood test asks what can be done between visits. Which conservative advice fits?
opciones: Lie down at the first warning sign, drink more fluid, change position slowly
Stand up quickly at the first warning sign, drink less fluid, keep the arm raised
Lie down after the test only, restrict salt intake, and avoid all morning draws
Sit upright through the warning signs, drink more fluid, and hold the breath in
preguntas.explicacion: Management of these episodes is conservative: avoid known triggers, take more fluid to improve filling, and change position slowly. Patients are taught the warning signs and told to get themselves supine when one starts, which often stops the faint and prevents a fall.

preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time drawn through an indwelling line comes back markedly prolonged although the patient takes no anticoagulant. What is the likely cause?

Contamination of the sample by the alcohol used to disinfect the skin surface
Excess citrate from a tube that was filled well beyond its stated volume line
Loss of citrate from a tube that was inverted more than six times after filling

preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of employers regarding handwashing facilities?

Employees may substitute alcohol hand rub at any time, even when sinks are available
A sink is required only in HIV and HBV research laboratories and production facilities
Facilities must be foot- or elbow-operated and located near the exit door of every draw room

preguntas.pregunta: What symptoms result from accidental damage to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve during a venipuncture?
