Pinpoint non-blanching spots smaller than 2 mm
Pooling of blood under the skin with swelling
Lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: The medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is prone to injury during venipuncture, and accidental damage results in painful paresthesias, dysesthesias and numbness; the phlebotomy chapter adds loss of sensation over the medial forearm. preguntas.pregunta: What does wearing two pairs of gloves do for a worker who suffers a sharps injury?
opciones: It cuts the volume of blood transferred, without stopping the puncture
It stops the needle from reaching the skin when the gauge is small
It removes the need to wash hands once the outer pair comes off
It counts as an engineering control under the bloodborne standard
preguntas.explicacion: Double gloving may reduce the volume of blood that gets through during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin, so it is a way of lessening an exposure and not of preventing one. preguntas.pregunta: A patient is blood type A. Which antigen is on the red cells and which antibody circulates in the plasma?
opciones: A antigen on the red cells; anti-B antibodies in the plasma
A antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
B antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
Neither antigen; both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: ABO typing looks at two glycoprotein antigens, A and B. Type A cells carry the A antigen, and because people are exposed to A and B antigens in food and microbes early in life, a type A person has naturally formed anti-B antibodies. Type B has the B antigen with anti-A, type AB has both antigens and neither antibody, and type O has no antigens but both antibodies.

preguntas.pregunta: A preterm infant on oxygen has a moderately hemolysed serum sample with an LDH ordered for monitoring. What approach did the neonatal laboratory and the surveyed neonatologists favour?
opciones: Report the approximate LDH with a comment that moderate hemolysis affects it, rather than rejecting it outright
Reject the LDH and every other analyte on the sample, since LDH is the analyte most sensitive to hemolysis
Correct the LDH with a formula based on the hemolysis index and report the adjusted value without a comment
Report the LDH only after a repeat heel sample, since a moderate index in a newborn always means in vivo hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: LDH is a basic monitoring test in premature babies receiving supplementary oxygen and is very sensitive to hemolysis, so the laboratory may be slightly more permissive in them: raise the hemolysis borderline a little and report the approximate LDH with a note that moderate hemolysis affects it. Correction formulas, by contrast, have been shown to be unreliable.

Draw through the IV, because it spares the patient a second needle stick

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks lost when asked, 'Have you eaten, taken your pills, or had any coffee since midnight?' How should the questioning be reworked?
opciones: Ask one thing at a time, in yes-or-no form, and re-explain who you are
Repeat the whole question more loudly and quickly to hold his attention
Switch to open-ended questions so that he can tell the story in his own words
Put every question to the caregiver, since he cannot answer reliably

preguntas.pregunta: How deep are adult chest compressions, and how soon can permanent brain damage begin once blood flow stops?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin in as little as 4 minutes
About 1 inch (2.5 cm); damage can begin after 10 minutes
About 3 inches (7.5 cm); damage can begin after 2 minutes
About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin only after 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions press the adult chest down about 2 inches, 5 centimeters, fast and hard with no pausing, letting the chest rise completely between compressions. Time is the reason CPR cannot wait: permanent brain damage or death can occur in as little as 4 minutes after blood flow stops, and death can follow 4 to 6 minutes after that, so CPR continues until heartbeat and breathing return or trained help takes over. If the person has normal breathing, coughing or movement, compressions are not started.

preguntas.pregunta: Whole blood for a PCR assay cannot be extracted until next week. Which storage plan follows the recommendations?
opciones: Separate the plasma or serum from the red cells and store it at −20 °C or colder
Freeze the whole blood tube at −20 °C or colder until the extraction can be done
Keep the whole blood tube at 2 to 8 °C, where it stays stable indefinitely for DNA
Keep the whole blood tube at room temperature, since cold storage lyses the white cells
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood is not stored below 0 °C: when a frozen sample thaws, heme is released, and heme inhibits the polymerase and quenches the fluorophores used to detect the product. If extraction cannot happen within an acceptable time the erythrocytes are removed and the plasma or serum is frozen at −20 °C or colder. There is no absolute limit for whole blood at room temperature or 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage there raises the risk of hemolysis and of nucleic acid degradation from white cell lysis.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles

The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube

preguntas.pregunta: Which urine examination is disturbed when the specimen is refrigerated before it is examined?
opciones: Crystal identification, because cold precipitates phosphates and urates in the sediment
Leukocyte esterase, because cold destroys the enzyme within 1 hour of refrigeration
Bacterial culture, because cold stops growth so the colony count becomes falsely low
Specific gravity, because cold urine reads falsely high on the refractometer
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigeration is the preferred way to hold urine, but it makes phosphates and urates precipitate, which can confuse the analysis of those analytes; when crystal differentiation is requested a separate aliquot is kept unrefrigerated. Refrigeration preserves, rather than lowers, the colony count for culture, and the documented false elevations of specific gravity are from dextran, intravenous contrast and proteinuria, not cold.

preguntas.pregunta: How long should an alcohol hand rub take, and how long should hands be rubbed with soap and water, according to the CDC?
opciones: About 20 seconds for the rub; at least 15 seconds of rubbing for the wash
About 2 to 6 minutes for the rub; at least 20 seconds for the wash
About 10 seconds for the rub; at least 60 seconds for the wash
About 30 seconds for the rub; at least 30 seconds for the wash
preguntas.explicacion: Rubbing sanitizer over all hand surfaces until dry should take around 20 seconds, and with soap and water the hands are rubbed together vigorously for at least 15 seconds; either time is acceptable. preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to ensure the immediate physical safety of the patient, staff or others, never for coercion, discipline, convenience or retaliation, only when less restrictive measures have failed, and under the order of a physician or other licensed practitioner responsible for the patient. Orders must never be written as standing orders or on an as-needed basis. For violent behavior each order is limited to 4 hours for adults, 2 hours for ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, up to 24 hours in total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, and the intervention ends as soon as possible.

Draw quickly while he stands, so that he can walk the dizziness off afterwards
Ask him to watch the needle closely so that he stays alert throughout

preguntas.pregunta: Why are iron tests usually done in the morning, often after a 12-hour fast?

Blood iron peaks around 4 p.m., so the morning gives a trough value
Blood iron is stable in serum for only two hours after waking
Blood iron falls once the 24-hour glycogen stores have been used up

1.5 mm
3.3 mm

preguntas.pregunta: Blood for serological testing is drawn at a rural clinic in midsummer and sent by car to the laboratory. Which two handling points apply to that specimen?
opciones: Let the blood clot before processing, and protect the sample from extreme temperatures during transport
Centrifuge the tube immediately after the draw, and keep the sample frozen at −20 °C during transport
Mix the tube by five inversions to prevent clotting, and keep the sample at 37 °C during transport
Let the blood clot before processing, and keep the sample on wet ice during the whole transport
preguntas.explicacion: For serological testing the blood is allowed to clot before it is processed, the specimen goes into properly labelled containers, and during transport it is protected from extreme temperatures; serum for prompt serology is then stored at 2 to 8 °C, and only long-term storage or delayed transport calls for freezing at −20 °C or lower. Spinning before the clot has formed is what produces fibrin in the serum, and wet ice is the transport rule for other specimen types.

To the state health department, which requires reports of all device failures
To the Ryan White notification system for emergency response personnel

Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an insulated bag with a cold pack so that it stays chilled

preguntas.pregunta: In the cubital fossa, where does the brachial artery run relative to the biceps tendon, and where is the median nerve?
opciones: The artery just medial to the tendon; the median nerve most medial of all
The artery just lateral to the tendon; the median nerve most lateral of all
The artery deep to the median cubital vein in the roof; the nerve lateral
The artery only at the apex of the fossa; the radial nerve most medial
preguntas.explicacion: The contents of the fossa run from lateral to medial: the radial nerve near the brachioradialis, the biceps tendon, the brachial artery just medial to that tendon, and the median nerve, the most medial structure, usually passing between the two heads of pronator teres. The artery divides into radial and ulnar arteries at the apex. The median cubital vein is not inside the fossa but in its roof.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her cholesterol figure cannot be set beside the one another laboratory gave her last year. Why not?

Laboratories report in different units, and only the units differ
Laboratories keep results on file for a single calendar year only
Laboratories round the figures differently when they issue reports

preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient do just before coughing a sputum specimen into the container?
opciones: Rinse the mouth with plain water for 10 to 15 seconds and spit the saliva out
Rinse the mouth with an antiseptic mouthwash and spit the rinse out completely
Eat a light breakfast so the cough reflex is stronger and the sputum comes up
Hold the breath for 10 to 15 seconds, which loosens secretions from the airway
preguntas.explicacion: Rinsing with clear water for 10 to 15 seconds clears contaminants from the mouth, and the saliva is expelled before the patient takes three deep breaths and coughs at about two-minute intervals until sputum comes up. Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C, the rule for serum awaiting prompt serological testing

preguntas.pregunta: On a rapid pregnancy cassette, what does the built-in control line tell the operator?
opciones: That the device worked and enough sample migrated through the strip; not whether the result is right
That the whole testing process, from sample application to interpretation, was performed correctly
That the result is positive, because a control line only develops in the presence of the analyte
That the kit lot has passed the manufacturer's quality control and is within its expiration date
preguntas.explicacion: Internal, procedural or built-in controls check that the test itself is functioning: the sample volume was adequate, the fluid moved through the strip, and any electronic functions worked. preguntas.pregunta: Which statement correctly distinguishes a critical value from a STAT test result?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far it lies outside the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT result is any value that falls outside the reference range
A critical value is any result outside the reference range; a STAT result is one that was reported within an hour of collection
A critical value is a result the instrument flags as invalid; a STAT test is one that must be confirmed by a second method
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are results that fall far outside normal ranges and signal potential pathology; they are defined solely by the degree of deviation from the established normal range, regardless of the patient's condition. STAT or urgent tests, by contrast, are designated by the ordering clinician and usually rest on prior knowledge of the patient's status. Both are handled in the post-analytical stage, when findings are communicated to the treatment team.

preguntas.pregunta: How long is an exposed worker followed with HIV antibody testing after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Baseline, then periodically for at least 6 months, for example at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
Baseline and one repeat at 7 days, when the 28-day PEP course is one quarter done
Baseline and one repeat at 1 to 2 months, the schedule used after the hepatitis B series
Baseline only, since a negative rapid test rules out infection from that exposure
preguntas.explicacion: HIV antibody is tested as soon as possible after exposure and periodically for at least 6 months, typically at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months; WHO's annex uses baseline, 6 to 12 weeks and 6 months. Workers on PEP also have blood counts and kidney and liver tests before and 2 weeks after starting. The 1-to-2-month test is the anti-HBs check after hepatitis B vaccination, and a baseline test only shows the worker's status at the time of exposure.

preguntas.pregunta: For which of these exposures do the CDC and WHO guidance say HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is NOT indicated?
opciones: A few drops of blood on intact skin
A splash of blood into the eye
A needlestick with a hollow-bore needle
Blood contact with a fresh abrasion on the hand
preguntas.explicacion: Exposure of intact skin to potentially infectious fluids is one of the situations where PEP for HIV and hepatitis B is not indicated, together with fluids not known to transmit HIV such as faeces, saliva, urine or sweat. The CDC adds that a small amount of blood on intact skin probably poses no risk and that no such transmission has been documented, and its PEP guidance lists mucous membranes, non-intact skin and perforated skin as the routes that warrant consideration. Eye splashes, hollow-bore needlesticks and abrasions are all on that list.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are finger-pricks not performed on neonates?
opciones: Puncturing the fingers of neonates can cause nerve damage
Neonatal fingers have no capillary bed close to the surface
The fingerprint lines are not formed, so the lancet cannot be oriented
Neonatal fingers are callused from grasping and flow is poor
preguntas.explicacion: Nerve damage if the fingers of neonates are punctured is a listed complication of capillary sampling. That is consistent with the site table, which assigns the heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and 3 to 10 kg, and the finger-prick only over 6 months and 10 kg. Calluses are the concern for the feet of children who are already walking.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4 and Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 age as a special consideration · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 site by age

preguntas.pregunta: A patient says 'I hate needles' and begins to tremble. What does WHO step 2 direct?
opciones: Reassure the patient and ask what would make them more comfortable
Tell the patient firmly that it will not hurt at all this time
Proceed as quickly as possible before the anxiety builds further
Ask a colleague to hold the arm firmly while you perform the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says that if the patient is anxious or afraid, the health worker reassures them and asks what would make them more comfortable. Promising that it will not hurt is the false reassurance listed among therapeutic communication pitfalls, rushing ignores the patient, and holding a patient down is a paediatric immobilization technique, not a response to an anxious adult.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague leaves a needle inserted in a medication vial's septum between doses. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: It opens a direct route for microorganisms into the vial and its contents
It counts as recapping, which the bloodborne pathogens standard prohibits
It exposes the drug to light and reduces its potency within minutes
It is acceptable in a clean medication area away from patient treatment
preguntas.explicacion: A needle is never left inserted in a vial septum for multiple uses, because it creates a direct route for microorganisms to enter the vial and contaminate the fluid; vials whose sterility is compromised or questionable are discarded. The same section asks that medications be drawn up in a designated clean area away from sinks, as close to administration time as possible. Recapping is a sharps rule about the used needle's cap, a different hazard, and the objection has nothing to do with light.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for medication preparation
preguntas.subtema: Aseptic medication preparation · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7

preguntas.pregunta: An order for a child calls for four different specimen types by skin puncture. What is the best approach?
opciones: Consider venipuncture, which may give more accurate results when more than two specimens are needed
Collect all four by skin puncture, starting with blood bank so the largest volume comes first
Collect two by heel-prick and two by finger-prick, so that no single site is over-punctured
Collect all four from one puncture, squeezing gently between specimens to keep the flow going
preguntas.explicacion: If more than two specimens are needed by skin puncture, venepuncture may provide more accurate laboratory results. Capillary blood also suits only a limited number of tests because of skin flora contamination and its small total volume. Squeezing dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and raises the chance of haemolysis.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 7.1.3 and 6.1.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3P k72 · PBT II.H.2 II.I · CCMA 3E4 site by condition · NCMA 2C.5

preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube is sent to the laboratory for a prothrombin time. Why will it be rejected?
opciones: Coagulation tests need plasma; serum has lost its clotting factors
Coagulation tests need serum; the red tube gives plasma instead
The red tube clots too slowly, beyond the 60 minutes the test allows
The clot activator in the red tube binds the calcium the test measures
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation testing is done on plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are removed when serum forms. The correct specimen is a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate, which chelates calcium and holds the sample in stasis until calcium chloride is added in the laboratory. The clot activator does not bind calcium; it does the opposite, it lets the blood clot.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: A self-sheathing needle is an example of which type of control under the standard?
opciones: An engineering control, which isolates or removes the hazard from the workplace
A work practice control, which changes the way a task is performed
Personal protective equipment, which is used when exposure remains after controls
An administrative control, such as the annual review of the Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) list self-sheathing needles, sharps disposal containers and sharps with engineered injury protections as engineering controls: devices that isolate or remove the bloodborne pathogens hazard. A work practice control alters how the task is done; the example the standard gives is banning two-handed recapping. PPE is specialized clothing or equipment worn by the employee. NIOSH's hierarchy of controls places elimination and substitution first, then work practices and administrative controls, then engineering controls, and PPE last.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Engineering Controls, Work Practice Controls; NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors, Hierarchy of Controls
preguntas.subtema: Engineering vs work practice controls · CPT D1 k12 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: Which patient right is guaranteed by federal law, as opposed to a facility's own bill of rights?
opciones: The right to a copy of one's medical records and to keep them private
The right to receive any treatment the patient requests, regardless of medical necessity
The right to free care in any hospital that accepts Medicare
The right to choose which staff member performs each procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Some patient rights are guaranteed by federal law, notably the right to get a copy of one's medical records and to have them kept private and secure; many states add protections, and insurers, medical organizations and facilities publish their own non-enforceable bills of rights. Other common rights are respectful treatment, freedom from discrimination, the right to refuse treatment and informed consent. The CMS condition adds that the right to make informed decisions is not a mechanism to demand treatment that is medically unnecessary.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Summary; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Federal patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32

preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for routine monitoring. Which test and tube are expected?
opciones: A PT/INR in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PTT test in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PT/INR in a lavender tube with EDTA
A CBC with differential in a lavender tube with EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: The PT/INR is used most often to check how well warfarin (Coumadin) is preventing clots, with the INR letting providers compare results from different laboratories, and the specimen goes in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate. The PTT is the test linked to monitoring heparin, and EDTA is the hematology anticoagulant.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR), What is it used for?; and StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", Specimen Requirements and Procedure

preguntas.pregunta: A patient loses consciousness during a draw. Which set of findings fits a vasovagal episode while it is happening?
opciones: Slow pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and dry warm skin
Slow pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and a bitten tongue
preguntas.explicacion: During the event the patient is typically bradycardic and hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic, and consciousness returns without help. A bitten tongue points instead towards a seizure, which is why it is looked for afterwards along with any sign of injury from a fall.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical

preguntas.pregunta: Which two plasma glucose measurements define a standard 75-g OGTT for diagnosing type 2 diabetes?
opciones: Fasting and 2 hours after the load
Fasting and 1 hour after the load
1 hour and 3 hours after the load
30 minutes and 2 hours after the load
preguntas.explicacion: Venous plasma glucose is measured fasting and two hours after the oral load, and the 2-hour value is the one that makes the diagnosis: under 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 is impaired glucose tolerance and 200 or more is diabetes. Some protocols draw every 30 to 60 minutes for up to three hours, and a 1-hour reference (under 200) exists, but the diagnostic pair is fasting plus 2 hours.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: OGTT samples · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens

preguntas.pregunta: In a published table of critical limits for urgent clinician notification, which adult glucose values require the physician to be notified immediately?
opciones: Below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) or above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L)
Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or above 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L)
Below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) or above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L)
Below 25 mg/dL (1.3 mmol/L) or above 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L)
preguntas.explicacion: The table of adult and pediatric critical limits sets glucose at below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L), where neuroglycopenic symptoms up to loss of consciousness occur, and above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L), the range of diabetic coma with osmotic diuresis and ketoacidosis; the limits apply after confirmation by repeat measurement in the same sample. The other pairs mix thresholds from elsewhere: 70 and 54 mg/dL mark hypoglycemia levels, 25 mg/dL is the neonatal limit, and 600 mg/dL characterizes the hyperosmolar state.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification (EJIFCC 2003), Table 1 (Glucose); Table 3 (neonatal); StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Glucose critical limits · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.d

preguntas.pregunta: The WHO pre-draw interview asks specifically about allergies to which three items?
opciones: Latex, povidone iodine and tape
Latex, alcohol and chlorhexidine
Bananas, avocado and kiwi
Vinyl, silicone and neoprene
preguntas.explicacion: The Annex C interview asks whether the patient is allergic to anything and tells the health worker to ask specifically about latex, povidone iodine and tape. Bananas, avocado and kiwi are the fruits of the latex-fruit syndrome, a reason to probe further rather than the question itself, and vinyl, silicone and neoprene are the latex alternatives used once an allergy is known.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cut himself badly is pale and clammy. Besides controlling the bleeding, what position does first aid recommend?
opciones: Lay him flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, and cover him with a blanket
Sit him upright with the head between the knees to improve breathing
Lay him on his side in the recovery position with the legs straight
Stand him up and walk him slowly to keep blood circulating
preguntas.explicacion: Pallor, clammy skin, a rapid pulse, dizziness and confusion are signs of shock from blood loss. For severe bleeding the guidance is to get help, keep the injured part still, lay the person flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, 30 centimeters, and cover them with a coat or blanket, avoiding movement if a head, neck, back or leg injury is possible. Lying down also reduces the chance of fainting by improving blood flow to the brain. The recovery position is for someone who is breathing after CPR, not for shock.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Symptoms and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Shock position · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10

preguntas.pregunta: What safety advantage do retractable lancets offer?
opciones: They retract and prevent needle-stick injuries
They allow many samples from one puncture
They eliminate transfer of blood into tubes
They can be heparinized for arterial blood
preguntas.explicacion: In the classification of blood-drawing devices, lancets appear among the passive safety-engineered devices with a single entry: retractable, they prevent needle-stick injuries. The other features belong to other rows of the same table: multiple samples from one venepuncture and no blood transfer are advantages of vacuum-tube systems, and heparinized use for arterial blood is listed for the hypodermic needle and syringe.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1 Devices for drawing blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k54 blood collection devices · PBT II.J lancets · NCMA 2C.5 capillary equipment

preguntas.pregunta: A prospective donor's blood pressure reads 186/86 mm Hg. What does the regulation require?
opciones: The responsible physician must examine and document before she may donate
She is permanently deferred, since systolic pressure over 180 is disqualifying
She may donate, because only the diastolic reading is used for screening
She is deferred for 8 weeks and asked to return with a physician's note
preguntas.explicacion: Systolic pressure must not measure above 180 or below 90 mm Hg, and diastolic must not measure above 100 or below 50. A donor with measurements outside those limits may still be permitted to donate, but only when the responsible physician examines the donor and determines and documents that donating would not adversely affect her health. The same escape clause covers an irregular or out-of-range pulse.
preguntas.subtema: Donor physical assessment · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening

preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is a non-fasting lipid profile acceptable?
opciones: Initial risk estimation in an untreated primary-prevention patient
Establishing the diagnosis of hypertriglyceridemia in a patient
Following a patient with a family history of genetic hyperlipidemia
Assessing a patient who is at risk for pancreatitis or has it
preguntas.explicacion: Two situations sit on the non-fasting side: initial risk estimation of an untreated primary-prevention patient, and clarifying the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. The other three options are on the list of cases where fasting is preferred or mandatory, together with residual risk estimation in treated patients. The clinical question decides whether the patient fasts.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cholesterol Screening", section Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: How does the ADA guidance define an 'undue burden' that excuses a particular aid or service?
opciones: Significant difficulty or expense, judged against the entity's resources
Any cost that exceeds the fee the entity charges for the service in question
Any request made with less than 24 hours of advance notice
Any aid the patient did not ask for in writing before the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Undue burden means significant difficulty or expense, weighed against the resources of the entity, and even then another effective aid must be offered if one exists. Reasonable advance notice may be required but not excessive notice, and walk-in requests are honoured to the extent possible; nothing ties the duty to a written request or to the price of the visit.
preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Limitations; and Who Decides Which Aid or Service Is Needed
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(4) / 2027 F.1.d(1)

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep the tube holder and pulls the used needle off it with a gloved hand. Which rule does this break?
opciones: Under OSHA, contaminated needles are removed only by a mechanical device or one-handed technique, when no alternative is feasible
Under OSHA, contaminated needles may be removed by hand as long as clean gloves are worn and the tube holder is disinfected afterwards
The WHO allows removal by hand provided the needle is dropped into a sharps container that is within arm's reach
Removal by hand is permitted when the holder is reused on the same patient within two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) prohibits bending, recapping or removing contaminated needles unless the employer can show no alternative is feasible or a specific medical procedure requires it, and then only with a mechanical device or a one-handed technique; shearing or breaking is always prohibited. WHO Annex E says an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and Chapter 3 prefers discarding barrel and needle together.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)(A)-(B); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex E
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D1 1G k30 · D3 k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: After a needle has been re-sheathed with the scoop technique on a work surface, what is the next step?
opciones: Disinfect the surface, so no blood is left behind on it
Rinse the surface with water and dry it with a paper towel
Cover the surface with fresh paper until the session ends
Leave the surface as it is until the end of the working shift
preguntas.explicacion: The manoeuvre is carried out close to a sharps container and the needle is discarded immediately afterwards. Because the cap was resting on the surface, that surface is then cleaned with disinfectant so that no blood is left on it. An exposed used needle is never taken apart by hand.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique

preguntas.pregunta: What does the light green PST contain, and what kind of sample does it provide?
opciones: Lithium heparin plus a gel separator; plasma for chemistries
Sodium heparin without gel; plasma for lithium and ammonia levels
A clot activator plus a gel separator; serum for chemistries
Potassium oxalate plus sodium fluoride; plasma for glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 describes the PST as a light green tube with lithium heparin anticoagulant and a gel separator, whose gel separates the plasma at the bottom of the tube; its use is chemistries. The dark green tube holds sodium or lithium heparin without gel, the serum separator tube has gel but no anticoagulant and gives serum, and oxalate with fluoride is the grey glucose tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine was collected at 9:00 a.m., but the office analyzer is down and the specimen cannot be tested until 3:00 p.m. What should be done with it?
opciones: Refrigerate it at 4 °C; a refrigerated specimen can still be tested up to 24 hours after collection
Keep it at room temperature with the lid closed; urine is stable for 8 hours if it is not agitated
Freeze it right away; freezing stops the breakdown of cells and casts until the analyzer is repaired
Discard it and recollect; urine cannot be used for a dipstick more than 2 hours after it is voided
preguntas.explicacion: Urine should ideally be examined within the first hour after collection because cells, casts and crystals are unstable. When that is not possible, the specimen is refrigerated at 4 °C, which slows decomposition, and it remains usable for up to 24 hours; anything older than 24 hours cannot be used for urinalysis. Leaving it at room temperature favors bacterial growth, and freezing is not the described alternative.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Urine storage before testing · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a · RMA III.C.4.b.v

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO order of draw for plastic vacuum tubes, what position does the light blue coagulation tube occupy?
opciones: Third, after the blood culture bottle and a non-additive tube
First, before the blood culture bottle and any other tube
Second, right after the blood culture bottle and before any plain tube
Fourth, after the culture bottle, the plain tube and the red clot activator
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 places the blood culture bottle first, a non-additive tube second and the light blue sodium citrate tube third. The red clot activator tube follows in fourth place. Candidates often remember the citrate tube as the first tube because many draws have no culture and no plain tube, but the table itself puts two positions ahead of it.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw

preguntas.pregunta: Why are the printed circles on a newborn screening card sized as they are?
opciones: A 12 to 13 mm circle is just filled by 75 µL, so it guides the collector to an adequate volume
A 12 to 13 mm circle holds exactly one 3.2 mm punch, so each printed circle equals one laboratory test
A 12 to 13 mm circle is the diameter of a newborn heel drop, so one drop fills one circle
A 12 to 13 mm circle prevents the hematocrit from changing the volume in each punch
preguntas.explicacion: By the CLSI standard for collection cards, printed circles have an inner diameter of 12 to 13 mm, 75 µL of blood just fills the area and 100 µL fills slightly beyond the print, so the circles guide the collector to neither too little nor too much blood. Laboratories can see at a glance when a spot falls well short of the 75 to 100 µL target. Hematocrit still alters the punch.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC5580822, Hall et al., Influence of Hematocrit and Total-Spot Volume on Performance Characteristics of Dried Blood Spots for Newborn Screening, Introduction and Conclusions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening acceptability

preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's arm carries a fistula with a palpable vibration under the fingertips. What does that vibration mean, and what is avoided on that arm?
opciones: A thrill, meaning the fistula is patent; draws, venous access and cuff readings are avoided
A thrill, meaning the fistula has clotted; draws and cuff readings may go ahead as usual
A pulsation, meaning the fistula is patent; only intravenous fluids are avoided on that arm
A pulsation, meaning steal syndrome has begun; the arm is used only for capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the fingertips lightly over a fistula picks up a thrill, a vibration that means the fistula is open, and a thrill is distinguished from a merely pulsating fistula. To protect veins for dialysis, peripheral access, blood draws and blood pressure readings are kept off that side.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dialysis Fistula", sections Clinical Significance and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes

preguntas.pregunta: For a spun microhematocrit, at what speed and for how long is the sealed capillary tube centrifuged?
opciones: 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
Roughly 3,000 rpm for 25 to 30 minutes
11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 10 to 15 minutes
1,500 to 2,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: In the microhematocrit method blood is drawn into a capillary tube about 75 mm long and 1 mm in diameter, both ends are sealed with clay or heat, and the tube is spun at 11,000 to 12,000 rpm for 4 to 5 minutes before being read on the holder scale or a card reader. The 3,000 rpm, 30-minute spin belongs to the older macrohematocrit method with a Wintrobe tube, which the capillary method has largely replaced.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle is recommended for venipuncture in a paediatric patient, and which gauge is avoided?
opciones: A 23-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly) with extension tubing; avoid 25 gauge or thinner because of haemolysis
A 21-gauge straight multisample needle on a tube holder; avoid 23 gauge because it collapses small veins
A 25-gauge winged steel needle (butterfly), which the WHO prefers because it is the least painful in children
A 23-gauge hypodermic needle on an auto-disable syringe; avoid butterflies because of air in the tubing
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric venepuncture the needle is a winged steel needle, preferably 23 gauge, with an extension tube; gauges of 25 or more of 25 or more are avoided because they may be associated with an increased risk of haemolysis. The butterfly is used with a syringe or an evacuated tube with an adaptor. Auto-disable syringes are designed for injection and are not appropriate for phlebotomy.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Equipment and supplies for paediatric patients

preguntas.pregunta: How does the viscosity of blood compare with that of water, and what does that viscosity affect?
opciones: Roughly five times that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly twice that of water; it raises resistance to flow
Roughly five times that of water; it lowers resistance to flow
Roughly the same as water, since plasma is 92 percent water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is viscous and sticky, with a viscosity about five times that of water, owing to the plasma proteins and the formed elements. Viscosity is resistance to flow, and it has a dramatic effect on blood pressure and flow: honey resists flow more than water, and blood behaves the same way relative to water. Plasma being mostly water does not make whole blood flow like water.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to give a sputum culture mentions he is on an antibiotic. What is the correct response?
opciones: Record it and tell the provider, since antibiotics can affect bacterial growth in the culture
Tell him to skip today's dose, since antibiotics can affect the bacterial growth in the culture
Ignore it, since antibiotics reach the bloodstream and not the airway secretions
Postpone the collection for 4 weeks, the interval used before a urea breath test
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics can suppress the growth the culture depends on, so the medication is documented and reported; the patient is told not to stop anything unless the provider says so. That is the same rule as in urine culture, where recent antibiotics can produce a false negative. The four-week hold belongs to the urea breath test for Helicobacter pylori.

preguntas.pregunta: Under chain of custody rules, when is a sample considered to be in custody?
opciones: In the authorized custodian's own possession, in a secured place
In a locked laboratory refrigerator, whoever holds the key to it
In the courier's vehicle, once the transport form has been signed
In the collector's work area, as long as the seals stay unbroken
preguntas.explicacion: A sample is deemed to be in custody when it is in the authorized custodian's actual physical possession, in a secured place, without access by unauthorized personnel and with no opportunity for tampering. Both halves matter: an unattended specimen in a room others can enter is not in custody, and neither is one held by somebody who never signed for it on the form.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has followed a strict low-carbohydrate diet for a week before an OGTT. Why is that a problem?
opciones: The test requires 3 days of unrestricted diet with at least 150 g of carbohydrate a day
The test requires 3 days of fasting so that glycogen stores are emptied first
The test requires a low-carbohydrate diet only on the day before, not for a week
The test requires the same diet the patient will follow after diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: For at least three days before the OGTT the patient must eat an unrestricted diet containing 150 g or more of carbohydrate per day, keep normal activity and avoid unusual or vigorous exercise; a week of carbohydrate restriction invalidates the conditions of the test. The only fast is the 10- to 16-hour one immediately before the morning of the test. MedlinePlus puts it simply: eat normally for several days beforehand.

Drinking plain water during the fasting hours
Taking a medicine the provider said to continue
Brushing teeth within 30 minutes of the draw

Formation of fibrin clots in the serum, and dilution of the anticoagulant in the tube
Falsely low potassium from the catheter material, and bacterial contamination of the tube
Air bubbles that lower the blood gas values, and loss of vacuum in the evacuated tube
preguntas.explicacion: Draws from indwelling catheters or during IV starts are more prone to hemolysis than venipuncture, which the study links to flow through the narrow tube, and samples contaminated by intravenous infusion were 2.2 % of that laboratory's rejections. preguntas.pregunta: What distance separates direct droplet transmission from airborne transmission in the microbiology definition?
opciones: About one meter: droplets travel a meter or less; airborne goes farther
About three meters: droplets travel three meters or less
About six feet: droplets travel six feet or less; airborne travels farther
There is no distance; the difference is whether a mask was worn
preguntas.explicacion: When a person coughs or sneezes, droplets of mucus that may carry pathogens are ejected; direct droplet transmission covers distances of one meter or less and is treated as a form of contact transmission, while transmission over more than one meter is called airborne and is classed as vehicle transmission through the air. Fine droplets can stay suspended, travel far, and dry into droplet nuclei; tuberculosis is the classic airborne example, needing as few as 10 organisms to infect. The 3 to 6 feet figure is the clinical rule of thumb for Droplet Precautions, a different framework.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a federal drug test reads 27°C three minutes after the void. What does the collector do?

Warm the container in the hand and read the temperature again in four minutes
Discard the specimen and start over with the ordinary collection procedure
Accept it and write the reading on the remarks line of the custody form
preguntas.explicacion: A reading outside 32° to 38°C is marked as out of range on the form, and the collector then performs a second collection under direct observation, sending both specimens to an HHS-certified laboratory rather than to an instrumented initial test facility. A comment goes on the remarks line as well, but the comment alone does not make the specimen acceptable, and rewarming it is not an option.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist stuck by a used needle agrees to have her blood drawn but refuses HIV testing that day. What does the standard require of the sample?
opciones: Keep it at least 90 days so the employee may still choose to have it tested for HIV
Test it for HIV anyway, since consent to the blood draw covers the serologic testing
Discard it, since HIV testing requires a fresh sample drawn after consent is given
Keep it 30 days, the period in which the written opinion has to be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(iii)(B) separates the two consents. If the employee agrees to baseline collection but not, at that moment, to HIV serology, the sample is preserved for at least 90 days; should she decide within those 90 days to have it tested, the test is run as soon as feasible. Testing without her consent is not allowed, and throwing the sample away would defeat the purpose of the rule. The written opinion has its own deadline, 15 days, and is unrelated to the storage period.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital brings in safety-engineered devices and its injury rate does not fall. Which two problems have been reported in that situation?
opciones: Trouble working the safety mechanism, and needles still discarded improperly
Shortage of sharps containers, and gloves supplied in only one size
Poor lighting at the bedside, and tubes filled in the wrong order
Late reporting of injuries, and no written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices are widely used, but the fall in injuries has not always followed. In one study the rate went from 1.9 to 2.2 per 100 healthcare workers after implementation, and the factors reported most often were difficulty operating the safety mechanism and needles that continued to be disposed of improperly. Both are training and work-practice problems, which is why buying a device is only one part of a prevention program.

preguntas.pregunta: In the protocol for the lactose tolerance blood test, what load is given and when are the glucose measurements taken?

75 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 60 and 120 minutes
50 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 30 and 60 minutes
100 g of lactose, with glucose measured at 0, 120 and 180 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The test uses 50 g of lactose with serial glucose measurements at 0, 60 and 120 minutes, and a rise under 20 mg/dL suggests intolerance; its sensitivity is 75% and its specificity 96%. The 75 g and 100 g loads are glucose, not lactose, and belong to the oral glucose tolerance tests. The vacuum stops the flow well before the tube can be overfilled
The colour of the stopper sets the volume for every manufacturer
The laboratory calculates it from the patient's haematocrit result
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for these assays is collected into commercially prepared tubes that already hold their trisodium citrate, and each carries a line showing the volume of blood that should go in. preguntas.pregunta: A urine drug screen is run on a patient in the emergency department for medical management only. Is a chain of custody required?
opciones: No: a purely clinical result is confidential and cannot be used against the patient
Yes: every drug screen carries the same documentation, regardless of purpose
No: chain of custody applies only to blood specimens, never to urine specimens
Yes: emergency department specimens always travel under a custody form
preguntas.explicacion: The result of medical drug testing is confidential information and cannot be evidence against the individual for disciplinary or penal action, so the chain of custody is not required for it. preguntas.pregunta: A week after a venipuncture the small clot at the site has disappeared. Which enzyme broke down its fibrin, and from what precursor was it made?
opciones: Plasmin, from plasminogen
Thrombin, from prothrombin
Fibrin, from fibrinogen
Heparin, from basophils
preguntas.explicacion: The gradual removal of a clot is called fibrinolysis: the inactive plasma protein plasminogen is converted into active plasmin, which slowly breaks down the fibrin, while bradykinin dilates the vessel again. Thrombin is the enzyme that builds fibrin, not the one that removes it; fibrin is the clot material itself; and heparin is an anticoagulant from basophils that opposes prothrombin.

The tubing is flushed with the light blue tube, which is then sent as the specimen
The tourniquet is tightened until the tubing fills, then the citrate tube goes on
A red clot activator tube is drawn first so that the serum tests are not delayed

preguntas.pregunta: A bottle of disinfectant concentrate breaks on the processing room floor. Which section of its safety data sheet guides the cleanup?
opciones: Section 6, on containment and cleanup after an accidental release
Section 4, on the first aid to give after contact with the chemical
Section 13, on disposal of the chemical and of its own container
Section 12, on what the chemical does if it reaches the environment
preguntas.explicacion: Section 6 covers the response to spills, leaks and releases: personal precautions such as removing ignition sources or ventilating, the protective equipment that keeps the chemical off skin, eyes and clothing, emergency steps including evacuation and when to call an expert, methods for containment such as covering drains, and the cleanup technique itself. One negative and one positive control material
A single control material at the medical decision level
Three controls: low, mid-range and high, every 8 hours

preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory compares specimen rejections by shift over one year. What did the published audit find, and what does it suggest for training?
opciones: Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the night shift, pointing training at the staff who collect at night
Two-thirds of rejections (66 %) came from the day shift, when volume is highest, pointing training at day staff
Rejections were evenly split between shifts, so training was aimed at the units with the most samples instead

preguntas.explicacion: In the year-long audit the proportion of specimen rejections was 66 % during the night shift against 34 % during the day, even though the night shift runs with fewer laboratory staff. A mandatory report of the quality failure to the accrediting organisation
A penalty against the laboratory's proficiency testing performance that year

preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine for culture cannot reach the microbiology laboratory for about 6 hours. What keeps the culture result valid?
opciones: Refrigerating it or placing it in a boric acid preservative tube, either of which holds it for up to 24 hours
Keeping it at room temperature, which is acceptable for up to 24 hours as long as the cup stays capped
Freezing it, since freezing stops bacterial growth more completely than refrigeration does
Adding a formaldehyde preservative, the additive that best protects bacteria for later culture
preguntas.explicacion: Urine for culture must be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or placed in a preservative; both boric acid and refrigeration hold the specimen adequately for up to 24 hours. Urine left at room temperature for more than 4 hours shows overgrowth of both pathogens and contaminants. Formaldehyde is used to preserve cells and causes false-positive strip reactions, and freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration.

preguntas.pregunta: Which natural anticoagulant is released by basophils, opposes prothrombin, and is also given as a drug to surgical patients at risk of clots?

Protein C
Thrombin
Plasmin

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist working alone finds an unresponsive adult who is not breathing. What is the first step?
opciones: Call 911 (or the local emergency number), get an AED if one is known to be nearby, then start CPR
Give 2 rescue breaths, then check the pulse for 10 seconds before calling
Start compressions for 2 minutes, then leave to look for an AED anywhere in the building
Place the person in the recovery position and monitor breathing until help arrives
preguntas.explicacion: After checking responsiveness by tapping and shouting, a lone rescuer calls 911 or the local emergency number as soon as the person is found unresponsive, retrieves an AED only if one is known to be nearby, and then begins CPR with 30 compressions and 2 breaths; the rescuer should not leave the person to search for an AED whose location is unknown. With help available, one person calls while another starts CPR. The recovery position is for a person who has started breathing again, and pulse checks are left to health professionals.

Keep the latex gloves in the room but double-glove with vinyl over them

preguntas.pregunta: A seated patient becomes pale and sweaty and says he is about to faint. What should happen right away?

He should stand up and walk slowly to a couch, since the movement restores the venous return

preguntas.explicacion: Patients should sit or lie down quickly during an acute episode, with their legs elevated, to help recovery from reflex postural hypotension, and should be kept horizontal afterwards and prevented from standing too soon; any injury from a fall needs immediate attention. preguntas.pregunta: A centrifuge's power cord has a frayed section exposing bare wire. What does OSHA's electrical standard require?
opciones: Remove it from service until repaired and tested; do not use it meanwhile
Wrap the frayed section in tape and continue using it until the next inspection
Plug it into a GFCI receptacle, which makes the damaged cord safe to use
Keep using it if the equipment is grounded and the operator wears gloves
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph 1910.334(a)(2)(ii) requires portable electric equipment, including cord-and-plug equipment and extension cords, to be removed from service when there is a defect or evidence of damage that might expose an employee to injury, and it may return to use only after the repairs and tests needed to make it safe have been done. Frayed cords, damaged enclosures and bent or missing plug prongs are the examples the eTool gives of hazards that can energize a metal enclosure. A GFCI reduces the consequence of a ground fault; it does not license the use of damaged equipment.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Electrical Safety, 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(2)(ii) and 1910.303(b)(1)

preguntas.pregunta: What is placed under the patient's arm before the draw begins?
opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm compress pack
A rolled cloth tourniquet
A sterile drape with a window
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the patient includes making the person comfortable, supine where that is possible, and laying a clean paper or towel under the arm that is going to be used. Warming the limb is a measure kept for veins that are hard to find, not a routine part of setting the patient up.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory rejects a sample as haemolysed. Which collection practices are recognized causes of haemolysis?
opciones: Pressing the syringe plunger, shaking the tube, and a short draw in the grey tube
Leaving the tourniquet on for more than one minute, and drawing the tubes in the wrong sequence
Using a 21 G needle in an adult, and inverting the citrate tube three to six times
Preparing the skin with povidone iodine, and labeling the tubes away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pressing the plunger raises the risk of haemolysis, Table 2.3 warns that a short draw in the fluoride tube may cause haemolysis, and vigorous shaking or overmixing of the tube produces haemolysis. A long tourniquet causes hemoconcentration, the wrong sequence causes additive carry-over, iodine raises potassium, and three to six gentle inversions is the correct handling of the citrate tube.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Step 7 and Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection"

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, laboratory tests are sorted into how many complexity categories, and which are they?
opciones: Three: waived, moderate complexity and high complexity
Two: waived and nonwaived, with no further split
Four: waived, PPM, moderate and high complexity
Three: home use, point-of-care and laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation grades every test system as waived, moderate complexity or high complexity, from the least to the most demanding. Moderate and high together are called nonwaived testing. Provider-performed microscopy is a subcategory inside moderate complexity, not a fourth category, and point-of-care describes where a test is run, not how it is classified.

preguntas.pregunta: Which three elements must valid informed consent for a research study include?
opciones: Disclosure of information, competency to decide, and a voluntary decision
Disclosure of information, a witness signature, and an approved study budget
Competency to decide, a voluntary decision, and payment for participation
Competency to decide, a signed waiver, and a copy filed with the sponsor
preguntas.explicacion: Valid research consent rests on three major elements: disclosure of information, competency of the patient or surrogate to make a decision, and the voluntary nature of that decision. Ethical standards in study design are monitored by an Institutional Review Board, which may waive the consent requirement only where risk to participants is minimal.

preguntas.pregunta: For a term newborn who needs several tests, which sampling method is preferred, and why?
opciones: Venipuncture, which is the method of choice for term neonates and causes less pain than heel-pricks
Heel-prick, which is the method of choice for term neonates because it causes less pain than venipuncture
Finger-prick, which the WHO recommends for term neonates because the finger has no bone risk
Arterial puncture, since capillary blood already resembles arterial blood in oxygen content
preguntas.explicacion: Venepuncture is the method of choice for blood sampling in term neonates and causes less pain than heel-pricks, but it requires an experienced and trained phlebotomist; if none is available the physician may need to draw the specimen. Finger-pricks are not used in neonates because of nerve damage, and the heel is reserved for small volumes.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.1.1 and 6.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee steadies the vein by pressing a thumb on the skin just ABOVE the intended puncture point. What is the correct anchoring technique?
opciones: Place the thumb below the site and pull the skin down and slightly away, making it taut
Place the thumb above the site but press down harder, so that the vein cannot roll sideways
Use the index finger over the vein itself to guide the shaft of the needle
Skip anchoring; ask the patient to make a fist, which fixes the vein in place
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 of the WHO procedure anchors the vein by holding the arm and placing a thumb below the venipuncture site; the free hand then uses the thumb to pull the skin down and slightly away from the draw site so it is taut. A finger over the vein is what Step 5 explicitly forbids after disinfection, and the fist is an addition that makes the veins prominent, not a replacement for anchoring.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's recordkeeping rule, 29 CFR part 1904, which forms record work-related injuries and illnesses?
opciones: The OSHA 300 log, the 301 incident report and the 300A summary posted each year
The sharps injury log, the training record and the employee medical record
The OSHA 200 log, which the Needlestick Act found sufficient for exposure tracking
The exposure determination, the written opinion and the Appendix A declination
preguntas.explicacion: Covered employers record each recordable injury and illness on the OSHA Form 300 log, prepare a Form 301 incident report with details of each case, and at the end of the year prepare the Form 300A summary and post it in a visible place. The sharps injury log, training records and medical records are kept under the bloodborne pathogens standard; the exposure determination, written opinion and declination are other documents of that same standard. Congress found the old OSHA 200 log insufficient, which is why the sharps log was added.

preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a rapid test "must be waived because we run it at the point of care." What is the correct reading of the term point-of-care testing under CLIA?
opciones: It describes where testing is done and says nothing about the test's complexity
It is a synonym for waived testing when the operator is not a laboratorian
It is the category for tests cleared by the FDA for home use
It refers to a laboratory licensed by a state whose rules are stricter than CLIA
preguntas.explicacion: Point-of-care is a location: the bedside or near the site of care. Some point-of-care tests are waived, but faster technology also lets nonwaived tests be run near the patient, so a test cannot be assumed waived just because of where it is performed. Home-use clearance is one route to waived status, and the state-licensed laboratory description is the meaning of CLIA-exempt.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Related terms ("Point-of-care testing")
preguntas.subtema: POCT is a location, not a category · CPT D1 k29 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D k111 · RMA III.C.2.a · NCMA 4.12

preguntas.pregunta: How often does OSHA require an employer's written Exposure Control Plan to be reviewed and updated?
opciones: At least once a year, and whenever the tasks, procedures or positions with occupational exposure change
Within 10 working days of each new hire with occupational exposure, and otherwise every three years
Once a year together with the annual employee training, and at no other time even if tasks change
Every time an exposure incident is reported, and kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iv) sets two triggers: a review at least every year, plus a review whenever new or changed tasks, procedures or job positions alter who is exposed and how. The same review has to take in new technology that cuts exposure and document, each year, which safer medical devices were considered and adopted. The other periods belong to other rules of the same standard: 10 working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine, three years is how long training records are kept, and employment plus 30 years is the retention of medical records. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a rewrite of the plan.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(iv), Exposure Control Plan

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia was found to lack capacity two weeks ago. What does that finding mean today?
opciones: Nothing by itself: the finding held for that time and that situation
It carries over until a judge rules that the patient has recovered
It carries over for the whole admission, once it is in the record
It removes the need to explain the draw, but not to ask permission
preguntas.explicacion: An assessment of capacity is valid only within the time, place and situation in which it took place; it is a snapshot and cannot be carried across to another moment. A history of dementia does not automatically mean the person lacks capacity, and the same patient may be lucid enough today to take part in the discussion. Competence is a court's decision.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Clinical Significance, When To Access Capacity

preguntas.pregunta: To stretch a kit, a testing site cuts each rapid test strip lengthwise so two patients can be tested per strip. What is the regulatory consequence?
opciones: The test is no longer waived and falls under the nonwaived CLIA requirements
It stays waived as long as the manufacturer's reading time is still respected
The site must run external controls with every patient sample from then on
The test remains waived because only the specimen volume was changed
preguntas.explicacion: Physically altering test components, such as cutting cards or strips to multiply the number of tests, and changing the timing of a test are both modifications. A modified test is no longer a waived test and becomes subject to the stricter requirements for nonwaived testing. Running more controls does not restore the waiver; only following the insert without modification does.

preguntas.pregunta: Which item on the test requisition allows the laboratory to judge later whether a specimen was transported within an acceptable time?
opciones: The date and, when appropriate, the time of specimen collection
The date the requisition was printed by the ordering office
The time the specimen was logged into the laboratory information system
The expected turnaround time promised to the ordering provider
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA requires the requisition to solicit the date and, if appropriate, the time of collection; combined with the receipt date and time the laboratory must document, this gives the transport interval that decides acceptability for time-sensitive tests. The printing date of the form and the promised turnaround say nothing about when blood left the patient, and the log-in time is the second half of the interval, not the first.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(6), Standard: Test request

preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen for a gastrointestinal molecular panel has to travel from a rural clinic. Which transport and storage plan matches the general guidelines?
opciones: Room temperature in stabilising media, or on ice; then 2 to 8 °C for four to seven days
Room temperature without media, or frozen; then 2 to 8 °C for up to twenty-four hours
On ice only, never at room temperature; then at −20 °C from the moment it arrives
Room temperature in stabilising media only; then at room temperature until extraction
preguntas.explicacion: For stool the variables listed are time, transport and storage temperature, stabilisation media and the patient's medications. Transport is either at room temperature when a stabilising medium is used or on ice, and storage runs four to seven days, at 2 to 8 °C or at room temperature if stabilised. Freezing on arrival is not part of that general scheme.

preguntas.pregunta: What is an external control for a waived test?
opciones: A liquid or similar material resembling a patient sample, tested to check the entire process
A built-in line or window on the device that confirms the sample moved through the strip
An electronic check the meter runs on itself at start-up to verify its internal functions
A patient sample previously tested by the referral laboratory and retested on site each month
preguntas.explicacion: External controls mimic patient specimens and are run exactly like one, so they monitor the process from sample application to result interpretation and show whether results fall within the ranges printed on the control or in its insert. They may come with the kit or be bought separately. Built-in lines and electronic self-checks are internal controls; they confirm the device worked, not the operator's whole procedure.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: What are the Types of Controls? (external controls); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Types of controls

preguntas.pregunta: Who should perform quality control testing at a waived site, and how should the control material be handled?
opciones: The same people who run patient tests, treating the control exactly like a patient sample
The most experienced operator only, using a shortened version of the patient procedure
The laboratory director personally, at the start of each shift, before staff arrive
A manufacturer's representative, who ships the control results back to the site
preguntas.explicacion: Quality control is meant to catch operator error as well as reagent or instrument failure, so it is run by the personnel who routinely perform patient testing, before or together with patient samples, and the control is treated and tested just as a patient sample would be. Over time, control testing should rotate among all operators, which is also how a site sees whether a problem follows one person.

opciones: A 2003 consensus of the United States National Committee for Clinical Laboratory Standards
The 2008 CDC Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities and its annexes
The FDA classification of blood specimen collection devices in 21 CFR 862.1675

preguntas.pregunta: One draw yields a filled culture bottle and a filled citrate tube. How many mixing movements does each receive?
opciones: Eight to ten for the culture bottle and three to six for the citrate tube
Three to six for the culture bottle and eight to ten for the citrate tube
Eight to ten for both containers, since both hold an anticoagulant
Three to six for both containers, since both are drawn before serum tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Once filled, the culture bottle is mixed eight to ten times, while the citrate tube is inverted three to six times straight after the blood goes in. Vigorous shaking is avoided in both cases, since it can froth or haemolyse the sample and spoil the clotting results.

preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO say the sharps container must be during a blood draw?
opciones: Within arm's reach and clearly visible
Outside the room, away from the patient
On the floor beside the chair
Behind the phlebotomist, by the waste bag
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 ends its description of vacuum systems with the rule that the sharps container must be within arm's reach and clearly visible, so that sharps can be disposed of safely; Annex E says the needle is discarded immediately and the disassembly is done close to the container. A container that is far away, out of sight or behind the operator invites the delay that leads to injuries.

preguntas.pregunta: After fainting, a patient wakes up within a minute and wants to get up and leave. What is the correct advice?
opciones: Keep the person lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes, preferably somewhere cool and quiet
Let the person stand as soon as consciousness returns, since the episode is over
Seat the person upright at once and offer a hot drink to raise the blood pressure
Keep the person lying down for at least an hour before allowing any movement
preguntas.explicacion: Keep the person lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes, preferably in a cool and quiet space, and, if lying down is impossible, to sit the person forward with the head between the knees. Patients should likewise be kept horizontal after the event and prevented from standing up too soon. No source calls for an hour on the floor.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care; and StatPearls, "Syncope", Treatment / Management

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient arrives without warning and asks for an interpreter. What may the clinic require under the ADA rules?
opciones: Reasonable advance notice, though walk-in requests are honoured where possible
Two working days of written notice for any auxiliary aid or service at all
That the patient book a later appointment, since no notice at all was given
That the patient pay the interpreter fee whenever notice was not given
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities may ask for reasonable advance notice from people requesting aids and services, based on how long it takes to obtain them, but may not impose excessive notice requirements, and walk-in requests must be honoured to the extent possible. Responsibility for effective communication rests directly on the entity, which cannot make the patient bring an interpreter.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fasting lipid panel and mentions having chewed sugar-free gum and smoked a cigarette that morning, but eaten nothing. Does the fast hold?
opciones: No: while fasting for a blood test the patient should also not chew gum, smoke or exercise, so the provider is told
Yes: only food and caloric drinks break a fast; sugar-free gum and tobacco are permitted before a lipid panel
Yes, provided the gum and the cigarette were more than two hours before the draw and the patient drank plain water
No: smoking breaks the fast but chewing gum does not, so only the cigarette needs to be reported to the provider
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting for a blood test means nothing to eat or drink except plain water for several hours before the draw, usually 8 to 12 hours, and during the fast the patient is also asked not to chew gum, smoke or exercise. When the instructions have not been followed exactly the patient tells the provider or the laboratory professional, because even a minor deviation can change the results, and the test may have to be rescheduled.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a throat swab culture collected?
opciones: The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed at the back of the throat near the tonsils
The head is tilted forward, the tongue depressed, and the swab rolled along the inner surface of both cheeks
The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed over the tongue and under it
The head is tilted back 70 degrees and the swab passed through a nostril until it reaches the throat
preguntas.explicacion: The patient tilts the head back and opens wide while the sterile swab is rubbed along the back of the throat near the tonsils, and the provider may scrape several times to raise the chance of catching the organism. Gagging is expected and the patient has to resist closing the mouth. The tongue is deliberately avoided, the cheek is where a buccal swab goes, and the nostril route is the nasopharyngeal swab.

preguntas.pregunta: Which ergonomic risk factors does OSHA identify for laboratory employees?
opciones: Static postures, repetition, forceful exertion, awkward postures and contact stress
Noise, ionizing radiation, chemical vapors and aerosols from biological specimens
Long shifts, night work, understaffing and fatigue from emergency procedures
Latex exposure, glove powder, hand lotions and frequent handwashing
preguntas.explicacion: Static postures while sitting or standing for long periods, repetitive movements when sorting samples or using the computer, forceful exertions, awkward postures and contact stress are the ergonomic risk factors, and carpal tunnel syndrome, tendonitis, tenosynovitis and back pain the resulting musculoskeletal disorders. Pipetting, microscope work and keyboarding are the typical tasks. Noise and radiation are separate physical hazards, and latex is an allergy hazard, each with its own OSHA guidance.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders, Hazard; OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Ergonomic Hazards

preguntas.pregunta: An employee with occupational exposure refuses the hepatitis B vaccine. Which document does the standard require?
opciones: The declination statement in Appendix A of the standard, signed by the employee
A written opinion from the evaluating healthcare professional, kept for 15 days
An entry in the sharps injury log noting the department and the employee's reason
A note in the training record, retained three years, that the vaccine was explained
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(iv) requires the employer to make sure that anyone who turns down the vaccine signs the statement printed in Appendix A. Serum separators and centrifuges, since both act on the separated serum
