preguntas.pregunta: A blood gas report shows a pH of 7.40. Where does this fall relative to the normal range for blood?
opciones: Right at the average; normal is 7.35 to 7.45
Slightly acidic; normal is 7.45 to 7.55
At the low end; normal runs 7.40 to 7.50
Slightly alkaline; normal is 7.0, like pure water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood pH averages about 7.4, with a healthy range of 7.35 to 7.45, so a reading of 7.40 sits in the middle of normal. Blood is somewhat more alkaline than pure water, whose pH is 7.0, and it carries many buffers that keep the value steady. A range starting at 7.45 or 7.40 would wrongly turn a normal reading into a low one.

2 hours for adults 18 and older
1 hour for adults 18 and older
8 hours for adults 18 and older

As soon as the instrument's internal electronic check has passed for that day's run of specimens
After the result has been confirmed by a second trained operator on the same instrument

opciones: A national list recommended by the HHS Secretary, split into core conditions and secondary conditions
A federal law that requires every state to screen for the same 35 conditions with the same cut-offs
The CDC's list of conditions its quality-assurance laboratory can produce reference spots for
Each state's legally required list, which the state divides into mandatory and optional tests
preguntas.explicacion: The RUSP is a national guideline listing conditions the Secretary of HHS recommends all newborns be screened for, divided into core conditions, which every program is designed to detect, and secondary conditions, which may be found while screening for a core one. preguntas.pregunta: What makes a laboratory result protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: An identifier linking it to a specific patient, such as a name, phone number or email
Only the patient's Social Security number or medical record number, not the name
Only the result itself, regardless of whether a name is attached
Only electronic storage; a printed result with a name attached is not PHI under the rule
preguntas.explicacion: Protected health information is health information that carries an identifier linking it to a specific patient, such as a name, Social Security number, telephone number, email or street address; the Privacy Rule specifies 18 such elements, and information about a patient's relatives, employers or household members counts too. PHI covers written, spoken, paper and electronic data of any size, inside or outside the facility. A result with all identifiers removed under the de-identification standard is no longer PHI.

preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA violation carries a criminal penalty of up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison?
opciones: Obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information under false pretenses
Knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information
Selling identifiable health information for commercial advantage or malicious harm
Failing to correct a violation due to willful neglect within the required period
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal provisions have three tiers: knowingly obtaining or disclosing individually identifiable health information, up to $50,000 and 1 year; doing so under false pretenses, up to $100,000 and 5 years; and doing so with intent to sell, transfer or use it for commercial advantage, personal gain or malicious harm, up to $250,000 and 10 years. Criminal cases are handled by the Department of Justice and can reach employees, nurses, secretaries and telephone operators, not only institutions. Uncorrected willful neglect is the top civil tier, not a criminal one.

preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube arrives in the laboratory with several small clots inside. Which collection error is associated with this finding?
opciones: The tube was not mixed enough after it was filled
The tube was inverted too many times in the figure-of-8 pattern
The tube was filled after the grey fluoride tube
The tube was drawn through a butterfly without a discard
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with anticoagulants need adequate mixing, for instance by inverting them in a figure-of-8 pattern, and inefficient mixing can leave small clots. Overmixing is the other extreme and leads to hemolysis, not clots. Drawing out of order risks additive carry-over, and the butterfly discard concerns air in the tubing, not clotting.

Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity in the hour before

preguntas.pregunta: An OGTT is ordered for an inpatient who has been on bed rest with pneumonia for a week. What should the phlebotomist recognize?
opciones: The test is not appropriate in hospitalized, acutely ill or inactive patients
The test is appropriate if the load is raised to 100 g to offset the bed rest
The test is appropriate if a fingerstick meter replaces the venous samples
The test is appropriate if only the fasting and 2-hour samples are drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Glucose tolerance is impaired by bed rest, and the OGTT should not be performed in hospitalized, acutely ill or inactive patients, nor in anyone with an infection, traumatic injury or severe illness; the result would not be interpretable, so the provider should be told. Changing the load, the specimen or the number of samples does not fix the problem, and venous plasma at fasting and 2 hours is already the standard protocol.

preguntas.pregunta: Which side of the upper limb does each of the two main superficial veins drain?

The cephalic drains the medial side; the basilic drains the radial side
Both drain the radial side, and the median cubital vein drains the medial
The cephalic drains the deep muscles; the basilic drains the skin only
preguntas.explicacion: The cephalic vein takes the radial, or thumb, side of the limb and the basilic takes the medial side; near the elbow the median cubital vein connects the two. preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away after a skin puncture?
opciones: It may be contaminated with tissue fluid or debris such as sloughing skin
It is arterial in oxygen content, and the test needs a venous value
It contains the alcohol that has not yet dried, which hemolyses the sample
It is the drop richest in platelets, which would clump in the microtube
preguntas.explicacion: The first drop is wiped away because it may be contaminated with tissue fluid or debris (sloughing skin). preguntas.pregunta: What makes an accidental arterial puncture more painful than a venous one?
opciones: Arteries have thicker walls and more nerves associated with them
Arteries have thinner walls and fewer nerves associated with them
Arteries carry a higher volume of blood at a much lower pressure
Arteries lie deeper and are always covered by the bicipital sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for a draw because they run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and carry more nerves with them, so puncturing one hurts more. preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a 24-hour urine collection at 7 a.m. asks what to do with the urine he passes at 7 a.m. on the first day. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Void into the toilet and discard it; collect every void after that, including the 7 a.m. void the next morning
Collect it as the first specimen of the period, and stop with the last void before 7 a.m. the next morning
Void into the toilet and discard it, and also discard the 7 a.m. void of the next morning to keep exactly 24 hours
Collect it as a separate first-morning specimen for urinalysis, and start the timed collection with the next void
preguntas.explicacion: The period starts with an empty bladder: the void at the starting time goes into the toilet and is not kept. From then on all urine is saved for 24 hours, and the void at the same clock time the next morning is the last one collected and does go into the container. Keeping the opening void or dropping the closing void both shift the measured period. The container is refrigerated throughout.

preguntas.pregunta: In the second step of blood typing, called back typing, what is mixed with red cells known to be type A and type B?
opciones: The patient's serum, to look for anti-A and anti-B antibodies
The patient's red cells, to look for the A antigen or B antigen
The patient's plasma with anti-D reagent, to look for Rh factor
The patient's whole blood, to look for clumping of the donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood typing has two steps. In ABO typing the sample's cells are mixed with anti-A and anti-B antibodies and watched for clumping. In back typing the serum, the liquid part without cells, is mixed with cells known to be type A and type B; since type A people have anti-B, type B have anti-A and type O have both, the serum reaction confirms the type. Rh typing is a similar but separate test.

preguntas.pregunta: A lactose tolerance blood test is abnormal. What test is recommended afterwards, and why?

A second lactose tolerance test, to confirm the result on another day
A blood culture set, to rule out bacterial overgrowth of the small bowel
A fasting glucose, to rule out the diabetes that flattens the lactose curve
preguntas.explicacion: An abnormal lactose blood test should be followed by a glucose tolerance test, which rules out a problem with the body's ability to absorb glucose: if glucose itself is poorly absorbed, the flat curve after lactose means nothing about lactase. preguntas.pregunta: You are choosing a vein in the antecubital area. Which vein is the most common venipuncture site, and what does it connect?
opciones: The median cubital vein, linking the cephalic and basilic veins
The basilic vein, linking the median antebrachial and axillary veins

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter needs a urine culture. From where should the specimen be taken?
opciones: Never from the drainage bag, whose contents are considered contaminated
From the drainage bag, after mixing it so the sample is representative
From the drainage bag, provided it was emptied less than 2 hours earlier
From the drainage bag, after adding boric acid to stop any overgrowth
preguntas.explicacion: When a catheter is already in place, urine that has pooled in the collection bag is regarded as contaminated and is never used for culture, no matter how recently the bag was emptied or what preservative is added afterward. preguntas.pregunta: Which pair appears among the contributing factors named for laboratory testing errors?
opciones: Improper patient preparation and transcription mistakes
Delayed billing and missing diagnosis codes on the form
Ordering too few tests for a complex discharge diagnosis
Holding serum at 2 to 8 degrees before serological testing
preguntas.explicacion: Errors arise across the preanalytical, analytical and postanalytical phases, and the factors listed are improper patient preparation, specimen collection errors, transport delays, instrument malfunction, reagent instability, transcription mistakes and poor communication of critical values. preguntas.pregunta: A clinic decides that stopper colour alone will tell staff in what sequence to fill tubes. What problem remains?
opciones: The sequence still has to be followed; colour by itself does not enforce it
Stopper colours are identical between manufacturers, so the risk is covered
Colour tells the phlebotomist how many inversions each tube will need
Colour identifies the additive, so carry-over between tubes cannot happen
preguntas.explicacion: Colour coding makes the tubes easy to tell apart, but an incorrect collection still follows when the sequence is not respected, which is why training matters. Colour codes can also differ from one laboratory to another, so they should be checked locally rather than assumed.

preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a 24-hour urine collection, the assistant asks the patient whether he understands. Why does that question not count as teach-back?
opciones: It can be answered yes or no, and patients tend to say yes whether they followed it or not
It tests the patient's memory instead of checking how well the explanation was delivered
It has to be asked at the very end of the visit, once every instruction has been given
It should be put to the caregiver, who is the person actually carrying out the collection
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back asks patients to say in their own words what they need to know or do. Questions that can be closed with a yes, such as asking whether something makes sense, are explicitly not teach-back, because a yes comes just as easily from someone who missed the point. The framing that works puts the burden on the explainer, not on the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: 'Do you understand the fasting instructions?' 'Yes.' Why does this exchange fail as teach-back?
opciones: It is a yes-or-no question; patients tend to say yes whether or not they understood
It tests the patient's memory, which is exactly what teach-back is designed to do anyway
It was asked in the middle of the visit rather than at the very end of it
It was asked of the patient instead of the companion who will supervise the fast
preguntas.explicacion: 'Do you understand?' and 'Does that make sense?' are not teach-back questions, because patients are likely to answer yes either way. Teach-back asks the patient to state in their own words what they need to know or do, is not a test of memory, and should be done in chunks during the visit rather than saved for the end.

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old comes for a lipid panel with her mother, who agrees to the draw. Which term describes what the mother gives?
opciones: Informed permission
Informed consent
Pediatric assent
Implied consent
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically under 18, cannot give informed consent; parents or legal guardians permit the intervention instead, and that process is called informed permission. Assent is what the child may add, valuable when reasonable. The exception to the rule is the legally emancipated minor, who consents alone.

preguntas.pregunta: In an adult finger-prick, why is a 2.2 mm lancet the longest typically used?
opciones: Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.4 mm, and pressure makes the puncture deeper than the lancet
Because the puncture depth should not go beyond 2.2 mm, and the lancet must match that limit exactly
Because the skin-to-bone distance on the side of an adult finger averages 2.33 mm
Because lancets longer than 2.2 mm are made only as surgical blades, which the WHO prohibits
preguntas.explicacion: The lancet chosen is slightly shorter than the estimated depth needed, because pressure compresses the skin and the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length. Since a finger-prick should not go beyond 2.4 mm, a 2.2 mm lancet is the longest typically used. The 2.33 mm figure is the posterior heel of a 3 kg baby, and surgical blades are prohibited for any skin puncture.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is slow to answer the pre-draw questions. What should you do?
opciones: Slow down, give him time to process, and do not interrupt him
Fill each silence by suggesting the answer you think is likely
Ask the questions in rapid succession so he finishes before tiring
Skip the interview and rely on what the requisition already says
preguntas.explicacion: Avoid hurrying older patients: some struggle with rapid-fire questioning or torrents of information, so speak more slowly, give time to process, and do not interrupt, because once interrupted a patient is less likely to reveal all concerns. Supplying answers or skipping the interview loses the allergy, fainting and fasting information the WHO interview exists to collect.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why single-use lancing devices and glucose meters are never shared between patients without cleaning.
opciones: Blood-contaminated devices have been implicated in hepatitis B outbreaks
Shared devices lose their calibration and read the glucose far too low
Shared devices carry latex particles from one patient's skin to the next
Shared devices void the manufacturer's warranty on the meter and lancets
preguntas.explicacion: Reusable finger-prick devices and point-of-care instruments such as glucose meters, once contaminated with blood, have been linked to outbreaks of hepatitis B. preguntas.pregunta: A newborn was born at 10 p.m. and the nurse wants the screening card collected at 8 a.m. the next morning. What does the timing guidance say?
opciones: Screening is done at 24 to 48 hours; a sample taken before 24 hours may have to be repeated
Screening is done at 6 to 12 hours; the earlier the better for the metabolic conditions
Screening is done at 48 to 72 hours; any earlier sample is discarded by the laboratory
Screening is done at 12 to 24 hours, at the same time as the hearing screen
preguntas.explicacion: Newborn screening usually happens when the baby is between 24 and 48 hours old, and a baby tested before 24 hours may need to be retested, because for some conditions the screening is not valid if blood is taken within 24 hours of birth. The same ideal window of 24 to 48 hours applies nationally, with alterations for premature or ill infants.

preguntas.pregunta: The label on a drum of laboratory reagent is smeared and hard to read. What does the Hazard Communication standard require of the laboratory?
opciones: Labels on incoming containers must not be removed or defaced
Labels may be replaced with the in-house number of the reagent
Labels may be taken off once the sheet is filed in the binder
Labels must be covered with tape until the drum is emptied out
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are covered by the Hazard Communication standard in a reduced way, and the first of those duties is that labels on incoming containers of hazardous chemicals are not removed or defaced. The others are keeping the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments and making them readily accessible during each work shift, and giving employees the information and training of paragraph (h). Filing the sheet does not release the container from carrying its own warning.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for culture is collected into a container with boric acid preservative, and the ward also wants a dipstick from the same cup. What should be expected?
opciones: The dipstick leukocyte reagent may be less sensitive and the initial pH altered, though the bacteria are preserved
The dipstick glucose and urobilinogen may read falsely positive, though the bacteria are preserved for culture
The dipstick leukocyte esterase may read falsely negative, and the culture will fail to grow at any concentration
The dipstick albumin may read falsely positive, and the bacteria will be killed within the first hour of storage
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the preservative commonly used to keep bacteria alive in urine, but it can reduce the sensitivity of the leukocyte reagent on the dipstick and change the initial pH, and in excessive concentration it can even prevent bacterial growth in the sample sent for culture. False-positive glucose and urobilinogen are the formaldehyde pattern, a false-negative leukocyte esterase belongs to mercury salts, and thymol gives false-positive albumin.

The purple EDTA haematology tube for the CBC
The light grey sodium fluoride tube
The dark green sodium heparin tube

Whether a tourniquet is needed
How many tubes one puncture yields
Which antiseptic to apply

preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes microaggressions from macroaggressions?
opciones: Micro: brief everyday slights between individuals; macro: overt and rooted in systems
Micro: always intentional insults; macro: unconscious and unintended snubs
Micro: cause no measurable harm; macro: the only form that causes real harm
Micro: only spoken remarks; macro: only physical acts of exclusion
preguntas.explicacion: Macroaggressions are overt, radical discrimination embedded in a society or system, with internment camps and the Tuskegee study as examples, and microaggressions are short everyday insults or snubs, often unintentional and rooted in unconscious bias, delivered verbally or non-verbally in one-on-one interactions. Repeated microaggressions cause documented harm.

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR is ordered along with a CBC. Which tube is used for the ESR specimen, and can it be shared with other tests?
opciones: It goes in a black-top ESR tube with 3.2% citrate or a lavender EDTA tube, and is not shared with other tests
It goes in the same lavender EDTA tube as the CBC, and the leftover blood is used for the sedimentation
It goes in a light blue citrate tube filled to 90%, and it can be shared with any PT ordered on the same draw
It goes in a plain red tube, and the serum is transferred to the Westergren tube in the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is usually collected in a black-top ESR vacuum tube containing 3.2% sodium citrate; whole blood in a lavender EDTA tube is also acceptable, and the sample must stay in its own ESR-designated tube because of the volume the test needs, so it cannot be shared. The test is run on anticoagulated whole blood, never on serum.

preguntas.pregunta: How quickly must an employer report a work-related fatality, and a work-related inpatient hospitalization, to OSHA?
opciones: A fatality within 8 hours; a hospitalization within 24 hours
A fatality within 24 hours; a hospitalization within 8 hours
Both within 72 hours, by telephone to the area office
Both within 60 days, on the OSHA 300A summary
preguntas.explicacion: Under the recordkeeping rule updated in 2015, as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, employers report every work-related fatality within 8 hours of learning of it, and every work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours. Reports can be made by phone to the nearest area office, to the 24-hour OSHA hotline at 1-800-321-6742, or through the online serious event form. The 300A summary is an annual posting, not a reporting channel, and 60 days is the HIPAA breach notification limit.

The operations in their work area where hazardous chemicals are present
The measures they can take to protect themselves from those chemicals
The requirements of the Hazard Communication standard itself

preguntas.pregunta: A housekeeper handles regulated waste bags twice a week, while every phlebotomist is exposed daily. How does the exposure determination list them?
opciones: Phlebotomists as a classification where all are exposed; the housekeeper with the task
Both as classifications where all employees are exposed, with no list of tasks needed
Only the phlebotomists, because the housekeeper wears gloves for that one task
Both by name in the medical record, which is where exposed workers are recorded
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(i) asks for three lists: job classifications in which every employee has occupational exposure, job classifications in which only some do, and the tasks or groups of related tasks that expose the people in that second group. Handling regulated waste is exactly such a task. Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) adds that the determination is made without regard to protective equipment, so gloves never take a job off the list. The medical record of (h)(1) is a separate document kept for each exposed employee, not the determination.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient had two beers at 11 p.m.; the fasting draw is at 7 a.m. How does that affect the sample?
opciones: Avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw; note it and tell the provider
It is fine, because eight hours have passed and beer counts only as a liquid
It is fine provided he drinks plain water now to dilute the alcohol
It is fine, because alcohol affects only the liver function tests
preguntas.explicacion: Alcoholic drinks should not be taken within 24 hours of the procedure, alongside the 12-hour fast and the ban on coffee and energy drinks that morning. Any phlebotomist trained in vacuum systems; the results are equivalent to those of a peripheral draw
No one; central lines may never be used for laboratory specimens under any protocol
Only laboratory technicians; they must draw a non-additive discard tube first

preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube with no anticoagulant has been filled. How long may the specimen need before it is spun?
opciones: Usually ten to fifteen minutes, and in some specimens up to an hour
Usually two to three minutes, and in some specimens up to ten minutes
Usually thirty seconds, the same contact time asked of an alcohol swab
Usually twenty-four hours, the interval allowed for a coagulation test
preguntas.explicacion: The red top carries no anticoagulant: contact with the tube wall sets off clotting, and the specimen is normally left ten to fifteen minutes before centrifugation, although clotting time varies and can reach a full hour. preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance for email communication with patients?
opciones: Encrypt all emails, keep the patient's name out of the subject line, and send the minimum information
Use a personal commercial email account so the message is not stored on the institution's servers
Put the patient's name in the subject line so the message is easy to locate later
Attach the full record whenever a patient asks a question, to avoid follow-up messages
preguntas.explicacion: Institutions should set email rules: the patient's name is left out of the subject line, the address is verified, only the bare minimum of information is transmitted, a standard disclaimer closes every message, all emails are encrypted, and staff never use personal or commercial accounts for patient communication, only the system the institution provides. Similar rules govern faxes, which sit in a secure area with a cover sheet explaining what to do if the fax is misdirected. Sending a whole record in reply to a question violates the minimum necessary principle.

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, which disinfectant is applied after the area has been cleaned with water and detergent?
opciones: Sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, a 1:10 bleach dilution prepared daily
Sodium hypochlorite 5.25 percent, used undiluted straight from the bottle
70 percent alcohol, the same solution used to prepare the skin
Sodium hypochlorite 0.05 percent, a 1:100 dilution, kept for a week
preguntas.explicacion: After the glass is removed with tongs, the fluid absorbed with paper towels and the area wiped with water and detergent until visibly clean, the spill area is saturated again with sodium hypochlorite 0.5 percent, which is 10,000 parts per million of available chlorine, made as a 1:10 dilution of 5.25 percent household bleach and prepared fresh each day. Undiluted bleach is not the instruction, 70 percent alcohol is WHO's skin antiseptic, and a solution kept for a week defeats the daily preparation rule. Gloves come off last, followed by handwashing and an incident record.

preguntas.pregunta: Before a fingerstick glucose, an assistant swabs the fingertip with alcohol and lances it while the skin is still wet. Why does the guidance advise against this?
opciones: Residual alcohol can dilute the drop or cause hemolysis, so the site must dry completely first
Alcohol left on the skin makes the meter read falsely high, because ethanol is measured as glucose
Alcohol is not recommended at all; the guidance calls for washing with cold water and no antiseptic
Wet alcohol stings on puncture, which is the only concern, so the result itself is not affected
preguntas.explicacion: The site is washed and dried thoroughly, using warm water to improve blood flow. Alcohol swabs are not routinely required, but if one is used the skin must be allowed to dry completely before lancing, because residual alcohol can dilute the sample or hemolyze it and affect the reading. Discomfort is not the point; sample integrity is. Cold water is not what the procedure describes.

Section 2, which also gives the signal word and the hazard statements

preguntas.pregunta: Blood has leaked onto the outside of a specimen tube. What does the standard require before it is transported?
opciones: Place it in a second container that prevents leakage and is labeled or color-coded
Wipe the tube with disinfectant and transport it in the usual rack with a new label
Discard the specimen as regulated waste and request a new draw from the patient
Place it in a puncture-resistant container, which is required for every leaking tube
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(B) says that when the outside of the primary container is contaminated, it goes inside a second container that prevents leakage during handling, processing, storage, transport or shipping and that is labeled or color-coded per the standard. Puncture resistance is added by (d)(2)(xiii)(C) only when the specimen could puncture the primary container, not for every leak. Nothing in the paragraph calls for discarding the specimen or for cleaning the tube in place of the secondary container.

preguntas.pregunta: NPSG.01.01.01 gives one example of the 'other procedures' that also need two identifiers. Which is it?

Point-of-care glucose
Peripheral IV insertion
Specimen centrifugation

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee wants to label the filled tubes at the bench. Why are tube identification and labelling both done with the patient present?
opciones: It cuts down the risk of mixing up which tube belongs to which patient
It lets the patient read the label and correct the spelling of the name
It shows that the fasting instructions were kept before the first tube
It lets the phlebotomist skip the wristband check on any later visit
preguntas.explicacion: Before the blood is withdrawn the identification data and the tube labelling are double-checked, and both the identification of the tubes and their labelling happen with the patient there, which is what lowers the risk of tube misidentification. The identification goal states the same requirement as its second element of performance.

preguntas.pregunta: How does a blood culture diversion device reduce contamination?
opciones: It sets aside a small first portion of blood, then collects the culture
It draws the whole set through a closed catheter connector, bypassing the skin
It splits one venipuncture into two sets so a second stick is unnecessary
It adds an antiglycolytic agent that keeps skin organisms from growing
preguntas.explicacion: Commercially available diversion devices first divert a small amount of potentially contaminated blood and then collect the blood for the culture; the CDC lists them as showing promise in further reducing contamination. Drawing through catheters raises contamination, a second set still needs a separate venipuncture, and antiglycolytic additives belong to the glucose tube, not to culture bottles.

preguntas.pregunta: A muscular patient has very prominent, easily visible veins. What is the guidance on tourniquet use in this case?
opciones: Avoiding the tourniquet is recommended when the veins are prominent
The tourniquet is still mandatory, applied about 3 inches above the site
A tighter tourniquet is used, because large veins collapse under vacuum
The tourniquet is applied only after the first tube has been filled
preguntas.explicacion: Controversy remains about tourniquets in blood sampling, and avoiding them, especially in patients with prominent veins, is recommended; otherwise a disposable tourniquet goes about 3 inches above the site. It does not describe the tourniquet as mandatory, does not call for extra tightness, and does not delay application until after the first tube.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands in a sputum cup holding a few milliliters of clear, watery fluid from the mouth. What should the medical assistant do?
opciones: Ask for a new specimen coughed up deeply, because thin, clear material is rejected
Send it as it is, because any material from the mouth still carries airway organisms
Add sterile saline to the cup and send it, because the volume is what was too small
Refrigerate it and send it the next morning, when a fresh specimen can be added to it
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is what comes up from the air passages on a deep cough, not spit. The thicker the material, the more likely it truly represents lower respiratory secretions and shows the organism causing the infection, and many laboratories will not accept a clear, runny sample for microscopy or culture. Volume and quality are both assessed, and collection may be repeated until 10 to 20 mL is obtained.

preguntas.pregunta: A physician's office asks the laboratory for the reference interval it uses for a test and for a list of substances that interfere with the assay. What does CLIA say?
opciones: Reference intervals must be available to the ordering person, and information affecting interpretation, like interferences, is given on request
Reference intervals are proprietary to the performing laboratory; only the manufacturer's package insert may be shared with the laboratory's clients
Reference intervals must be printed on every report, but interference data are released only to CMS or its agent on request
Reference intervals and interference data are provided only when the laboratory holds a certificate of accreditation from CAP
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1291(d) the pertinent reference intervals or normal values, as determined by the performing laboratory, must be available to the authorized person who ordered the test and to whoever uses the result; under (e) the laboratory must, on request, make available its list of test methods and performance specifications, and must provide information that may affect interpretation, test interferences being the example given, with updates whenever changes affect the results.

preguntas.pregunta: Which parts of a practice does the toolkit say have to be covered by language access services?
opciones: Scheduling, signage, front desk, the visit, billing and follow-up messages
Only the clinical visit, where medical information is actually exchanged
Only the front desk and the signage, where written English predominates
Only scheduling and billing, where the written records are generated
preguntas.explicacion: Language access services are provided when patients, or companions taking part in the visit, want to use a language other than English, and every aspect of the practice that needs them should be considered: appointment scheduling, signage, the front desk, the clinical visit, billing, follow-up communication, patient portals, secure messaging and patient feedback.

preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient booked for a glucose challenge test asks whether she must fast. What is the answer?
opciones: No fasting; she drinks the glucose and one sample is drawn an hour later
Fast at least 8 hours; samples are drawn before and 2 hours after the drink
Fast 9 to 12 hours; the test is normally scheduled for the morning
No fasting; a single sample reflects her average glucose over 3 months
preguntas.explicacion: The glucose challenge test used to screen for gestational diabetes needs no fasting: the patient drinks a sugary drink and blood is taken one hour later; a high result leads to an oral glucose tolerance test, which does require fasting and repeated samples. The 9-to-12-hour fast is for cholesterol and the 3-month average is the A1C.

preguntas.pregunta: Which four elements must a patient prove to win a medical malpractice suit?
opciones: Duty, breach of duty (negligence), causation and damages
Assault, battery, negligence and abandonment
Intent, foreseeability, restitution and injunction
Duty, consent, documentation and insurance coverage
preguntas.explicacion: A simple mistake is not malpractice by itself. The plaintiff must establish four elements: a duty to the patient, meaning the clinician was responsible for that patient's care; a breach of that duty, the negligence, measured against the standard of care; causation, that the act or omission produced the bad outcome; and damages, the loss for which compensation is sought. The tort pathway states it the same way, duty, breach, proximate cause, damages. Assault, battery and abandonment are separate torts, and restitution and injunctions are remedies.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit; StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Tort Liability Pathway

preguntas.pregunta: An Rh negative mother delivered a healthy Rh positive first baby and received no RhoGAM. What is the concern for a second Rh positive pregnancy?
opciones: Her anti-Rh antibodies could cross the placenta and destroy the fetus's red cells
Her anti-A and anti-B antibodies could cross the placenta if the baby is type AB
The first baby's Rh+ cells remain in her blood and agglutinate her own cells
A second Rh+ fetus would sensitize her only if it were also ABO incompatible
preguntas.explicacion: A first pregnancy is usually safe because fetal cells rarely cross the placenta, but at birth the Rh negative parent can be exposed to the baby's Rh positive cells and begin making anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh positive pregnancy those antibodies can cross the placenta and hemolyze fetal red cells, causing hemolytic disease of the newborn, which ranges from mild anemia to fetal death.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's spouse comes to the front desk, with other patients waiting behind him, and asks why the patient is here today.
opciones: Ask the patient whether he objects, and talk away from the desk
Answer at the desk, since a spouse needs no written authorization
Refuse any contact until the spouse produces a signed authorization
Send the spouse to the laboratory, which released the result
preguntas.explicacion: Two rules meet here. Information may be shared with a spouse, parent, guardian or other caregiver involved in the person's care without a formal written agreement, but when other people are present the patient is asked first whether there is any objection. And the conversation itself does not belong at a counter or in a hallway: anything specific waits until the patient is in a private room, with only what is relevant said out loud.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: HIPAA and Communication With Patients

preguntas.pregunta: How does the American Diabetes Association define 'fasting' for a fasting plasma glucose?
opciones: No caloric intake at all for at least 8 hours
No food or drink, including water, for 12 hours
No solid food for 8 hours; sweetened drinks allowed
No caloric intake at all for at least 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA diagnostic criteria define fasting as no caloric intake for at least 8 hours, with a fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher meeting the threshold for diabetes. Water carries no calories and is allowed; sweetened drinks do carry calories. Twelve hours is the general recommendation for morning sampling, and 24 hours is the alcohol-free window.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Diagnostic Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital hires per diem and contract phlebotomists for a busy season. How does the bloodborne pathogens standard treat them?
opciones: They are covered, and the plan must describe how the standard is met for them
They are covered after ninety days, the period allowed for a new hire's training
They are covered by the staffing agency's plan alone, never by the host facility
They fall outside the standard, since the exposure determination lists job titles
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan states plainly that part-time, temporary, contract and per diem employees fall under the bloodborne pathogens standard, and that the written plan should say how the requirements will be met for them. Nothing in paragraph (c) sets a waiting period: training comes at the time of initial assignment under (g)(2)(ii)(A), and the hepatitis B vaccine within ten working days of that assignment under (f)(2)(i). The exposure determination is a list of job classifications and tasks, so it does not exclude anyone by employment status.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse tells the phlebotomist that the patient in bed 12 is the one who needs the draw. Under the Joint Commission International patient identification goal, why is that not enough?
opciones: The room number or location cannot be used as an identifier; at least two identifiers such as name and birth date are needed
Only the bar-coded wristband counts as an identifier, so the nurse's statement must be confirmed by scanning it
The location is acceptable as one identifier, provided a second identifier such as the ordering physician's name is added
Two staff members must independently confirm the bed number before a specimen can be collected
preguntas.explicacion: The first international patient safety goal requires at least two ways of identifying the patient, for example name, identification number, birth date or a bar-coded wristband, and it excludes the room number or location outright. The wristband is one valid option, not the only one; the physician's name identifies the order, not the patient; and a second witness does not turn a location into an identifier.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.1, IPSG 1

preguntas.pregunta: In which phase of laboratory testing do fasting errors and patient identification errors occur?
opciones: Preanalytical
Analytical
Postanalytical
Interpretive
preguntas.explicacion: Errors can occur in the preanalytical, analytical and postanalytical phases; improper patient preparation and specimen collection errors belong to the preanalytical phase, along with transport delays. Instrument malfunction and reagent instability are analytical, and transcription mistakes and poor communication of critical values are postanalytical.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee scrubs for ten minutes before a sterile procedure, believing longer is safer. What is the effect?
opciones: No added benefit, and more risk of irritating the skin
A longer lasting effect on the resident skin flora
The same effect as a rub, which needs no drying time
A shorter effect, since the antiseptic is rinsed away
preguntas.explicacion: The usual scrub with an antimicrobial agent runs about two to six minutes, following the manufacturer and the institution. Scrub times of ten minutes or more add nothing and raise the risk of skin irritation, and irritated skin is harder to keep clean. Some institutions use shorter staged techniques or an alcohol-based formulation instead, applied as the manufacturer directs and left to dry completely before sterile gloves go on.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis

preguntas.pregunta: How is the specimen for a galactosemia or phenylketonuria screen obtained from a newborn?
opciones: The heel is cleaned with alcohol, punctured, and a few drops are collected
The heel is cleaned with chlorhexidine, punctured, and a full tube is filled
A finger is cleaned with alcohol, punctured, and a few drops are collected
A vein of the hand is cleaned with alcohol and a small tube is filled
preguntas.explicacion: For both screens the provider cleans the baby's heel with alcohol, sticks it with a small needle, collects a few drops of blood and bandages the heel. Neither test calls for any special preparation of the baby. The finger is not used at this age, and the volume is drops onto the screening card rather than a filled tube.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Galactosemia Tests, What happens during a galactosemia test?; MedlinePlus, PKU Screening, What happens during a PKU screening test?

preguntas.pregunta: Two isolation gowns carry different fluid barrier levels. What do those levels come from?
opciones: A four-level standard for medical gowns, from the lowest barrier up
The number of layers of fabric the manufacturer sewed together
The quality level that also grades gloves for micro-perforation
The hazardous materials scale that runs from level A down to D
preguntas.explicacion: Medical gowns are graded against a published standard for medical gowns that sets four levels of fluid barrier protection, and separate guidance sets gown standards for handling hazardous drugs. Choosing well means matching the level to the setting, sterile gowns for surgery and non-sterile ones for contact exposure. The acceptable quality level is a glove measure, and levels A through D are the hazardous materials scale, where level A is the most protective.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE

preguntas.pregunta: After filling three tubes at the bedside, a phlebotomist carries them to the nurses' station and labels them there. Which requirement was broken?
opciones: NPSG.01.01.01 EP 2: label specimen containers in the presence of the patient
NPSG.01.01.01 EP 1: use at least two identifiers when collecting any specimens
NPSG.02.03.01: report critical results within the established time frame
NPSG.07.01.01: follow the current CDC or WHO hand hygiene guidelines
preguntas.explicacion: Goal 1 has two elements of performance. EP 1 is about the identifiers themselves; EP 2 says that containers for blood and other specimens are labelled in the presence of the patient. Walking unlabelled tubes away from the bedside defeats EP 2 even if the identification at the bedside was perfect. StatPearls makes the same point: identify and label the tubes with the patient present.

preguntas.pregunta: About what share of older adults have hearing loss?
opciones: About one-third
About one-half
About one-quarter
About two-thirds
preguntas.explicacion: Age-related hearing loss is common, affecting about one-third of older adults, and the chance of developing it increases with age. That is why the guidance asks the clinician to make sure the patient can hear before proceeding: check for a working hearing aid, look for excess earwax, and be aware of background noise.

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee argues that a mislabelled tube is just paperwork, since the analyser will still give a correct number. Which published figures answer that?
opciones: Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 18 such errors harms
A tenth of transfusion deaths trace to identification, and 1 in 100 such errors harms
Half of transfusion deaths trace to identification, but no such error has harmed
A quarter of transfusion deaths trace to labelling, and 1 in 3 such errors harms
preguntas.explicacion: Of all the steps before the analysis, collection is arguably the most critical, because an identification error sends the right number to the wrong person. Up to 50 % of transfusion-related deaths follow an identification error, mislabelled blood specimens can end in a haemolytic transfusion reaction, and as many as one in eighteen identification errors leads to patient harm.

preguntas.pregunta: Which materials are acceptable alternatives to natural rubber latex for a patient with latex allergy?
opciones: Vinyl, silicone or neoprene
Powder-free natural rubber latex
Natural rubber without antioxidants
Cornstarch-coated latex gloves
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are advised to ask for equipment made of vinyl or silicone instead of latex, and the alternatives in use include neoprene, polyvinyl chloride, silicone and vinyl; powder-free and latex-free gloves have markedly reduced the prevalence of latex allergy. Powder-free latex is still latex, and it is the natural proteins, not only the added chemicals, that cause the type I reaction.

preguntas.pregunta: How is phenylketonuria detected in the newborn screen?
opciones: Tandem mass spectrometry on dried blood spots from a heel prick at about 24 to 48 hours of life
Bacterial growth inhibition on a urine-soaked filter strip collected at the first well-baby visit
Measurement of tyrosine in cord blood collected at delivery, before the first feeding
DNA sequencing of the PAH gene on a buccal swab taken in the delivery room
preguntas.explicacion: PKU is first identified through universal newborn screening on dried blood spots obtained by heel prick at approximately 24 to 48 hours of life, analysed by tandem mass spectrometry for the phenylalanine concentration and the phenylalanine-to-tyrosine ratio. A positive screen is confirmed with quantitative plasma amino acids, and diet should begin ideally within the first 7 to 10 days of life.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phenylketonuria", sections Evaluation and Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C PKU collection information · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening

preguntas.pregunta: Under NPSG.01.01.01, which of the following may never be used as a patient identifier?
opciones: The room number or bed location
The telephone number on file
An assigned identification number
Any other person-specific identifier

EP 1 adds the one exclusion that examiners like to test: the patient's room number or physical location is not an identifier, because it belongs to the bed, not to the person.

preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's point-of-care potassium is critical again today, as it was at the last two visits and is documented in the chart. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy for this instance, even though earlier critical values are known
Skip the call, because a critical value that has already been reported for the same patient does not need to be reported again
Report it only if today's value differs from the previous critical result by more than 10 %, and otherwise just record it
Record it in the log and report all of the day's critical values together to the provider at the end of the clinic session
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are treated as reportable events even when previous critical values are already known for that patient, and the critical value reporting policy is followed consistently each time one is obtained. Departing from the policy is considered only in exceptional cases supported by evidence, such as an obvious testing or pre-analytical error. Both the result and any action taken are documented whenever a critical value occurs.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these procedures is named in the CLIA regulation itself as a test a Certificate of Waiver site may perform?
opciones: Spun microhematocrit test
Automated sedimentation rate
Serum hCG color comparison
Benchtop hemoglobin A1c
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation's own list includes non-automated dipstick urinalysis, non-automated fecal occult blood, visual ovulation and urine pregnancy tests, non-automated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, copper sulfate hemoglobin, home-use glucose meters, spun microhematocrit and single-analyte hemoglobin instruments. The sedimentation rate is waived only when non-automated, and pregnancy tests only on urine.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are 3 separate stool specimens recommended for an ova and parasite examination?
opciones: Parasites are not shed in the stool every day, so several samples raise the chance of finding them
Each specimen is examined for a different infection: amebiasis, giardiasis or strongyloidiasis
The first specimen is used for culture, the second for the smear and the third for molecular testing
The specimens are pooled to reach the 8 to 10 mL that the microscope smear requires
preguntas.explicacion: Parasites and their eggs may be absent from the stool on a given day, so collecting several specimens over a few days makes the examination more sensitive; three different specimens are the usual recommendation. In the laboratory a small smear of each is placed on a slide and examined under the microscope, and molecular tests may be added. The 8 to 10 mL figure is the volume of each sputum specimen for tuberculosis.

preguntas.pregunta: Tourniquets have been found contaminated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. By which two routes does that happen?
opciones: Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and reuse of a contaminated band
Poor hand hygiene by the patient and storage of the band in a closed tray
Reuse of a contaminated band and application over a sleeve rather than skin
Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and washing the band between patients
preguntas.explicacion: Up to a quarter of tourniquets have been found carrying this organism, and the two causes named are the phlebotomist's lack of hand hygiene and the reuse of bands that are already contaminated. That is why a disposable band is preferred and why gloves go on before the band.

preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism is described for winged steel needles that carry a safety feature?
opciones: A needle-locking mechanism that also prevents the set being reused
A blunting mechanism that dulls the tip once the last tube is filled
A colour change in the tubing that shows the set has been used once
A hinged shield activated by pressing the wings against each other
preguntas.explicacion: Winged steel needles with a passive or an active safety feature use a needle-locking mechanism that cuts the risk of a stick and stops reuse, and they make the transfer of blood safer when a syringe is used. Joined to vacuum tubes, they still need the first tube to be additive-free or discarded.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles with safety mechanism

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fills a preservative-containing urine tube only to one-third of the marked line. What is the problem?
opciones: Too little urine leaves the preservative too concentrated, which can inhibit bacterial growth in the culture
Too little urine leaves the preservative too dilute, so it cannot keep the bacteria from multiplying in transit
The tube should be filled to the line with sterile normal saline so the preservative ratio is restored
Too little urine is acceptable for culture, since only 15 to 30 mL is needed for an accurate analysis
preguntas.explicacion: The preservative-to-specimen ratio matters in both directions. Overfilling past the line dilutes the preservative and weakens its action; underfilling leaves an excess of preservative that can suppress the very bacteria the culture is looking for. Topping up with saline dilutes the specimen and the colony count, and the 15 to 30 mL figure applies to urinalysis in a plain cup, not to a preservative tube with a fill line.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives
preguntas.subtema: Preservative fill line · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i

preguntas.pregunta: What share of needlestick injuries did older studies blame on recapping, and what does current hospital surveillance show?
opciones: Between 10% and 25% then; about 5% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 40% and 60% then; about 20% in the surveillance hospitals now
About 5% then; between 10% and 25% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 10% and 25% then; none at all since the standard prohibited it
preguntas.explicacion: Older studies traced ten to twenty-five percent of needlestick injuries to recapping a used needle. Recapping by hand has been discouraged for years and is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard unless no alternative exists, yet it still causes about five percent of the injuries counted in surveillance hospitals. The share fell; it did not disappear, and that is the point of the rule.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)

preguntas.pregunta: During a child's venipuncture, why does the second adult grasp the child's wrist palm-up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder, and the firm grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the fingers open so the veins of the hand stay visible
It warms the forearm, which lifts the flow of blood sevenfold
It frees the elbow, which the phlebotomist then holds instead
preguntas.explicacion: The immobiliser reaches across the child and grasps the wrist palm-up: reaching across anchors the child's shoulder and stops twisting or rocking, while the firm grasp on the wrist gives the phlebotomist a tourniquet. The immobiliser's other, outstretched hand holds the elbow. Keeping the child warm is a separate measure that may raise the flow.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with early dementia clearly explains what the draw is for and why she agrees to it. Who consents?
opciones: She does; a diagnosis alone does not remove the right to give informed consent
Her daughter must, because a dementia diagnosis removes decision-making capacity
A psychiatrist must certify her competency before any venipuncture is done
No one needs to; consent is waived because the test is low risk
preguntas.explicacion: Cognitive impairment, mental illness or severe illness do not by themselves revoke the right to consent as long as the person can understand, evaluate and communicate a decision. A psychiatrist is asked to evaluate only when decision-making ability is questioned or unclear, and the waiver exception applies when the patient voluntarily waives, not because the test is minor.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Patients with Impaired Decision-Making Capacity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 k49 · PBT II.D · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3

preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000 require?
opciones: Revising the OSHA standard to add safer devices, annual device review, employee input and a sharps injury log
Creating the bloodborne pathogens standard itself, with the hepatitis B vaccine offer and exposure control plans
Replacing the OSHA standard with the CDC's Standard Precautions for every healthcare employer
Requiring every employer to keep the OSHA 300 log, a form that had not existed before 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Public Law 106-430, signed November 6, 2000, ordered changes to the existing 1991 bloodborne pathogens standard: adding safer medical devices such as sharps with engineered injury protections and needleless systems to the definition of engineering controls, requiring the Exposure Control Plan review to reflect new technology and document annual consideration of safer devices, soliciting input from non-managerial direct-care employees, and establishing the sharps injury log. OSHA revised the standard in 2001; Congress found the existing OSHA 200 log insufficient rather than creating it.
preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430 (Nov. 6, 2000), secs. 2 and 3; OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention: Standards
preguntas.subtema: Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse changes the needle but reuses the syringe to give medication to a second patient. According to the CDC, this practice is which of these?
opciones: Unsafe: a syringe is contaminated after one use, even with a new needle
Safe, since the needle is the only part that touches the patient
Safe if the second dose is injected through IV tubing rather than into tissue
Unsafe only if the first patient has a known bloodborne infection
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's rule is One Needle, One Syringe, Only One Time. Once used, both the syringe and the needle are contaminated and must be discarded; medication must not be given from the same syringe to more than one patient even when the needle is changed or the injection is given through a length of IV tubing. Reusing a syringe for more than one patient is one of the practices the CDC lists as having caused outbreaks of viral, bacterial and fungal infection, and the rule does not depend on the first patient's known status.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Basic safe injection practices
preguntas.subtema: One needle, one syringe · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7

preguntas.pregunta: After the explanation a patient nods and holds out his arm, then says 'Wait, I don't want this.' The needle has not touched him. Per WHO step 2?
opciones: Stop; the patient may refuse the test at any time before the blood is taken
Proceed, because verbal consent was already given when he offered the arm
Proceed if the ordering clinician confirms by telephone that the test is needed
Ask him to sign a refusal form first; until then the consent still stands
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says to discuss the test, obtain verbal consent, and remember that the patient has the right to refuse at any time before the blood sampling, which is why the WHO insists that the patient understand the procedure. An earlier nod does not lock the patient in, a clinician's wish does not override the refusal, and no paperwork is a precondition for stopping.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 · CMA E.3.b (both outlines) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which needle gauge range does WHO Table 3.1 reserve for blood donation, and why does a larger gauge apply?
opciones: 16 to 18 G; collection for transfusion needs a larger gauge than blood drawing
21 to 22 G; the standard adult phlebotomy needles are used for donation as well
19 to 20 G; the intermediate sizes are set aside for donor collection only
23 G; a small needle protects the donor's vein during a long collection
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 ticks 16 to 18 G for adults in the blood donation column, and Section 3.1.1 explains that blood collection for transfusion requires a larger gauge than the one used for drawing blood samples. The 21 and 22 G needles are the adult phlebotomy sizes, 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable, and 23 G is the small-vein and butterfly size.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1; and Section 3.1.1, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: Which urine specimen is best for a urine hCG pregnancy test, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because it is the most concentrated and holds enough hormone
The first void of the morning, because overnight urine is the most dilute of the whole day
A specimen taken 2 hours after a large drink, because dilution reduces false-positive results
A midstream clean-catch taken at any hour, because the hormone level does not vary at all
preguntas.explicacion: Human chorionic gonadotropin is produced during pregnancy and detected in urine. The first specimen of the day is usually best because it is the most concentrated and therefore carries enough hormone to be picked up. The patient voids into a sterile cup, or with a home kit dips the strip or passes it through the stream, following the package directions.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619), How the Test is Performed

preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives labelled with the patient's full name and the room number only. Why does it fail the labelling checklist item used by CAP-accredited laboratories?
opciones: Primary specimen containers must carry at least two identifiers, and a room number is not an identifier
Primary specimen containers must carry the name plus a bar code; a handwritten room number is not machine-readable
Primary specimen containers must carry three identifiers when the specimen is collected on an inpatient unit
Primary specimen containers must carry the name and the collector's initials; the room number is merely optional
preguntas.explicacion: The CAP Laboratory General Checklist requires the collector to positively identify the patient before collection using at least two identifiers (GEN.40490) and requires primary specimen containers to be labelled with at least two identifiers (GEN.40491); the parallel Joint Commission International goal excludes the room number or location as an identifier outright. A name plus a location therefore leaves the tube one identifier short.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.2, CAP checklist items GEN.40490 and GEN.40491
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 3E12 k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a

preguntas.pregunta: The patient is lying comfortably and the tray is ready. In WHO step 2, what is placed under the arm at this point?
opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm moist cloth
A leak-proof plastic bag
A rolled-up tourniquet
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 makes the patient comfortable in a supine position where that is possible and then places a clean paper or towel under the arm. Warm cloths over the puncture area are a paediatric measure for dilating vessels, leak-proof bags are for transporting the samples, and the tourniquet goes four to five finger widths above the site at the next step.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2

preguntas.pregunta: How is the donor identified at a federal drug test collection site?
opciones: With a photo identification, and the collector identifies themself on request
With a photo identification, which the collector photocopies for the file
With two spoken identifiers, name and date of birth, matched to the order
With the employer representative vouching for the donor at the door
preguntas.explicacion: The collector verifies the donor's identity with a photo identification and, if the donor asks, must show identification in return, such as an employee badge or an entry on an employee list. The two spoken identifiers are the rule for a clinical draw such as a blood culture, not for this collection, and the procedure begins without delay even if the employer's representative has not arrived.
preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 4 and 5

preguntas.pregunta: Trace a drop of blood returning from the arm. From the right atrium it passes through which valve, and into which chamber?
opciones: The tricuspid valve, into the right ventricle
The mitral valve, into the left ventricle
The pulmonary valve, into the pulmonary trunk
The bicuspid valve, into the right ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: Systemic blood enters the right atrium from the venae cavae, passes the right atrioventricular (tricuspid) valve into the right ventricle, is pumped through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk to the lungs, returns to the left atrium, crosses the mitral (bicuspid) valve into the left ventricle and leaves through the aortic valve. The bicuspid valve is on the left side only.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Right Ventricle; Heart Valve Structure and Function; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Pathway of Blood through the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1

preguntas.pregunta: A technologist reads the Gram stain of a positive blood culture bottle and sees organisms. Does that belong on the urgent notification list, which is full of numbers?
opciones: Yes; qualitative findings sit on that list beside the numerical limits
No; only a quantitative result can be defined as a critical limit
No; microbiology findings go through the infection control route instead
Yes, but only once the organism has been identified to species level
preguntas.explicacion: The urgent notification lists come in two parts. Alongside the numerical limits there is a table of qualitative findings that must reach the treating physician at once: organisms seen on the Gram stain of a blood culture or of a body cavity fluid, a rise in cerebrospinal fluid cells or organisms there, sickle cells or malarial parasites on a film, and drugs detected in urine.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), Table 2

preguntas.pregunta: Rapid test kits and their controls are taken straight from the refrigerator to run a patient sample. What does good practice call for first?
opciones: Allow the refrigerated reagents, kits and sample to reach room temperature before testing
Warm the reagents briefly in a water bath so the reaction is not slowed by the cold
Run the test at once, since reagents are most stable right out of the refrigerator
Discard the kit, because a refrigerated kit cannot be used at room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigerated reagents, test kits and patient samples are given time to come to room temperature before testing when the insert specifies it. Extreme temperatures degrade reagents, change reaction times and can cause premature expiration, so the insert's storage and operating ranges govern. Warming devices and shortcuts are not in the guidance; waiting is.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Preparing for Testing; CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Preparing the Testing Area, Test Materials, and Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Reagents to room temperature · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.f

preguntas.pregunta: Which technique describes a deep nasal swab?
opciones: Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, rotate several times, repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, hold still 10 seconds, and use a new swab per nostril
Insert to the depth of the ear opening, rotate several times, then repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch and withdraw at once, then place the swab tip into a dry sterile tube
preguntas.explicacion: With the head tilted back 70 degrees, the swab is gently rotated as it goes in, stopping under an inch when resistance is met at the turbinates. It is rotated several times against the nasal wall and the same swab is then used in the other nostril. The tip goes into a viral transport tube and the applicator stick is cut off. The ear-opening depth belongs to the nasopharyngeal swab.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Deep Nasal Swab
preguntas.subtema: Deep nasal swab · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2B.20

preguntas.pregunta: Nobody read the refrigerator thermometer over a long holiday weekend and the log has three empty rows. What should the person filling it in on Monday do?
opciones: Leave those rows blank, because there is no temperature data for them
Enter the Monday reading in the blank rows and initial each of them
Enter the average of the readings before and after the gap
Enter the acceptable range midpoint and note that the site was closed
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is blunt: if a reading was missed and no temperature data exist for that stretch, the entry stays blank, and nobody invents or guesses what the reading would have been. Where weekends or closures are foreseeable, the answer is a data logger that records minimum and maximum values, not a log filled in afterwards from memory.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: A vacuum-tube system is being used on a small child. What adjustment does the WHO device table call for, and why?
opciones: A smaller tube with reduced vacuum (1 to 5 ml), to reduce haemolysis
A larger tube with full vacuum, so the sample is collected before the vein collapses
A butterfly set with a discard tube, to remove the air from the tubing
A 16 to 18 G needle, so the tube fills before the tourniquet limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 says that with vacuum systems a smaller tube with reduced vacuum should be used for paediatric patients, and for retractable evacuated systems specifies a 1 to 5 ml tube with lower vacuum to reduce haemolysis. The discard tube is the butterfly rule for air in the tubing, and 16 to 18 G is the blood donation gauge in Table 3.1, far too large for a child.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Vacuum-tube systems and Manually retractable evacuated tube systems

preguntas.pregunta: Before a hospital adopts a new safety needle across its draw stations, what must the product evaluation show?
opciones: That the feature works reliably, staff accept it, and patient care does not suffer
That the device costs no more than the one it replaces over a full year
That the manufacturer has registered and listed it with the federal agency
That the injury rate has already fallen in the department that will use it
preguntas.explicacion: Devices with safety features should be evaluated on three points before they are adopted: the safety feature works effectively and reliably, the device is acceptable to the worker who will use it, and it does not harm patient care. The recommended process adds training in the new device, clear written criteria, on-site follow-up for informal feedback, and monitoring after implementation. Registration and listing are what the manufacturer owes the device regulator, not what the evaluation measures.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Evaluating a new device · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia becomes confused when told about the blood draw. How should the phlebotomist communicate?
opciones: Address the patient directly with simple wording, one idea at a time, and ask yes-or-no questions
Speak to the caregiver instead, since the patient cannot take part in decisions about care
Raise your voice and repeat the same sentence until the patient acknowledges it
Give the full explanation once, quickly, so the patient does not have time to become anxious
preguntas.explicacion: With a patient who has cognitive impairment, address the patient directly, use simple wording and present one idea at a time, ask questions in a yes-or-no or multiple-choice format, explain or re-explain who you are and what you will do, reassure the patient they are not being judged, and rephrase rather than speak too quickly or loudly if they hear but do not understand.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for older patients with cognitive impairment, Tips for communicating
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3C special needs, dementia · PBT II.B patient communication, special needs

preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a fasting glucose says he skipped breakfast but had a coffee with sugar an hour ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: He has broken the fast; tell the provider, since the test may need rescheduling
Coffee does not count as food, so the draw may proceed as a fasting sample
Proceed and mark the sample 'non-fasting' only if he also ate solid food
Wait one more hour so the sugar clears, then draw it as a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting means no food or drink except plain water; juice, coffee, soda and other beverages get into the bloodstream and affect results, and a patient who eats or drinks before the test should tell the provider because the test may have to be rescheduled. A fasting glucose needs at least 8 hours without caloric intake, not one more hour.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Can I drink anything besides water, and What if I make a mistake
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2

preguntas.pregunta: A chemistry panel gives results the clinician cannot explain, and the tube was set down without being inverted. What does the table warn about?
opciones: Blood not thoroughly mixed with its additive can give erroneous results
Blood not mixed with its additive loses the vacuum it was drawn under
Blood left unmixed separates into serum before it reaches the laboratory
Blood left unmixed cools too quickly and the additive stops working at all
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote to the order-of-draw table asks for additive tubes to be inverted gently and warns that erroneous results may follow when the blood is not thoroughly mixed with the additive. The movement described elsewhere is a figure-of-8, and it is done as soon as the tube comes off the needle.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote c

preguntas.pregunta: The sharps container in a drawing station is full to the top, so a phlebotomist sets the used needle on the tray to dispose of it later. Which risks are being ignored?
opciones: Injuries happen when sharps containers are overfilled and when used needles are not placed in them immediately
The needle should have been recapped with two hands and left on the tray until a container was available
The needle should have gone into the regulated-waste bag, since bags are acceptable whenever containers are full
There is no added risk once the safety feature is activated, so the delay is acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: Used needles are placed immediately into an approved sharps container located near the point of use; injuries also occur when needles end up in regular waste bags or when sharps containers are overfilled or mishandled. Routine recapping is no longer recommended because manipulating a used needle raises the risk of puncture, and the WHO requires the container to be within arm's reach and clearly visible.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern (recapping and disposal); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Several tubes are needed from one venipuncture. Which system does the WHO's Step 7 say to use, and what if it is not available?
opciones: Evacuated tubes with a needle and tube holder; otherwise a syringe or a winged needle set
A syringe, because it lets the phlebotomist control the pressure; otherwise evacuated tubes
A winged needle set attached to a syringe; otherwise a hypodermic needle and syringe
Evacuated tubes only; if they are not available the draw is postponed
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says that when multiple tubes are needed, evacuated tubes with a needle and tube holder are used because the tubes fill directly, and that a syringe or winged needle set is the alternative when that system is unavailable. Chapter 3 gives the reasons: closed vacuum systems reduce direct exposure to blood and make multiple samples from one puncture easier.
