preguntas.pregunta: How should the reasons for taking a blood sample be recorded in a service?
opciones: Clearly defined in a written protocol or in documented instructions
Agreed verbally between the phlebotomist and the ordering clinician
Written on the tube label at the moment the specimen is collected
Left to the judgement of whoever is drawing blood on that shift
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance asks that the indications for blood sampling be clearly defined, either in a written protocol or in documented instructions such as a laboratory form. Written standard operating procedures for each step also appear among the elements of quality assurance.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.2

preguntas.pregunta: Which containers does the equipment list accept for collecting the blood itself?
opciones: Glass or plastic tubes with rubber caps, vacuum tubes, or screw-capped glass
Vacuum tubes only, since caps of any other kind cannot hold a vacuum
Glass tubes with screw caps only, because plastic reacts with additives
Plastic tubes with rubber caps only, since glass may break in transport
preguntas.explicacion: Blood may be collected into sterile glass or plastic tubes with rubber caps, into vacuum-extraction tubes, or into glass tubes with screw caps, and which of them is used depends on what has been agreed with the laboratory. Isolation rooms, contact tracing, daily temperature checks and visitor logs
Sterile gloves, sterile fields, surgical scrub and sterile drapes for each draw
Testing every patient on admission and treating those who test positive

preguntas.pregunta: A skin biopsy is sent for histopathology and a second piece for bacterial culture. Which pair of handling instructions is correct?

Histopathology piece sterile and refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C; culture piece in 10 % neutral buffered formalin
Both pieces in 10 % neutral buffered formalin, the culture piece being rinsed in sterile saline before plating
Both pieces sterile at room temperature, since formalin is reserved for cytology and body fluid specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Tissue for histopathology is preserved in 10 % neutral buffered formalin, whereas tissue for microbiology or molecular testing must stay sterile and refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C unless freezing is specifically required. preguntas.pregunta: A patient due for a drug level asks whether to skip the morning dose so the result comes out low. What is the right answer?
opciones: No: doses are not stopped or changed without talking to the provider first
Yes: the dose is always held on the morning of a therapeutic drug level
Yes, if the level is a trough, since a trough must be drawn off therapy
No, but the dose may be delayed two hours without a new order
preguntas.explicacion: Patients must not stop or change their medicines before a drug level without speaking to the provider; the provider is the one who says whether the times of any doses need to change. A surrogate signs for any patient who carries a psychiatric diagnosis
Consent is waived, because the admission paperwork already covers draws
The nearest relative decides once a psychiatric diagnosis is on the record

preguntas.pregunta: Smoke starts pouring from a centrifuge in the processing room while two patients sit in the waiting area. Under the RACE sequence, what is the first action?

Activate the alarm system and call the operator
Confine the fire by closing the doors
Extinguish it with the nearest CO2 unit
preguntas.explicacion: RACE orders the response to a fire: R, rescue or remove all occupants from danger; A, activate the alarm system; C, confine the fire by closing doors; E, evacuate or extinguish. preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a hydrogen breath test finished a course of antibiotics ten days ago. Why does that matter?
opciones: Antibiotics should be avoided for at least 4 weeks before the test
Antibiotics should be avoided for at least 24 hours before the test
Antibiotics raise breath hydrogen, so the cutoff moves from 20 to 30 ppm
Antibiotics have no effect; only bowel preparation for colonoscopy does
preguntas.explicacion: Proper performance of hydrogen breath testing calls for no antibiotics in the four weeks before the test, and no testing within two weeks of bowel preparation for colonoscopy or surgery. 2 to 8 °C, that is 36 to 46 °F
18 to 22 °C, that is 64 to 72 °F
10 to 25 °C, that is 50 to 77 °F

preguntas.pregunta: Which chamber pumps blood into the systemic circuit, and why is its wall so much thicker than its counterpart's?
opciones: The left ventricle; it must overcome the high resistance of the long systemic circuit
The right ventricle; it must push blood through the dense capillary beds of both lungs
The left atrium; it receives oxygen-rich blood from all four of the pulmonary veins
The right atrium; it receives blood from both venae cavae and from the coronary sinus
preguntas.explicacion: The ventricles are the primary pumping chambers, and the left ventricle is the major pump for the systemic circuit, ejecting blood into the aorta. Although both ventricles move the same volume per beat, the left wall is much thicker because it must generate far more pressure to overcome the resistance of the long systemic circuit; the pulmonary circuit is shorter and offers less resistance.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a catheterized urine specimen for culture obtained?

The urethral opening is washed with an antiseptic, a needle is passed through the lower abdomen, and urine is aspirated
The patient voids the first portion into the toilet and the midstream portion into a sterile container held by the nurse
A thin catheter is passed into the bladder without cleansing, and the first urine to drain is discarded before collecting
preguntas.explicacion: A nurse or trained technician cleans the area around the urethral opening with an antiseptic, passes a thin rubber tube through the urethra into the bladder, lets the urine drain into a sterile container and removes the catheter. preguntas.pregunta: On a lactose tolerance blood test the glucose rises 24 mg/dL in two hours. How is that read?

Normal: any rise above 20 mg/dL rules out lactose intolerance
Abnormal: a rise under 30 mg/dL is diagnostic of lactose intolerance
Invalid: the rise has to be measured at 30 minutes, not at two hours
preguntas.explicacion: A glucose rise of more than 30 mg/dL within two hours of the lactose drink is normal, a rise of less than 20 mg/dL is abnormal, and 20 to 30 mg/dL is inconclusive, which is where 24 falls. preguntas.pregunta: A faint during a blood draw is usually vasovagal. Which other forms of reflex syncope are described alongside it?

Cardiac arrhythmia and orthostatic syncope, such as rising from a lying position
Hypoglycaemic syncope and febrile syncope, such as a faint during an infection
Carotid sinus syncope and cardiac syncope, such as a faint from a heart block
preguntas.explicacion: Reflex syncope covers episodes in which the control of blood pressure fails and brain perfusion drops. Prominent forearm veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture

A copy of its CLIA certificate and the qualifications of its laboratory director and testing personnel

preguntas.pregunta: How is a federal drug test specimen split between the two bottles?
opciones: At least 30 mL into bottle A and at least 15 mL into bottle B
At least 15 mL into bottle A and at least 30 mL into bottle B
At least 22.5 mL into each bottle, so the volumes match
All of it into bottle A, keeping bottle B for a later recollection
preguntas.explicacion: In the donor's presence the collector unwraps the sealed bottles and pours at least 30 mL into the A bottle and at least 15 mL into the B bottle, then caps both. As a laboratory still: only the incoming label rules apply to it

preguntas.pregunta: In which stage of point-of-care testing do most errors and interfering factors arise?
opciones: The pre-analytical stage, when the sample is collected, handled, prepared and loaded
The analytical stage, while the device is actually measuring the loaded sample
The post-analytical stage, when results are transcribed and communicated to the team
The stages contribute equally, since single-use devices remove most handling steps
preguntas.explicacion: POCT has three stages: pre-analytical (collecting, transporting, preparing and loading the sample), analytical (running the test) and post-analytical (communicating and interpreting results, including critical values). The pre-analytical phase is the most critical controllable variable, and most interfering factors occur there, through errors such as misidentification, hemolysis, clotting, under- or overfilling, prolonged tourniquet time, bubbles and microclots. Such errors decrease with operator experience and training.

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen that was poorly mixed reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. How does the clot affect the reading?
opciones: It disrupts the stacking of red cells and lowers the value obtained
It disrupts the stacking of red cells and raises the value obtained
It leaves the value unchanged, since only the plasma column is read
It raises the value, in the same way that a tilted tube raises it
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux, the coin-like stacks of red cells whose settling is being measured, so the value comes out lower than the patient's true one. The faults that raise the value are physical ones: a tilted tube, vibration, warmth and an inadequate fill.

The device is left in place and the tourniquet reapplied

The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer

preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?
opciones: Serum; it is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. Plasma is the fluid part of circulating blood, still carrying fibrinogen and the other factors; serum is what remains liquid after the blood clots in a tube. The buffy coat is the layer of white cells and platelets in a spun, unclotted sample, and whole blood has all the formed elements suspended.

preguntas.pregunta: Cortisol follows a diurnal rhythm. When is secretion at its peak?
opciones: Near the time of awakening, after rising in the last hours of sleep
Around 4 p.m., after rising steadily through the afternoon
At night, when ACTH release from the pituitary is highest
About two hours after the first meal of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Cortisol secretion follows a diurnal rhythm: levels begin to rise in the final hours of sleep, peak near the time of awakening, decline gradually through the day and reach their lowest concentration at night; healthy adults produce 8 to 30 mg per day. preguntas.pregunta: How do Transmission-Based Precautions relate to Standard Precautions, according to the CDC?
opciones: A second tier added to Standard Precautions for patients with certain known or suspected infections
A replacement for Standard Precautions once a pathogen has been confirmed by the laboratory
The first tier, applied to every patient until an infection has been ruled out
A set that covers bloodborne pathogens only, while Standard Precautions cover respiratory ones
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission-Based Precautions are the second tier of basic infection control, used in addition to Standard Precautions for patients who may be infected or colonized with agents that need extra measures. They never replace the first tier, and they are triggered by known or suspected infection, not applied to everyone. The three categories are Contact, Droplet and Airborne, chosen by the route of transmission; bloodborne exposure is handled by Standard Precautions and the OSHA standard.

preguntas.pregunta: A 1-hour gestational screening result comes back at 152 mg/dL. What happens next?
opciones: She returns fasting for a 3-hour, 100 g glucose tolerance test
She is told she has gestational diabetes and is started on a diet
She repeats the same 50 g screening drink at her next prenatal visit
She returns fasting for a 2-hour, 75 g glucose tolerance test
preguntas.explicacion: Above 140 mg/dL the screen is not a diagnosis: the patient comes back after an 8- to 14-hour fast for the diagnostic test, a 100 g load with a draw before the drink and one every 60 minutes for three hours. About one in five patients fails the screen, and roughly two out of three of those turn out not to have gestational diabetes. The 75 g 2-hour test belongs to the one-step pathway.

preguntas.pregunta: Where does latex rank among the causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room?
opciones: Second, after muscle relaxants
First, ahead of muscle relaxants
Third, after antibiotics and dyes
Second, after the antiseptic used on skin
preguntas.explicacion: Latex allergy is among the most common causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room, and its prevalence grew with the wider use of latex gloves from the 1980s onward. It is named the most common cause of contact urticaria in occupational health, and the second most common cause of intraoperative anaphylaxis, behind muscle relaxants.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Introduction and section Epidemiology

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic performs only fingerstick glucose and other tests on the CLIA waived list. Which CLIA certificate does it need?
opciones: A certificate of waiver from CMS
A certificate of compliance
A certificate of accreditation
A certificate for PPM procedures
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate of waiver is issued to a laboratory that restricts itself to the waived tests listed in 42 CFR 493.15(c) and no others. A certificate of compliance follows an inspection finding compliance with all condition-level requirements; a certificate of accreditation rests on accreditation by an organization approved by CMS; and a certificate for PPM procedures covers a physician, midlevel practitioner or dentist doing only provider-performed microscopy plus, if desired, waived tests. A registration certificate lets an entity do moderate or high complexity testing until surveyed.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (1)-(5); 42 CFR 493.15(c)

preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what must a laboratory's written policies guarantee about a patient's specimen?
opciones: Positive identification and integrity from collection or receipt through testing and reporting
Positive identification at the moment of collection, after which the accession number takes over
Positive identification by a second staff member whenever the patient cannot state their own name
Integrity during transport above all, since the analyzer confirms the identity when it is received
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen identification standard covers the whole span, not a moment: written policies and procedures must ensure positive identification and optimum integrity of the patient's specimen from the time it is collected or received until testing is finished and the result is reported. Labeling at the bedside is where that chain starts, but it does not end there.

preguntas.pregunta: How may the sample for a donor's hemoglobin or hematocrit be obtained?
opciones: By fingerstick or venipuncture, but not from the earlobe
By fingerstick or from the earlobe, but not by venipuncture
By venipuncture only, since capillary values are unreliable
By fingerstick only, since venipuncture wastes donor volume
preguntas.explicacion: The hemoglobin level or hematocrit value is determined on a sample obtained by fingerstick, by venipuncture, or by a method that gives equivalent results; blood obtained from the earlobe is not acceptable. The earlobe is the trap in this rule, because it looks like just another capillary site and is named specifically to rule it out.

preguntas.pregunta: A dark green sodium heparin tube and a light green PST are both ordered. Which comes first in the WHO sequence?
opciones: The dark green sodium heparin tube, then the light green PST
The light green PST, then the dark green sodium heparin tube
Either one, because both contain heparin and share position 6
The light green PST, because gel tubes precede plain heparin tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists the dark green sodium heparin tube at position 6 and the light green plasma separator tube, with lithium heparin and a gel separator, at position 7. They are two separate rows, not a shared position, and the gel tube comes after the plain heparin tube. Footnote d confirms that the PST, if used, is drawn in the position shown.

preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old with small, difficult veins needs one tube of blood. Which device does the WHO device table favour, and what advantage does it list?
opciones: A winged (butterfly) needle, which allows better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle
A vacuum-tube system, which eliminates blood transfer and allows numerous samples from a single puncture
An auto-disable syringe, which prevents reuse and reduces the risk of needle-sticks
A 21 G straight needle with a syringe, which is the most common means of blood sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 describes winged steel needles as good for drawing blood from paediatric patients or from patients with small or difficult veins, allowing better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle, at higher cost and with the air-in-the-tubing caveat. Auto-disable syringes are explicitly not recommended for phlebotomy, and Table 3.1 gives no 21 G option for children.

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
preguntas.explicacion: In a 7 pound (3 kg) baby the distances from skin to bone are: 3.32 mm at the medial and lateral heel, 2.33 mm at the posterior heel and 2.19 mm at the toe. The posterior heel is to be avoided to reduce the risk of hitting bone. The tibial artery is the risk of the medial aspect of the heel, and the 0.85 mm lancet is simply the size available for premature neonates.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine for porphyrins is ordered. Which container feature does this analyte require?
opciones: An amber-colored container, because porphyrins are light sensitive
A clear container, so the laboratory can see the color of the pooled urine
A vacuum tube, which draws the sample without opening the container
A sterile container, because porphyrin testing requires a bacteriological culture
preguntas.explicacion: Light-sensitive analytes such as porphyrins and urobilinogen call for amber containers, in addition to the general requirements that the container be non-absorbing and free of interfering agents. Sterile collection is mandatory for culture, not for chemistry, and vacuum systems are limited to chemical analysis because the pressure difference breaks up brittle casts and lowers cast counts.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is transferring blood from a syringe into three tubes. How is the rack handled?
opciones: Keep the tubes in the rack, draw the rack closer, and inject downwards
Lift each tube out of the rack and hold it steady in the free hand
Keep the tubes in the rack and tilt them so the blood runs down the wall
Lift the rack up to eye level so the coloured stoppers stay in view
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, the tubes stay in their rack and the rack is moved towards the worker, with the blood injected downwards into the appropriately coloured stopper. Holding a tube in the free hand is what the needle-stick precaution for this step is meant to avoid.

preguntas.pregunta: Why do devices with safety features reduce needlestick injuries without eliminating them?
opciones: Some cannot be activated until the needle is out, and some users bypass them
Their shields are made of plastic, which a needle can pierce from inside
They are sold only for hypodermic needles, not for blood collection sets
They must be removed before the tube is filled, leaving the tip exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Several things keep the risk above zero. With some designs the safety feature cannot be engaged until the needle has already left the patient; a needle can be dislodged during the procedure and leave the sharp exposed; some workers do not activate the feature at all; the feature itself can fail; and with some systems users can work around it, as when a needle is used to connect parts of a needleless intravenous system. Training and monitoring after implementation are what close that gap.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Use of Improved Engineering Controls in a Prevention Strategy

preguntas.pregunta: How much alcohol-based hand rub goes on the hands, and how is it worked in?
opciones: About 3 to 5 mL, rubbed over every surface until the hands are dry
A single small drop, rubbed into the palms and wiped with a towel
About 15 to 20 mL, poured over the hands and rinsed off with water
Enough to fill a cupped hand, left to evaporate without any rubbing
preguntas.explicacion: When hands are not visibly soiled the alcohol rub is the preferred method, and it is used as the manufacturer directs: roughly three to five millilitres in the palm, rubbed vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry, which takes about twenty seconds. Rubbing until dry is what does the work, so wiping the product off with a towel or letting it sit unrubbed cuts the contact short, and the rub is never rinsed away with water.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications; CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, duration

preguntas.pregunta: Tubes of blood go from the draw room to the in-house laboratory in a closed rack, and the facility applies Universal Precautions to all specimens. Is a biohazard label required?
opciones: Not while they stay in the facility and are recognizable as specimens; it is required once they leave
Yes, always: every container of blood must carry the fluorescent orange-red biohazard label
No, never: labeling applies to regulated waste containers, not to specimens of blood
Only if the primary container becomes contaminated on the outside and needs a second container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(A) requires specimen containers for storage, transport or shipping to be labeled or color-coded and closed, but it exempts facilities that handle all specimens under Universal Precautions, provided the containers are recognizable as specimens; the exemption holds only inside the facility, and the label returns the moment specimens leave it. Labeling is not limited to waste: (g)(1)(i)(A) covers containers used to store, transport or ship blood. Outside contamination triggers a second container under (d)(2)(xiii)(B), a different rule.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(A) and (g)(1)(i)(A), specimen containers and labels

preguntas.pregunta: The bevel is inside the vein and blood has appeared. How is the needle advanced from there?
opciones: Along the vein, at whichever angle of entry proves easiest
Straight down at ninety degrees until the hub meets the skin
Back out a few millimetres and then in again at a steeper angle
Sideways across the vein so the bevel opens against the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The vein is entered swiftly at thirty degrees or less, and the needle then continues along the vein at the easiest angle of entry rather than being pushed deeper. Driving it beyond the lumen of the vein is what produces a haematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment

preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What are physical safeguards and How do you protect electronic information; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Storage of PHI Data and Computers

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a sore throat says she gargled with antiseptic mouthwash on the way to the office. Why does that matter for a throat culture?
opciones: Antiseptic mouthwash is specifically to be avoided before the test, which is otherwise unprepared for
Antiseptic mouthwash is required before the test, so the swab picks up only pharyngeal organisms
Antiseptic mouthwash makes the patient gag more, which prevents the swab from reaching the tonsils
Antiseptic mouthwash stains the pharynx, so the provider cannot see where to place the swab
preguntas.explicacion: The one preparation instruction for a throat swab culture is to skip antiseptic mouthwash beforehand, since it works against the organisms the culture is meant to grow. Everything else about the test needs no preparation. Rinsing the mouth with plain water belongs to sputum collection, where the aim is to wash away oral contaminants rather than to kill anything.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a drug level ordered as a trough but says he took this morning's dose an hour ago. What matters?
opciones: Timing relative to the dose changes the result; report it before drawing
The level is stable through the day, so proceed and label the tube as ordered
Draw it now and relabel the sample as a peak level instead of a trough
Wait 30 minutes, which is the standard window for any trough sample
preguntas.explicacion: For TDM the test may need to be scheduled before or after the regular dose depending on the medicine, and the level in the blood varies over time as the body processes the drug. The trough is the point just before the next dose; a sample an hour after dosing is not that. Relabelling it as a peak invents a measurement that was not ordered.

preguntas.pregunta: Two boxes of gloves list different acceptable quality levels. What does a lower number mean?
opciones: A better glove, with fewer pinholes and micro-perforations
A thicker glove, made to be worn as the outer of two pairs
A cheaper glove, meant for handling clean supplies only
A sterile glove, treated so that microbes are eliminated
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptable quality level is a measure of how many defective units a batch may contain, so a lower figure means a higher quality glove with less potential for micro-perforation and fewer pinholes. The recommended minimum is 1.5 for surgical gloves and 2.5 for medical examination gloves. Sterility is a separate property: surgical procedures call for sterile gloves, which have been treated to eliminate microbes, and evidence supports two layers during surgery.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE

preguntas.pregunta: Immediately after washing a needlestick with soap and water, what does NIOSH tell the worker to do?
opciones: Report the incident to the supervisor and seek medical care right away
Wait 72 hours to see whether symptoms appear before reporting
Test the discarded needle for virus before deciding whether to report
Start the hepatitis B vaccine series on their own before reporting
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH's steps are to wash punctures and cuts with soap and water, flush splashes, irrigate eyes, report the incident to the supervisor and immediately seek medical care to determine the risk; it adds that an incident report should be completed where applicable. The 72-hour figure is the outer limit for starting HIV PEP, not a waiting period. WHO's annex specifically says not to test discarded needles or syringes for virus, and any prophylaxis or vaccination is decided during the medical evaluation.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Treatment and Reporting; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 3

preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is taught the boundaries of the fossa before palpating it. Which muscles form its lateral and medial borders?
opciones: Brachioradialis on the lateral side and pronator teres on the medial side
Pronator teres on the lateral side and brachioradialis on the medial side
Biceps brachii on the lateral side and brachialis on the medial side
Brachialis on the lateral side and supinator on the medial side of the fossa
preguntas.explicacion: The triangle is bounded laterally by the medial edge of brachioradialis and medially by the lateral edge of pronator teres, with an imaginary line between the epicondyles of the humerus closing it above. Brachialis and supinator lie deeper: they form the floor rather than the sides.

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives with her adult son, who answers every question for her. How should you handle the visit?
opciones: Ask the patient how she sees her son's role, and keep addressing her directly
Speak mainly to the son, since he manages her medications at home
Ask the son to leave the room before any question is put to her
Record the son as her legal decision-maker for the rest of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Check with the patient about how they see the companion's role, to protect privacy, and keep the patient involved, sitting so both can be addressed face to face and not directing remarks only to the companion. Asking the companion to step out is an option for sensitive topics, and legal authority to decide exists only for a named health care agent or proxy.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether to skip his blood-pressure pill before a fasting draw. What is the correct guidance?
opciones: Do not stop a medicine unless the provider said to; ask the provider
Skip every medicine on the morning of the draw, because all pills break a fast
Take it only with a little juice so that the stomach is protected
Take it after the draw with water, never before a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should ask the provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines are fine; for some tests the provider may ask them to stop, but a medicine is never stopped unless the provider says so. Vitamins and supplements should also be reported. Juice is on the list of drinks that break a fast.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being evaluated for pulmonary tuberculosis. Which sputum collection and storage instruction is correct?
opciones: Three early-morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each, kept in a refrigerator
One early-morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL, kept at room temperature
Three specimens collected at any time of day, each frozen at −20 °C
Three early-morning specimens of 2 to 3 mL each, kept in a CO2 incubator
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early-morning sputum specimens, 8 to 10 mL each, is collected and stored refrigerated; in patients who cannot cooperate the organism may be recovered from gastric contents obtained by stomach aspiration. Freezing is not part of the instruction, a single specimen is not a series, and the carbon dioxide incubator belongs to cerebrospinal fluid awaiting culture.

preguntas.pregunta: Where should the sharps container sit while a phlebotomist is drawing blood at the bedside?
opciones: Visible and within arm's reach, and sealed once it is used up
On the cart outside the room, so the patient does not see it
In the utility room, where the used needles are carried after
On the floor by the bed, where it cannot be knocked over easily
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table asks for puncture and leak-proof containers that are sealed after use, kept visible and within arm's reach, and the reason given is that this prevents needlestick injury to patients, health workers and the wider community. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same in regulatory language: during use the container is easily accessible and as close as feasible to where sharps are used, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician with similar training and experience would provide
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is judged against the standard of care, defined as what a reasonable physician in the community with similar training and experience would do for that patient; it does not demand perfection, and some states speak of gross negligence. Malpractice itself is the failure to provide the degree of care another clinician in the same position with the same credentials would have provided, resulting in injury. Facility policies and patient expectations may be evidence, but the legal yardstick is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty

preguntas.pregunta: A processor inspects centrifuged serum tubes and sets aside the ones that look pink. Why do current recommendations favour an automated hemolysis index over this visual check?
opciones: Visual detection is inaccurate: serum looks hemolysed only above about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, whereas the index is reproducible
Visual detection is accurate for serum but not for plasma, so the index is needed only for anticoagulated tubes
Visual detection is reliable above 0.5 g/L, but only the index can detect hemolysis before centrifugation
Visual detection cannot distinguish hemolysis from lipemia, whereas the index reports both as a single value
preguntas.explicacion: Sample quality used to be judged by looking at the tube before and after spinning, but visual detection is inaccurate: after separation, free hemoglobin becomes visible only around 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the cut-off for clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. Chemistry analyzers measure the serum indices, hemolysis included, with high reproducibility, which is why systematic automated measurement is strongly recommended.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: Which group of items are the preanalytical quality indicators proposed by the IFCC working group on laboratory errors and patient safety?
opciones: Inappropriate containers, insufficient volume, hemolyzed or clotted samples, improper storage, transport damage
Reagent lot changes, calibration drift, control values out of range, instrument downtime and maintenance
Turnaround time, corrected reports, critical value notification time, legibility and delivery of reports
Repeat test rate, physician satisfaction, cost per test, proficiency testing scores and staff competency
preguntas.explicacion: The IFCC WG-LEPS indicators for the preanalytical phase cover appropriateness of test selection, patient and sample identification, samples collected in inappropriate containers or with insufficient volume, hemolyzed or clotted samples, improperly stored samples and samples damaged in transport. Calibration and controls are analytical measures; turnaround, corrected reports and critical value timing are post-analytical ones.

preguntas.pregunta: What target serum trough range is given for vancomycin, varying with the indication?
opciones: 10 to 20 micrograms per millilitre
1 to 2 micrograms per millilitre
30 to 40 micrograms per millilitre
100 to 200 micrograms per millilitre
preguntas.explicacion: Trough concentrations let the team judge whether the dosing regimen is working and how the drug is being cleared. The target serum trough depends on the indication and typically runs from 10 to 20 micrograms per millilitre. It is obtained ideally within the 30 minutes before a dose, once steady-state conditions have been reached.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasted twelve hours before a blood count on his own initiative, though nobody asked him to. What is the concern?
opciones: Fasting when it was not ordered can itself skew some test results
Fasting beyond eight hours voids any test drawn that same morning
Fasting without an order has to be logged as a protocol deviation
Fasting is harmless here, and the sample is unaffected either way
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told plainly not to fast unless the provider asks them to, because fasting for some blood tests may itself affect the results and hand the provider an inaccurate picture of the patient's health. The instruction is to follow the preparation instructions given; no rule voids a sample because the fast ran long.

preguntas.pregunta: A transplant patient is scheduled for a tacrolimus level. What timing does the reported reference range assume?
opciones: The sample is taken 12 hours after the dose
The sample is taken 2 hours after the dose
The sample is taken immediately before the dose
The sample is taken at any hour of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Tacrolimus is reported as 5 to 25 ng/mL with the sample drawn 12 hours after the dose, and the two other drugs used to suppress the immune response against transplanted organs carry the same note: cyclosporine 25 to 525 ng/mL and sirolimus 4 to 14 ng/mL, both at 12 hours. A level drawn off that schedule cannot be read against the published range.

preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old with an emergency medical condition needs urgent labs and no parent can be reached. What protects the team that proceeds?
opciones: The emergency exception, also called the doctrine of implied consent
The mature minor doctrine, because the child understands the test
Informed permission, granted on the spot by the hospital administrator
Title X of the Public Health Service Act, covering minors' services
preguntas.explicacion: EMTALA requires a screening exam regardless of consent, and that when an emergency condition is found in an unaccompanied minor, life- or limb-saving care proceeds without waiting for parental consent, protected by the emergency exception rule or doctrine of implied consent, which assumes a reasonable parent would agree. Title X covers reproductive services.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", section Issues of Concern

preguntas.pregunta: Where do the coronary arteries arise, and where does most of the blood from the coronary veins drain?
opciones: From the ascending aorta; into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium
From the aortic arch; into the coronary sinus and then the left atrium
From the pulmonary trunk; directly into the superior vena cava
From the ascending aorta; into the four pulmonary veins and left atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The right and left coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta, and they are the only branches of that segment. After passing through the myocardial capillaries most cardiac veins empty into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium on its posterior wall, just above and medial to the opening of the inferior vena cava.

preguntas.pregunta: A PNAS study examined false beliefs about biological differences between Black and White patients held by medical trainees. What did those beliefs lead to?
opciones: Lower ratings of Black patients' pain and less accurate treatment recommendations
Higher rates of hypertension among the trainees who held the beliefs
More referrals of Black patients for kidney transplantation
Overtreatment of pain in Black patients compared with White patients
preguntas.explicacion: Medical students and residents who endorsed beliefs such as thicker skin or less sensitive nerve endings rated Black patients' pain lower and made less accurate treatment recommendations, a legacy visible in the undertreatment of pain. The kidney example runs the other way: race-corrected eGFR delays diagnosis and reduces access to transplantation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", section Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: When must HIV post-exposure prophylaxis begin, and how long does the course last, according to the CDC?
opciones: As soon as possible and within 72 hours; a 28-day course
As soon as possible and within 7 days; a 14-day course
As soon as possible and within 24 hours; a 7-day course
Within 72 hours; a 6-month course, the length of follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who seek care within 72 hours are evaluated rapidly; PEP is not recommended more than 72 hours after exposure because it is unlikely to work, and the regimen is 28 days of a three-drug antiretroviral combination. WHO's annex gives the same limits: start within 72 hours and take the drugs continuously for 28 days. Six months is the length of antibody follow-up after an exposure, not the length of treatment, and the CDC's occupational page adds that PEP must start within 72 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist arrives at room 412 to collect a CBC. Which pair of identifiers satisfies The Joint Commission's NPSG.01.01.01 for laboratory services?
opciones: The patient's stated full name plus the assigned identification number
The room number 412 plus the assigned identification number on the band
The patient's stated full name plus the physical location of the bed
The assigned identification number read from the chart, used on its own
preguntas.explicacion: NPSG.01.01.01 asks for at least two identifiers whenever blood or other specimens are collected. The goal's rationale accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and EP 1 states outright that a room number or physical location is not used as one. A single identifier from the chart does not reach two.

preguntas.pregunta: Two heel-pricks on an infant have failed to give a satisfactory sample. What is the next step?
opciones: Seek a second opinion on whether to try again or cancel the tests
Make a third attempt on the other heel with a longer lancet
Switch to a finger-prick, which is allowed once the heel has failed twice
Repeat the puncture on the same site, since it is already open
preguntas.explicacion: There is a strict limit on the number of times a paediatric patient may be stuck: if no satisfactory sample has been collected after two attempts, seek a second opinion to decide whether to make a further attempt or cancel the tests. Reusing a puncture site is prohibited, and site choice follows age and weight, not the number of failures.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vessels are the only arteries in the post-natal body that carry relatively deoxygenated blood?
opciones: The pulmonary trunk and its branches
The four pulmonary veins to the left atrium
The coronary arteries off the ascending aorta
The venae cavae entering the right atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The pulmonary trunk and the pulmonary arteries it divides into are the only post-natal arteries carrying relatively deoxygenated blood, from the right ventricle toward the lungs, and the pulmonary veins are the only post-natal veins carrying highly oxygenated blood, into the left atrium. The coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta with oxygenated blood; the venae cavae are veins.

preguntas.pregunta: For which purpose is an arterial sample, rather than a venous one, the indicated specimen?
opciones: Gathering data on arterial blood gases
Gathering data on a complete blood count
Gathering data on coagulation factor levels
Gathering data on a fasting plasma glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Routine draws use veins because they are superficial and the puncture is more comfortable, and arterial sampling is reserved for the case where arterial blood is what the test needs, namely blood gases. The counts, clotting studies and chemistries of everyday work are all run on venous blood.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology

preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures and the first dose of an IV antibiotic are ordered together for a patient with suspected sepsis. What is the correct sequence?
opciones: Draw the blood cultures first, then let the antibiotic be started
Start the antibiotic and draw the cultures at any point within 24 hours
Draw one set before the antibiotic and the second set after the first dose
Draw the cultures 12 hours after the dose, when the drug is at its trough
preguntas.explicacion: Blood should be collected for culture before antimicrobial therapy whenever possible; that is step 4 of the CDC procedure and the recommendation for suspected sepsis in its overview. Without a culture taken before antibiotics, the causative organism is more likely to stay unknown and therapy is harder to de-escalate. The 24-hour period defines the septic episode for counting sets, and the 12-hour figure is a drug-level timing, not a culture rule.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model step 4; and Overview (2022), section 1

preguntas.pregunta: How is a newborn in a hospital cot identified before drawing blood?
opciones: Use a band attached to the baby, ask the parent for the first and last names, and match the form
Use the band attached to the cot and the cot number, since a newborn cannot wear a band safely
Ask the nurse on duty to confirm the cot number and rely on that as the single identifier
Match the mother's wristband to the form, since the baby is registered under her record
preguntas.explicacion: For paediatric and neonatal patients, use a wrist or foot band only if it is attached to the patient, never the bed number or a band attached to the bed or cot; to ask a parent or legal guardian present for the child's first and last names; and to check that name, date of birth and hospital or file number on the laboratory form match the patient.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.1 Patient identification

preguntas.pregunta: The ward holds two patients named John Ramirez. Beyond the full name and date of birth, what does the accepted practice add before the draw?
opciones: One further general identifier, such as the social security number or address
The bed each of the two men occupies, written by hand on both laboratory forms
The middle initial only, since the ward clerk keeps the two charts well apart
The list of tests ordered, because the two requisitions ask for different work
preguntas.explicacion: Every admitted patient carries an ID bracelet, and the name and date of birth are asked and recorded. The accepted consensus adds one more general identifier, a social security number or an address, because supplementary data lowers the rate of preventable errors. Location never counts: the identification goal rules out the room number or physical place.

preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens beyond HIV and the hepatitis viruses are named as transmissible through this procedure?
opciones: Viral haemorrhagic fevers and dengue, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Influenza and tuberculosis, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Viral haemorrhagic fevers and measles, with tetanus through the puncture wound
Dengue and influenza, with tetanus and rabies through the puncture wound itself
preguntas.explicacion: Drawing blood can expose workers and patients to bloodborne pathogens, and the list runs beyond HIV and hepatitis B and C to the viruses of Crimean Congo haemorrhagic fever, Ebola, Lassa and Marburg, and to dengue. Malaria and syphilis may also travel in contaminated blood.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: Training records under the bloodborne pathogens standard must be kept for how long?
opciones: Three years from the date the training took place
One year after the last entry, like the extinguisher record
Thirty years beyond the end of the worker's employment
Six years from the date the record was last in effect
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(ii) fixes the period at 3 years counted from the date of the training session. The other numbers are real but belong to other rules: one year after the last entry is the retention of the annual maintenance record for portable fire extinguishers in 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(3); employment plus 30 years is the employee medical record in (h)(1)(iv); and six years is the HIPAA retention for policies and documentation in 45 CFR 164.530(j)(2).
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(2)(ii), Training Records

preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient bites a phlebotomist's forearm and breaks the skin. Under the standard, this contact is best described as which of these?
opciones: A parenteral exposure, since piercing the skin barrier by a human bite is listed as parenteral
Not an exposure incident, because saliva is not OPIM outside dental procedures
An occupational exposure but not an exposure incident, because no needle was involved
A contact exposure that requires Contact Precautions rather than post-exposure follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines parenteral as piercing the mucous membranes or the skin barrier through events such as needlesticks, human bites, cuts and abrasions, and an exposure incident as parenteral or mucous-membrane or non-intact-skin contact with blood or OPIM arising from the employee's duties. A bite that breaks the skin is therefore a parenteral route, and if blood is involved the post-exposure evaluation of (f)(3) applies. Saliva is OPIM only in dental procedures, but the bite itself is the parenteral event; needles are one example of the route, not the only one.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Parenteral, Exposure Incident
preguntas.subtema: Parenteral exposure · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11

preguntas.pregunta: Blood was drawn with a syringe and must be transferred into evacuated tubes. How does the WHO say the tube should be held and filled to prevent a needle-stick?
opciones: Place the tube in a rack and fill it with one hand, or use a needle shield between needle and hand
Hold the tube firmly in the free hand and pierce the stopper at an angle toward the fingers
Remove the stopper, rest the tube in the palm and inject slowly against the inner wall of the tube
Hold the tube against the patient's arm so the syringe can be steadied on the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says best practice with a syringe or winged set is to put the tube in a rack before filling, and to use one hand to fill it or a needle shield between the needle and the hand holding the tube. The stopper is pierced from directly above with slow, steady pressure and is never removed, because that releases the vacuum. Holding the tube in the hand is exactly the exposure the step is designed to avoid.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k59 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9

preguntas.pregunta: Under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens standard, what does the term "Universal Precautions" mean?
opciones: Treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they carried a bloodborne pathogen
Treating as infectious only the blood of patients whose chart shows HIV or hepatitis B
Reasonably anticipated contact of skin, eyes or mucous membranes with blood in the course of one's duties
Controls that isolate or remove the hazard from the workplace, such as sharps containers and safer needles
preguntas.explicacion: In the standard's definitions, Universal Precautions is one approach to controlling infection: every specimen of human blood, and certain other body fluids, is handled as though it were known to carry HIV, HBV or another bloodborne pathogen. Nothing depends on a chart, a test result or a diagnosis, so the same barriers apply to every patient. The other two definitions sit next to it in paragraph (b): reasonably anticipated contact in the course of one's duties is Occupational Exposure, and devices that isolate or remove the hazard are Engineering Controls.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Universal Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard and universal precautions · CPT D1 1J k31 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C k99 · CMA I.B.4 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: A printed report shows the patient's name and ID, the test, the result with units, and the report date, but not where the test was done. Which CLIA report element is missing?
opciones: The performing laboratory's name and the address of its location
The name and address of the authorized person who ordered the test
The date and time the specimen was received in the laboratory
The identity of the testing personnel who performed the test
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(c) lists what a test report must show: positive patient identification, the name and address of the location where the testing was done, the report date, the test performed, the specimen source when appropriate, the result with its units or interpretation, and any information on the condition and disposition of unacceptable specimens. Receipt time and the identity of testing personnel belong to the test record system under 493.1283, not to the report itself.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(c), Standard: Test report

preguntas.pregunta: A new technician shakes each tube vigorously right after collection to make sure the additive mixes. What does the evidence quoted in the rejection study say about this?
opciones: Tubes should be inverted gently several times; instant vigorous mixing may itself produce hemolysis
Vigorous shaking is required for citrate tubes and optional for EDTA tubes, per manufacturers' data sheets
Shaking is harmless for whole blood but must be avoided once the tube has been centrifuged
Tubes must be shaken for one full minute, since gentle inversion leaves fibrin filaments in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers' data sheets and CLSI documents recommend gentle inversion of vacuum tubes several times to bring blood and additive together; a study cited found that mixing immediately after collection for a minute with 15 inversions may not even be mandatory and that instant mixing can cause hemolysis, and a later trial saw no fibrin or microclots with five gentle inversions, or even with none. Shaking is never the instruction.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: How are goggles or a face shield handled when the equipment is being taken off?
opciones: By the strap or the earpieces, never by the front surface
By the lower rim, which stays clean during a procedure
By the front, folded inward so the outside faces itself
By the strap, and then wiped dry with the gown's sleeve
preguntas.explicacion: Eye protection comes off second, after the gloves. The front of it is the contaminated side, the part that met whatever was sprayed or splashed, so it is handled by the strap or the earpieces and dropped into the right container for reprocessing or disposal. The same idea governs the mask, taken off by the ties or straps behind the head without touching the front or the mouth area.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE

preguntas.pregunta: Gloves worn for one draw are still clean to look at. What does the infection control table say?
opciones: One pair per procedure or patient, and gloves are never washed for reuse
One pair per session, and gloves may be washed if they stay unsoiled
One pair per patient, and gloves may be reused after an alcohol rub
One pair per procedure, and gloves are changed only when visibly soiled
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is one pair of non-sterile gloves for each procedure or patient, with two prohibitions beside it: the same pair is not used on more than one patient, and gloves are not washed so that they can be used again. The device itself is single use for the same reason.

preguntas.pregunta: A woman asks how to clean herself before giving a clean-catch urine sample. What should the medical assistant tell her?
opciones: Spread the labia and use two wipes, front to back: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Spread the labia and use two wipes, back to front: one for the inner folds, a second over the urethral opening
Clean the urethral opening with one wipe after retracting the surrounding skin, as done for the head of the penis
Rinse the area with warm water and soap, then dry, exactly as done before placing an infant collection bag
preguntas.explicacion: For a clean-catch, a woman sits with her legs apart, separates the labia with two fingers and uses the first sterile wipe on the inner folds and the second on the urethral opening, always wiping from the front toward the back. Retracting the foreskin is the instruction for uncircumcised men, and washing with soap and water is the routine before an infant bag. The labia stay separated while she voids.

preguntas.pregunta: Which behaviour is listed as a trigger to look further into a patient's decision-making capacity?
opciones: Blanket acceptance or refusal of the care being offered
Asking several detailed questions about the tests ordered
Requesting that a relative be present during the draw
Preferring one particular arm for the venipuncture
preguntas.explicacion: The triggers listed are an inability to voice a decision, blanket acceptance or refusal of care, an absence of questions about the treatment offered, excessive or inconsistent reasons for refusing, a new inability to manage daily activities, agitation or disruptive behaviour, labile mood, hallucinations and clinical intoxication. Asking questions points the other way.

preguntas.pregunta: After identity is verified, which patient factors should be asked about and recorded before the draw?
opciones: Any special diet, medications, supplements and herbal preparations
Insurance plan, the copayment collected and the status of the referral
Blood type, previous transfusions and history of blood donation
Height, weight and the vital signs recorded at the previous visit
preguntas.explicacion: Once identification is confirmed, double-check fasting status and preparation and to ask about and record patient factors with a documented effect on results: a distinct diet, medications, nutritional supplements and herbal preparations. preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is filled below its mark. Which way do the clotting times move, and why?
opciones: They lengthen, because the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma present
They shorten, because the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma present
They lengthen, because the tube loses part of its vacuum during the short draw
They shorten, because the citrate binds less calcium when the tube is not full
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate tubes come pre-loaded with a fixed amount of anticoagulant and marked with the volume of blood wanted. Draw less than that and the anticoagulant is in excess for the plasma collected, which prolongs the clotting time reported. Full filling is what keeps the nine-to-one proportion intact.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist spends three minutes searching for a vein with the tourniquet in place before drawing a chemistry panel. What effect does this have on the specimen?
opciones: Hemoconcentration, which falsely elevates laboratory results
Haemolysis, because the prolonged pressure ruptures red cells in the vein
Dilution of the sample with tissue fluid, as happens when a finger is squeezed
Platelet clumping in the tube, producing a falsely low platelet count
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet should come off within 1 minute, because prolonged constriction produces hemoconcentration and falsely elevated results; the WHO gives two minutes as the outer limit, and three minutes exceeds both. Tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's warning about squeezing a finger-prick, and platelet clumping is the EDTA artifact, not a tourniquet effect.

A judge, because capacity is settled by the judiciary system

preguntas.pregunta: Blood placed in a plain glass tube clots on its own. Which factor starts that in-vitro clotting, and through which pathway?

Factor III (tissue factor), through the extrinsic pathway
Factor IV (calcium ions), through the common pathway
Factor I (fibrinogen), through the fibrinolytic pathway
preguntas.explicacion: The intrinsic, or contact activation, pathway is most often started when factor XII, the Hageman factor, touches foreign material, and a blood sample put into a glass test tube is the classic example. preguntas.pregunta: A 22-year-old of normal weight has never had a high glucose result, has no first-degree relatives with diabetes and had no problems in an earlier pregnancy. What is true of her screening?

She must still be screened, since no patient is exempt during pregnancy

She may skip the screen only if a fasting glucose is drawn in its place
preguntas.explicacion: Patients at low risk may not need the screening test, but every one of the conditions has to hold: no previous high glucose result, an ethnic group at low risk, no parent, sibling or child with diabetes, under 25 years old and of normal weight, and no poor outcome in an earlier pregnancy. Immediate phototherapy, since the probe is more accurate than a blood test

A conjugated bilirubin by probe, which detects cholestasis without a blood draw

preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking large doses of vitamin C has a urine reagent strip run. Which pair of pads can read falsely negative?

The protein and bilirubin pads
The nitrite and ketone pads

preguntas.pregunta: During a surgical hand scrub, how are the hands and forearms held while rinsing, and why?
opciones: Hands above the elbows, so water runs off the least clean part
Hands below the elbows, as in the routine wash at the sink
Hands flat against the sink, so the water reaches the cuticles
Hands at the same height, so the soap is rinsed off evenly
preguntas.explicacion: In routine handwashing the hands stay below the elbows, so water travels from the less contaminated area to the more contaminated one. The surgical scrub reverses that: once scrubbed, the hands are the cleanest part and the forearms and elbows are relatively less clean, so hands are kept elevated and away from the body and the water is allowed to run from the fingertips toward the elbows. Getting the position backwards washes the forearm over the hand.

preguntas.pregunta: How soon after intake do drugs generally appear in urine, and how long are they detectable after a small dose?
opciones: They appear in 1 to 2 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 days
They appear in 1 to 2 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 weeks
They appear in 6 to 8 hours and are detectable for 1 to 3 days
They appear within minutes and are detectable for about 48 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Drugs generally first show up in urine one to two hours after intake, and after a small dose they can be found for one to three days. In plasma the times are shorter, often one to two days. A full draw only when the tube will be held longer than five days before use

Proceed; fasting is required only to diagnose metabolic syndrome

With the fluorescent orange BIOHAZARD label and a red bag for the waste

The tubing holds enough blood to soak through the container
The tubing keeps the shield from sliding over the used needle
The tubing has to be cut with scissors before it is discarded
preguntas.explicacion: A needle on a length of flexible tubing is awkward to get into a sharps container, and that awkwardness is itself an injury hazard. preguntas.pregunta: If a tourniquet becomes necessary for life-threatening limb bleeding, where is it placed?

Directly over the wound, tightened until the bleeding stops
4 to 5 finger widths above the wound, released every 2 minutes
Just below the joint nearest the wound, loosened every 10 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: A tourniquet is used only when continuous pressure has not stopped extremely severe bleeding, and it is applied to the limb 2 to 3 inches, 5 to 7.7 centimeters, above the wound, avoiding the joint and moving above it toward the torso if necessary, preferably over clothing or padding rather than bare skin. Hepatitis A, since the wound was contaminated with blood

The chain is repaired by having the laboratory re-analyze the specimen
The chain holds, because the tamper-evident seal was never broken
The chain holds, because the analyst can testify to the result obtained
preguntas.explicacion: When inconsistencies persist and the prosecution cannot prove who had the item at a given time, the chain is deemed broken and the defense may ask the court to annul the resulting evidence; evidence without a maintained record can be ruled inadmissible and its legitimacy and integrity questioned. Adding heparin to every syringe on arrival in the laboratory, and asking the ICUs to send samples only during the day shift
Accepting clotted gas samples with a cautionary comment, and moving all blood gas testing to the core laboratory
Requiring each ICU to centrifuge gas samples before sending them, and doubling the frequency of the courier rounds

Only clinical staff who document care in the medical record
Only the privacy official and the contact person for complaints

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen for a molecular assay will sit for several hours before extraction. Why is it either processed at once or refrigerated?
opciones: Its low pH and urea denature the nucleic acid at ambient temperature
Its bacteria multiply at ambient temperature and consume the target
Its bilirubin breaks down in the light and quenches the fluorescent dye
Its specific gravity climbs as it evaporates, concentrating inhibitors
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is processed immediately or held at 2 to 8 °C for two reasons. First, the generally low pH of urine and its urea content denature DNA at 25 °C and above. Second, prolonged storage in the cold encourages uric acid, calcium oxalate and phosphorus to precipitate, and those precipitates can themselves inhibit the amplification, so neither extreme is harmless.

preguntas.pregunta: How small a risk must still be disclosed to a patient, according to the federal decision that shaped informed consent?

A risk of ten percent, no matter what harm it would cause
A risk of one percent, but only for elective procedures
A risk of five percent, unless the patient asks for more
preguntas.explicacion: A federal court held that a patient must be told about a risk as low as one percent when the harm in question is death or a life-altering complication such as paralysis. Because the three branches of government have left the minimum standard vague, these rights are usually enforced after the fact, through tort claims brought by patients.

preguntas.pregunta: A group A strep antigen kit's insert describes testing both a throat swab and a colony from a culture plate. Under a Certificate of Waiver, which specimen may the site test?

Either one, because the kit itself is categorized as waived
Only the culture, because the swab requires an extraction step
Neither, because any test with two specimen types is nonwaived
preguntas.explicacion: Waived tests are approved only for direct, unprocessed specimens that need no operator manipulation: whole blood, urine, a throat or nasal swab, stool, saliva. When one insert covers both a processed and an unprocessed specimen, the waiver applies only to the unprocessed one. Group A strep antigen testing is waived on a throat swab and not on a microbiology culture; urine hCG is waived, serum hCG is not.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the second glove removed once the first one is already off?

The bare hand pinches its outer surface at the fingertips
The bare hand pulls it off by the cuff and turns it over
Both gloves are peeled together before the first is dropped
preguntas.explicacion: The first glove is taken off by grasping the palm surface with the other gloved hand and dropping it into the right container. For the second, the fingers of the now bare hand go underneath it at the wrist, so that bare skin never touches the contaminated outside, and it is peeled off over the first. The light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate

Use a pencil, because permanent marker dissolves in the transport medium
Use a pen and cover the writing with clear tape so the ink cannot smear
Label the outer shipping bag instead, so that the tube itself stays easy to read

Sealed in tamper-evident bags, grouped under one form for the whole case
Double-bagged in biohazard bags, with the form taped to the outer bag
Boxed with absorbent material, with the form kept at the collection site

A darkened room, with a torch held close to the page being read
Handwritten notes in a small neat script on unlined white paper
A relative reading the paperwork aloud in place of the patient

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse auscultating a patient hears the 'lub' and then the 'dub'. What produces the second heart sound, S2?
opciones: Closing of the semilunar valves during ventricular diastole
Closing of the atrioventricular valves during ventricular systole
Opening of the semilunar valves during the ventricular ejection phase
Contraction of the atria pushing blood into a stiff, hypertrophic ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy heart has two audible sounds: S1, the lub, comes from the atrioventricular valves closing as the ventricles contract, and S2, the dub, from the semilunar valves closing as the ventricles relax. Heart sounds are vibrations caused by valve closure, and abnormal sounds are called murmurs. An atrial push into a stiff ventricle is S4, rarely heard and a sign of left ventricular failure.

preguntas.pregunta: When is routine gestational diabetes screening performed in an uncomplicated pregnancy?

Between 12 and 16 weeks of gestation
Between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation
At the first prenatal visit, in every patient

preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's HIV result in a crowded elevator. Under HIPAA this conversation is which of these?
opciones: A violation: oral disclosure of identifiable health information is PHI
Permitted, since both are workforce members of the same covered entity
Permitted, since spoken information is not covered, only written or electronic
A violation only if a patient's relative happens to be in the elevator
preguntas.explicacion: PHI covers written, paper, spoken and electronic information, and the elevator conversation about an identifiable patient is the very example used to illustrate an oral violation; discussions of patient information do not belong in public places, hallways, cafeterias or shared phone lines. preguntas.pregunta: Why is phlebotomy blood loss considered even more serious in the neonatal ICU than in adult intensive care?
opciones: NICU infants lose 10 to 90% of their circulating blood volume to phlebotomy in the first 2 weeks of life
NICU infants lose 340 to 660 mL of blood per week to diagnostic testing, the same as adult ICU patients
NICU infants lose about 25% of their circulating volume per day, mostly from line flushes
NICU infants cannot receive transfusions, so every millilitre drawn is permanently lost
preguntas.explicacion: Neonatal ICU infants lose 10 to 90% of their circulating volume to blood draws during the first 2 weeks of life alone, whereas adult ICU patients lose roughly 340 to 660 mL per week, with an 18% rise in anemia risk for each 50 mL. Many ICU patients then need transfusion, with its risks, so the best strategy is to prevent phlebotomy-driven anemia from the start.

preguntas.pregunta: After a report has gone to the ordering physician, the laboratory discovers a transcription error in one result. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Promptly notify the ordering person, issue a corrected report promptly, and keep duplicates of the original and the corrected report
Issue a corrected report within 30 days and destroy the original so that only the corrected version remains on file
Correct the value in the LIS and rely on the next routine report to carry the corrected result to the physician
Notify the ordering person by telephone with read-back, which replaces the need for a corrected written report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(k) has three parts when a reported result is found to be wrong: the laboratory promptly notifies the authorized person who ordered the test, and whoever uses the result, of the reporting error; it issues a corrected report promptly; and it maintains duplicates of both the original and the corrected report. preguntas.pregunta: What compression rate is kept during adult CPR?
opciones: 100 to 120 per minute, letting the chest rise fully between compressions
80 to 100 per minute, starting the next push before the chest rises
60 to 80 per minute, matched to the normal resting adult pulse rate
140 to 160 per minute, matched to the resting pulse rate of an infant
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are fast and hard, in the band of 100 to 120 per minute, and the chest is allowed to come all the way back up after each one. preguntas.pregunta: From the moment the donor hands over the specimen until the bottles are sealed, who has to keep it in sight?
opciones: Both the donor and the collector keep visual contact with the specimen
The collector alone, because the donor is no longer part of the process
The donor alone, so that the collector cannot be accused of tampering
A second collector acting as a witness for the whole of the procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Both the collector and the donor must keep the specimen in view from the moment it changes hands until the bottles have been sealed for shipment to the laboratory or the testing facility. Only after the seals are on is the donor told that watching is no longer necessary and allowed to wash their hands. That unbroken line of sight is the start of the documented chain of custody.

Active devices; the user must slide a sleeve forward over the blade
Passive devices; they prevent reuse but do not reduce needle-sticks
Active devices; the mechanism can trigger during probing and require a new puncture

preguntas.pregunta: Which vascular injury is associated with puncturing the medial aspect of a newborn's heel?

Rupture of the plantar vein, with a spreading haematoma
Thrombosis of the calcaneal branch, with local necrosis
Puncture of the tibial nerve, with loss of the venous branch used

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital chaplain asks for the names of admitted patients of his denomination. What does the privacy rule allow?
opciones: Telling him, provided the patient was informed and did not object
Telling him, since clergy are workforce members of the hospital
Refusing, unless each patient signed a written authorization first
Refusing, because religious affiliation is never disclosed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clergy and religious figures may be told which patients belong to their denomination, on the condition that the patient was informed first and raised no objection. That is why these preferences, along with who may visit and who should be notified, are asked at admission and put in writing. Disclosure can still happen in an emergency or when an incapacitated patient could not consent, if it is consistent with that person's best interest and the reasoning is documented.

preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient with low vision cannot make out the video remote interpreting screen. Under the ADA guidance?

VRI is sufficient as long as it meets the four performance standards
Written notes replace the interpreter, since VRI was properly offered
The patient must now bring his own interpreter, because VRI failed
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA allows VRI where it would be effective, but VRI is not effective in every case, for example for a person who has difficulty seeing the screen because of vision loss or positioning; then an on-site interpreter may be required. Meeting the technical standards does not cure that, and the entity may never shift the duty to the patient.

Winged sets for paediatric use look like adult hypodermic needles

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen preserved with formaldehyde is run on a reagent strip. What should the laboratory expect?
opciones: False-positive leukocyte esterase, urobilinogen and glucose readings on the strip
False-negative leukocyte esterase, urobilinogen and glucose readings on that strip
False-positive albumin readings on the strip, the same effect thymol produces
False-negative leukocyte esterase readings, the same effect mercury salts produce
preguntas.explicacion: Formaldehyde preserves cell structure but distorts several pads, giving falsely positive leukocyte esterase, peroxidase, urobilinogen and glucose reactions. Each preservative has its own signature: thymol falsifies albumin upward, mercury salts falsify the leukocyte reaction downward, hydrochloric acid shifts the pH, and boric acid dulls the leukocyte pad and alters the starting pH.

preguntas.pregunta: Which design feature does the FDA recommend for every type of sharps injury prevention feature, regardless of mechanism?
opciones: The user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated
The feature should retract the sharp fully within the housing of the device
The feature should activate passively, without any action by the user
The feature should be reversible so that a jammed device can be cleared
preguntas.explicacion: The two recommendations FDA Table 1 applies to all features are that the user can easily tell whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal. Full retraction is the recommendation for retractable sharps only, passive operation is one of two acceptable mechanisms rather than a requirement, and reversibility contradicts the table.
