preguntas.pregunta: What characteristics does the WHO ask the phlebotomist to look for when choosing a vein?
opciones: A vein of good size that is visible, straight and clear
The vein closest to the surface, even if it curves or branches
The largest vein, even if it can only be felt with the tourniquet on
A vein on the back of the hand, which the WHO prefers for adults
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 tells the phlebotomist to extend the arm, inspect the antecubital fossa or forearm, and locate a vein of a good size that is visible, straight and clear, adding that it should be visible before the tourniquet goes on. The back of the hand is the preferred site for an IV, and a vein found only under the tourniquet fails the WHO's visibility criterion.

preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act add for covered entities that use electronic health records?
opciones: An audit trail accounting for disclosures, tracking who accesses records and when
A requirement to keep paper copies of every electronic record for 6 years
An exemption from breach notification for encrypted records affecting under 500 patients
A rule allowing shared passwords within a department to speed access
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH promoted adoption and meaningful use of electronic health records and strengthened HIPAA: covered entities with an EHR must provide an audit trail accounting for disclosures, systems track who signs on and off, when, and what data they viewed or downloaded, patients may obtain electronic copies of records held in an EHR, and a patient who pays out of pocket in full may ask that the information not be shared with the health plan. Unique user names and unshared passwords are what make that tracking possible; shared passwords defeat it.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse gets red, irritated hands from her gloves but has no itching and no hives. What does that suggest?
opciones: Irritant contact dermatitis, which is not a true latex allergy
A type I hypersensitivity, the reaction behind a true latex allergy
Allergic contact dermatitis, which adds pruritus and urticaria
Latex-fruit syndrome, in which foods and gloves both provoke it
preguntas.explicacion: Irritant contact dermatitis produces erythema of the skin and comes from friction or contact with chemicals; it is a non-immunologic reaction, so the person does not have a true latex allergy and may need only a protective barrier for the skin. Allergic contact dermatitis is the delayed type IV reaction and brings pruritus and urticaria after exposure.

preguntas.pregunta: A grey top tube for glucose is drawn short and the laboratory reports the sample as haemolysed. What does the WHO table say about this tube?
opciones: It requires a full draw, because a short draw may cause haemolysis
It requires a half draw, because its additive is concentrated for small volumes
It needs no fill requirement, since fluoride keeps glucose stable for five days
It should be filled last only when a haemolysed sample is expected
preguntas.explicacion: In the uses column for the oxalate/fluoride tube, Table 2.3 states that glucose specimens require a full draw and that a short draw may cause haemolysis. The five-day glucose stability is a separate property of the antiglycolytic agent and does not remove the fill requirement. The grey tube is drawn last (position 10) in every case, not only when haemolysis is suspected.

preguntas.pregunta: A courier leaves a box of specimens on the dashboard of a parked car in direct sunlight for an hour. Beyond the heat, what does prolonged light exposure do to the samples?
opciones: UV irradiation can oxidatively degrade nucleic acids, so samples are covered to shield them from unnecessary light
Visible light fades the bar codes, so samples are relabelled on arrival before they can be accessioned
UV irradiation sterilises the specimen surface, so samples intended for culture are treated as contaminated
Light activates clotting in anticoagulated tubes, so samples are inverted again before they are centrifuged
preguntas.explicacion: Light exposure brings two problems: the temperature swings that come with sitting in the sun, and UV irradiation, which over long exposure leads to oxidative degradation of nucleic acid polymers. The example given for this variable is a sample forgotten in direct sunlight, and the countermeasure is simple: protect specimens from unnecessary light by covering them. Minimising transport time is the surest protection of all.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 1 and section 4.3 Light exposure

preguntas.pregunta: A sedimentation rate is set up from a tube that turns out to hold a small clot, and a second one from an icteric patient. What happens to each reading?
opciones: The clotted one reads low; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads high; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads low; the icteric one reads high from the extra pigment
Both read high, since neither plasma settles at the expected sedimentation rate
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux formation the test depends on, so the value comes out lower than it should. Icteric samples from patients with liver disease give a dark yellow plasma that is visually hard to tell from the settled red cells, and a hemolysed sample turns the plasma red for the same reason, blurring the boundary the reading is taken from.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: A patient phones a week after a draw to say the bruise has turned greenish-yellow. What does that indicate?
opciones: The normal sequence of healing, which ends at the usual skin colour
An infection developing under the skin at the site of the puncture
A deep periosteal bruise that will need a radiograph of the elbow
Fresh bleeding into the same area from the original puncture wound
preguntas.explicacion: A bruise starts pinkish red and tender, turns bluish, then greenish-yellow, and finally returns to the normal skin colour as it heals, over days to months. What would prompt a call to a clinician is streaks of redness, pus or fever, which point to infection, or extreme pressure in the area.

On the patient's lap, so the phlebotomist can reach the tubes without turning
On the far side of the patient, so the sharps container stays nearest the phlebotomist
Inside the sharps container tray, so used and unused items stay together
preguntas.explicacion: Step 1 ends with the instruction to keep the rack with the sample tubes close to the health worker but away from the patient, to avoid its being accidentally knocked over. preguntas.pregunta: A point-of-care glucose on a diabetic inpatient is critical for the third time today; the nurse says the team already knows the patient runs high. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy each time, even when earlier critical values are known
Skip the report, because a known pattern of critical values exempts later results from the notification policy
Report it only if it is higher than the previous critical value recorded for the patient earlier that day
Report it only after a venous sample confirms it, since a point-of-care glucose is not treated as a critical value
preguntas.explicacion: Critical values are treated as reportable events even if earlier critical values are already known for the patient, and the reporting policy is followed consistently for each instance. The only acceptable deviation is an exceptional case backed by sufficient evidence, such as an obvious testing error or a preanalytical error, that justifies setting the value aside. Documentation of the result and of the actions taken accompanies every critical value obtained at the point of care.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Reporting Critical Findings)

preguntas.pregunta: A piece of clot breaks free from the vessel wall and travels in the bloodstream. What is the traveling piece called?
opciones: An embolus
A thrombus
A hematoma
A plaque
preguntas.explicacion: A thrombus is a clot that forms within an intact or slightly damaged vessel and stays attached; when part of it breaks loose and moves with the blood it is called an embolus, and once it lodges it is an embolism, which in the heart, brain or lungs is an emergency. A plaque is the fatty buildup of atherosclerosis in an artery wall; neither term names a clot that has broken loose.

Devices with passive safety features, and containers emptied twice a shift
Single-use devices, and containers sealed with a tamper-proof lid on top
Devices used on a single patient, and containers kept within arm's reach

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist packs three tubes and the paper requisition together inside the same plastic transport bag. What does WHO best practice say?
opciones: Use a leak-proof bag with an outside compartment for the request form, so the form is not contaminated
Use a leak-proof bag and fold the form around the tubes, so the two travel together as one unit
Use a leak-proof bag and staple the form to the outside, so the courier can read the destination
Use a leak-proof bag and place the form in a second bag, so it can be discarded on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Step 10 of the WHO phlebotomy procedure is to pack the samples safely in a plastic leak-proof bag that has an outside compartment for the laboratory request form; keeping the requisition outside is what protects it from contamination. When several tubes travel together they go in a rack or padded holder so they do not break in transit, and the labels on tubes and forms are rechecked before dispatch.

preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factor is calcium, and why does that matter for citrate and EDTA collection tubes?
opciones: Factor IV; removing calcium from a sample keeps it from clotting
Factor I; it is converted into fibrin at the end of the cascade
Factor III; damaged cells release it to start the extrinsic path
Factor XIII; it stabilizes the fibrin mesh once it has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Calcium ions are factor IV, drawn from diet, platelets and bone, and needed for the entire clotting process. Sodium citrate and EDTA both act by forming calcium salts that remove calcium from the sample, which is how those tubes keep blood from clotting. Fibrinogen is factor I, tissue factor is III, and the fibrin-stabilizing factor is XIII.

preguntas.pregunta: In the Swiss cheese model applied to laboratory medicine, when does an error reach the patient?
opciones: When the holes in every defensive layer line up and no layer detects and corrects the error
When a single layer fails, since each layer protects a different phase and none of them overlaps
When the analytical layer fails, because the extra-analytical layers cannot stop an analytical error
When more than half of the layers fail, which is the threshold at which the system is declared unsafe
preguntas.explicacion: Reason's model pictures a system as a stack of Swiss cheese slices in which each slice is a defensive layer and the holes are opportunities for an error to pass to the next process; an adverse patient outcome happens when all the holes line up and the system fails to detect and rectify the error. In laboratory medicine the slices are equipment, training, supervision and quality assurance procedures, and management aims to close the gaps and strengthen the defences rather than rely on any single one.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3.3

preguntas.pregunta: Which distinction between capacity and competence is correct?
opciones: Capacity is a clinical call for one decision; competence is a legal finding by a judge
Capacity is decided by a judge; competence is assessed by the treating clinician
Both are legal findings that differ only in the standard of evidence required
Capacity is permanent once established; competence is specific to one situation
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity is a functional determination that a person can or cannot make a particular medical decision, relative to their baseline and to the situation and stakes. Competence is the ability to take part in legal proceedings, presumed until disproved at a hearing, and decided by a judge, never by medical providers.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Issues of Concern, Relevant Definitions

preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fingerstick glucose test with cold hands. How is the site prepared?
opciones: Wash and dry the site with warm water; alcohol is optional, and if used the skin must dry fully first
Swab with alcohol and puncture while still damp, since warm water would dilute the sample
Warm the hand with a cloth for 10 minutes, then clean with povidone iodine and let it dry
Rub the fingertip briskly until it reddens, then puncture without any cleaning step
preguntas.explicacion: The testing site is washed and dried thoroughly, using warm water to improve blood flow. Alcohol swabs are not routinely required, but if one is used the skin must dry completely before lancing to avoid diluting the sample or hemolysing it. No temperature or time is specified for warming, and povidone iodine is not used for capillary punctures in children.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures

preguntas.pregunta: In a hospital where emergency samples hemolyse at 13.5 % and the rest at about 3 %, what did the authors point to as the difference?
opciones: Emergency blood is usually drawn while the catheter is being placed
Emergency blood is usually hand carried instead of going by pneumatic tube
Emergency blood is usually collected into tubes that have no separator gel
Emergency blood is usually drawn by staff who work without a tourniquet
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis in the non-emergency samples of that facility ran near 3 %, against 13.5 % in the emergency department. Emergency blood is routinely taken during intravenous line placement, whereas inpatients and outpatients get a straight stick, and drawing through a catheter is known to hemolyse more. Transport was ruled out: hand carried and tube-sent samples hemolysed alike.

preguntas.pregunta: An assistant wipes the counter with disinfectant and immediately lays out urine reagent strips on the damp surface. Why is that a problem?
opciones: Moisture from a wet or newly cleaned surface can damage the strip and cause incorrect results
The disinfectant neutralizes the color chart, so the pads can no longer be compared to it
Strips exposed to room air for more than 30 seconds lose their nitrite and glucose reactivity
The counter must be dry so that the timer can be started at the exact moment of dipping the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Testing is done in a well-lit, clean and dry area; work surfaces are cleaned and dried before and after testing, and equipment is dried before use. Placing test strips on a moist or freshly cleaned surface may damage the strip and produce wrong results. Reagent strips also stay in their original container, because their shelf life is short and expired or mishandled strips read inaccurately.

preguntas.pregunta: How are patients told that free interpreter services exist at the practice?
opciones: Interpretive services posters displayed in waiting and reception areas
A line printed on the appointment reminder card handed at check-out
A notice read aloud by the clinician at the start of every encounter
A leaflet mailed to every household in the languages of the county
preguntas.explicacion: Practices list the languages their qualified bilingual clinicians speak in their directories, and display interpretive services posters in waiting and reception areas so patients learn that free interpreter services are available. Section 1557 separately obliges covered entities to post notices of non-discrimination and of the availability of language assistance.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's arm shows no vein crossing the antecubital area, but a prominent vein runs straight up the middle of the forearm into the fossa. Which anatomical variant is this?
opciones: A dominant median antebrachial vein joining the basilic and cephalic
No communication at all between the cephalic and the basilic veins
A median cubital vein present, with the cephalic absent in the upper arm
Venae comitantes, the paired deep veins that travel with the arteries
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein has several recognized variants: the usual pattern, in which it connects the basilic and cephalic veins; a dominant median antebrachial vein of the forearm joining basilic and cephalic in the fossa; a median cubital vein present with the cephalic undeveloped in the upper arm; and no communication at all. Venae comitantes are the paired deep veins that run with the arteries.

No record is needed, since the judgment of the exposed employee settles the matter
The employee signs the hepatitis B declination form that is kept with the plan
The incident goes in the sharps injury log with the type and brand of the device

preguntas.pregunta: What information does the Nadler equation need to estimate a patient's total blood volume?

Sex, age and weight
Height, weight and hematocrit
Age, weight and hemoglobin
preguntas.explicacion: Two equations estimate total blood volume from the sex, height and weight of the patient. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has fainted vomits while still on the floor. What should be done?

Sit the person upright at once and offer sips of cold water
Raise both legs higher and keep the person face upwards
Place a rolled towel behind the neck and keep the head back
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps for a person who has fainted are to check the airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing at the neck and raise the feet above heart level. preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about N95 respirators for healthcare workers is correct?

Any worker may use them without fit testing, as with a surgical mask
They protect against droplets only and are replaced by a surgical mask for airborne pathogens
They require fit testing only when used against chemical vapors under Level C
preguntas.explicacion: Loosely woven cloth masks give the least protection and NIOSH-approved respirators the most, that proper fit is a key part of that protection, and that all healthcare workers required to use respirators, N95 included, should be fit tested; where fit testing cannot be completed, a NIOSH-approved powered air-purifying respirator may be considered. Both inside the patient room, so the corridor stays free of contamination
Put on inside the room and taken off outside, next to the waste container

preguntas.explicacion: Donning takes place outside the patient room, and so does doffing, with one exception spelled out in the sequence: a respirator is not removed until after leaving the room, because the air inside is the hazard it was worn against. preguntas.pregunta: Why may a child who is already walking be a harder capillary draw?

The heel bone has fused and the skin-to-bone distance drops below 2 mm
Walking children are over 10 kg, so only venipuncture is appropriate
The plantar surface of a walking child carries the tibial artery superficially
preguntas.explicacion: If the child is walking, the feet may have calluses that hinder adequate blood flow, which is one reason the finger-prick takes over above 6 months and 10 kg. To hand the chart to the first available radiology clerk
To keep the chart closed unless the patient asks to see it
To leave the chart at the desk until the images are done

Transmission of hepatitis B, as happens with reusable finger-prick devices

Three samples from a single bowel movement, each smeared on a separate card window
One sample from each of 3 bowel movements on 3 different days, sent in a preservative vial
Two samples from one bowel movement, from the first and the last part of the stool
preguntas.explicacion: The home kit asks for 3 different bowel movements; from each one the patient samples two areas of the stool and smears each on one of the two places on that card, then mails the cards to the laboratory. preguntas.pregunta: Why do the blood volume equations use separate formulas for men and women?
opciones: Women tend to carry a lower blood volume than men of the same size
Women tend to carry a higher blood volume than men of the same size
Women's plasma fraction is 40% rather than the 60% seen in men
Women's volume is estimated from weight alone, without their height
preguntas.explicacion: Women tend to have a lower blood volume than men, which is why Nadler gives one formula for each. Inside the room, immediately after the gloves
Inside the room, before the gown so the ties are reachable
At the nurses' station, once hands have been washed

preguntas.pregunta: What glucose load is given to a nonpregnant adult for a standard diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test?

50 g of glucose, taken without any prior fasting
100 g of glucose after a fast of 8 to 14 hours
1.75 g of glucose per kilogram of body weight

The Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended
preguntas.explicacion: Several federal requirements touch exposure management: the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Extension Act of 2009 mandates notification of emergency response personnel possibly exposed to selected diseases, and the CDC keeps the list of those exposures. The Needlestick Act amended the OSHA standard on devices and logs; the FMLA gives eligible employees unpaid, job-protected leave; and the ADA limits how employers ask about illness and requires reasonable accommodation when work restrictions apply.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides describing labels, data sheets and training, what must a written hazard communication program contain?
opciones: A list of the hazardous chemicals present, and how non-routine tasks are handled
A copy of every safety data sheet, arranged by section and by supplier
The exposure limits of each chemical and the results of air monitoring
The signed acknowledgment of each employee who attended the training
preguntas.explicacion: The written program has to describe how the requirements for labels and other warnings, safety data sheets and employee information and training will be met, and it must also include a list of the hazardous chemicals known to be present, identified the way the corresponding data sheet identifies them, and the methods the employer will use to tell employees about the hazards of non-routine tasks and of chemicals in unlabeled pipes in their work areas. The list may cover the whole workplace or be made area by area.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(e)(1)(i) and (e)(1)(ii), Written hazard communication program

preguntas.pregunta: Which tube is filled immediately after the blood culture bottle in the recommended order of draw?
opciones: The non-additive tube
The light blue citrate tube
The lavender EDTA tube
The grey fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: In the recommended sequence the culture bottle is drawn first and the non-additive tube second, ahead of the light blue citrate tube at position three. EDTA sits at eight and the grey oxalate/fluoride tube last at ten. Keeping the bottles ahead of everything else protects the culture from additive carried over on the needle, and the citrate tube keeps its own place because it needs a full draw.

preguntas.pregunta: On the 3-hour gestational glucose tolerance test, how many abnormal values are needed for the diagnosis?
opciones: Two or more of the four values
One value, whichever hour it is
Three or more of the four values
All four of the values must be high
preguntas.explicacion: Gestational diabetes is established by two or more abnormal results on the 3-hour test. When only one value is above normal, the provider may simply ask for changes in diet and repeat the testing afterwards, so a single high hour settles nothing. That is why four measurements are taken rather than one, and why the screening step is not a diagnosis on its own.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gestational Diabetes", Evaluation; MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), What Abnormal Results Mean

preguntas.pregunta: A green-top heparin tube arrives for a viral PCR. Why do current guidelines say to reject it, and which tubes are recommended instead?
opciones: Heparin inhibits DNA amplification in a dose-dependent way and is carried through extraction; EDTA or ACD tubes are recommended
Heparin chelates the magnesium the polymerase needs for amplification; citrate or fluoride tubes are recommended instead
Heparin degrades RNA through its own nuclease activity during storage; serum tubes with clot activator are recommended instead
Heparin causes hemolysis during centrifugation and releases heme into the plasma; plain red-top tubes are recommended instead
preguntas.explicacion: Heparin has been shown to inhibit DNA amplification in a dose-dependent fashion, with the degree depending on the polymerase used, and it is recovered during both DNA and RNA extraction, so the consensus is that heparinised plasma is unsuitable for molecular infectious disease testing and current guidelines say heparin-containing specimens should be rejected. The recommended anticoagulants are K2/K3-EDTA and acid citrate dextrose, chelating agents that sequester the calcium the DNA-degrading nucleases depend on.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.3 Specimen collection containers

preguntas.pregunta: Which serious adverse event is described as rare during phlebotomy?
opciones: Loss of consciousness accompanied by tonic clonic seizures
Loss of consciousness lasting under a couple of minutes only
Pain at the puncture site with anxiety about the procedure
Bruising and haematoma at the site of the venepuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Serious adverse events tied to drawing blood are rare, and the example given is loss of consciousness with tonic clonic seizures. Pain at the site, anxiety and fainting are put in the less severe group, and bruising with haematoma is the best documented event of all.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the process that stops blood loss after a vessel is damaged?
opciones: Hemostasis
Hemolysis
Hemorrhage
Hemopoiesis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the process by which the body seals a ruptured vessel and prevents further blood loss; its failure produces hemorrhage, excessive bleeding. Hemolysis is the breakdown of red cells with release of hemoglobin, as happens after an incompatible transfusion, and hemopoiesis, from roots meaning blood and production, is the making of the formed elements in the marrow.
preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions; 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements

preguntas.pregunta: A blood count drawn in EDTA reports a platelet count far below the patient's usual value, and the smear shows clumps. Which repeat specimen is suggested?
opciones: A repeat count on blood collected into a citrate tube
A repeat count on blood collected into a heparin tube
A repeat count on serum from a clot activator tube
A repeat count on the same EDTA tube after warming it
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets can clump in EDTA because of antibodies that act only in the presence of that anticoagulant, and the analyser then reports a falsely low count. The way round it is to repeat the count on blood taken into a citrate tube instead. Serum has no platelets left to count.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation

preguntas.pregunta: An older patient has just given her history to the rooming assistant. What does the guidance ask of the next person?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating it tires her
Take the whole history again, so two versions can be compared
Take the history only from the relative who came with her today
Skip the history, since a form was filled in the waiting room
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is advised in taking the history of an older patient: where possible, have the patient tell their story only once, even if other staff in the office would normally help gather it, because giving the account to one member of staff and then again can be tiring. Preliminary data may instead be requested from records or from forms filled in at home.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Obtaining a thorough history

preguntas.pregunta: Incorrect urine collection stayed at 9.2 % in the audited hospital even after staff began speaking to patients. What were patients told about?
opciones: The sampling itself, the type of container, and collecting the midstream portion
Fasting for twelve hours, the type of container, and the time of the first void
The volume required, the transport temperature, and the use of a preservative
The sampling itself, the labelling of the cup, and the delivery time to the bench
preguntas.explicacion: Urine testing is unusually exposed to preanalytical trouble because the patient, not a trained collector, takes the sample. In that laboratory the receiving secretary explained the sampling, the container types, sterile and with or without preservative, and how to catch the midstream portion. Even so, incorrect collection remained at 9.2 % of the urine samples received.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart records a vascular graft in the arm the phlebotomist was about to use. What does that mean for the draw?
opciones: The graft is a listed contraindication, so another site is chosen
The graft is acceptable if the puncture is made well below it
The graft is acceptable once the tourniquet is placed above it
The graft only rules out the arm when dialysis is being given
preguntas.explicacion: Among the contraindications tied to the site are scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, a vascular graft, a haematoma, venous fibrosis felt on palpation, a previous radical mastectomy on that side, and any device placed for venous access.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications

preguntas.pregunta: In the table position for infant venipuncture, why does the immobilizer reach across the child to hold the wrist palm up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder against twisting, and the wrist grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the child's face turned away so the needle is never seen by the child
It compresses the brachial artery, which slows the flow and prevents a haematoma
It frees the phlebotomist's second hand to apply a rubber tourniquet above
preguntas.explicacion: Two adults stand on opposite sides of an examination table: the immobilizer lays the child on its back with the head on the outstretched arm, pulls the child close, grasps the elbow, and reaches across with the other arm to hold the wrist palm up. Reaching across anchors the shoulder and prevents twisting or rocking, and a firm grasp on the wrist effectively provides the phlebotomist with a tourniquet.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Preparation

preguntas.pregunta: Why is there no single free-hemoglobin concentration above which every test result must be rejected?
opciones: The interference is optical, chemical or immunological, so the acceptable limit depends on the test and the method
The interference affects only enzymes, so a single limit applies to LDH and CK and none to other analytes
The interference disappears once the serum is diluted, so any sample can be reported after dilution
The interference is constant across analyzers, but each laboratory is free to pick its own limit
preguntas.explicacion: Free hemoglobin interferes in different ways, optically, chemically, or by interacting with antigen or antibody in immunoassays, so the upper limit of hemoglobin tolerated in serum or plasma is test- and method-dependent; the reagent's method description should state the serum index limitations, and laboratories are advised to load those cut-offs into their analyzers. Even specific proteins such as CRP and haptoglobin can be affected.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: A bronchoalveolar lavage specimen for molecular detection of Pneumocystis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is being sent from the bronchoscopy suite. How is it transported and stored?
opciones: Transported on ice; stored at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, or at −20 to −80 °C for the long term
Transported at room temperature; stored at 4 °C for up to 4 hours, then discarded as unsuitable
Transported on wet ice only if RNA is the target; stored at room temperature for up to 7 days
Transported frozen at −70 °C; stored at 4 to 8 °C for up to 7 days with a mucolytic additive
preguntas.explicacion: For bronchoalveolar lavage the general guideline is transport on ice, storage at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, and −20 to −80 °C for long-term keeping; time and temperature are the preanalytical variables listed for it. Wet ice reserved for RNA targets is the CSF entry, 4 to 8 °C for 7 days with N-acetyl-L-cysteine or dithiothreitol is the sputum entry, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the minimum weight for a blood donor?
opciones: 50 kilograms, that is 110 pounds
45 kilograms, that is 100 pounds
57 kilograms, that is 125 pounds
68 kilograms, that is 150 pounds
preguntas.explicacion: The donor must weigh a minimum of 50 kilograms, which the regulation gives as 110 pounds; the same floor appears in the eligibility criteria used by blood centers. It is part of the day-of-donation physical assessment, together with temperature, blood pressure, hemoglobin or hematocrit, pulse and the skin examination.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a history of latex allergy and the phlebotomist has no elastic band at hand. What must she not do?
opciones: Use a latex glove as a tourniquet on that patient
Ask a colleague to bring a latex-free band to the room
Draw the sample without applying a tourniquet at all
Use a clean band that has been reprocessed since its last use
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table is explicit that a latex glove must not be used as a tourniquet where the patient has a history of latex allergy, since some patients react to latex. The gloves themselves are chosen the same way: a pair of well-fitting, clean, disposable latex or latex-free gloves for each patient or each procedure. An employer also has to keep hypoallergenic gloves or similar alternatives within reach for workers who react to the ones normally supplied.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Tourniquet and Gloves; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii)

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum returns a haemolysis index around 700 µmol/L and the neonatologist still wants the C-reactive protein. What does the laboratory expect at that level?
opciones: The C-reactive protein would read low, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein would read high, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein can be issued with a note, as is done for LDH
The C-reactive protein is unaffected, since haemoglobin interferes optically
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins withstand hemolysis better than many routine chemistry analytes, but severe in vitro hemolysis still reaches them: above an index of roughly 622 µmol/L this marker is underestimated. In 199 newborn samples it was rejected for that reason, and a repeat draw two to five hours later brought the index down and made every result reportable.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion

preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist asks where the reason for each draw is meant to be written down. Where does the WHO expect the indications to be set out?
opciones: In a written protocol, or in documented instructions such as a laboratory form
In the verbal handover the ward nurse gives the phlebotomist each morning
On the tube labels, which carry the tests along with the patient details
In the training record each phlebotomist keeps for supervised sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Provision of clear instructions asks that the indications for blood sampling be clearly defined, either in a written protocol or in documented instructions, and it offers the laboratory form as the example. Tube labels carry names, file number, date of birth and the time of the draw; training and supervision are handled in a separate part of the chapter.

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO Annex C script, what is the patient told about where the results will go?
opciones: They are returned to the named clinician who ordered the tests
They are mailed to the patient's home address within one week
They are read to the patient by the phlebotomist before leaving
They are posted in the patient portal on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: The script says the tubes will be labelled with the patient's name and details, sent to the laboratory, and that the results will be returned to the doctor whose name the worker mentions, the clinician who ordered the tests. It then asks whether the patient has questions, understood the explanation, and is willing to be tested.

preguntas.pregunta: A nonpregnant adult's 2-hour value on a 75-g OGTT is 165 mg/dL. How is it interpreted?
opciones: Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
Normal glucose tolerance (below 200 mg/dL)
Diabetes, since it exceeds 126 mg/dL
Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: At two hours, below 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 mg/dL is impaired glucose tolerance (what a provider may call prediabetes) and 200 mg/dL or higher is diagnostic of diabetes, so 165 is impaired tolerance. The 126 cutoff applies to fasting glucose repeated on two tests, and 100 to 125 defines impaired fasting glucose, another fasting category; below 200 is the 1-hour reference, not the 2-hour one.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results and What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic buys needles from one company, tube holders from another and tubes from a third. What is the guidance on mixing components from different manufacturers?
opciones: Needle, holder and tubes should come from the same manufacturer, since mixing brands can cause problems in use
Mixing brands is acceptable as long as every component is within its expiration date and sterile
Only the needle and the holder must match; the tubes are interchangeable across manufacturers
Mixing brands is acceptable for adults but not for paediatric tubes with reduced vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Needle, tube holder and tubes are chosen from the same manufacturer to ensure compatibility; otherwise the volume aspirated, the gel stability and the additives can be affected. The WHO device table lists mixing components from different manufacturers as a disadvantage of vacuum systems that can create a problem during use. Neither text limits the rule to adults or to two of the three parts.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the CDC, when is the source patient tested for hepatitis C after an occupational exposure?
opciones: As soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours, ideally by RNA testing
Within 72 hours, using an antibody test with no reflex to RNA
At 3 to 6 weeks, when HCV RNA becomes detectable in the source
At 4 to 6 months, alongside the exposed worker's final antibody test
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC guidance tests the source patient as soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours, with a nucleic acid test for HCV RNA as the preferred option, or an antibody test with reflex to NAT if positive; the exposed worker is tested at the same time with an antibody test and reflex to RNA. If follow-up is indicated, the worker has an RNA test at 3 to 6 weeks and a final antibody test at 4 to 6 months. Those later dates are the worker's schedule, not the source's, and 72 hours is the HIV PEP window.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient known to take clonazepam has a negative benzodiazepine screen. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The immunoassay targets oxazepam and may miss other benzodiazepines
The specimen was collected outside the 1-to-2-hour appearance window
The patient's urine was too dilute for any immunoassay to read it
Benzodiazepines are only measurable in blood, never in urine at all
preguntas.explicacion: A negative result means the substance the assay looks for was not detected, either because the concentration sat below the threshold or because there was no use in the relevant window. False negatives are common when the analytes an immunoassay targets are not known: benzodiazepine testing often aims at the metabolite oxazepam and may miss clonazepam or alprazolam. A negative does not rule out use.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Drug Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings

preguntas.pregunta: A platelet count comes back under 20,000/µL on a patient with no bleeding at all. Which possibility does the notification list tell the laboratory to rule out first?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia caused by the EDTA in the tube itself
Dilution of the specimen by an intravenous infusion nearby
A clot in the tube that has trapped part of the platelets
Interference from lipemia on the optical platelet channel
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet count below 20,000 per microlitre is listed as needing urgent notification because of the bleeding risk, and the note attached to it is a caution rather than a diagnosis: exclude EDTA-induced thrombocytopenia before the call is made. The upper limit on the same line, above one million, is flagged for the opposite reason, the risk of thrombosis.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the phlebotomist whether her potassium result means she has kidney disease. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Say that the ordering provider interprets results, and route the question to that provider
Read the reference interval aloud and show her where her own value falls against it
Tell her the value is normal for her age, since age-based intervals are on the report
Refuse to discuss the report at all, because privacy rules bar giving results to patients
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA puts interpretation on the far side of the bench: reference intervals go to the authorized person who ordered the test and to whoever is responsible for using the results, and results themselves are released only to those people. Nerve injury and added pain from poor needle technique
Haematoma at the site and bleeding after the needle is out
Expired tubes and a needle and holder of different makes

preguntas.pregunta: Which word choice matches plain-language guidance for talking with patients?
opciones: 'Helpful' rather than 'beneficial'
'Exacerbate' rather than 'make worse'
'Abdomen' rather than 'tummy or belly'
'Venipuncture' rather than 'blood draw'
preguntas.explicacion: The examples are direct: say 'helpful' instead of 'beneficial' and 'make worse' instead of 'exacerbate', and use everyday words such as tummy or belly rather than abdomen, avoiding acronyms. If a medical term matters, ask whether the patient knows it and define it simply. The three distractors each run the advice backwards.

preguntas.pregunta: Which preanalytical problem is the leading cause of test or sample rejection in clinical laboratories, and how large is it?
opciones: In vitro hemolysis, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
Clotted samples, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
In vivo hemolysis, present in about 2 % of routine samples and most rejected specimens
Insufficient volume, up to 22 % of routine samples and the majority of unsuitable specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis was recognised as the most frequent preanalytical error, and in vitro hemolysis is the leading cause of rejection: it can reach 3.3 % of all routine samples and accounts for 40 to 70 % of unsuitable specimens, close to five times more than other causes such as incorrect or clotted samples. Fewer than 2 % of samples with detectable hemolysis are hemolysed in vivo, so the problem is created during collection and transport.

preguntas.pregunta: Apart from the antiseptic, what is the one procedural difference between a diagnostic and a medico-legal blood alcohol draw?
opciones: A chain of custody is adopted so the specimen can be traced
A second specimen is drawn from the opposite arm as a control
The specimen is frozen immediately rather than refrigerated
The tube is sealed with tamper-evident tape by a police officer
preguntas.explicacion: Correct diagnostic preanalytical handling already gives a forensically defensible result: transport, processing at room temperature for under three hours, short-term storage at 4 °C and long-term storage frozen all meet the forensic requirement. The only remaining differentiation is adopting a chain of custody for traceability whenever the request has an explicit medico-legal purpose. Freezing is for monthly or yearly storage.

As a laboratory error until the second card in a two-screen state confirms it
As a result to be reported directly to the parents by the phlebotomist who collected it

Within 72 hours of opening, unless it is kept in a clean medication area

preguntas.pregunta: Occupational hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers fell sharply after the 1980s. What is that credited to?

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who takes warfarin has a point-of-care INR of 1.5. What does this value indicate?

It is above the usual therapeutic target of 0.8 to 1.1, so the patient may be at risk of serious bleeding
It is within the usual therapeutic target of 1.0 to 2.0, so no change in the warfarin dose is expected
It is a normal value for someone who is not on anticoagulants, so the warfarin can be discontinued
preguntas.explicacion: For a person not taking anticoagulants the PT is about 11 to 13.5 seconds and the INR 0.8 to 1.1. For most patients on warfarin the provider aims to keep the INR between 2.0 and 3.0: results above 3.0 carry a higher bleeding risk, while results below 2.0 may leave the patient at risk of developing a blood clot. An INR of 1.5 is therefore under target and the dose is reviewed by the provider, not stopped by the tester.

The tube was drawn through an intravenous catheter during an IV start
The tube was inverted too many times right after it was collected
preguntas.explicacion: Blood must be allowed to clot before serum is processed; the high rate of fibrin-containing samples in the emergency laboratory was linked to the short interval between collection and centrifugation, on average about 10 minutes. Waiting longer does not produce fibrin, catheter draws are tied to hemolysis rather than fibrin, and inversion helps additives mix instead of causing strands.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are older adults 20 to 30% more prone to dehydration, a factor that can make veins harder to access?
opciones: A less sensitive thirst mechanism, immobility, diabetes, renal disease and polypharmacy
A higher proportion of body water, which is lost faster through thinner and less elastic skin
Overactive antidiuretic hormone, which makes the kidneys waste water in the collecting ducts
Greater sweating from more active glands, especially during long hospital stays in summer
preguntas.explicacion: Older individuals are 20 to 30% more prone to dehydration because of immobility, an impaired thirst mechanism, diabetes, renal disease and polypharmacy, and that the hypothalamic thirst response is less sensitive in older adults. Diuretics, laxatives and some antihypertensives add risk, as do reduced cognition and dependence on caregivers for fluids in institutional settings.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist splashes a disinfectant concentrate into her eye. Which section of the product's Safety Data Sheet gives the first-aid measures?
opciones: Section 4, First-Aid Measures, by route of exposure
Section 2, Hazard Identification and signal word
Section 8, Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
Section 6, Accidental Release and cleanup measures
preguntas.explicacion: Section 4 of the SDS describes the initial care an untrained responder should give after exposure, organized by route: inhalation, skin and eye contact, and ingestion, with the main symptoms and any need for immediate medical attention. Section 2 classifies the hazard and carries the signal word and pictograms; Section 8 lists exposure limits, engineering controls and the PPE to wear before handling; Section 6 covers containment and cleanup of spills. For the injured eye the practical first step is the eyewash facility, which 29 CFR 1910.151(c) requires within the work area.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic freezer that stores patient samples has a continuous temperature monitoring system with an alarm. How often must its temperature still be checked and recorded?
opciones: Daily, and before the room is used for testing, regardless of the alarm or data logger
Weekly, since a continuous monitoring system replaces the manual daily check
Only when the alarm sounds, because the logger already records the temperature
Monthly, when the log sheet is reviewed and filed with the quality records
preguntas.explicacion: Whether a refrigerator or freezer has a temperature alarm, a chart recorder, a digital data logger or a continuous monitoring system, its temperature is checked and recorded daily, and testing rooms are checked before use. A sample freezer is often kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), but the range that counts is the one the manufacturer's instructions give for what is stored inside, since waived testing under CLIA requires following those instructions.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient has veins that are hard to see and three tubes are needed. What is recommended instead of keeping the tourniquet on while the veins are located?
opciones: Using a venous illumination device to visualize the veins
Applying a second tourniquet below the first to raise the pressure
Drawing with a syringe, which tolerates a longer tourniquet time
Switching to a 16 to 18 gauge needle so the tubes fill faster
preguntas.explicacion: Venous illumination devices are recommended rather than a prolonged tourniquet to find non-prominent veins, especially when two or more tubes are to be collected, because they avoid the venous stasis that alters biochemistry and coagulation results. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is the WHO's blood donation size, and neither a second tourniquet nor a syringe extends the permitted time.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic finished its security risk analysis two years ago and has bought new equipment since. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Repeat it regularly, and whenever practice or technology changes
Repeat it only after a breach has actually been discovered
Repeat it every six years, when the documentation is renewed
Treat the first one as final once the flaws found were fixed
preguntas.explicacion: Security requirements put the weight on risk analysis, and it is not a one-time exercise: the system in place is audited to find flaws and gaps in the integrity, confidentiality and security of health information, everything found goes through the risk management process and is corrected, and the analysis is repeated regularly because new technology keeps arriving and clinical practice keeps changing. The six-year figure is how long the required documentation is kept.

preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory only analyzes patient specimens. Do the extra rules for HIV and HBV research laboratories apply to it?
opciones: No: those rules cover culture and production work, not diagnostic analysis
Yes: any laboratory that handles blood must meet them along with the rest
Yes, but only in the area where HIV testing is performed on patient samples
No: they apply only to facilities that manufacture the hepatitis B vaccine
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(1) draws the line itself. The extra requirements are for research laboratories and production facilities that culture, produce, concentrate, experiment with or manipulate HIV and HBV, and they do not reach clinical or diagnostic laboratories that only analyze blood, tissues or organs. A production facility is defined in (b) as one working at industrial scale, in large volume or at high concentration with the viruses themselves, which is not the same as making a vaccine. Everything else in the standard still applies to the hospital laboratory.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum lithium level is ordered on a patient taking lithium carbonate. Which heparin tube does the WHO table specify?
opciones: Sodium heparin, because a lithium heparin tube would interfere with the result
Lithium heparin, because it is the anticoagulant of the light green PST as well
Either sodium or lithium heparin, as the table allows for an ammonia level
Neither; lithium is measured in the pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 is explicit in the uses column of the dark green tube: for a lithium level use sodium heparin, and for an ammonia level either heparin will do. Lithium heparin is indeed the anticoagulant of the light green PST, which is exactly why it is the wrong choice when lithium itself is being measured. The ACD tube is for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a child's positive lead level to the state health department as state law requires. Under HIPAA this disclosure is which of these?
opciones: Permitted without authorization, as required by law and for public health
Permitted only with the parent's signed authorization
A breach that must be reported to the individual within 60 calendar days of discovery
Permitted only if the child is treated as an emancipated minor
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.512 lists uses and disclosures that need neither authorization nor an opportunity to object: those required by law, and those to a public health authority authorized to collect information to prevent or control disease, injury or disability, including disease reporting and surveillance; reports of child abuse or neglect to an authorized authority are in the same paragraph. preguntas.pregunta: A rural clinic uses needles and syringes rather than an evacuated system. Which advantages does that conventional device offer?
opciones: Widely available, least expensive, and needing no special training
Widely available, least expensive, and needing no blood transfer step
Safest of all devices, cheapest of all, and needing no special training
Widely available, safest of all devices, and giving many tubes per stick
preguntas.explicacion: The hypodermic needle and syringe is listed as widely available, the least expensive option, supplied in a wide range of lengths and gauges, and usable without special training. What it does not avoid is the transfer of blood into tubes, which is where its needle-stick risk comes from.

preguntas.pregunta: How does capillary blood compare with venous blood, and what limits its use?
opciones: Similar to arterial blood in oxygen content; limited by skin flora contamination and small volume
Similar to venous blood in every analyte; limited only by the pain of the puncture
Similar to arterial blood in oxygen content; limited by its high platelet count
Poorer in oxygen than venous blood; limited by dilution with tissue fluid in every sample
preguntas.explicacion: Blood from a capillary specimen is similar to an arterial specimen in oxygen content and is suitable for only a limited number of tests because of its higher likelihood of contamination with skin flora and its smaller total volume. Dilution with tissue fluid is a consequence of squeezing, not as a property of every capillary sample.

preguntas.pregunta: A very icteric sample and a very lipemic one both give unusable point-of-care readings. Which remedies are described for each?
opciones: Dilution for the excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation for the excess lipid
Ultracentrifugation for the excess bilirubin, and dilution for the excess lipid
Warming for the excess bilirubin, and a longer spin for the excess lipid
Dilution for both, since neither pigment nor lipid can be spun out of a sample
preguntas.explicacion: How such errors are handled depends on the device and the manufacturer's instructions, but two routes are named: dilution can resolve sample errors caused by excess bilirubin, and ultracentrifugation can clear those caused by excess lipid. At the point of care these three interferences can only be spotted by looking at a centrifuged aliquot, not measured as an index.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is choosing a needle for a routine draw. On what basis is the gauge decided?
opciones: The one that fits the most prominent vein with little discomfort
The widest one the tray holds, so the tubes fill more quickly
The finest one the tray holds, so the puncture hurts far less
The one that matches the colour of the stopper being filled
preguntas.explicacion: The gauge chosen is the one that fits comfortably into the most prominent vein while causing little discomfort. Going too wide tears the vein and bleeds into the tissue; going too fine damages the blood cells, which invalidates tests that need whole cells or free haemoglobin.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient had a radical mastectomy on the left side two years ago. Where should the blood be drawn?
opciones: From the right arm; a history of ipsilateral radical mastectomy contraindicates the left
From the left arm, provided the tourniquet stays on for less than one minute
From either arm, since the contraindication applies only during the first six months after surgery
From the left hand only, below the level of the surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Among the site-specific contraindications, the phlebotomy chapter lists a history of radical mastectomy on the same side, alongside scar tissue, cellulitis or abscess, a vascular graft, a hematoma, venous fibrosis on palpation and any venous access device. The chapter sets no time limit after which the arm becomes acceptable and no exception for the hand or for a short tourniquet time.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the wide variation in the superficial veins of the elbow a practical concern?
opciones: Mispuncture has caused bruising, haematoma, altered sensation
Mispuncture makes the tourniquet slip below the level of the vein
Variation changes which tubes may be filled from a single puncture
Variation means the median cubital vein is absent in most patients
preguntas.explicacion: Because the pattern differs so much from patient to patient, adverse effects from puncturing the wrong vessel have been reported across health systems: bruising, haematoma and sensory changes. That variation is the argument put forward for using an illuminator to see the vein first.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen sat uncovered on a sunlit counter for three hours before testing. Which two analytes are most likely to have broken down?
opciones: Bilirubin and urobilinogen
Glucose and ketone bodies
Protein and nitrite
Leukocyte esterase and blood
preguntas.explicacion: Bilirubin and urobilinogen are unstable in light and warmth and decompose when a specimen is left exposed, which is why light-sensitive analytes travel in amber containers. Prolonged daylight is also listed among the causes of a false-negative urobilinogen. Room temperature adds a second problem, since it favors the growth of bacteria, which can falsify the blood reaction and shift the pH of the sample.

preguntas.pregunta: At the end of a 24-hour urine collection, what does the laboratory do before analysis?
opciones: Records the total volume and submits a representative sample of the pooled urine
Discards the first and last voids and analyzes the pooled urine in between
Divides the urine into three numbered tubes for chemistry, culture and cytology
Records the collection time and refrigerates the whole volume for 24 hours before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Once the full period is over, the total volume is measured and written down, and a representative portion of the mixed urine is sent for analysis; the daily excretion is calculated from that volume. The first void of day one is the only one discarded, and the closing void is kept. Three numbered tubes are the cerebrospinal fluid routine. If a full day is not feasible, a shorter timed collection can be used provided the exact time is recorded.

preguntas.pregunta: The requisition reads 'Maria Lopez, DOB 03/14/1961'; the wristband reads 03/14/1967. The patient confirms her name. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Defer the blood sampling until the discrepancy has been resolved
Proceed, since the name matched and the date of birth is secondary
Draw the sample now and have the wristband corrected afterwards
Ask the patient which date is right and correct the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Before any blood is withdrawn, the identification data and the tube labelling are double-checked, and if any discrepancy appears among those data the sampling is deferred until the issue is resolved. A matching name does not cancel a mismatched date of birth, and the phlebotomist does not settle the conflict by editing the paperwork on the spot.

preguntas.pregunta: What does a valproate level mainly reflect, given the short half-life of that drug?
opciones: Short-term compliance, which makes the measurement low-yield
Long-term usage across the preceding weeks of treatment
The unbound fraction, untouched by any change in protein binding
The risk of a breakthrough seizure over the coming month
preguntas.explicacion: Valproate has a short half-life, which makes measuring it low-yield and primarily a reflection of short-term compliance. Phenytoin, with its long half-life, gives a level that reflects long-term usage instead. Free levels, not total levels, are what show the unbound and pharmacologically active fraction when protein binding has been altered.

preguntas.pregunta: Dried blood spot cards and dry buccal swabs are left in an outdoor specimen lock box for pickup, and the courier is delayed on a humid day. What is the concern?
opciones: High humidity compromises dried specimens kept at ambient conditions, degrading nucleic acids and inviting microbial growth
High humidity rehydrates the dried specimens, so the volume recovered falls below the minimum the assay requires
High humidity matters only for the buccal swabs; dried blood spots stay stable under any ambient conditions
High humidity fixes the dried specimens in place, so they must be soaked in transport medium before extraction
preguntas.explicacion: Dry oral and buccal swabs and dried blood spots kept under ambient conditions are the sample types that high humidity compromises: viral and microbial nucleic acids degrade during prolonged storage, water contributes to reactive oxygen species that break down DNA, and humid conditions make the specimens prone to fungal and bacterial contamination. The scenario given for this variable is a delayed pickup from an uninsulated lock box; when storage cannot be controlled, those sample types are avoided or validated first.

preguntas.pregunta: A 17-year-old on active military duty arrives alone for a drug level. Who consents to the draw?

A parent reached by telephone, because he is still younger than eighteen years
The ordering clinician, invoking the emergency exception under EMTALA
A parent, because emancipation applies only to minors who are married
preguntas.explicacion: Minors who are married, on active military duty, or living apart from their parents and managing their own finances are generally considered emancipated, and emancipated minors can consent to or refuse care without parental permission or notification. Ask the caregiver to introduce you, then begin without further delay
Begin the draw quickly, since explanations add to the confusion
Postpone the draw until a family member is able to attend in person

preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient had to be moved from lying to sitting just before the draw. What should the phlebotomist do about it?
opciones: Record the change of position so the results can be interpreted
Cancel the draw and reschedule it for the following morning
Wait 2 minutes, then draw; no note is needed for a brief change
Return the patient to the supine position and draw at once
preguntas.explicacion: Position is meant to be maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before venipuncture; when a change cannot be avoided, it is documented so the laboratory results can be read in that light. preguntas.pregunta: A control on the chemistry analyzer falls out of range and the technologist troubleshoots it. Under CLIA, when may the patient results from that run be reported?

As soon as the control is repeated and lands inside its range on a second attempt
At once, with a note on the report that the control was out of range at that time
After the technical consultant signs the instrument maintenance log for that day
preguntas.explicacion: One of the technical consultant's duties is to make sure patient test results are not reported until every corrective action has been completed and the test system is functioning properly. preguntas.pregunta: An intensive care manager asks why the laboratory's improvement plan targets the medical units and not the surgical ones. What did the rejection audit show?
opciones: Non-surgical intensive care rejected about four times as many specimens as surgical
Surgical intensive care units rejected about four times as many specimens as medical ones
Neurology intensive care showed the lowest rejection ratio of all the intensive care units
Rejection ratios in intensive care matched those of the adult emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: Inside intensive care the split was wide: 40 % of the rejections came from non-surgical units and 10 % from surgical ones. Neurology intensive care was the worst single unit at 14 %, twice the internal medicine unit at 7 % and three times the surgical units at 4.5 %. That is why the training effort was pointed at the medical units rather than spread evenly.

preguntas.pregunta: Blood splashes into a phlebotomist's eye while she uncaps a tube. What is the first thing to do?
opciones: Irrigate the eye with clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant, then report the exposure
Apply an antiseptic eye drop, then complete the incident report before seeking care
Squeeze the eyelids shut and wait for the occupational health nurse to examine it
Flush with a dilute bleach solution, which inactivates bloodborne viruses on contact
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC and NIOSH give the same immediate steps: wash needlesticks and cuts with soap and water, flush splashes to the nose, mouth or skin with water, and irrigate eyes with clean water, saline or sterile irrigants; then report the exposure to the department that manages exposures and seek medical care right away. OSHA's laboratory guidance suggests irrigating eyes and mucous membranes for 15 minutes. The CDC adds that there is no evidence that antiseptics or squeezing reduce transmission and that caustic agents such as bleach are not recommended.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads her record and says one entry is wrong. What right does she have?
opciones: To ask for a correction, which the provider may accept or deny
To have the entry deleted within thirty days of the request
To have the entry rewritten by the clinician who made it
To bill the provider for the time spent finding the mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the rights the privacy rule gives are the right to a notice of privacy practices, to ask that disclosures be restricted, to say how information should be handled and communicated, to inspect and review one's own information and request a change to anything that looks wrong, to obtain a copy, to receive an accounting of disclosures, and to complain to the Office for Civil Rights. The request for a change is a request: the provider may accept or deny it, and a documented diagnosis a patient dislikes is not erased for that reason.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides the tests listed in the regulation itself, by which two routes does a test become waived?
opciones: FDA clearance for home use, or a manufacturer's waiver application with supporting data
State agency approval, or two years of acceptable proficiency testing at the site
A CMS inspection of the site, or accreditation by a CMS-approved organization
A Certificate of Registration, or categorization as PPM by the physician
preguntas.explicacion: Three doors lead to waived status: the tests named in 42 CFR 493.15(c), tests cleared or approved by the FDA for home use, and tests a manufacturer submits to the FDA with scientific data showing the waiver criteria are met (a CLIA Waiver by Application, for a test first categorized as moderate). Inspections, accreditation and site-level proficiency testing concern the laboratory, not the test.

At least ten seconds, covering the palms and the backs of the hands
At least two minutes, covering the forearms as far as the elbows
At least thirty seconds, covering the fingertips and the nails only

preguntas.pregunta: In the one-year audit of an emergency laboratory, what was the single most frequent reason for rejecting biochemistry specimens?
opciones: Fibrin clots, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Hemolysis, found in 28 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Insufficient volume, found in 35 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
Lipemia, found in 22 % of the rejected biochemistry samples
preguntas.explicacion: For biochemistry the leading cause was fibrin clots at 28 %, followed by inadequate volume at 9 %; for coagulation, blood gases and CBC the leaders were clotted samples at 35 % and inadequate volume at 13 %. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist sustains a needlestick from a used needle. According to the WHO's infection prevention table, what is the time limit after which post-exposure prophylaxis is no longer effective?
opciones: 72 hours
24 hours
48 hours
7 days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.2 of the WHO guideline pairs each practice with its opposite. On the Do side: report any needle or sharps injury at once, seek help, and start post-exposure prophylaxis as soon as possible following the local protocol. On the Do-not side: do not put off PEP after contact with potentially contaminated material, because past 72 hours it no longer works. The lesson for the exam is twofold: report at once, and the window is three days, not one day and not a week.

preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the CLIA quality standards for moderate and high complexity testing is accurate?

They differ only in proficiency testing rules
High complexity sites are inspected; moderate sites are not
Moderate sites follow the insert only, like waived sites

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist pours a bleach solution from a labeled jug into a basin she will use and empty during her own shift. Must she label the basin?
opciones: No: a portable container for her own immediate use is exempt
No: containers under one liter are exempt from workplace labels
Yes: every container in the work area needs the full label
Yes: unless the jug's own label is carried alongside the basin
preguntas.explicacion: The standard does not require labeling a portable container into which a hazardous chemical is transferred from a labeled container when it is intended only for the immediate use of the employee who performs the transfer. The exemption is narrow: it turns on immediate use by that same person, not on the size of the container, so a bottle filled for the next shift or for someone else falls back under the workplace labeling rule. Drugs a pharmacy dispenses for direct administration are exempt too.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and heads to the cafeteria still wearing her gloves and lab coat. What does the standard require?
opciones: All PPE must be removed before leaving the work area and placed in a designated container
Gloves must be removed, but the lab coat may be worn out if it is not visibly soiled
PPE may be worn out if hands are washed first with soap and running water
PPE may be worn out if it is penetrated by blood, so long as it is changed within the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vii) requires all personal protective equipment to be removed before the employee leaves the work area, and (d)(3)(viii) says removed PPE goes into a designated area or container for storage, washing, decontamination or disposal. The rule covers every item, coat included, and does not depend on visible soiling. Handwashing after glove removal, in (d)(2)(v), is an additional duty, not a permit to keep PPE on, and a garment penetrated by blood comes off immediately under (d)(3)(vi).

preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes in the order of draw share the same mode of action on calcium. Which are they?

The light blue citrate tube and the grey fluoride tube
The purple EDTA tube and the dark green heparin tube
The grey fluoride tube and the light green PST tube
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate at position 3 and EDTA at position 8 are both described as forming calcium salts to take calcium out of play, which is why both tubes stop the blood clotting. Heparin works instead by inactivating thrombin and thromboplastin, and the grey tube pairs oxalate with an antiglycolytic agent.

The catheter lumen is too narrow, so the tubes fill slowly and the sample clots inside
The nursing staff alone may access it, and only for blood cultures
The results are valid only if a non-additive tube is drawn first and discarded

preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC ask occupational health services to establish for reporting infectious exposures?
opciones: A timely, confidential, non-punitive mechanism available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A written form reviewed by the supervisor and filed within 60 calendar days
A monthly review meeting where exposures of the previous month are discussed
A punitive policy, so that workers who fail to follow precautions are held accountable
preguntas.explicacion: Recommendation 7.b.2 asks for a timely, confidential and non-punitive mechanism for personnel to report potentially infectious exposures and reach exposure management services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with access to expert clinicians and prompt laboratory testing on the same footing. The background explains why: exposures are significantly underreported because of time constraints, fear of reprimand, not knowing how to report and worries about cost coverage. A punitive policy would deepen exactly that problem, and 60 days is a HIPAA breach figure.

preguntas.pregunta: While verifying a date of birth with a hard-of-hearing patient, which technique applies?
opciones: Say the digits one at a time, 'six, one', rather than 'sixty-one'
Say the year louder, because numbers are especially hard to lip-read
Show the date on the wristband and ask him to confirm it with a nod
Skip the date of birth and use the room number as the second identifier
preguntas.explicacion: Give context when a patient has trouble hearing the difference between certain letters and numbers, for example 'm as in Mary' or 'five, six' instead of 'fifty-six'. Shouting distorts language sounds, the WHO wants the patient to state identifiers rather than nod at them, and The Joint Commission excludes the room number as an identifier.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is filling an evacuated tube from a syringe. In what position is the tube held, and with what pressure?
opciones: Upright, pierced from directly above, with slow and steady pressure
Upright, pierced from directly above, with one firm push on the plunger
Tilted, pierced through the side of the stopper, with steady pressure
Upright, with the stopper taken off first and the blood run down the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The stopper is pierced with the needle directly above the tube, using slow and steady pressure, and the plunger is not pressed because the extra pressure raises the risk of haemolysis. The stopper is never removed either, since taking it off releases the vacuum inside.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7

preguntas.pregunta: In an intensive care cohort, what did each additional 5 mL of average daily phlebotomy volume predict?
opciones: Higher odds of a hemoglobin nadir below 80 g/L and of red cell transfusion
Higher odds of a hemoglobin nadir below 80 g/L, but not of red cell transfusion
Lower odds of red cell transfusion, because anemia was detected earlier
No measurable change in hemoglobin, only a longer stay in the unit
preguntas.explicacion: For every 5 mL increase in average daily phlebotomy, the odds ratio for a hemoglobin nadir under 80 g/L was 1.18 and for red cell transfusion 1.17, and the association held whichever nadir threshold was used to define acquired anemia. Those 5 mL were a stronger predictor of both outcomes than a one-point rise in the day-1 severity score, which is the argument for phlebotomy stewardship.

preguntas.pregunta: After a post-exposure evaluation, how soon must the employer give the employee a copy of the healthcare professional's written opinion?
opciones: Within 15 days of completing the evaluation
Within 10 working days of the exposure incident
Within 30 days of the exposure incident
Within 90 days, once the baseline sample is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5) obliges the employer to obtain the evaluating professional's written opinion and hand the employee a copy within 15 days of the completion of the evaluation. The other periods belong elsewhere in the standard: 10 working days is the window for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment, and 90 days is how long a baseline blood sample is preserved when the employee consents to the draw but not yet to HIV testing. Thirty days is not a deadline in this standard.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion
