preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's positive result in a crowded elevator. Is that a HIPAA problem?
opciones: Yes, because protected health information covers spoken communications, not only written records
No, because the rule reaches only electronic records and the papers printed out from them
No, because both of them work for the same covered entity and are part of its workforce
Yes, but only if a patient or a visitor from outside the organization actually overheard them
preguntas.explicacion: Protected health information is protected in any form or medium: electronic, paper or oral. A conversation naming a patient in a public space is a disclosure like any other, which is why the surgeon discussing a case in a full elevator is the standard example of a violation. Belonging to the same workforce permits access for a job reason, not conversation in public.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Definition of PHI

preguntas.pregunta: Along which vein does the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve travel, and at what level does it reach the surface?
opciones: With the basilic vein, about ten centimetres above the medial epicondyle
With the cephalic vein, about ten centimetres above the lateral epicondyle
With the median cubital vein, at the apex of the cubital fossa itself
With the basilic vein, about two centimetres below the medial epicondyle
preguntas.explicacion: This sensory nerve runs down the arm inside the brachial fascia together with the basilic vein and leaves that fascia roughly ten centimetres above the medial epicondyle, dividing into an anterior and a posterior branch. Its closeness to the basilic vein is what puts it at risk during a draw.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Introduction

preguntas.pregunta: Which safeguard applies when faxing protected health information?
opciones: Keep the fax machine in a secure area and use a cover page saying what to do if misdirected
Place the fax machine at the reception desk so that staff can retrieve incoming pages quickly
Send faxes overnight so that they arrive before the office opens and are not seen
Confirm receipt by mailing a paper duplicate of every fax to the recipient on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Fax machines are kept in a secure area away from the public, patients and most staff; the first page is a disclaimer telling the recipient what to do if the fax reached the wrong number; faxes are sent during working hours except in emergencies, so that they are picked up rather than left in the tray; and the sender contacts the other party to confirm the fax was collected. A machine at reception and overnight transmissions both leave PHI exposed, and mailing duplicates adds a second disclosure instead of a confirmation.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Faxes

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient who has just hurried up three flights of stairs sits down in the drawing chair. According to the phlebotomy guidance on position, what should happen before the draw?
opciones: The patient stays seated for at least 15 minutes before the draw, and any unavoidable change of position is recorded
The patient lies down for 2 minutes and the draw proceeds, because lying down offsets the effect of the exertion
The draw proceeds at once, because position affects only patients who are drawn lying down in the hospital
The patient stands for 5 minutes to let the blood volume redistribute, then sits and is drawn immediately
preguntas.explicacion: Changing position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the procedure; in an office setting the patient should sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand, and when a change of position is unavoidable it is recorded so the results can be interpreted accordingly. Outpatients are also told to avoid excessive physical activity in the 24 hours before collection.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position and fasting)

preguntas.pregunta: The tubes are filled and the needle is discarded. Which closing steps does the WHO list before the patient leaves?
opciones: Check labels and forms, perform hand hygiene, ask how the patient feels and check the site for bleeding
Invert every tube 8 to 10 times, remove the gloves and send the patient out while the tubes clot in the rack
Apply ice to the site for 15 minutes, then recheck the labels once the patient has gone
Ask the patient to bend the arm over the gauze and hold it for five minutes before standing
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 runs through the closing routine: discard the sharp into the sharps container, check the label and forms for accuracy, discard the other items in the right waste category, perform hand hygiene again, recheck the labels before dispatch, tell the patient the procedure is over, ask how they feel, verify the site is not bleeding, and say something reassuring. Bending the arm is what Step 6 forbids.

preguntas.pregunta: How does underfilling a tube contribute to haemolysis?
opciones: The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up greater than one to nine
The ratio of anticoagulant to blood ends up smaller than one to nine
The vacuum left in the tube pulls the red cells against the stopper
The additive settles at the bottom and never reaches the red cells
preguntas.explicacion: Among the recognized causes of haemolysis is underfilling a tube so that the proportion of anticoagulant to blood rises above one to nine. It is the same arithmetic that lengthens clotting times in a short-drawn citrate tube, where the plasma is outnumbered by the anticoagulant.

preguntas.pregunta: What do surveillance data say about how often needlestick injuries are actually reported?
opciones: About half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees some 30 per 100 beds a year
Nearly all are reported, since the sharps injury log is reviewed every month
About one in ten goes unreported, mostly among housekeeping employees
Half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees about 300 per 100 beds a year
preguntas.explicacion: Estimates put 600,000 to 800,000 needlestick and other percutaneous injuries a year in the United States, and about half of them are never reported. Surveillance data suggest an average hospital sees roughly 30 needlestick injuries per 100 beds per year. Under-reporting matters twice over: the worker misses post-exposure management, and the institution loses the record it needs to see where the hazard is. That is why employers are told to establish procedures that encourage reporting.

preguntas.pregunta: A contract cleaning crew works nights in a laboratory that stores hazardous chemicals. What must the laboratory's program provide for?

A copy of the crew's own written program, kept in the laboratory office

A separate storage room for the chemicals while the crew is on site

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's stat chemistry goes into a green top tube. Which heparin salts may it hold, and what is tested?

preguntas.pregunta: Why has a needle and vacuum tube assembly been singled out as carrying a higher injury risk?
opciones: It has to be taken apart or handled after use, which has raised injury rates
It holds a larger volume of blood than a syringe of the very same gauge
Its needle is longer, so it reaches deeper into the vein of the patient
It cannot be fitted with a shield, so no safer version of it is made
preguntas.explicacion: Devices that must be taken apart or manipulated once the draw is over, such as prefilled cartridge syringes and phlebotomy needle and vacuum tube assemblies, are an obvious hazard and have been linked to higher injury rates. Safer versions do exist: hinged or sliding shields for phlebotomy and winged-steel needles, sliding shields on vacuum tube holders, and needles that retract into the holder. Length and blood volume are not what the injury data point to.

preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding unencrypted patient results is stolen from a laboratory courier's car. How soon must the affected individuals be notified?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days after the breach is discovered
Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 30 days after the breach is discovered
Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 90 days after the breach is discovered
Within 60 days of the end of the calendar year in which the breach came to light
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice goes out without unreasonable delay and never later than 60 days after discovery, in writing by first-class mail or by email if the person agreed to that. preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fainted during a draw remains unresponsive for more than five minutes, with jerking movements and loss of bladder control. What does this episode indicate?
opciones: It is not simple syncope but more likely a seizure, which needs urgent evaluation
It is a prolonged vasovagal episode; keep the legs raised and wait calmly for recovery
It is typical syncope, since jerking and incontinence are common during a faint
It is near syncope, because the patient never fully lost postural tone
preguntas.explicacion: Any episode lasting more than a few minutes is not syncope but more likely an acute neurologic process such as a seizure, and, unlike seizure patients, people with syncope keep sphincter control, rarely show tonic-clonic activity and are not confused on waking. Emergency services are called if the person does not become alert within a couple of minutes.

preguntas.pregunta: A light blue tube reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. Which collection faults are recognized causes?

A tourniquet released too early, a needle angle below fifteen degrees, or a warm room
An expired needle, a second puncture in the same arm, or a bandage applied too tightly
A tube filled from a syringe, a tube stored upright, or a label written after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting in a citrate specimen is traced to a traumatic venipuncture, activation of coagulation inside the collection device, or the anticoagulant not being properly mixed with the blood. Newborn samples are collected by nurses who work outside the barcode system

preguntas.pregunta: In the sequence of steps of a venipuncture as explained to patients, when is the elastic band taken off the arm?

After the needle is taken out and the spot has been covered with a bandage strip
Before the needle is inserted, once the vein below it has swollen with blood
Only if the patient reports throbbing at the site while the tube is filling

Roughly twenty-five per cent of them all
Fewer than ten per cent of all of them
Almost exactly fifty per cent of them all

preguntas.pregunta: For a patient on Droplet Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for staff entering the room and for the patient?
opciones: Staff don a mask on entry; the patient wears a mask as source control and when transported
Staff don a fit-tested respirator; the patient is placed in an airborne infection isolation room
Staff don gown and gloves; the patient's room is disinfected at least daily
Staff need no mask if the patient is masked; the door must remain closed at all times
preguntas.explicacion: Droplet Precautions apply to pathogens carried in respiratory droplets produced by coughing, sneezing or talking. The CDC asks for source control by masking the patient, a single room if possible, a mask donned by staff on entering the room or patient space, and a mask on the patient plus cough etiquette whenever transport is medically necessary. The respirator and the AIIR are Airborne Precautions; gown and gloves are Contact Precautions; and the masked-patient exemption for escorts applies to transport under Airborne Precautions, not to staff entering a Droplet room.

preguntas.pregunta: The plastic bins that hold used racks in the draw room have dried blood on the bottom. What does the standard require?
opciones: Clean and decontaminate them as soon as feasible, on top of the routine schedule
Discard them as regulated waste, since a soiled reusable bin cannot be cleaned
Line them with plastic wrap, which is then replaced at the end of the work shift
Clean them at the next scheduled inspection, which the standard sets once a year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(C) treats bins, pails, cans and similar reusable receptacles that are likely to become contaminated in two ways at once: they are inspected and decontaminated on a regularly scheduled basis, and they are also cleaned immediately or as soon as feasible whenever contamination becomes visible. preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a sharp, shooting pain and tingling down the forearm the moment the needle enters near the basilic vein. What does this indicate?
opciones: Probable injury to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, which runs near the basilic vein
Normal discomfort of a basilic puncture, which resolves as soon as the tourniquet is released
An arterial puncture, since arteries have more nerves and produce tingling
A vasovagal prodrome, which typically begins with tingling in the puncture arm
preguntas.explicacion: The basilic vein runs with the artery and nerve, and severing the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve nearby causes loss of sensation in the medial forearm; the nerve chapter adds that damage during venipuncture produces painful paresthesias, dysesthesias and numbness. The vasovagal prodrome is lightheadedness, warmth, nausea and sweating, not arm tingling.

preguntas.pregunta: Which action during a draw is the one experimentally shown to contaminate a specimen with antiseptic alcohol?
opciones: Pressing the soaked swab on the site while the needle is still drawing
Wiping the site with the swab in a spiral from the centre outwards
Letting the alcohol dry for a full minute before inserting the needle
Using 2 mL of antiseptic instead of the 1 mL usually applied
preguntas.explicacion: Contamination requires the needle to be suctioning while it is in direct contact with the alcoholic antiseptic, which is what happens when the soaked swab is pressed on the site to stop bleeding as the needle is withdrawn. With the correct amount of antiseptic, about 1 mL, and a full minute of drying, the probability drops to 5% or less; even excess antiseptic without that pressure did not contaminate evacuated tubes.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is buying new chairs for its draw station. Why do the armrests need to be adjustable?

So the tourniquet can be anchored to the rest during the draw
So the arm stays above heart level while the tubes are filling
So the patient can be held in one posture for a full 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: A clean, convenient, private and well-designed environment is asked for in the outpatient setting, with a comfortable chair for the patient and for the provider. preguntas.pregunta: How much can swabbing with ethanol raise the measured blood alcohol concentration in intoxicated subjects?
opciones: About 0.05 g/L, whether an evacuated tube or a syringe was used
About 0.50 g/L, whether an evacuated tube or a syringe was used
About 0.05 g/L, but only when a syringe is used instead of a tube
About 6.0 g/L, which is why the effect is called unpredictable
preguntas.explicacion: When experiments involve inebriated subjects, swabbing with ethanol gives an average increase of about 0.05 g/L in the measured concentration, and the effect appears with pre-evacuated tubes and with syringes alike. Spurious values from chemical contamination are erratic and unpredictable, and readings anywhere from 0.005 to 6.0 g/L have been reported, but 6.0 is the extreme of that range, not the average.

preguntas.pregunta: What total blood volume does the CDC consider optimal for diagnosing bacteremia in an adult, and over what period is it collected?
opciones: 40 to 60 mL from at least two sets within a 24-hour period
20 to 30 mL from a single set within a 24-hour period
10 to 20 mL from at least two sets within a 5-minute period
80 to 100 mL from four sets within a 48-hour period
preguntas.explicacion: The optimal volume is 40 to 60 mL, reached by collecting at least two sets, by peripheral venipuncture, within a 24-hour period and before antibiotics whenever possible; the standard of practice is two to four sets per septic episode. A single set of 20 to 30 mL falls short, and the laboratory is encouraged to comment on single-set cultures so that more sets are drawn. The five minutes in one distractor is only the interval used in the CDC's contamination-rate example.

Completion of a CMS-approved course and a passing score on the site's written competency examination
A month of running external controls only, until the results fall consistently within range

preguntas.explicacion: Every test is practiced under the eye of an experienced person before patient samples are tested and results reported, and all training goes into the staff personnel file. preguntas.pregunta: Which set of practices does the CDC list as Standard Precautions for all patient care?
opciones: Hand hygiene, risk-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, patient placement, equipment cleaning and safe injections
Gown and gloves on room entry, dedicated equipment and daily room disinfection, for every patient
A fit-tested N95 respirator and an airborne infection isolation room, for every patient
Treating only blood and the listed body fluids as infectious, regardless of patient diagnosis

It is performed at the bedside or in an exam room rather than in a laboratory
It has been cleared by the FDA as substantially equivalent to a marketed test
It is a moderately complex procedure done by a physician during the visit

preguntas.pregunta: Under which doctrine is a supervising physician or employer held liable for the acts of an employee working within the scope of employment?
opciones: Respondeat superior, a form of vicarious liability
Strict liability, applied to inherently dangerous activities
Proportional liability, apportioned by degree of fault
Sovereign immunity, which limits awards against governments
preguntas.explicacion: Vicarious liability holds an employer responsible for the torts of employees acting within the scope of their employment, on the policy view that the employer is better placed to absorb the loss; when a midlevel provider working under a physician's license is sued, the plaintiff focuses on the supervising physician under the doctrine of respondeat superior. Proportional liability reduces an award by the claimant's own share of fault, strict liability applies to dangerous activities and defective drugs or devices, and sovereign immunity caps damages against governmental entities.

preguntas.pregunta: Anticoagulated specimens from a neonatal unit clot at 6.67 %, against 0.36 % elsewhere in the same hospital. Which explanation fits the published data?
opciones: Drawn-out, difficult venipuncture and failure to mix the tube afterwards
Excess anticoagulant in the microtubes chosen for very small blood volumes
Transport of the microtubes upright in a rack instead of a padded holder
The longer wait before newborn serum is separated from the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting inside a tube that contains an anticoagulant is attributed to two things: a challenging or prolonged venipuncture, and a tube that was not mixed properly once filled. Newborn draws are hard, which is why their clotting ratio ran roughly eighteen times the hospital average. Published median figures for clotted samples elsewhere sit between 0.05 % and 0.21 %.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the WHO order-of-draw table say about tubes that contain an additive once they have been filled?

Leave them standing upright until the additive has dissolved on its own
Invert them only if the local laboratory has not already specified otherwise
Shake them firmly for a few seconds so the additive reaches all the blood
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote c of Table 2.3 instructs the phlebotomist to gently invert additive tubes to mix them well, and warns that test results can be wrong when blood and additive are not mixed thoroughly. Step 7 adds that the number of inversions is the one the local laboratory specifies, which is a detail of how many, not a licence to skip mixing. Shaking is exactly what to avoid.

preguntas.pregunta: An instructor compares the analytical phase of the laboratory with the rest of health care using the sigma scale. Which comparison is the one drawn in the literature?

Health care sits at 4 sigma, roughly level with airline baggage handling
Health care sits at 5 sigma, matching the analytical phase of the laboratory
Health care sits at 3 sigma, ahead of airline baggage handling at about 2
preguntas.explicacion: Measured on the sigma scale, health care as a whole performs at 1 to 2 sigma, which compares poorly with an industry such as airline baggage handling at roughly 4 sigma, and the overall defect rate in United States health care has been put at 31 to 69 %. Against that background the analytical phase of the laboratory, close to 5 sigma, is the exception rather than the rule.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory is writing its specimen identification policy. Under CLIA, over what span must positive identification and integrity of a patient's specimen be assured?

From the moment the specimen is accessioned until the analyzer finishes the run
From collection until the specimen is centrifuged and the aliquots are labeled
From receipt in the laboratory until the specimen is discarded at the end of its retention period
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1232 asks for written policies that keep the specimen positively identified and in optimum condition across the whole chain: it starts when the specimen is collected or received and ends only when testing is finished and the result has been reported. It should differ between hospitals, so devices are not mixed up
It should change once the safety feature has been activated once

preguntas.pregunta: How long after a patient's death does HIPAA continue to protect their health information?
opciones: For 50 years after death
For 6 years after death
For 30 years after death
Indefinitely, with no time limit
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(f) requires a covered entity to comply with the Privacy Rule for the PHI of a deceased individual for 50 years following the death; the 2013 Omnibus Rule changed the protection from indefinite to this fixed period. During that time an executor, administrator or other person with authority over the estate is treated as the personal representative. Six years is the retention period for HIPAA documentation, and employment plus 30 years is the OSHA rule for employee medical records.

To the ordering provider only; the patient must obtain the results through that provider's office
To any caller who can supply two patient identifiers, since positive identification is what the regulation requires
To the ordering provider and to any physician or relative who states that they are involved in the patient's care

The evaluating healthcare professional who provides the written opinions after exposure incidents
The laboratory director or other responsible person named on the biohazard warning signs
The Assistant Secretary and the Director, who may examine and copy the plan on request

preguntas.pregunta: The CDC states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Which rule in the OSHA standard expresses the same principle?
opciones: Hands are washed immediately or as soon as feasible after gloves are removed
Gloves are worn whenever hand contact with blood can reasonably be anticipated
Disposable gloves are replaced as soon as feasible when torn or punctured
Utility gloves may be decontaminated and reused while they remain intact
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA paragraph (d)(2)(v) requires handwashing immediately or as soon as feasible after removing gloves or other PPE, which is the regulatory form of the CDC's statement. OSHA's Hospitals eTool gives the reasons: gloves may have small defects, may tear in use, and hands can be contaminated while gloves come off, so gloving never replaces washing and gloves must be changed between patients. The other three options are also OSHA glove rules, in (d)(3)(ix), (A) and (C), but they govern when gloves are worn or replaced, not hand hygiene.

Falsely lowered laboratory results after prolonged constriction of the veins
Clotting inside the tube after the anticoagulant has failed to mix properly

preguntas.pregunta: On the one-step 2-hour 75 g test used in pregnancy, which fasting value counts as abnormal?
opciones: 92 mg/dL or higher
95 mg/dL or higher
100 mg/dL or higher
126 mg/dL or higher
preguntas.explicacion: The one-step test is abnormal at 92 mg/dL fasting, 180 at one hour and 153 at two hours. That stricter fasting cutoff is part of what separates it from the 3-hour 100 g test, whose fasting threshold is 95, and it identifies milder hyperglycemia as gestational diabetes. Outside pregnancy, 100 to 125 mg/dL is impaired fasting glucose and 126 on two tests diagnoses diabetes.

preguntas.pregunta: Which subject must hazard communication training cover, beyond the hazards of the chemicals themselves?
opciones: Ways to detect that a hazardous chemical is present or being released
The disposal contractor's route and the landfill that receives the waste
The chemical formula of each product and its molecular weight
The purchase price of each product and the budget for replacing it
preguntas.explicacion: Training has to include at least four things: the methods and observations that can reveal the presence or release of a hazardous chemical in the area, such as monitoring by the employer, continuous monitoring devices, or the appearance or smell of the chemical when it escapes; the physical and health hazards, including asphyxiation, combustible dust, pyrophoric gas and hazards not otherwise classified; the measures employees can take to protect themselves; and the details of the program, the labels and the data sheet, including the order of its information.

preguntas.pregunta: A man says part of his semen sample spilled outside the container. What should he be told?
opciones: Report the loss to the laboratory, because every fraction of the ejaculate is meant to be collected
Keep it to himself, because the laboratory reports concentration per millilitre and volume does not count
Top the container up with sterile saline to the mark the instructions on the lid show him
Bring a second sample later the same day, since two samples are added together for the count
preguntas.explicacion: Clear instructions are given beforehand precisely so that all fractions of the ejaculate end up in the container, and any loss has to be reported when the sample is handed in. Volume itself is one of the measurements made. Because composition varies from one occasion to another, collecting 2 or 3 separate samples gives more accurate data, but they are analyzed separately, not pooled.

preguntas.pregunta: Which coagulation pathway is set off by trauma to the tissues around a vessel and is completed within seconds?
opciones: The extrinsic pathway, started by factor III
The intrinsic pathway, started by factor XII
The common pathway, started by factor X
The fibrinolytic pathway, started by plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: The extrinsic (tissue factor) pathway is the quicker and more direct one: damaged cells outside the bloodstream release factor III, thromboplastin, which with calcium and factor VII activates factor X, and the whole sequence takes seconds. The intrinsic pathway begins inside the blood when factor XII meets a damaged wall or a foreign surface and takes minutes. Both feed the common pathway.

preguntas.pregunta: A tube reaches the laboratory with no label on it, and the courier says he knows which patient it came from. What does the CLIA specimen identification standard require?

Accept it and label it from the requisition, since the courier can confirm where it came from
Accept it and note the discrepancy on the report as an unacceptable specimen condition found
Accept it when the order is stat, and label it once the ordering provider confirms the source

preguntas.pregunta: A new tube brand asks for ten inversions on its insert while the poster on the wall says eight. What settles the number?
opciones: The number the local laboratory specifies for the tubes it has in use
The larger of the two numbers, since extra mixing carries no penalty
The smaller of the two numbers, since extra mixing produces haemolysis
The number printed on the poster, which follows the published sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Before tubes are sent, those holding an additive are inverted the number of times the local laboratory specifies, which is what the guidance points to when brands disagree. Neither extreme is safe on its own: overmixing can haemolyse the sample and too little mixing leaves small clots.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient raises a fist at the front-desk staff but does not strike. In tort terms this may be which of the following?
opciones: Assault: an intentional act creating apprehension of imminent harmful contact
Battery: harmful or offensive contact that actually occurs
Negligence: an unintentional failure to act as a reasonable person would
Strict liability: harm during a known dangerous activity, regardless of fault
preguntas.explicacion: Common law defines assault as an intentional act that creates a reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful or offensive contact; if the strike lands, battery is added to the assault. The example of a patient threatening front-desk staff and raising a fist is the one used to illustrate it, with the note that reasonableness matters, since a person several meters away would not yet cause apprehension. Negligence is unintentional, and strict liability attaches to inherently dangerous activities or defective products without regard to fault.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: How does the CDC sequence describe removing a mask at the end of doffing?
opciones: By the ties or straps behind the head, never by the front
By the front panel, pulling it down under the chin first
By the nose bridge, lifting it up and over the head
By the ear loops after untying the gown, keeping gloves on
preguntas.explicacion: The front or mouth area of the mask or respirator is never touched; it is removed by releasing the ties or straps around the back of the head, bottom ties first and then the top, lifting it away from the face, and discarded in the proper container. The front is considered contaminated, which is also why eye protection is lifted from behind the head. Gloves are the first item off, so they are already gone by the time the mask is removed.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and, out of habit, starts to push the cap back onto the used needle with both hands. Which OSHA rule does this break?
opciones: Contaminated needles are not recapped, bent or removed unless no alternative is feasible or a procedure requires it
Contaminated needles may be recapped with a one-handed technique whenever the phlebotomist finds it convenient
Contaminated needles may be sheared or broken with a mechanical device, but they may never be bent by hand
Recapping is permitted whenever the employer documents that it is faster than reaching the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(vii) forbids recapping, bending or removing a contaminated needle, and forbids shearing or breaking one outright, mechanical device or not. The only way around it is for the employer to show that there is no feasible alternative or that a specific medical or dental procedure demands it, and even then the job has to be done with a mechanical device or with one hand. Convenience and speed are not exceptions, and the one-handed technique is the method for the exception, not a general permission. The standard's own definition of a work practice control gives this very example: banning two-handed recapping.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) and (b), Definitions: Work Practice Controls

preguntas.pregunta: Why do accreditation bodies treat a mislabeled blood specimen as one of the most dangerous laboratory errors?
opciones: Mislabeling can lead to a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood
Mislabeling always causes hemolysis of the specimen during centrifugation
Mislabeling invalidates the CLIA certificate of the laboratory that reports the result
Mislabeling is the most common reason a specimen clots before it is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Identification errors can lead to inappropriate treatment, and a mislabeled blood specimen may end in a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood; up to half of transfusion-related deaths trace back to identification error, and as many as 1 in 18 identification errors produce an adverse outcome. The error is about the patient, not about the specimen clotting or hemolyzing, and it does not by itself void a certificate.

preguntas.pregunta: Among the preanalytical quality indicators tracked by that emergency laboratory, which one affected the largest share of samples?

The presence of a fibrin clot inside the tube, near 28 %
An insufficient volume of specimen, near 22 %
Visible or measured hemolysis of the serum, near 2 %

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen was left out overnight and the strip now reads a pH of 8.5. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The specimen is stale and bacteria have split its urea, releasing ammonia
The specimen is stale and bacteria have consumed all the glucose it contained
The patient has been drinking cranberry juice, which pushes the pH upward
The patient is on a high-protein diet, which pushes the pH upward as well
preguntas.explicacion: Urine pH normally falls between 4.5 and 8, usually 5.5 to 6.5, and it is slightly acidic because of metabolic activity. The commonest reason for an alkaline reading is an old specimen in which bacteria have grown and broken urea down into ammonia. Bacteria metabolizing glucose push the pH down, not up, and cranberry juice and a high-protein diet are both listed among the causes of acid urine.

opciones: It holds the tube in place and shields the phlebotomist from direct contact with blood
It creates the vacuum that pulls the blood into the tube once the needle is in the vein
It retracts the used needle automatically in every model once the last tube is filled
It mixes the additive with the blood by rotating the tube as it fills

preguntas.pregunta: A frail 88-year-old has thin, fragile skin. What does the WHO say about adhesive strips in such patients, and how is the problem avoided?
opciones: Repeated strips can break down the skin in the very young and very old; use enough pressure and observe the site
Adhesive strips are mandatory for the elderly because their bleeding time is longer; apply two overlapping strips
Adhesive strips are avoided only in neonates; in the elderly a strip is applied and left for 24 hours
Adhesive strips are replaced by a pressure bandage wrapped around the arm for at least one hour
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 7, in its list of complications, names skin breakdown from repeated use of adhesive strips, particularly in very young or very elderly patients, and says it can be avoided if sufficient pressure is applied and the puncture site is observed after the procedure. preguntas.pregunta: Why must urine for culture be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or preserved?
opciones: Bacteria multiply in standing urine, raising colony counts and causing false-positive cultures
Bacteria die in standing urine, lowering colony counts and causing false-negative cultures
Leukocytes lyse in standing urine, so the culture would miss the pyuria that defines infection
The pH of standing urine falls, which inhibits the growth of the causative organism on the plate
preguntas.explicacion: The concern is growth, not death: colony-forming units that do not reflect the patient's true bladder urine rise while the specimen waits, which produces false-positive cultures and overtreatment. Studies found counts about 10 % higher after 4 hours at room temperature and more than 135 % higher after 24 hours. Leukocyte lysis is a urinalysis problem, and standing urine becomes more alkaline, not more acidic.

The use of two different anatomic sites for the two sets
The transport time from the bedside to the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's procedure states that the volume of blood collected, not timing, is most critical, and its 2022 overview has the two sets drawn within a few hours of each other by peripheral venipuncture. Rotating the swab in sweeping circles for 10 to 15 seconds in each nostril

Back to front on a female infant, and from the base of the penis upward on a male infant who is uncircumcised
With an antiseptic solution on both, as is done before passing a catheter

preguntas.pregunta: A competent adult refuses a blood draw and the phlebotomist does not proceed. Which ethical principle is being honored?

Beneficence, doing what is in the patient's medical best interest
Justice, distributing resources equitably across patients
Nonmaleficence, avoiding actions known to expose the patient to harm
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights rest on a small set of ethical principles: valuing the patient's dignity, acting with goodwill to preserve life and autonomy, avoiding known harm, and distributing resources fairly. Respect for autonomy is the principle at work when a patient with capacity decides against advice; the clinician should still explain the reasons for the recommendation at the level a reasonable person would need, and document capacity, but the decision belongs to the patient. preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous vancomycin trough is ordered for a patient at steady state. What is the correct collection window?

Within the 30 minutes after the infusion has finished
Within the 2 hours before the next dose is given
Within the 12 hours after the previous dose was given

The onset of a seizure

preguntas.pregunta: Hospital surveillance data show that percutaneous injuries cluster in which two moments of the work?

About 62% happen while the container is being replaced by housekeeping
Nearly all happen during disposal, once the device is inside the container
About one quarter happen during use and the rest while recapping needles
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries do not wait for the sharps container. preguntas.pregunta: Which devices make up the open systems of blood sampling?
opciones: Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to vacuum tubes
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and retractable lancets used on the fingertip
preguntas.explicacion: Open systems are the hypodermic needle with a syringe and the winged steel needle attached to a syringe. Closed systems, which are preferred because they have proved safer, are the ones where the blood goes straight into the tube without being transferred by hand.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.2
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4

preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample shows no visible hemolysis, yet its plasma hemoglobin is just under 0.5 g/L. According to the study by Koseoglu and colleagues, which results can already be clinically altered?
opciones: LDH, AST, potassium and total bilirubin
Albumin, chloride, glucose and total protein
Amylase, alkaline phosphatase and uric acid
Triglycerides, magnesium and HDL-cholesterol
preguntas.explicacion: That study provided evidence of clinically significant differences from visually undetectable to moderate hemolysis for LD and AST, potassium and total bilirubin. Albumin, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, chloride, HDL-cholesterol, CK, glucose, magnesium, total protein, triglycerides, UIBC and uric acid also shifted statistically, but their biases stayed within the conventional CLIA limits, which is why the three distractors are made of those names.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient with no wristband arrives at the draw station. Which pair satisfies the two-identifier requirement?
opciones: The full name the patient states and the telephone number held on file
The full name the patient states and the number of the chair she uses
The assigned identification number, read twice off the requisition form
The full name on the requisition and the tests printed underneath it
preguntas.explicacion: The goal accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and asks for at least two of them whenever specimens are collected for clinical testing. A physical location is expressly excluded, one identifier read twice is still one identifier, and the tests ordered are not among the identifiers the goal names.
preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale and EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · NCMA 2C.1

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum shows a very high hemolysis index and the CRP is rejected; a repeat heel sample two hours later has a low index and a reportable CRP. What does this pattern indicate?
opciones: The first hemolysis was in vitro, produced during a difficult collection, not by disease in the patient
The newborn has intravascular hemolysis that resolved spontaneously between the two collections
The first sample was contaminated by intravenous fluid, which diluted the C-reactive protein
The analyzer's hemolysis index was miscalibrated on the first run and corrected on the second
preguntas.explicacion: In the newborn series, hemolysis indices were far higher than in patients with documented severe intravascular hemolysis, which pointed to in vitro hemolysis from complicated blood collection; every CRP rejected for severe hemolysis became reliable after a repeat sampling. A true in vivo process would not vanish in two hours, and the index is an automated measurement, not the part that failed.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A cyclosporine level is ordered on a transplant patient. Which specimen does the laboratory accept for that test?
opciones: Whole blood collected in EDTA
Serum from a tube without gel
Heparinized plasma kept on ice
Serum separated and frozen at –20 °C
preguntas.explicacion: For cyclosporine monitoring only whole blood in EDTA is accepted. Serum without gel is what the source recommends for drugs such as phenytoin, ice and darkness are the methotrexate rule, and frozen serum is the storage advice for delayed serological testing, so each distractor is a correct instruction for another specimen. Specimen type is the first acceptability criterion a processor checks.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k129 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)

preguntas.pregunta: Blood drawn into a syringe is being transferred into several tubes. Why does the sequence of tubes still matter?
opciones: Additive left on the needle can be carried into the tube filled next
The vacuum of each tube is spent in the sequence printed on its label
The plunger has to be pressed harder for every tube after the first
Serum tubes clot faster whenever they are filled after additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: One route of contamination described for tube collection is anticoagulant sticking to the needle and passing into the next tube, so a transfer from a syringe is not exempt from the sequence. The order published by the WHO is given for vacuum tubes and for syringe and needle alike.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k54 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.F · CCMA 3E6 k132 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who says she has no immigration papers hesitates at the consent form. What does the guidance note here?
opciones: Fear of deportation can make patients hesitate to sign consent forms
Consent from a patient without papers must be witnessed by two staff
A verbal consent will not stand for a patient who declines to sign
The form is set aside and the draw is recorded in the chart as refused
preguntas.explicacion: Among the cultural differences that complicate consent, the text notes that undocumented immigrants might hesitate to sign consent forms out of fear of deportation. Consent is a communication process rather than a signature, the WHO obtains verbal consent for a routine draw, and hesitating over a form is not the same thing as refusing the test.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A 2F k17 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A first heel-prick yields too little blood. The phlebotomist wants to reuse the same lancet on the same spot. What is the rule?
opciones: Do not puncture more than once with the same lancet or reuse a site: it can cause bacterial contamination and infection
A second puncture with the same lancet is acceptable if the site is cleaned again with alcohol and allowed to dry
The same lancet may be reused once on the other heel, since the blade has touched only that patient's skin
Reusing the site is preferred, because a fresh puncture nearby raises the risk of osteomyelitis of the calcaneus
preguntas.explicacion: There are two prohibitions for the lancet: do not puncture the skin more than once with the same lancet, and do not use a single puncture site more than once, because either can lead to bacterial contamination and infection. A surgical blade is also never used for a skin puncture. Osteomyelitis of the heel bone is listed as a complication of capillary sampling, not as a reason to reuse a site.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 one lancet, one puncture · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)

preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old arrives alone for a blood draw her physician ordered. Who normally agrees to the procedure on her behalf?
opciones: A parent or legal guardian, in a process properly called informed permission
The patient herself, since a minor who understands a procedure may agree to it
The ordering physician, who decides for any patient younger than eighteen years
A parent or guardian, unless the phlebotomist judges the patient mature enough
preguntas.explicacion: Children under 18 generally cannot give informed consent; a parent or legal guardian permits the intervention, and that process carries the name informed permission. The exception is the legally emancipated minor, for example one who is married, serving in the military, financially independent, or a mother. Which minors qualify is a matter of state law, not of a bedside judgment about maturity.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Children
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2G · CCMA 7B k216 minors · CMA II.E.3.c exceptions · CMAA 3D k40 consent

preguntas.pregunta: For an adult finger-prick, which fingers are recommended, and which are avoided?
opciones: The middle and ring fingers; the thumb and index have calluses and the little finger has thin tissue
The index and middle fingers; the ring and little fingers are too close to the ulnar nerve branch
The thumb and index finger; the middle and ring fingers have the thinnest tissue over the bone
Any finger except the thumb; the little finger is preferred because it is the least sensitive
preguntas.explicacion: The fingers to puncture are the second and third, meaning the middle and ring fingers, as the ones to puncture. The thumb and index finger are avoided because of calluses, and the little finger because its tissue is thin. The lancet goes on the side of the ball of the finger, perpendicular to the lines of the fingerprint. The finger is the usual capillary site in an adult.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 finger selection · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)

preguntas.pregunta: When is vancomycin usually at steady state, the condition for a valid trough?
opciones: After the third dose
After the first dose
After the fifth dose
After 24 hours of therapy
preguntas.explicacion: Steady state is typically achieved after the third dose of vancomycin, and trough levels are ideally drawn within 30 minutes before a dose under those conditions. The drug's terminal half-life is 4 to 6 hours in adults with normal kidneys and lengthens with renal dysfunction, which is why timing is tied to doses rather than to the clock.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", sections Pharmacokinetics and Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices should a facility replace first when it plans which safety products to bring in?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles that enter a vein or artery
Solid suture needles used in the operating room
Glass capillary tubes used at the patient's side
Lancets used for finger and heel sticks in clinic
preguntas.explicacion: Priorities are set from data: how injuries are happening in that institution, which devices are used there, and what local and national figures say about injury and disease transmission. The highest priority goes to the devices with the greatest impact on preventing occupational infection, and those are the hollow-bore needles used in veins and arteries, the ones that carry blood. The team that makes these decisions is multidisciplinary and includes the workers who use the devices.
preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features, step 2
preguntas.subtema: Setting priorities · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory collects blood cultures into evacuated tubes instead of bottles. Does the septum disinfection step still apply?
opciones: Yes: the rubber septum of the evacuated tubes is disinfected the same way
No: evacuated tubes are supplied sterile and their stoppers need no prep
No: the alcohol used on a stopper interferes with the culture broth
Yes, but sterile saline is used on tubes and alcohol only on bottles
preguntas.explicacion: The step covers the rubber septum on the blood culture bottles or on the evacuated tubes alike, disinfected with 70% isopropyl alcohol, and it comes after the venipuncture site is disinfected and before the first set is drawn. Skipping it on tubes leaves the same route for skin organisms that disinfecting a bottle top is meant to close, and contaminated cultures cost the patient unnecessary antibiotics.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model steps 2 and 3
preguntas.subtema: Bottle preparation · CPT D4 4A k79 blood culture bottle preparation · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: A requisition asks for a CBC (EDTA), a prothrombin time (citrate) and a basic metabolic panel (serum separator tube). Using the WHO order of draw, in what sequence are the three tubes filled?
opciones: Light blue citrate, then the serum separator tube, then purple EDTA
Purple EDTA first, then the serum separator tube, then light blue citrate
Serum separator tube, then light blue citrate, then purple EDTA
Light blue citrate, then purple EDTA, then the serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 numbers the tubes from 1 to 10. The coagulation tube is number 3, the serum separator tube (red-grey tiger or gold) is number 5, and EDTA is number 8, so citrate comes first, the SST second and EDTA last among these three. Step 8 gives the reason for a fixed sequence: it prevents the additive of one tube from contaminating the next.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7

preguntas.pregunta: A benchtop chemistry analyzer just had its lamp and pump, both critical parts, replaced by the service technician. What does CLIA require before patient testing resumes?
opciones: Control material testing, as after a complete reagent change or major maintenance
A full calibration verification with three levels, regardless of the control results
Enrollment of the affected analytes in a new proficiency testing event
Written approval from the state agency, since a critical part changed the test system
preguntas.explicacion: Control materials must be tested before resuming patient testing whenever a complete change of reagents is introduced, major preventive maintenance is performed, or a critical part that may influence performance is replaced. Calibration verification is a separate requirement, also triggered by major maintenance, but the immediate gate to patient testing is acceptable control results, which must be documented.
preguntas.subtema: QC after maintenance or reagent change · CPT D1 1E / k27 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c

preguntas.pregunta: A new clinic laboratory is writing the manual for everything that happens before testing. Which item needs a written policy under the specimen submission and handling standard?
opciones: Specimen acceptability and rejection criteria
Calibration verification of the analyser
Competency assessment of the testing staff
Enrolment in an approved proficiency testing programme
preguntas.explicacion: That standard lists eight written policies where they apply: patient preparation, specimen collection, labeling, storage and preservation, transport conditions, processing, acceptability and rejection, and referral. Calibration verification belongs to the analytic systems, competency assessment to the general laboratory systems, and proficiency testing to its own separate subpart.
preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5D · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: A requisition lists a complete blood count, a lipid panel, a coagulation panel and a troponin. For which of these tests is fasting usually required?
opciones: The lipid panel
The blood count
The clotting panel
The troponin test
preguntas.explicacion: Common tests that usually require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol or lipid panels, and the basic metabolic panel, with liver function tests and the renal function panel sometimes added; a triglycerides test and calcitonin are also listed among tests needing fasting. A CBC, coagulation tests and cardiac enzyme tests such as troponin are described without any preparation, which is why most blood tests need none.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What types of blood tests require fasting; MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, section What are the different types of blood tests
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)

preguntas.pregunta: How must contaminated reusable sharps be stored while they wait for reprocessing?
opciones: So that no employee has to reach into the container by hand to retrieve them
Immersed in a 1:10 bleach dilution for at least 10 minutes in an open pan
In a red bag closed before removal, like other regulated waste
In a labeled container that is emptied by hand only when three-quarters full
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(E) forbids storing or processing contaminated reusable sharps in any way that requires employees to reach by hand into the container holding them, and (d)(2)(viii) requires that container to be puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom and labeled or color-coded. Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4) adds that reusable containers are never opened, emptied or cleaned manually. A red bag is for soft regulated waste, and the 1:10 hypochlorite dilution is WHO's spill disinfectant, not a storage method for sharps.
preguntas.subtema: Reusable sharps · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A site's two external controls for a rapid test have both failed twice. Which source of error listed in the guidance is worth checking first at the bench?
opciones: Whether the caps of the positive and negative control vials were switched and cross-contaminated them
Whether the operator read the cassette before the minimum time printed in the insert had elapsed
Whether the room temperature log shows a reading above the manufacturer's storage limit last night
Whether the positive control was applied to the sample well or to the result window by mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the actions for unexpected control results, the guidance lists checking that controls and reagents were not cross-contaminated by accidentally switching caps, alongside outdated materials, wrong storage and not following the instructions. Swapped caps contaminate both vials, which fits two controls failing together. Reading time and application errors are real operator faults but are not the cap example.
preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Actions for Unexpected QC Results
preguntas.subtema: Sources of QC failure · CPT D1 1F / k28 · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · RMA III.C.3.d

preguntas.pregunta: Under which two federal laws does HHS OCR say HHS-funded programs must provide language access services free of charge?
opciones: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the ACA
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act together with the ADA
HIPAA and the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act (ADAAA)
EMTALA and Title X of the Public Health Service Act (family planning)
preguntas.explicacion: Two federal laws require language access services at no charge in programs receiving HHS funds: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, each with implementing regulations. Title VII and the ADA are anti-discrimination laws cited elsewhere; EMTALA and Title X govern emergencies and minors.
preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Limited English Proficiency (LEP), Your Right to Language Assistance Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 4.11

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's husband telephones the laboratory for her results, saying he will pass them along to her. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Release results only to authorized persons and to those responsible for using them
Release results to any adult of the household once his identity has been confirmed
Release results to him if the patient named him in the notice of privacy practices
Release results to him, because a spouse counts as the patient's personal representative
preguntas.explicacion: Test results go only to authorized persons, meaning individuals authorized under state law to order tests or receive results, plus whoever is responsible for using them and the laboratory that requested the test. The one widening is the patient's own access: on request, a laboratory may give the patient or the patient's personal representative the completed reports it can authenticate as hers.
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7E k220 release of information · NCMA Law and Ethics 3 · CMAA 3C k36

preguntas.pregunta: May an employer use a sign or a placard instead of putting a label on a fixed process container?
opciones: Yes, if it names the containers it covers and is available each shift
Yes, if the container is emptied and refilled at least once a week
No, every container of a hazardous chemical must carry its own label
No, unless the safety data sheet is posted beside the container
preguntas.explicacion: For individual stationary process containers the employer may use signs, placards, process sheets, batch tickets, operating procedures or similar written materials instead of affixing a label. Two conditions come with it: the alternative has to identify which containers it applies to and carry the same information a workplace label would, and the written material has to be readily accessible to the employees in their work area throughout each work shift.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(7), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Signs instead of labels · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: Parents ask about the small hard lumps that appeared on their infant's heel after several heel sticks. What are they?
opciones: They are calcified nodules that usually disappear by 30 months of age
They are calcified nodules that usually need surgical removal after 1 year
They are scars, which form only after a single deep puncture into the heel
They are haematomas that persist because infants lack clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Calcified nodules are a risk of capillary sampling that sometimes occurs in infants and usually disappears by 30 months of age. The other risks are excessive bleeding, fainting, a slight risk of infection whenever skin is broken, scarring when there have been multiple punctures in the same area, and damage to blood cells that may require a repeat from a vein.
preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Capillary sample, Risks
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k74 post-procedural complications · PBT II.I complications · RMA III.C.4.a.ii capillary stick

preguntas.pregunta: Before a venipuncture on a 6-week-old, the tray holds chlorhexidine and alcohol. Which is ruled out at this age?
opciones: Chlorhexidine, which is not to be used on children under 2 months of age
Alcohol, which is not to be used on children under 2 months of age
Both, since the WHO requires povidone iodine for all neonatal skin antisepsis
Neither, since antisepsis is optional in neonates as in glucose testing
preguntas.explicacion: Paediatric venepuncture follows standard skin antisepsis with one addition: chlorhexidine is not used on children under 2 months of age. For capillary punctures in children povidone iodine is ruled out and alcohol is allowed to air dry. The optional alcohol swab applies to glucometer fingersticks, not to neonatal venepuncture.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Drawing blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B pediatric collection, D3 3G antiseptic · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E5 prepare site

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory proposes to keep reporting potassium on hemolysed samples by applying a correction formula based on the hemolysis index. What did the follow-up study on this idea conclude?
opciones: Corrective formulas are unreliable and misleading, because cell contents are not released uniformly
Corrective formulas are reliable for potassium and LDH but not for AST and total bilirubin
Corrective formulas work only when the hemolysis is visually undetectable, below 0.5 g/L
Corrective formulas are acceptable if the corrected result is flagged as an estimate in the report
preguntas.explicacion: Following the study that graded hemolysis, Lippi and colleagues showed that formulas meant to adjust results for the degree of hemolysis are unreliable and potentially misleading, because the mechanical injury of blood cells and the release of their contents into serum or plasma do not happen homogeneously. The answer to a hemolysed potassium is a new sample, not an arithmetic correction, flagged or not.
preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist keeps a water bottle at the draw station and applies lip balm between patients. Which rule applies?
opciones: Eating, drinking and applying lip balm are all prohibited where exposure is reasonably likely
Drinking is allowed from a closed container, but cosmetics and lip balm are prohibited
Both are allowed if the counter is decontaminated with disinfectant at the end of the shift
Both are allowed as long as the water is not stored in a refrigerator with specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(ix) prohibits eating, drinking, smoking, applying cosmetics or lip balm, and handling contact lenses in work areas where there is a reasonable likelihood of occupational exposure. A closed bottle is not an exception the standard grants. End-of-shift decontamination in (d)(4)(ii)(A) is a housekeeping duty and does not license eating at the bench, and (d)(2)(x), which keeps food and drink out of refrigerators and countertops holding blood, is a second, separate prohibition.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ix) and (d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Work practice controls at the bench · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1

preguntas.pregunta: Ninety seconds have passed with the tourniquet on and the phlebotomist still cannot find a vein. What should happen next?
opciones: Release the band before two minutes and look again with a vein illuminator
Keep the band on until a vein appears, then draw all the tubes without pause
Tighten the band further until the radial pulse disappears at the wrist
Release the band and draw from the peripheral access line already in place
preguntas.explicacion: One guideline asks for the band to come off within a minute of placement and another sets the ceiling at two minutes, so at ninety seconds it is released. Illumination devices are recommended in place of a long application for veins that are hard to see, especially when two or more tubes are due.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Preparation and Technique or Treatment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time · CPT D3 3E k60 k67 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11

preguntas.pregunta: A 30 kg child is scheduled for an oral glucose tolerance test. How much glucose should the child receive?
opciones: 52.5 g, from 1.75 g per kilogram
75 g, the standard adult load
30 g, one gram per kilogram
100 g, the load used in pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: Children receive 1.75 g of glucose per kilogram of body weight, up to a maximum of 75 g; for 30 kg that is 30 × 1.75 = 52.5 g. The cap is the part candidates forget: a 50 kg child would compute to 87.5 g but receives 75 g, which is also the adult load. The 100 g drink belongs to the 3-hour test used after a positive gestational screen, never to a child's OGTT.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: OGTT pediatric load · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E k139

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory forwards a specialised assay to a distant laboratory and passes the result on to the ordering physician. What else must the referring laboratory tell that physician?
opciones: The name and address of the laboratory that actually performed the test
The reason the assay could not be performed on its own premises
The date on which the specimen was dispatched to the other laboratory
The name of the courier service that carried the specimen there

preguntas.pregunta: When does the serum peak concentration of intravenous vancomycin occur?
opciones: Immediately after the infusion is completed
Within the 30 minutes before the next dose
Four to six hours after the infusion, one half-life later
At steady state, after the third dose has run
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset with a serum peak concentration immediately following completion of the intravenous infusion. So the tourniquet can be anchored on the rest instead of the arm
So the tray of tubes can be balanced within the patient's reach
So the arm stays below heart level throughout the whole procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is expected to be comfortable for both people, with the armrests set to a convenient position that also allows appropriate action if the patient has a vasovagal episode. preguntas.pregunta: A nurse hands you povidone iodine to prepare a 2-year-old's finger for a capillary puncture. What is the correct action?
opciones: Do not use povidone iodine for capillary punctures in children; apply alcohol and let it air dry
Use povidone iodine, since alcohol is not effective against skin flora on a child's finger
Use povidone iodine only on the heel; on the finger either antiseptic is acceptable
Use chlorhexidine instead, which the WHO prefers over alcohol for children under 2 months
preguntas.explicacion: Povidone iodine is not used for a capillary skin puncture in paediatric and neonatal patients; alcohol is used instead, as in adults, applied to the entry site and allowed to air dry. preguntas.pregunta: According to paragraph (d)(2)(i) of the standard, when is personal protective equipment required?

Instead of engineering controls, when the employer documents that safer devices cost more
Only when an exposure incident has already occurred and follow-up is under way
Before engineering controls are considered, as the first line of protection
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(i) sets the order: engineering and work practice controls are used to eliminate or minimize exposure, and where exposure remains after those controls, PPE is used as well. OSHA's Evaluating and Controlling Exposure page reads this to mean that if an effective, clinically appropriate control such as a safety-engineered sharp exists, the employer must evaluate and implement it; cost is not an exemption in the text. PPE is preventive, not something that starts after an incident.

Temperature, lighting, noise level and the number of operators per shift

Water quality, air exchanges per hour, and the distance to the nearest sink

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices account for most of the percutaneous injuries hospitals report to national surveillance?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles, above all hypodermic and winged-steel needles
Suture needles, followed by the scalpel blades used in minor surgery
Glass items, above all broken capillary tubes and specimen slides
Retractable lancets used for the finger and heel sticks of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Of nearly 5,000 percutaneous injuries reported over four years of surveillance, 62 percent involved hollow-bore needles: hypodermic needles on disposable syringes accounted for 29 percent and winged-steel needles for 13 percent. Glass followed at 17 percent and suture needles at 15 percent, and phlebotomy needles themselves for 4 percent. Hollow-bore needles matter most because they carry a measurable volume of blood, which is why devices used to enter a vein or an artery get the highest priority for replacement with safer ones.

preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The civil tiers rise with culpability: a violation the person did not know about, a violation due to reasonable cause rather than willful neglect, willful neglect corrected within the required period, and willful neglect not corrected, which carries the top per-violation penalty and the highest annual cap. Criminal penalties are separate and escalate from knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, to doing so under false pretenses, to doing so for commercial advantage, personal gain or malicious harm. The Office for Civil Rights enforces the civil side.

preguntas.pregunta: Which veins join to form the brachial vein, and is the brachial vein superficial or deep?
opciones: The radial and ulnar veins; it is a deep vein
The cephalic and basilic veins; it is superficial
The median cubital and cephalic veins; it is superficial
The axillary and subclavian veins; it is a deep vein
preguntas.explicacion: The radial and ulnar veins parallel the forearm bones and join to form the brachial vein, a deep vein that flows into the axillary vein; the deep veins run in pairs around the arteries as venae comitantes and merge into the brachial vein at the cubital fossa. The cephalic and basilic are the superficial veins, and the axillary and subclavian lie downstream of the brachial.

preguntas.pregunta: In a spun hematocrit tube, what makes up the thin pale layer between the packed red cells and the plasma?
opciones: Leukocytes and platelets, normally under 1 percent of the sample
Reticulocytes, normally 1 to 2 percent of the red cell count
Plasma proteins, roughly 7 percent of the plasma volume
Fibrin strands with trapped platelets from a forming clot
preguntas.explicacion: That pale band is the buffy coat. It holds the formed elements that are not red cells, the white cells and the platelets, and normally amounts to less than 1 percent of the sample. Reticulocytes are immature red cells, not a separate layer; the plasma proteins are dissolved in the plasma above; and fibrin only appears if the sample has been allowed to clot, which an anticoagulated hematocrit tube has not.

A self re-sheathing syringe with a sleeve over the needle

preguntas.pregunta: When is RhoGAM (Rh immune globulin) normally given to an Rh negative pregnant patient?
opciones: In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 3 hours after the birth
In weeks 12 to 14 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
Only within 72 hours after the birth of a second Rh positive baby
preguntas.explicacion: RhoGAM temporarily prevents the Rh negative parent from forming anti-Rh antibodies by destroying any fetal Rh positive cells that cross the placenta, and it is normally given during weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours of birth. preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist who has never had chickenpox or the vaccine is assigned to a patient with varicella on Airborne Precautions. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Restrict her from the room if immune personnel are available to do the draw
Let her draw with an N95, since the respirator makes immunity irrelevant
Let her draw with a surgical mask, since varicella spreads by droplets
Restrict her permanently from all patients on Transmission-Based Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Airborne Precautions recommendations restrict susceptible healthcare personnel from entering the rooms of patients known or suspected to have measles, chickenpox, disseminated zoster or smallpox when other, immune personnel are available, and they call for immunizing susceptible persons as soon as possible after an unprotected contact with a vaccine-preventable infection. The respirator is required for those who do enter, but it does not remove the preference for immune staff. Varicella is on the airborne list, not the droplet list, and the restriction is patient-specific, not permanent.

preguntas.pregunta: How often should hand hygiene be performed when two different samples are collected from the same patient?

Once before the first procedure and once after the last one
Only after the second procedure, when the gloves come off
Only if the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath

Applying the tourniquet early on
Dimming the room lighting
Offering a sugary drink first

The finger-prick must never exceed 1.5 mm, and most lancets are longer than that

preguntas.pregunta: Which two terms did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act add to the definitions in the bloodborne pathogens standard?

preguntas.pregunta: A doorknob contaminated by an infected person's hands is an example of which element of disease transmission?
opciones: A fomite, in indirect contact transmission
A vehicle, like contaminated food or water
A mechanical vector, like a fly carrying bacteria
A droplet nucleus, the residue of an evaporated droplet
preguntas.explicacion: Indirect contact transmission works through fomites, inanimate objects that pick up pathogens from an infected person or reservoir and pass them to a new host who touches them and then a portal of entry; doorknobs, towels and tablecloths are the everyday examples, and improperly sterilized syringes, needles and catheters are the clinical ones behind many healthcare-associated infections. opciones: Symptomatic anaemia, which calls for a fuller evaluation
A normal recovery, since pallor lingers after every faint
A seizure rather than a faint, as the tongue was not bitten
Hemoconcentration from the tourniquet used during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: After a simple vasovagal event the examination should be entirely normal. Pallor that carries on suggests symptomatic anaemia and, like a bitten tongue or an atypical story, prompts a search for another cause rather than a comfortable label.

preguntas.pregunta: A donor has healed needle scars along both forearms. What does the skin examination require?
opciones: Deferral: arms must be free of scars indicative of injected drugs of abuse
Deferral only if the puncture marks are still fresh and inflamed today
Collection from another site, such as a hand vein, and documentation
Collection as usual, since scars do not affect the sterility of the unit
preguntas.explicacion: The skin examination has two parts. The site chosen for the draw has to be clear of infection, of inflammation and of lesions, and the arms and forearms must show no punctures or scars that point to injected drugs of abuse. The second half is not about the sterility of the unit but about the donor's own risk of a transfusion-transmitted infection, so moving to another site does not answer it.
