preguntas.pregunta: OGTT samples will wait more than an hour before they can be separated from the cells. Which tube should they be collected in?
opciones: Grey top with sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate
Light blue top with sodium citrate, filled completely
Green top with lithium heparin and a gel separator
Lavender top with EDTA, inverted eight to ten times
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma should be separated from cells within 60 minutes (serum within 90) unless the tube carries a glycolysis inhibitor. Sodium fluoride inhibits enolase at 2.5 mg of fluoride per mL of blood and is paired with potassium oxalate as the anticoagulant; glucose then stays stable for 72 hours at room temperature. That is the grey fluoride/oxalate tube, last in the order of draw and requiring a full draw. Heparinized plasma reads about 5% lower than serum.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3

preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: When using, disclosing or requesting PHI, a covered entity must make reasonable efforts to limit it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) lists the exceptions: disclosures to or requests by a health care provider for treatment, uses and disclosures to the individual, those made under an authorization, disclosures to the Secretary for compliance, and uses required by law or for compliance with the rule. Payment, operations and research disclosures all remain subject to the minimum necessary limit.
preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary

preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) allows a covered entity to disclose PHI to a business associate, and to let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if the entity obtains satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must obtain the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the haematology specimen collected first in a skin puncture?
opciones: To minimize the effects of platelet clumping
To prevent carry-over of the citrate additive
To use the first drop before it is contaminated
To keep tissue fluid out of the chemistry tube
preguntas.explicacion: In skin punctures the haematology specimen is collected first, then chemistry, then blood bank, and that this order is essential to minimize the effects of platelet clumping. Additive carry-over is the reason given for the venous order of draw, which the capillary order reverses. The first drop is wiped away in every case because it may carry tissue fluid or debris.

It sits on the published list of factors that increase clot formation

It sits on the published list of factors that reduce tube vacuum

preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA tube for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate sat in a rack for four hours before the test was set up. What effect is expected?
opciones: A falsely low ESR, because delayed red cells lose their biconcave shape; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely high ESR, because delayed red cells aggregate faster; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely low ESR, because the anticoagulant loses activity; testing should start within 4 hours
A falsely high ESR, because plasma viscosity falls on standing; testing should start within 6 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Delays in processing make red cells lose their biconcave shape, which reduces the ESR, so the test should be started within 2 hours of collection; clotted blood also lowers it by disturbing rouleaux formation. The factors that raise the value are different: a warm room, direct sunlight, tube tilt (3° from vertical can add up to 30 %), vibration, and air bubbles from an under-filled tube.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors

preguntas.pregunta: Which form of syncope is the most common, and which of its triggers matter in a phlebotomy setting?
opciones: Vasovagal syncope, triggered among other things by pain or emotional upset, with bradycardia and hypotension
Carotid sinus syncope, triggered by pressure on the neck, with tachycardia and high blood pressure
Situational syncope, triggered by coughing or urination, with normal heart rate and pressure
Cardiac syncope, triggered by exertion, with ventricular tachycardia and pallor
preguntas.explicacion: The vasovagal episode is the most common form of reflex syncope and may be triggered by pain or emotional upset, though often no trigger is found; it accounts for nearly half of all cases, with severe pain and stress among its situations, leading to vasodilation and bradycardia. During the event the patient is typically bradycardic, hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic.

The diagnosis code and the name of the insurance carrier that covers the requested test
The room number and the bed number where the specimen was collected

preguntas.pregunta: Which structure lies beneath the median cubital vein and protects it, helping to prevent haematoma formation?

The medial cutaneous nerve
The brachial artery
The dorsal venous arch

preguntas.pregunta: Which item meets the standard's definition of a contaminated sharp?
opciones: A broken capillary tube with dried blood on it
A sealed tube of blood in a transport rack
A dressing soaked with liquid blood that would drip if squeezed
An unused lancet still in its sterile package
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines contaminated sharps as any contaminated object able to penetrate the skin, and lists needles, scalpels, broken glass, broken capillary tubes and exposed ends of dental wires. Two things are needed: the object can pierce skin, and blood or OPIM is present or reasonably anticipated on it. A sealed tube does not penetrate skin; a dripping gauze pad is regulated waste of the liquid kind, not a sharp; and an unused lancet can pierce but is not contaminated, so it is not yet a contaminated sharp.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Contaminated, Contaminated Sharps, Regulated Waste

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these events meets OSHA's definition of an "exposure incident"?
opciones: Blood splashes into a technician's eye while a tube is being uncapped
A drop of blood lands on the intact skin of a gloved hand
A technician is assigned to a job where contact with blood is reasonably anticipated
A contaminated needle is found in a regulated waste bag, without any parenteral contact
preguntas.explicacion: The definition names the routes that count: the eye, the mouth or another mucous membrane, skin that is not intact, or a parenteral route such as a needlestick, with the contact coming from the employee's duties. A splash to the eye is mucous-membrane contact and qualifies. Intact gloved skin is not a listed route. A job where contact is reasonably anticipated is Occupational Exposure, the neighbouring definition, not an incident. A contaminated needle in a waste bag is regulated waste in the wrong container, but without parenteral contact there is no exposure incident. The label matters because reporting an exposure incident is what obliges the employer to make the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up available at once.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Exposure Incident; and (f)(3), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up

preguntas.pregunta: How is pressure maintained on the site after the needle is removed?
opciones: Gauze pressed over the site as the needle comes out, then taped in place, or a bandaid applied over it
The patient bends the elbow over the gauze, which keeps pressure on the vein without tape
An ice pack wrapped in a towel is held on the site for 15 minutes to prevent a hematoma
The tourniquet is reapplied loosely over the gauze for one minute to compress the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, clean gauze is used to apply pressure as the needle is swiftly removed, pressure is continued, and the gauze is taped in place to provide continuous pressure against a hematoma; alternatively a bandaid goes over the gauze. Bending the arm is what the WHO forbids, and ice is first aid for a bruise that has already formed.

preguntas.pregunta: A Muslim woman asks for a female phlebotomist. What is the culturally competent response?

Explain that staff assignments cannot be changed for religious reasons alone
Proceed with the male phlebotomist if her husband gives his agreement
Ask her to sign a waiver acknowledging the delay before rescheduling

preguntas.pregunta: During check-in a patient admits to having eaten a pastry two hours before a fasting glucose. What is the correct action?
opciones: Report it to the provider; the test may need to be rescheduled for a day when the patient can fast
Draw the sample anyway and write the time of the pastry on the tube so the laboratory can adjust the result
Have the patient wait in the lobby for six more hours and then draw, since 8 hours will have passed by then
Draw the sample and order a random glucose instead, since the two tests share the same normal value
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient eats or drinks anything other than water during the fast, the instruction is to tell the provider, who may reschedule the test for another time when the patient can fast, because nutrients absorbed from food change the levels of substances in the blood and an inaccurate result gives an inaccurate picture of health. Fasting and random glucose have different normal values, and no note on the tube converts one into the other.

Between 30 and 45 degrees

Dried, at or below room temperature, for no longer than twelve hours
In viral transport medium at 2 to 8 °C, for as long as seventy-two hours

preguntas.pregunta: Which fuels define a Class B fire?
opciones: Flammable liquids and gases, such as organic solvents
Ordinary combustibles that leave ash, such as paper
Combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings
Energized electrical equipment such as a centrifuge motor
preguntas.explicacion: Class A fires involve ordinary combustibles, fuels that burn and leave ash, and Class B flammable liquids and gases; many organic solvents and compressed gases in a laboratory are Class B hazards. Combustible metals are Class D, handled with a specialized dry powder extinguisher, and 29 CFR 1910.157 treats electrical equipment as Class C, distributing those units by the pattern of the A or B hazards present. The most common laboratory extinguishers are dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide.

preguntas.pregunta: A whole-blood sample is spun in a centrifuge. Which component settles at the very bottom of the tube?
opciones: The erythrocytes, the heaviest formed elements
The buffy coat of leukocytes and platelets
The straw-colored plasma, over half the sample
The serum, once the clotting factors are gone
preguntas.explicacion: In a spun sample the heaviest formed elements, the red cells, pack at the bottom; above them sits a thin pale layer of white cells and platelets, the buffy coat; and the plasma, a pale straw-colored liquid, floats on top as the lightest component and makes up more than half of the sample. Serum is not a layer of whole blood: it is plasma minus its clotting factors, obtained only after the blood has clotted.

preguntas.pregunta: A stat laboratory measured its errors the same way in 1996 and again in 2006. What did the comparison show?

The error rate fell by about a third, and the analytical share grew to a half
The error rate held steady, while the preanalytical share fell to under a third

preguntas.pregunta: A NICU infant had its first screening card collected at 12 hours of age. What is recommended?
opciones: Re-screen seven days after admission, since the first was taken before 24 hours
Re-screen at 6 months of age, when premature enzyme systems have matured enough
No repeat is needed, since NICU laboratories run more sensitive assays on preterm blood
Repeat only if the infant is on total parenteral nutrition

It can take up to 3 days, and any organism at all that grows in the dish is a sign of infection

preguntas.pregunta: A vancomycin trough is ordered and the next dose is due at 10:00. When should it be drawn?
opciones: Within the 30 minutes before the 10:00 dose, at steady state
Immediately after the 10:00 infusion has finished running
Exactly 2 hours after the 10:00 dose has started
At any point between doses, as long as the time is recorded on the tube
preguntas.explicacion: A serum trough is ideally obtained within 30 minutes before a dose is given, under steady-state conditions, which are typically reached after the third dose; the usual target trough is 10 to 20 μg/mL. The peak, by contrast, occurs immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed. A random time between doses is neither.

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse applied povidone-iodine to the perianal area shortly before a guaiac stool card was prepared. What can this cause?
opciones: A false-positive result, since iodine oxidizes the guaiac reagent
A false-negative result, since iodine is a reducing agent like vitamin C
An invalid card, since iodine prevents the developer from wetting the paper
An unchanged result, since antiseptics interfere only with immunochemical kits
preguntas.explicacion: Iodine oxidizes the guaiac compound directly, and as little as 0.005 mL of a 1:1000 dilution of povidone-iodine has produced a false positive in vitro; the antiseptic should not be applied to the perianal area, or to the urinary tract during catheterization, before the test. Chlorine-generating toilet sanitizers also give false positives with guaiac, whereas non-chlorine sanitizers lower the sensitivity of immunochemical kits.

preguntas.pregunta: Which aid is called particularly useful for people with hearing loss who do not use sign language?
opciones: Real-time captioning, also known as computer-assisted real-time transcription
A tactile interpreter, working alongside a support service provider
A qualified reader supplying an audio recording of printed material
A videophone connected to the free video relay service for signers
preguntas.explicacion: Real-time captioning, known as computer-assisted real-time transcription, has a transcriber type what is being said into a computer that projects the words onto a screen, on-site or remotely, and is described as particularly useful for people who are deaf or have hearing loss but do not use sign language. Qualified readers and audio recordings serve people with vision loss.

preguntas.pregunta: Who may perform the post-exposure evaluation the bloodborne pathogens standard requires?
opciones: A licensed professional whose scope of practice covers vaccination and follow-up
Only a physician licensed in the state where the exposure incident happened
The employer's safety officer, who then signs the written opinion for the file
Any registered nurse in the facility, working under the employer's supervision
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) create the term licensed healthcare professional for exactly this: someone whose legally permitted scope of practice lets them independently carry out what paragraph (f) requires, the hepatitis B vaccination and the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. Paragraph (f)(1)(ii)(C) says the work is done by or under the supervision of a licensed physician or of another such professional, so it is not limited to physicians, and it is not something a safety officer or an employer may supervise.

preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen is collected an hour after a contrast-enhanced scan from a patient who jogged to the appointment. Which two readings should be treated with caution?
opciones: Specific gravity, raised by the contrast, and the electrolytes, moved by exercise
Nitrite, raised by the contrast, and the pH, moved by the exercise beforehand
Bilirubin, raised by the contrast, and the ketones, moved by the exercise
Protein, raised by the contrast, and the specific gravity, moved by exercise
preguntas.explicacion: Contrast agents can produce a false-positive specific gravity, and exercise can alter both the specific gravity and the electrolyte concentration of the sample. Neither is a laboratory fault, which is why the collection history matters: an alkaline pH can also read as protein, and bacterial growth in a sample left standing can produce a false-positive blood reaction and shift the pH.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c

preguntas.pregunta: Which religious group refuses blood transfusions and blood products?
opciones: Jehovah's Witnesses
Orthodox Christians
Baha'i believers
Seventh-day Adventists
preguntas.explicacion: Jehovah's Witnesses refuse blood transfusion and blood products, while whether to prolong life is an individual choice. The entries for the Baha'i faith, Buddhism and the Eastern Orthodox church each state that transfusion is acceptable or allowed. Knowing these positions is what lets a phlebotomist respond without judgment.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", section Jehovah's Witness (Health)

preguntas.pregunta: A chemical carries two hazards: one warrants the signal word Danger and the other Warning. What appears on the label?
opciones: Only Danger, since one signal word appears and it is the more severe
Both words, each next to its own hazard statement
Only the word Warning, since the less severe word applies to the mixture as a whole
Neither; when hazards conflict the label shows pictograms only
preguntas.explicacion: There are only two signal words. Within a hazard class, Danger marks the more severe hazards and Warning the less severe ones, and a label carries a single signal word no matter how many hazards the chemical has; when one hazard calls for Danger and another for Warning, only Danger appears. The hazard statements, by contrast, are all included, and may be combined to improve readability. Pictograms never replace the signal word; they are a separate required element.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Signal Words and Hazard Statements

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must the patient write on a 24-hour urine container when the collection is finished?
opciones: Name, the date, and the time the collection was completed
Name, the date, and the time the first void was discarded
Name, date of birth and the volume of each individual void
Name, the test ordered and the preservative that was added
preguntas.explicacion: The patient labels the container with his or her name, the date and the time of completion, and returns it as instructed. The completion time is what defines the end of the timed period; the volume of each void is never recorded separately, because the laboratory measures the total volume of the pooled urine, and any preservative is added and labeled with a hazard symbol by the laboratory, not by the patient.

preguntas.pregunta: A specimen is going out as a Category B infectious substance. How must the package be built?
opciones: As a triple packaging: a primary receptacle, a secondary packaging and a rigid outer box
As a double packaging: a leakproof primary receptacle and a rigid outer box with a liner
As a triple packaging whose outer layer may be a padded envelope for small volumes
As a triple packaging in which only the outer box has to resist punctures and leaks
preguntas.explicacion: Category B substances travel in a triple packaging: primary receptacle, secondary packaging and a rigid outer packaging. The primary receptacles must sit inside the secondary so that they cannot break, be punctured or leak into it under normal transport, and the secondary is secured in the outer packaging with cushioning. At least one outer surface measures 100 mm by 100 mm or more.

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of any blood-drawing procedure is described as the most important, and when is it done?
opciones: Planning ahead, usually at the start of the session
Planning ahead, usually once the patient is seated
Site selection, usually at the start of the session
Site selection, usually once the tourniquet is on
preguntas.explicacion: Planning ahead is called the most important part of carrying out any procedure, and it is normally done at the start of a phlebotomy session rather than patient by patient. It sits alongside a suitable location, quality control and the standards of care set for patients and staff.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.1

preguntas.pregunta: Which area of skin loses sensation when the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is injured?
opciones: The medial forearm and the skin over the olecranon, stopping at the wrist
The medial forearm and the medial half of the palm, including two fingers
The lateral forearm and the skin over the thumb, stopping at the wrist
The whole forearm and the back of the hand as far as the finger tips
preguntas.explicacion: The nerve supplies the skin of the medial forearm together with the skin overlying the olecranon, and none of the forearm cutaneous nerves cross the wrist, so the hand is spared. Damage during a venipuncture has produced painful paraesthesias, dysaesthesias and numbness in that territory.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", sections Introduction and Clinical Significance

preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen is drawn at 08:00 and reaches the analyser at 11:30. Why may the result be reported lower than it should be?
opciones: Testing should begin within two hours; standing changes the red cell shape
Testing should begin within twelve hours; standing dilutes the citrate added
Testing should begin within thirty minutes; standing lets the plasma evaporate
Testing should begin within twenty-four hours; standing warms the specimen up
preguntas.explicacion: Timely handling matters for this test: it should be started within two hours of collection, because red cells that stand too long lose their biconcave shape and stack less readily, which lowers the reading. Anisocytosis and poikilocytosis interfere with stacking in the same direction.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6

preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, what happens right after the broken glass has been removed with tongs?
opciones: Absorb the fluid with paper towels, wipe with detergent, then apply hypochlorite
Apply hypochlorite directly to the wet blood, then wipe with paper towels
Rinse the area with running water, then discard the towels in regular waste
Remove gloves and wash hands, then record the incident before cleaning further
preguntas.explicacion: The sequence is fixed: wear non-sterile gloves; sweep up the glass with tongs or a pan and brush, never with the hands, and put it in a sharps container or, if too large, wrapped in paper in a separate container; absorb as much fluid as possible with disposable paper towels; wipe with water and detergent until visibly clean; saturate with 0.5 percent hypochlorite; rinse the tongs, brush and pan under running water; remove gloves; wash hands with soap and water and dry with single-use towels; and record the incident if a specimen was lost or anyone was exposed.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex F, Blood spillage
preguntas.subtema: Spill cleanup sequence · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.6.b · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.9

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of details does the WHO describe as the information typically required on a specimen label?
opciones: First and last names, file number, date of birth, and the date and time of collection
First and last names, date of birth, ordering physician and the working diagnosis
First and last names, home address, social security number and time of collection
First and last names, file number, name of the test ordered and the phlebotomist's initials
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 says the label must be clearly written with what the laboratory requires, which is typically the patient's first and last names, file number, date of birth, and the date and time the blood was taken; the labels and forms are rechecked before dispatch. Address or social security number are extra identifiers for confirming who the patient is, not as the label content the WHO lists.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure

preguntas.pregunta: The tubes are filled and the patient is still in the chair. What is the first of the closing steps?
opciones: Discard the used device into the sharps container
Write the labels for the tubes that have been drawn
Perform hand hygiene once more, ahead of every other step
Place the tubes into the leak-proof transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: The step that closes the procedure opens with discarding the used needle and syringe or sampling device into a puncture-resistant sharps container. Only then come the label and form check, the sorting of other waste, hand hygiene again, and a last look at the labels before dispatch.
preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the guidance describe informal caregivers as 'hidden patients'?
opciones: They carry a higher risk of health problems, poor sleep and burnout
They are billed at the same rate as the patient they bring to clinic
They are recorded in the chart as a second patient at every visit
They may consent on the patient's behalf without any paperwork
preguntas.explicacion: Family caregivers face emotional, financial and physical demands, often giving medications, injections and other treatments on top of their own jobs and families. They tend to carry a higher risk of physical and mental health problems, sleep trouble and chronic conditions, so they are viewed as hidden patients, with staff alert for illness, stress and burnout.
preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Consider caregivers as "hidden patients"

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following counts as "regulated waste" under the OSHA standard?
opciones: Gauze caked with dried blood that could release it while being handled
A pair of exam gloves worn for a draw, with no blood on them at all
An alcohol swab used to clean the skin before the needle, with no blood on it
A gauze pad with one dry spot of blood that cannot be released during handling
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers five things: blood or OPIM (other potentially infectious materials) that is liquid or semi-liquid; items that would release it in that state if squeezed; items caked with dried blood or OPIM that could shed it while being handled; contaminated sharps; and pathological or microbiological waste containing blood or OPIM. The caked gauze is the third case. Gloves and a swab with no blood on them would release nothing if squeezed and are not caked, and a pad with one dry spot that cannot release anything fails the same test: the definition asks for dried blood that is caked AND capable of coming off during handling.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Sharps containers and regulated waste · CPT D1 k30 k32 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

preguntas.pregunta: A review of consent forms measured how often all four required elements were documented. What share was found?
opciones: 26.4% of the forms
46.4% of the forms
76.4% of the forms
96.4% of the forms
preguntas.explicacion: Bottrell and colleagues found the four required elements, the nature of the procedure and its risks, benefits and alternatives, documented on consent forms only 26.4% of the time. Thin documentation is what leaves the team exposed when a patient later claims they were never fully informed about what was done.
preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Inadequate Documentation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7

preguntas.pregunta: A centrifuge with blood inside its rotor chamber cannot be fully decontaminated before the repair technician arrives. What does the standard require?
opciones: A readily observable label saying which parts remain contaminated, and telling the technician
Sending the centrifuge for service in a red bag, which replaces the label
Decontaminating it anyway, since the standard allows no exceptions for equipment
Recording the contamination in the sharps injury log before the technician touches it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiv) requires equipment that may be contaminated to be examined and decontaminated before servicing or shipping unless the employer can show that is not feasible; in that case (d)(2)(xiv)(A) demands a readily observable label per (g)(1)(i)(H) stating which portions remain contaminated, and (d)(2)(xiv)(B) requires that information to reach affected employees, the servicing representative or the manufacturer before handling. A red bag substitutes for a label on waste, not on equipment, and the sharps injury log records percutaneous injuries only.
preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiv) and (g)(1)(i)(H), contaminated equipment
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated equipment for servicing · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8

cuerpo: The NHA Certified Phlebotomy Technician exam has **120 questions: 100 are scored and 20 are unscored pretest items**. You get **2 hours**. That is one minute per question with no slack, so the exam rewards knowing the material cold rather than reasoning each item out from scratch.

**A new version of the exam went live on January 7, 2026.** It comes from a job analysis NHA completed in 2024, and NHA's own announcement described the change as having minimal impact on topics and content areas. Study materials written for the previous test plan are not wrong, but they were not built to its weights.

The test plan groups everything into **five domains**: Safety and Compliance, Patient Preparation, Routine Blood Collections, Special Collections, and Processing. It also lists a block of **Core Knowledge** (anatomy of the circulatory system, medical terminology, and the like) that is not a domain of its own: those facts show up inside whichever domain applies them.
guia.fuente: NHA Certified Phlebotomy Technician (CPT) Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis

cuerpo: NHA does not grade the CPT as a percentage. Every NHA exam is reported on a **scaled score, and the passing score is 390 out of 500**. NHA publishes that number in its annual pass-rate report, and it does not publish how many correct answers map to 390, because that depends on the difficulty of the particular set of questions you get.

For the same reason, this app cannot tell you "you would have passed". What it can do is hold you to a study target: the practice tests here use **70 % as the bar**, and the guide says so on every result screen. If you clear 70 % consistently on tests that follow the official split, you are studying at the level the exam expects.

In 2024, NHA administered **57,457 CPT exams and 75.96 % of candidates passed**. Roughly one in four did not. The domains where that quarter loses points are the ones with a single right answer: order of draw, tube additives, tourniquet time, needle angle.
guia.fuente: NHA, Pass Rates for NHA Examinations Administered in 2024 (revised 1/8/25); NHA CPT Test Plan

cuerpo: These are the areas of the official outline and how many scored questions each one gets in a 100-question practice test in this app:

**Safety and Compliance: 26 of 100** (26 %) · **Patient Preparation: 20 of 100** (20 %) · **Routine Blood Collections: 28 of 100** (28 %) · **Special Collections: 12 of 100** (12 %) · **Processing: 14 of 100** (14 %).

Every practice test here draws **exactly that many questions from each area**, so it **matches the official content outline**. A practice test that pulls at random from the whole bank does not follow the outline at all, and it hides the areas where you are weak by burying them in the ones where you are strong. The diagnostic uses the same proportions, which is why its result by area tells you something.
guia.fuente: NHA CPT Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis (exam in effect since January 7, 2026)

cuerpo: NHA released updated CPT study materials on October 8, 2025, and the **new certification exam on January 7, 2026**. Anyone testing after that date sits the new version; there is no choice between old and new.

The five domains and their weights in this app are the ones in the 2024-job-analysis test plan, which is the plan for the January 2026 exam. If you are using a book or a course written before 2025, compare its table of contents with the areas listed here; the names and the emphasis are what changed.
guia.fuente: NHA News Center, New CPT Certification Exam & Study Materials Available; NHA CPT Test Plan

cuerpo: Every exam in this app includes questions that do not count. They are pretest (or pilot) items: new questions the certifying body is trying out before using them for real. They are mixed in with the scored ones, they look exactly the same, and **you are not told which is which**.

The practical consequence is simple: **answer every question as if it counts.** Do not burn time trying to spot the experimental ones, and do not let a strange or very hard question rattle you: it may well be one that will never affect your score.

The practice tests in this app have **100 questions and no pretest items**, because there is no point in making you answer questions that do not count. The time limit matches the real exam's time for the scored plus unscored total, so the pace here is slightly more generous than the real thing.
guia.fuente: NHA CPT Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis (exam in effect since January 7, 2026)

guia.titulo: How the practice tests here are built
cuerpo: Each numbered practice test in this app is a **fixed set of questions**: Practice Test 3 is the same Practice Test 3 every time you open it, and it shares no question with Practice Test 2 or 4. That is what lets you work through them one by one, compare your score with last week's, and finish the set.
The order of the questions, and the order of the four options inside each question, is shuffled every time. You cannot pass by remembering that "the third one is B".

The timer runs at the pace of the real exam. The result screen shows your score against the study target, the time you took, and a breakdown by area, and every question you missed goes into your review list until you get it right three times in a row.

Every explanation names the public document it comes from: an OSHA regulation, a CDC guideline, a CLIA rule, a WHO guideline, a NIH source. None of the questions come from a textbook or from a real exam form.

To be plain about what these practice tests are: they are **not a copy of the real exam** and they are not the questions the certifying body administers. They **match the official content outline** — the areas, their weights, the number of questions and the pace — and every item is written by us from public sources. This app is an independent study aid, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by any certifying body.
guia.fuente: NHA CPT Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis (exam in effect since January 7, 2026)

guia.titulo: What is free and what is not
cuerpo: Without paying you can do four things. You can answer the first **3 questions of every area**, always the same ones, so that you see what the questions and the explanations look like in each part of the outline. You can take **a diagnostic** — a short test with the same proportions as the real exam that tells you your score by area — and repeat it every seven days with new questions. Every day you also get **five questions** from the whole bank, with their explanations. And you can read this whole guide.

What you cannot do for free is study an area to the end, take a full-length practice test, or review your mistakes. Those are the product, and they are unlocked with a single one-time purchase for this certification, or one purchase for every certification in the app. There is no subscription and there are no advertisements, and there never will be.

The number of questions and the number of practice tests you see on the home screen and on the purchase screen are read from the content itself. They are never typed in by hand, so they cannot promise more than the app contains.
guia.fuente: NHA CPT Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis (exam in effect since January 7, 2026)

guia.titulo: What this app does not cover
cuerpo: This app follows the national outline published by the National Healthcareer Association (NHA). It does not cover the rules of your state, your employer's protocols, or the eligibility routes to sit the exam (training programs, work experience, documentation). Check those with the certifying body and with your program.

It is not an official product of the certifying body and has no connection with it. The outline is public; the questions and the explanations are ours, written from public sources you can open and read. If you find a mistake, tell us: every report is checked against the source and corrected in the content, without waiting for a new version of the app.
guia.fuente: NHA CPT Test Plan, based on the 2024 job analysis (exam in effect since January 7, 2026)

calculos.titulo: Estimated blood volume: Nadler equation for a man
calculos.enunciado: A phlebotomist is asked how much circulating blood a 1.75 m, 70 kg man has, to judge how much can safely be drawn for a research protocol. Use the Nadler equation.

pasos.texto: For men, blood volume is 0.3669 times height cubed, plus 0.03219 times weight, plus 0.6041. The source prints no units; with height in meters and weight in kilograms the result comes out in liters, which is the only reading consistent with the article's own average of nearly 5 liters.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: Height in meters cubed: 5.359, the H³ term that the coefficient 0.3669 multiplies (kept to three decimals; the final answer is rounded once at the end).
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: Multiply each coefficient by its measurement. The height term is 1.966 and the weight term 2.253.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: The three parts add to 4.823 liters. Rounded to the nearest tenth: 4.8 L, close to the average adult figure of nearly 5 liters given earlier in the same article.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

calculos.trampa: Entering the height in centimeters (175³ = 5,359,375) produces millions of liters, and entering it in inches produces a number in the hundreds. If the result is not somewhere near 5 liters for an average adult, the units went in wrong.

practica.enunciado: Man, 1.80 m, 85 kg. Nadler blood volume?
Man, 1.65 m, 60 kg. Nadler blood volume?

calculos.titulo: Estimated blood volume: Nadler equation for a woman
calculos.enunciado: Estimate the circulating blood volume of a 1.62 m, 60 kg woman with the Nadler equation, and say why the answer is lower than a man's of similar size.

pasos.texto: For women the coefficients are 0.3561 for height cubed, 0.03308 for weight, and a constant of 0.1833. As with the men's equation: meters, kilograms, liters.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: 1.62 × 1.62 × 1.62 = 4.252, the H³ term that the women's coefficient 0.3561 multiplies (three decimals kept until the end).
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: The height term is 1.514 and the weight term 1.985.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: About 3.7 liters. Women tend to have a lower blood volume than men, and the article adds that a woman's blood volume rises by roughly 50 percent during pregnancy, which this equation does not model.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

calculos.trampa: Using the men's coefficients for a woman overstates her volume (here it would give about 4.1 L). The equations differ in all three numbers, not just the constant, so the sex line is chosen first.

practica.enunciado: Woman, 1.70 m, 70 kg. Nadler blood volume?
Woman, 1.55 m, 50 kg. Nadler blood volume?

calculos.titulo: Estimated blood volume from weight and BMI (Lemmens-Bernstein-Brodsky)
calculos.enunciado: For an 80 kg adult whose BMI is 22, estimate the blood volume with the Lemmens-Bernstein-Brodsky equation, and explain where the familiar "70 mL per kilogram" comes from.

pasos.texto: Blood volume equals 70 times weight divided by the square root of BMI over 22. Weight in kilograms gives milliliters. The source presents it as more accurate than Nadler at higher body weights.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: With a BMI of exactly 22 the denominator is 1, and the equation collapses to 70 mL per kilogram. That is the origin of the 70 mL/kg rule of thumb: it is this equation at a BMI of 22.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: 5,600 mL, or 5.6 liters, for the 80 kg adult.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.titulo: See what a higher BMI does
pasos.texto: At the same 80 kg but a BMI of 33 the estimate falls to about 4,570 mL: fat tissue carries less blood per kilogram, which is exactly what the square-root term corrects for.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

calculos.respuesta: 5,600 mL (5.6 L) at BMI 22; about 4,570 mL if the BMI were 33
calculos.trampa: Applying 70 mL/kg to a heavy patient with a high BMI overestimates the blood available. The 70 is not a universal constant: it is the value at BMI 22, and the equation shrinks it as BMI rises.

practica.enunciado: 65 kg adult, BMI 22. Blood volume?
90 kg adult, BMI 30.25. Blood volume (nearest 10 mL)?

calculos.titulo: Citrate tube: the 9:1 ratio and the minimum fill
calculos.enunciado: A light blue coagulation tube contains 0.3 mL of 3.2 percent sodium citrate. How much blood must enter the tube to keep the required blood-to-citrate ratio, and what is the smallest acceptable fill for a prothrombin time?

pasos.texto: Coagulation plasma is collected in 3.2 percent sodium citrate tubes at a plasma-to-anticoagulant ratio of 9:1. Nine parts blood for every one part citrate.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK606118) — Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies

pasos.titulo: Blood volume that matches the citrate
pasos.texto: One part is 0.3 mL, so nine parts is 2.7 mL of blood; the full tube holds 3.0 mL in total.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK544269) — Prothrombin Time

pasos.texto: Tube filling must be within 90 percent of the full collection volume for prothrombin time: at least 2.43 mL of blood, in practice "to the line".
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK544269) — Prothrombin Time

pasos.texto: A short draw leaves excess anticoagulant relative to plasma and prolongs clotting times, so the result would be falsely long and the tube must be recollected.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK544269) — Prothrombin Time

calculos.respuesta: 2.7 mL of blood (9:1); not less than about 2.4 mL (90 percent)
calculos.trampa: Topping up an underfilled citrate tube from a syringe or another tube changes both the ratio and the clotting state of the sample; the only fix is a fresh, properly filled tube. Likewise, drawing more blood into the tube than its vacuum allows is not possible: the vacuum is set for exactly 9:1.

practica.enunciado: A larger citrate tube holds 0.5 mL of citrate. Blood for 9:1, and the 90 percent minimum?
A pediatric citrate tube draws 1.8 mL of blood. How much citrate does it hold for 9:1?

calculos.titulo: Citrate tube: what an underfilled draw does to the ratio
calculos.enunciado: The vein collapsed and only 1.8 mL of blood entered a citrate tube that holds 0.3 mL of citrate (designed for 2.7 mL). What is the actual ratio, and is the tube acceptable?

pasos.texto: Divide both sides by 0.3: six parts blood to one part citrate instead of nine to one.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK606118) — Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies

pasos.titulo: Same ratio the other way round
pasos.formula: citrate : blood = 1 : 6, which is greater than 1 : 9
pasos.texto: The WHO lists underfilling a tube so that the ratio of anticoagulant to blood is greater than 1:9 among the errors that make a sample unusable.
pasos.referencia: WHO Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), NCBI Bookshelf NBK138675, cap. 1 Introduction

pasos.titulo: Compare the fill with the 90 percent floor
pasos.texto: The tube is 67 percent full. The acceptance threshold is 90 percent of the full collection volume, so the tube falls short by a wide margin.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK544269) — Prothrombin Time

pasos.texto: Excess anticoagulant compared to plasma prolongs clotting times, so the PT and aPTT would read falsely long. Discard and recollect with a fresh tube.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NBK544269) — Prothrombin Time

calculos.respuesta: 6:1 instead of 9:1 (67 percent full): reject and recollect
calculos.trampa: Sending it anyway "because the lab only needs 1 mL of plasma" misses the point: the volume of plasma is enough, but its citrate concentration is one and a half times too high, and the clotting time it produces is a measurement of the tube, not of the patient.

practica.enunciado: 2.4 mL of blood in the same 2.7 mL tube. Percent full and ratio? Acceptable?
2.5 mL of blood in the 2.7 mL tube. Percent full? Acceptable?

calculos.titulo: Blood culture volume: bottles, sets and the total draw
calculos.enunciado: An adult needs two sets of blood cultures, each set an aerobic and an anaerobic bottle, drawn from two separate sites. Following the CDC target volumes, how much blood goes in each bottle, each set, and in total?

pasos.texto: The CDC's collection steps say to collect 10 mL of blood in each bottle.
pasos.referencia: CDC — Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, abril 2025)

pasos.texto: A set is two bottles, for a target total of 20 mL in each set.
pasos.referencia: CDC — Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, abril 2025)

pasos.texto: The same line gives 40 mL when collecting two sets. Each set is drawn from a different site.
pasos.referencia: CDC — Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, abril 2025)

pasos.titulo: Why volume is the variable that matters
pasos.texto: Blood cultures are the first bottles in the order of draw and the volume per bottle drives their sensitivity; underfilled bottles miss low-level bacteremia. The 40 mL is planned before the needle goes in, together with whatever other tubes are ordered.
pasos.referencia: CDC — Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, abril 2025)

calculos.respuesta: 10 mL per bottle, 20 mL per set, 40 mL for two sets
calculos.trampa: Splitting a single 20 mL draw between the two sets (10 mL per set, 5 mL per bottle) halves the volume in every bottle and defeats the purpose of two sites. Two sets means two venipunctures and 40 mL.

practica.enunciado: Three sets are ordered. Total blood?
Two culture sets plus two 4 mL tubes. Total blood planned?

calculos.titulo: Blood donor minimum weight: pounds against kilograms
calculos.enunciado: A prospective whole-blood donor weighs 105 lb. The eligibility rule states the minimum as 50 kg (110 lb). Convert the weight and decide.

pasos.texto: FDA regulations require the donor to weigh a minimum of 50 kilograms (110 pounds); StatPearls states the same 110 pounds or 50 kg.
pasos.referencia: 21 CFR Part 630 — General Requirements for Blood and Blood Components, and Blood Donor Eligibility (eCFR, vigente 2026-09-04)

pasos.texto: 1 kg = 2.2 lb. 105 divided by 2.2 is 47.73, rounded to the nearest tenth 47.7 kg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: The two figures printed in the rule agree with each other under the same factor, so 2.2 is the right factor to use here.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Blood Donation (NCBI Bookshelf NBK525967, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: The donor is below the minimum in either unit (105 lb is also below 110 lb) and is deferred.
pasos.referencia: 21 CFR Part 630 — General Requirements for Blood and Blood Components, and Blood Donor Eligibility (eCFR, vigente 2026-09-04)

calculos.respuesta: 47.7 kg: under the 50 kg (110 lb) minimum, deferred
calculos.trampa: Using the NIST rounded factor 0.45 gives 47.3 kg, and using 2.2 gives 47.7 kg; the decision is the same, but on a borderline donor (say 110 lb) the two factors disagree by half a kilogram. The eligibility rule prints both units so the comparison can be made without converting at all.

practica.enunciado: Donor weighs 121 lb. kg, and eligible by weight?
Donor weighs 108 lb. kg, and eligible by weight?

calculos.titulo: A unit of whole blood as a share of total blood volume
calculos.enunciado: A whole-blood donation stops once 450 mL has been collected. For an adult with the average circulating volume of about 5 liters, what percentage of the blood volume is that?

pasos.texto: Once 450 mL of blood is collected, the needle is removed and pressure is applied.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Blood Donation (NCBI Bookshelf NBK525967, acceso abierto)

pasos.titulo: Average total volume in the same unit
pasos.texto: The average human adult has nearly 5 liters of circulating blood; converted to milliliters so the two figures can be divided.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Physiology, Blood Volume (NCBI Bookshelf NBK526077, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: A unit is about 9 percent of an average adult's blood volume.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls — Blood Donation (NCBI Bookshelf NBK525967, acceso abierto)

pasos.texto: OpenStax describes a donated unit as approximately 475 mL, about 1 pint, which gives 9.5 percent. Either way, a little under a tenth, replaced as plasma within about a day and as cells in 4 to 6 weeks.
pasos.referencia: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e (CC BY 4.0), section 18-2-production-of-the-formed-elements

calculos.trampa: Dividing 450 by 5 (liters) gives 90, and some candidates then report "90 percent". Both numbers must be in milliliters, or both in liters (0.45 ÷ 5 = 0.09), before the percentage is taken.

practica.enunciado: Same 450 mL unit from a person with 4 L of blood. Percent?
What volume is 10 percent of a 4.5 L blood volume?

calculos.enunciado: A patient's chart lists 176 lb; the blood-volume estimate and the maximum-draw policy need kilograms. Convert, and note how the clinical factor and the NIST factor differ.

pasos.texto: Dividing pounds by 2.2 gives kilograms: 80 kg.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.titulo: NIST approximate factor, as a check
pasos.texto: NIST's approximate conversion multiplies pounds by 0.45 to get kilograms: 79.2 kg. The two-digit factor is rounded, which is why it lands 0.8 kg lower.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: For dosing and volume estimates the clinical 2.2 lb per kg is the convention taught in the dose calculation sources; the answer is stated to the nearest tenth of a kilogram when it does not come out whole.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

calculos.respuesta: 80 kg (79.2 kg with the rounded NIST factor)
calculos.trampa: Multiplying by 2.2 instead of dividing turns 176 lb into 387 "kg", and every mg/kg or mL/kg figure downstream is then more than double. Kilograms are always the smaller number.

practica.enunciado: 154 lb in kg?
99 lb in kg?

calculos.titulo: Patient height: feet and inches to centimeters
calculos.enunciado: The chart gives a height of 5 ft 10 in. The Nadler equation needs meters. Convert to centimeters and then to meters.

pasos.texto: Five feet is 60 inches; add the 10 inches for 70 inches.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Dose Calculation Desired Over Have Formula Method

pasos.texto: The inch is defined as exactly 2.54 cm; NIST lists the same 2.54 for inch to centimeter.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric

pasos.texto: Meters are what the blood-volume equation takes; 1.778 m, or 1.78 m to the nearest hundredth. Height is read on the stadiometer to 0.1 cm or one-eighth of an inch.
pasos.referencia: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf): Anthropometric Measurement

calculos.trampa: Writing 5 ft 10 in as "5.10 ft" and multiplying by 30.48 gives 155.4 cm, five inches short. Feet and inches are a mixed unit: convert to inches first, then apply one factor.

practica.enunciado: 5 ft 4 in in cm (nearest tenth)?
6 ft 1 in in cm?

calculos.titulo: Temperature: Fahrenheit to Celsius before a blood culture
calculos.enunciado: A patient's temperature is recorded as 101.3 °F before a blood culture draw. Convert it to Celsius and say whether it is above the commonly used fever threshold.

pasos.texto: NIST gives the exact conversion from Fahrenheit to Celsius as (°F − 32) / 1.8.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.texto: Subtract 32 first, then divide by 1.8: 38.5 °C exactly.
pasos.referencia: NIST Office of Weights and Measures: SI Units — Temperature (fórmulas °C/°F/K)

pasos.texto: A temperature over 100.4 °F (38 °C) most often means a fever caused by an infection or illness, which is the usual reason blood cultures are ordered.
pasos.referencia: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia: Body temperature norms (001982)

calculos.trampa: Dividing by 1.8 before subtracting 32 (101.3 ÷ 1.8 − 32 = 24.3) gives an impossible body temperature. The 32 comes off first, always.
